translation:
TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
- Findings of severe osteoarthritis of the patellofemoral joint with a large full-thickness cartilage defect of the patella at its lateral portion, with multiple areas of subarticular bone marrow edema locally in the patella (ICRS grade 4) and a focus of bone marrow edema locally in the femoral condyle, as well as marginal osteophytes on the latter.
- Degenerative tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with subluxation of it.
- Mild osteoarthritis changes with joint effusion and presence of small marginal osteophytes on the femoral and tibial condyles as well as in the intercondylar notch, without narrowing of the joint space.
- Normal appearance of the lateral meniscus, the collateral ligaments, the cruciate ligaments, the tendons, the articular cartilage of the femur, and the remaining bone marrow.
- Presence of a small ruptured Baker's cyst.

translation:
Clinical History:
Knee pain under investigation.
Findings:
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
The lateral meniscus is of preserved morphology and signal, with no signs of tear.
Increased central signal of the posterior horn and part of the body of the medial meniscus peripherally, appearing to contact the inferior articular surface, suggesting a non-displaced tear, with mild edema of the regional soft tissues.
Cartilage of the femorotibial compartments and femoral trochlea without alterations.
Superficial patellar chondropathy.
Minimal joint effusion. No popliteal cysts.
Mild increased signal of the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon, with no signs of tear. Mild edema of the suprapatellar retroquadriceps fat pad.
Mild increased signal of the proximal third of the patellar tendon, with no signs of tear.
Pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Mild soft tissue edema, deep to the pes anserine tendons.
Impression:
Findings suggestive of a peripheral tear of the medial meniscus with mild regional soft tissue edema.
Minimal joint effusion.
Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis. Edema of the suprapatellar retroquadriceps fat pad, probably reactive.
Mild proximal patellar tendinosis.
Mild friction phenomena deep to the pes anserine tendons.

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: One month of knee pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Focal subchondral marrow edema at the anterior peripheral margin of the medial tibial plateau. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate, multiloculated Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: High-grade radial tear of the posterior root with moderate peripheral extrusion and superimposed complex tearing of the body and posterior horn.
Medial compartment cartilage: Large areas of full-thickness chondrosis along the weightbearing femoral condyle with underlying subchondral cystic change/edema. Diffuse high-grade tibial cartilage loss with full-thickness loss at the peripheral margin.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the femoral condyle and tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness cartilage loss along the superior aspect of the medial patellar facet with underlying subchondral cystic change and edema. Diffuse thinning of the trochlear cartilage, without focal defect.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intact, with thickening of the proximal ligament suggestive of prior injury. Bowed morphology and periligamentous edema likely secondary to meniscal extrusion.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: Mild patellar tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Moderate to severe medial compartment osteoarthritis with complex meniscal tearing and reactive subchondral edema at the peripheral medial tibial plateau.

Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus. Grade II degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus. CONCLUSION: Grade II meniscopathy in the medial and lateral menisci.

translation:
Clinical History:
Bilateral patellar tendinopathy.
Findings:
No significant bone marrow alterations.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
Lateral meniscus with preserved morphology and signal, without categorical criteria for tear.
Increased central signal of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus that does not appear to contact the articular surface, without features of a tear.
Cartilage of the femorotibial compartments and femoral trochlea without alterations. Thin focal chondral ulcer of near-full thickness of the medial facet of the patella, without secondary bone changes. The remaining femorotibial cartilage without alterations.
No significant joint effusion. Small popliteal cyst with probable leakage.
Mild increased signal at the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon and at the proximal insertion of the patellar tendon, without signs of tear.
Pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Impression:
Thin grade 3 chondral ulcer of the medial facet of the patella.
Mild proximal patellar and distal quadriceps tendinosis.
Small popliteal cyst with probable leakage.

report:
Na seriji MR presjeka desnog koljena nalazi se uredna morfologija i intenziteti signala kolateralnih
ligamenata stražnjeg križnog ligamenta, iliotibijalnog traktusa, patelarne tetive i tetive m.
kvadricepsa.
Stanje po kompletnoj rupturi prednjeg križnog ligamenta na hvatištu za femur.
Povišeni su intenziteti signala stražnjeg roga medijalnog meniska, moguće u sklopu
degenerativnih promjena, bez jasnih znakova rupture.
Lateralni menisk uredne je morfologije i intenziteta signala.
Patela je medioponirana, Wiberg 2 uz primjerenu debljinu artikulacijske hrskavice
femoropatelarnog zgloba.
Reducirana je debljina artikulacijske hrskvice femorotibijalnog zgloba medijalnog kompartmenta
uz hondromalaciju I./II. stupnja.
Sitna Bakerova cista aksijalno dimenzija oko 8 x 3 mm.
Ostale prikazane koštane, mekotkivne i neurovaskularne strukture uredne su morfologije i
intenziteta signala.
translation:
On the series of MR images of the right knee, there is normal morphology and signal intensity of the collateral ligaments, posterior cruciate ligament, iliotibial tract, patellar tendon, and quadriceps tendon.
Status post complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament at the femoral attachment.
Increased signal intensity of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, possibly in the setting of degenerative changes, without clear signs of rupture.
The lateral meniscus is of normal morphology and signal intensity.
The patella is medially positioned, Wiberg type 2, with appropriate thickness of the articular cartilage of the femoropatellar joint.
Reduced thickness of the articular cartilage of the femorotibial joint of the medial compartment with chondromalacia grade I/II.
A small Baker's cyst, axial dimensions approximately 8 x 3 mm.
All other visualized bony, soft tissue, and neurovascular structures are of normal morphology and signal intensity.

report: Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı normal. Gastroknemyus-semimembranozus bursasındaki küçük sıvı koleksiyonu sızdırmıyor. Çapraz ve yan bağlar normal. Posterolateral ve posteromedyal köşe yapıları korunmuş. Medyal menisküs yırtık içermiyor. Lateral menisküsün arka boynuzundaki horizontal yırtık serbest kenara ulaşıyor; alt eklem yüzeyi de yırtılıp medyale katlanmış. Menisküslerdeki ince kalsifikasyonlar kondrokalsinozis/psödogut ile uyumlu. Patella apeksindeki, tibyal platonun posterolateralindeki ve medyal femoral kondilde ağırlık taşıyan kesimdeki tam kat eklem kıkırdağı kayıplarına gerek bu kesimlerde, gerekse patellanın daha lateralinde subkondral medüller fibrokistik ve fibrovasküler değişiklikler eşlik ediyor. Ekstensör mekanizma korunmuş.
translation: The intra-articular fluid volume is normal. The small fluid collection in the gastrocnemius-semimembranosus bursa does not extend. The cruciate and collateral ligaments are normal. The posterolateral and posteromedial corner structures are intact. The medial meniscus does not contain a tear. The horizontal tear in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus reaches the free edge; the inferior articular surface is also torn and folded medially. Fine calcifications in the menisci are consistent with chondrocalcinosis/pseudogout. Full-thickness articular cartilage loss at the apex of the patella, the posterolateral tibial plateau, and the weight-bearing portion of the medial femoral condyle is accompanied by subchondral medullary fibrocystic and fibrovascular changes both in these areas and more laterally in the patella. The extensor mechanism is intact.

report:
Mediales Kompartiment:
Ossäre Belastungsreaktion am medialen Tibiaplateau sowie geringer am medialen Femurcondylus mit Nachweis von Osteophyten. Medial deutlich ausgedünnter Knorpel am medialen Femurcondylus und Tibiaplateau Grad III-IV nach Outerbridge. 
Komplexer Riss der Pars intermedia des Innenmeniskus mit horizontaler und radiärer Komponente (Serie 3/ Image 116, Serie 5/ Image 23). Mukoide Degeneration des Innenmeniskushinterhorns.
Gering Flüssigkeit um das MCL.

Laterales Kompartiment:
Umschriebener 5 x 7 mm messender Knorpeldefekt dorsal am lateralen Femurkondylus (Serie 5/ Image 27).
Intakter Außenmeniskus. Intaktes LCL.

Patellares Gleitlager:
Zweitgradiger Knorpeldefekt am anterioren Femurcondylus (Serie 7/ Image 22).

Patella:
Einzelne zweitgradige Knorpeldefekte retropatellär der medialen und lateralen Patellafacette.

Bänder:
Intakte Kreuzbänder.

Muskulatur und Weichteile:
Ansatztendinopathie der Quadrizepssehne.
Kleiner freier Gelenkkörper im dorsalen Recessus (Serie 6/ Image 15)
Umschriebene, ovaläre 1,1 x 2,5 x cc 2,1 cm messende T2-hyperintense, T1-hypointense Läsion im subkutanen Fettgewebe anterolateral auf Höhe des Gelenkspalts (Serie 4/ Image 21). Geringer Gelenkerguss.
translation:
Medial Compartment:
Osseous stress reaction at the medial tibial plateau and to a lesser degree at the medial femoral condyle with evidence of osteophytes. Markedly thinned cartilage medially at the medial femoral condyle and tibial plateau, grade III-IV according to Outerbridge.
Complex tear of the intermediate portion of the medial meniscus with horizontal and radial components (Series 3/ Image 116, Series 5/ Image 23). Mucoid degeneration of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus.
Small amount of fluid around the MCL.

Lateral Compartment:
Well-circumscribed cartilage defect measuring 5 x 7 mm on the dorsal aspect of the lateral femoral condyle (Series 5/ Image 27).
Intact lateral meniscus. Intact LCL.

Patellofemoral Compartment:
Grade II cartilage defect at the anterior femoral condyle (Series 7/ Image 22).

Patella:
Individual grade II cartilage defects on the retropatellar surface of the medial and lateral patellar facets.

Ligaments:
Intact cruciate ligaments.

Musculature and Soft Tissues:
Insertional tendinopathy of the quadriceps tendon.
Small loose body in the dorsal recess (Series 6/ Image 15).
Well-circumscribed, ovoid T2-hyperintense, T1-hypointense lesion measuring 1.1 x 2.5 x 2.1 cm in the subcutaneous fat tissue anterolaterally at the level of the joint space (Series 4/ Image 21). Small joint effusion.

report:
MRI of right Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS, SG T1W


> Small size of lateral meniscus with absent bow-tie sign, in favor of lateral meniscus tear.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of  grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration.
> Wearing of articular cartilage and subchondral bone marrow edeama, especially at lateral aspect of knee joint; large spur formation.
   Wearing articular cartilage of patella and spur, in favor of grade 3 patellar chondromalacia.
> The contour of ACL and PCL is in a straight line but increase signal intensity inside, in favor of grade 1 injury.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with thick suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.

Impression: 
1. Lateral meniscus tear.
2. Osteoarthritis of right knee joint, more severe at lateral compartment.
3. Synovitis of right knee and complex patellar plicae and suprapatellar burisitis.
4. Grade 3 patellar chondromalacia.
5. Grade 1 injury of ACL and PCL.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management

   Wearing articular cartilage of patella and spur, in favor of grade 3 patellar chondromalacia.
> The contour of ACL and PCL is in a straight line but increase signal intensity inside, in favor of grade 1 injury.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with thick suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.

Impression: 
1. Lateral meniscus tear.
2. Osteoarthritis of right knee joint, more severe at lateral compartment.
3. Synovitis of right knee and complex patellar plicae and suprapatellar burisitis.
4. Grade 3 patellar chondromalacia.
5. Grade 1 injury of ACL and PCL.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management

Patella alta (Insall-Salvati ratio 1.5), Wiberg type III.
Irregular, slightly depressed medial contour of the patella in the region of the apex, possibly consistent with an impaction fracture. Extensive surrounding bone marrow edema.
In the region of the lateral femoral condyle, anterior to the insertion of the popliteus tendon, there is also a depressed bone contour over an area of approximately 9 mm in diameter, which may correspond to an impaction fracture. Extensive surrounding bone marrow edema.
Thickening and edema of the medial patellar retinaculum with discontinuity of fibers in the central portion consistent with a rupture. A small amount of effusion suprapatellarly and in the medial recess with a more prominent suprapatellar fat pad.
The described changes are most likely secondary to lateral patellar dislocation.
A small compact bone island in the lateral femoral condyle and tibia.
Grade 1 chondromalacic changes of the cartilage of the medial patellar facet.

Early enthesopathic changes at the insertion of the quadriceps tendon and at the patellar insertion of the patellar ligament.
Complete suprapatellar plica.
The anterior cruciate ligament shows slightly increased signal intensity at the tibial insertion, possibly consistent with a post-distension state or minor partial tear.
The posterior cruciate ligament shows normal signal intensity and intact continuity.
Linear hyperintensity in the red zone of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, which may correspond to a vascular structure, without evidence of a tear.
The lateral meniscus shows normal signal intensity, without signs of a tear.
The medial collateral ligament shows normal signal intensity and intact continuity.
Enthesopathic changes at the proximal insertion of the lateral collateral ligament.
Enthesopathic changes and minor bursitis of the popliteus tendon.
Normal appearance of the iliotibial tract and pes anserinus.
Baker's cyst measuring approximately 22x12x27 mm (AP x LL x CC).

translation:

Meniscal tear and lateral chondral lesion of the right knee.
Findings:
Cruciate and collateral ligaments without alterations.
Medial meniscus with preserved morphology and signal, no signs of tear.
Complex tear of the anterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus with a segment extending into the meniscotibial recess at the level of the body. Mild diffuse meniscal extrusion.
Partial and full-thickness chondral ulcers of the weight-bearing zone of the lateral femorotibial compartment, measuring up to approximately 7 x 5 mm in their anteroposterior and mediolateral axes respectively at the level of the posterior weight-bearing region of the lateral femoral condyle, with secondary bone changes.
Cartilage of the medial femorotibial and patellofemoral compartments without significant alterations.
Minimal joint effusion. No popliteal cysts.
Edema of the suprapatellar retroquadriceps fat pad.
Quadriceps tendon, patellar tendon, pes anserinus tendons, biceps femoris tendon and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Impression:
Complex tear of the lateral meniscus with a segment extending into the meniscotibial recess at the level of the body. Mild diffuse meniscal extrusion.
Chondropathy grade 3 and 4 lesions of the lateral femorotibial compartment.
Minimal joint effusion.
Edema of the suprapatellar retroquadriceps fat pad, findings that could represent patellar malalignment phenomena.

report:
МР находка: Няма данни за ставен излив. Костите, формиращи дясната колянна става, са с нормална структура и форма. Наличие на Фабела. Вижда се малък костномозъчен едем в епифизата на фемура и епиметафизата на тибията от латералната страна. Няма данни за фрактура. Предната кръстна връзка е със запазена цялост, но дифузно повишен сигнален интензитет – изменението вероятно съответства на частично скъсване на влакната на връзката. Задна кръстна връзка – б.о. В задния рог на медиалния менискус се вижда хиперинтензна лезия, която не достига до ставните краища на тибията и фемура. Хрущял на пателата – б.о. Фоса поплитеа – нормално изобразяване. Колатерални лигаменти, ретинакулуми – със запазена цялост. 
Заключение: МР данни за парциална руптура на предната кръстна връзка. Лезия на задния рог на медиалния менискус – grade 2c. Локлани костномозъчни едеми в тибията и фемура латерално.
translation:
MRI Findings: No evidence of joint effusion. The bones forming the right knee joint have normal structure and shape. Presence of a fabella. A small bone marrow edema is seen in the femoral epiphysis and the tibial epimetaphysis on the lateral side. No evidence of fracture. The anterior cruciate ligament is intact in continuity but shows diffusely increased signal intensity – the change likely corresponds to a partial tear of the ligament fibers. Posterior cruciate ligament – unremarkable. A hyperintense lesion is seen in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, which does not reach the articular surfaces of the tibia and femur. Patellar cartilage – unremarkable. Popliteal fossa – normal appearance. Collateral ligaments, retinacula – intact.
Conclusion: MRI findings of partial rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament. Lesion of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 2c. Local bone marrow edema in the tibia and femur laterally.

report:
COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:One-year history of right knee pain with instability.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Complex tear posterior horn medial meniscus consistent with a focal radial tear as well as inferiorly surfacing oblique tear, the latter extending into the medial meniscal body which is slightly peripherally extruded. The posterior root is intact. The anterior horn is intact.

The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal tibial mid fibers of the superficial medial collateral ligament. Components of the deep medial collateral ligament including the posterior oblique ligament are intact.

The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact.

Minimal lateral patellar subluxation. The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 16 mm, above the upper limit of normal. The patellar retinacula are intact.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Mild patellofemoral chondrosis. Mild to moderate medial femorotibial chondrosis with subtle cartilage thinning. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex tear posterior horn medial meniscus with slight medial meniscal extrusion.
2. Mild to moderate tricompartment chondrosis most pronounced along the medial femorotibial compartment suggesting evolving mild osteoarthritis of the right knee.
3. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the superficial medial collateral ligament. Component of the deep medial collateral ligament are intact.
4. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear.
5. Lateralization of the tibial tubercle, which may predispose to patellofemoral maltracking/instability. At most minimal lateral patellar subluxation.

translation:
LEFT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade I degeneration is observed in the lateral meniscus. Grade II degeneration in the medial meniscus and an appearance consistent with a horizontal tear in its posterior horn are present. The medial meniscus appears extruded. The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps is normal. A 9 mm subcortical cyst at the anterior aspect of the medial tibial plateau level and bone marrow edema in the adjacent bone are observed. A partial tear is observed at the femoral attachment of the medial head of the gastrocnemius. Edema is observed in the infrapatellar fat pad.

report:
MRI of left Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

* The contour of ACL not in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, in favor of tear.
  Laxity contour of MCL with increased signal intensity on F/S T2WI, in favor of partial tear.
> The contour of PCL and LCL in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside PCL and proximal LCL on F/S T2WI, in favor of grade 1 injury.
> Some joint effusion and  suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plica; mild hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of mild synovitis.
> Abnormal signal intensity is noted in proximal tibia ( more prominent at posterior tibial plateau and intercondylar eminance) and distal femur, which shows low signal intensity on T1WI and high signal intensity on T2WI, in favor of bone contusion.
  Suspicious of mild impaction of lateral femoral condyle. 
   > Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of lateral meniscus, and unclear contour of central portion, in favor of bucket handle tear of lateral meniscus.
> Bone marrow edema over low pole of patella and mild increased signal intensity of patellar tendon on F/S T2WI, in favor of grade 1  injury.
  Mild laxity of medial patellar retinuaculum with increased singal intensity on F/S T2WI, in favor of grade 2 injury.
  Howevere, no dislocation of patella in this study.
> Mild muscle edema over vastus lateralis and medialis muscle and subcutaneous edema.
Impression: 
1. C/W ACL tear.	
2. High grade partial tear of MCL.
3. Grade 1-2 injury of PCL and grade 1 injury of proximal LCL.
4. C/W bucket handle tear of posterior horn of lateral meniscus. 
5. Bone contusion of left proximal tibia and distal femur and low pole patella.
6. R/O transient patellar dislocation with impaction of lateral femoral condyle and low pole of patella and suspicious of partial tear of medial patellar retinaculum.
7. Synovitis and patellar plicae of left knee and small Baker's cyst.  
8. Mild muscle edema over vastus lateralis and medialis muscle and subcutaneous edema.  
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

report:
Na učinjenim MR presjecima kroz lijevo koljeno vide se difuzno zone masne supstitucije, bez
koštanog edema. Vidi se blaga anteriorna translacija tibije.
Vide se sitne fisure hrskavice lateralnog kompartmenta femorotibijalnog zgloba kao i trohlearne
hrskavice - hondromalacija II. stupnja. Hondromalacija I. stupnja hrskavice medijalnog platoa
tibije kao i patelarne hrskavice.
Prednji križni ligament je nabran, promijenjenih intenziteta signala, bez jasnog prikaza vlakana
na samom havtištu za femur - kompletna ruptura.
Stražnji križni ligament održan, primjerenih intenziteta signala.
Menisci su umjereno degenerativno izmjenjeni.
Kosa ruptura stražnjeg roga medijalnog meniska s otvaranjem na tibijalnu plohu.
Edem posterolateralne zglobne čahure, bez evidentne meniskokapsularne separacije.
Bez znakova rupture lateralnog meniska.
Anterolateralni ligament je povišenih intenziteta signala u smislu distenzije, moguće i parcijalne
rupture.
Kolateralni ligamenti su bez znakova rupture.
Tetiva m. kvadricepsa i loigament patele primjerenog prikaza.
Burzitis tetive m. semimembranosus.
Manji zglobni izljev, predominantno suprapatelarno.
Ostali nalaz neupadljiv.
translation:
On the obtained MR images through the left knee, diffuse zones of fatty substitution are seen, without bone edema. Mild anterior translation of the tibia is seen.
Fine fissures of the cartilage of the lateral compartment of the femorotibial joint as well as the trochlear cartilage are seen - chondromalacia grade II. Chondromalacia grade I of the cartilage of the medial tibial plateau as well as the patellar cartilage.
The anterior cruciate ligament is buckled, with altered signal intensity, without clear visualization of fibers at the femoral insertion - complete rupture.
The posterior cruciate ligament is intact, with appropriate signal intensity.
The menisci are moderately degenerative in appearance.
Oblique tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with opening onto the tibial surface.
Edema of the posterolateral joint capsule, without evident meniscocapsular separation.
No signs of tear of the lateral meniscus.
The anterolateral ligament shows increased signal intensity consistent with distension, possibly also partial rupture.
The collateral ligaments show no signs of tear.
The quadriceps tendon and patellar ligament are of appropriate appearance.
Bursitis of the semimembranosus tendon.
Minor joint effusion, predominantly suprapatellar.
The remaining findings are unremarkable.

report:
MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Clicking, locking, exclude meniscal tear..

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination. The extensor mechanism is intact. There is patella alta. The Insall Salvati ratio measures about 1.6.
The finding is associated with advanced patellofemoral joint osteoarthritic change with extensive denuding of the articular cartilage and with extensive subcortical cyst formation particularly seen along the apex and lateral facet of patella. Prominent trochlear and patellar osteophytes are demonstrated.

The medial patellar retinaculum is attenuated likely related to previous lateral dislocation and partial disruption. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact.

There is a degenerative medial meniscal tear. There is maceration and linear signal seen in the posterior horn extending into the body. An oblique inferiorly surfacing tear of the body and posterior horn is a demonstrated. The finding is associated with severe chondral denuding and exuberant marginal osteophyte formation seen to the medial joint compartment. There is also subcortical edema seen to the weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.

The lateral meniscus is macerated and not identified at the body and posterior horn. Findings are in keeping with extensive maceration and degenerative tearing of the body and the posterior horn of lateral meniscus. The finding is associated with denuding of the entire articular cartilage of lateral joint compartment associated with prominent lateral joint compartment osteophyte formation. There is also subcortical sclerosis and mild edema seen within the lateral joint compartment. An intraosseous cyst is seen to the lateral femoral condyle with 3 cm in keeping with subcortical tear.

The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate and medial collateral ligament are intact.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon appear intact.

There is a large knee effusion with reactive synovitis. There is no significant Baker's cyst. In the lateral popliteal fossa there is a large intraosseous loose body projecting anterior to the proximal fibers of the lateral head of the gastrocnemius measuring about 2.4 cm in maximum dimension. Smaller loose bodies are likely present in this region.

INTERPRETATION: 

Severe tricompartmental osteoarthritic change most severely affecting patellofemoral and lateral compartments. Degenerative meniscal tears laterally and medially with cartilaginous denuding to the lateral medial and patellofemoral compartments.

Loose bodies.

Patella alta with attenuation of the medial patellar retinaculum likely related to prior transient lateral dislocation of the patella.

FINDINGS:

There is a large knee joint effusion with synovitis. There is no popliteal cysts.

There are moderate degenerative changes in the medial and patellofemoral compartments with high-grade cartilage thinning involving the lateral patellar facet and lateral aspect of femoral trochlea.

There is diffuse intrasubstance degeneration with maceration, extrusion and degenerative tearing of the lateral meniscus. The medial meniscus demonstrates intrasubstance degeneration without a well-defined linear tear.

There is intrasubstance mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

Otherwise the extensor mechanism, the medial collateral ligament, the pes anserine tendons, the semimembranosus, the popliteus, the distal biceps femoris, the lateral collateral ligament and the IT band are unremarkable.

CONCLUSION:

2. Diffuse intrasubstance degeneration with maceration and degenerative tearing of the lateral meniscus with intrasubstance degeneration of the medial meniscus. There is no well-defined linear tear.

3. Intrasubstance mucoid degeneration of the ACL without ligament injury.

4. Knee joint effusion with synovitis without popliteal cyst.

Recent patellar dislocation. Underlying femoropatellar dysplasia, predisposing factor.

translation:
The articular bodies are congruent.
Patchy zones of red marrow reconversion in the metadiaphysis of the femur.
Chondromalacia of the patellar cartilage grade I–II. Denudation of the trochlear cartilage in the medial part with a small focus of bone edema (chondromalacia grade IV).
Thinning of the articular cartilage of the femorotibial joint with dissection changes and chondromalacia grade III of the medial femoral condyle and the lateral tibial plateau. Marginal osteophytosis of all articular surfaces of the femorotibial joint and the patellofemoral joint.
The described findings correspond to moderate gonarthrosis.
Minimal joint effusion.
The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are of appropriate signal intensity, without signs of rupture.
Septated ganglion cyst adjacent to the posterior cruciate ligament measuring 14 × 5 mm on sagittal sections.
The lateral meniscus is of altered signal intensity in the sense of myxoid degeneration with a visible chronic complex rupture of the body on the background of a degeneratively changed meniscus, extending to the tibial articular surface. Also complex rupture of the posterior horn and root.
Extrusion of the body of the lateral meniscus beyond the articular surface by up to 3 mm.
A defect of the inferior popliteomeniscal fascicles is visible with formation of a ganglion cyst along the popliteus tendon, measuring 20 × 8 mm on axial sections.
The medial meniscus is of altered signal intensity in the form of myxoid degeneration, without signs of rupture. Minor extrusion in the body region by up to 2 mm.
The medial collateral ligament is of appropriate signal intensity, without signs of rupture.
The lateral collateral ligament is of reduced tension with altered signal intensity at the femoral attachment, probably due to distension.
Minor effusion in the sheath of the popliteus tendon, which is of altered signal intensity at the femoral attachment as part of tendinopathic changes.
In the region of the tibial insertion, a minor partial rupture of the semimembranosus tendon.
The pes anserinus tendons and the iliotibial tract are of appropriate signal intensity.
The quadriceps tendon and the patellar ligament are of altered signal intensity in the region of the attachment in the sense of enthesopathic changes.
The neurovascular structures are appropriately visualized.

Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.

Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.

Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.

Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

Complex tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with mild extrusion.

The medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is no significant Baker's cyst.

There is mild prepatellar edema and edema overlying the lateral aspect of the knee.

There is a small knee effusion.

INTERPRETATION: 

Complete anterior cruciate ligament tear with anterior tibial drawer.

No significant meniscal tears.

translation:
MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
On evaluation of the lateral meniscus, the cruciate and collateral ligaments, and the articular cartilage, no significant findings are observed.
The medial meniscus shows abnormal signal, discontinuity at the posterior horn, and subluxation with abnormal signal in the body.
Bone marrow edema in the medial tibial condyle is attributed to the meniscal tear.
Additionally, intra-articularly, thickening of the synovial membrane is identified, which is also observed within the Baker's synovial cyst at the medial popliteal fossa, while simultaneously a subcortical cystic lesion is demonstrated adjacent to the insertion of the posterior cruciate ligament and an edematous lesion subcortically at the tibial eminence.

CONCLUSION:
1. Degenerative tear of the medial meniscus.
2. Synovitis within a moderate joint effusion in the knee joint, with the presence of focal edema and cystic lesions, raises suspicion of inflammatory arthritis and therefore rheumatological evaluation is recommended.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.  

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES: 
Alignment is anatomic.  No acute fracture. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process.  No aggressive osseous lesions.  

JOINT SPACE:
0.8 cm osseous body identified posteriorly, medial to the distal posterior cruciate ligament. 
Moderate joint effusion. Moderate, ruptured Baker's cyst.

Medial meniscus:  Oblique undersurface tear of the posterior horn and body with dominate complete radial tear at the posterior root of the medial meniscus. Mild extrusion of the body. 
Medial compartment cartilage: High-grade chondrosis anterior weightbearing portion of the femoral condyle with subchondral cystic change/edema.  

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear. 
Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild chondrosis.    

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: 
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade chondrosis of the patella and to less extent trochlea with areas of full-thickness cartilage loss with subchondral cystic change/edema.     

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.  
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Mucoid degeneration of the distal PCL with small intraosseous ganglion at insertion.  

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.  
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.  
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal. 

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: Mild patellar tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.  
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad.  No lateral patellar tilt or translation.  No patella alta.  Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 11 mm. 

MUSCLES/TENDONS: 
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy.  Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact. 

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. 

IMPRESSION:
1.	Tear of the medial meniscus with dominate radial tear at the posterior root . 
2.	Intra-articular osseous body.
3.	Moderate joint effusion and moderate Baker's cyst.
4.	Tricompartment chondrosis.

translation:
MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1-weighted pulse sequences, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo.

FINDINGS
A small joint effusion is observed in the joint cavity.
On evaluation of the lateral meniscus, the cruciate and collateral ligaments, and the bone marrow, no pathological findings are observed.
The medial meniscus shows simple degeneration without tear.
On evaluation of the articular cartilage, chondral osteophytes are observed in the anterior portion as well as on the posterior weight-bearing surface of the lateral femoral condyle.
In places, small foci of chondrocalcinosis are observed.
On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, a shallow femoral trochlea is observed (sulcus angle 170°), as well as a small area of edema in the lateral prefemoral fat pad.

CONCLUSION
The shallow femoral trochlea and the edema in the prefemoral fat pad are consistent with patellar maltracking.
Early degenerative changes with the presence of chondral osteophytes and the presence of a small joint effusion.

report: Regelrechte Artikulationsverhältnisse femorotibial und femoropatellar. Flächig vollschichtige Chondropathie der lateralen Patellafacette mit lefzenartigem chondralen Rand auf Höhe des Patellafirstes. Assoziiert reaktive subchondrale Zysten- sowie Ödembildung. Fokale vollschichtige Chondropathie auch randständig an der lateralen Trochlea mit ebenfalls kleiner subchondraler Zysten- und Ödembildung. Femorotibial gering verschmälerter Knorpelbesatz ohne tiefgreifende Chondropathie. Innenmeniskus im Hinterhorn mukoid signalalteriert. Keine fassbare meniscale Rissbildung. translation: Normal femorotibial and femoropatellar articulation. Broad full-thickness chondropathy of the lateral patellar facet with a flap-like chondral edge at the level of the patellar ridge. Associated reactive subchondral cyst and edema formation. Focal full-thickness chondropathy also at the margin of the lateral trochlea with likewise small subchondral cyst and edema formation. Femorotibial mildly narrowed cartilage coverage without deep chondropathy. Medial meniscus with mucoid signal alteration in the posterior horn. No detectable meniscal tear. Postoperative changes after previously placed tibial intramedullary nail partially captured. Prominent joint effusion. Local reactive synovitis.

report:
COMPARISON:   

CLINICAL HISTORY:Chronic right knee pain overlying the patella/patellar tendon. Clinical suspicion for patellofemoral pain syndrome.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The medial meniscus is intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 14, within normal limits. No patellofemoral subluxation.

Scattered foci of mild chondrosis throughout the patellofemoral compartment. Scattered foci of mild chondrosis throughout the medial and lateral femorotibial compartments.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. No evidence of discrete meniscal, ligament, or tendon tear.
2. Mild tricompartment chondrosis.

translation: MRI findings: No evidence of joint effusion. The bones forming the right knee joint are of normal shape and signal intensity. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia is intact. The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact. MRI findings of a lesion of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 3 against a background of reduced meniscal volume. In the posterior horn of the meniscus, a thickened hyperintense line with oblique course is seen, reaching the edge of the meniscus. Behind the medial intercondylar eminence, a multiloculated, bilayered meniscal cyst measuring 12/10 mm is visualized. Its anterior horn is intact. Normal appearance of the lateral meniscus. Normal appearance of the lateral and medial collateral ligaments. Patella, retinacula, patellar cartilage – normal appearance. Patellar ligament and quadriceps femoris tendon – normal appearance. Conclusion: MRI findings of a lesion of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 3. Multiloculated meniscal cyst dorsal to the medial intercondylar eminence.

report: МР находка: МР данни за хеморагичен ставен излив. Вижда се изразен костномозъчен едем в латералния кондил на фемура. Костномозъчен едем се изобразява и в дясната половина на пателата. Артикулиращия хрущял на фемура и тибията е със запазена цялост. Вижда се лезия в предния рог на медиалния менискус – 2b степен. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. МР данни за увреда на медиалния пателарен ретинакулум. Последният е с прекъсната цялост на фона на изразен мекотъканен едем по съседство. Нормално представен медиален колатерален лигамент. Кръстните връзки са със запазена цялост. МР данни за парциална увреда на латералния колатерален лигамент. Последният се представя с дифузно уголемен напречник и повишен интензитет на сигнала. Изразен мекотъканен и подкожен едем по съседство на лигамента. Латералният пателарен ретинакулум е със запазена цялост. Като допълнителна находка се визуализира фрагментация в областта на туберозитас тибие, както при болест на Osgood-schlatter. Сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис, лигамент на пателата – нормално изобразяване. Поплитеална ямка – б.о.  Заключение: МР данни за хемартроза. Контузионен костномозъчен едем в латералния кондил на фемура и в дясната половина на пателата. Увреда на латералния колатерален лигамент. Руптура на медиалния пателарен ретинакулум. Лезия в предния рог на медиалния менискус – grade 2b.
translation:
MRI findings: MRI evidence of hemorrhagic joint effusion. Pronounced bone marrow edema is seen in the lateral femoral condyle. Bone marrow edema is also visualized in the right half of the patella. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia is intact. A lesion is seen in the anterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 2b. Normal appearance of the lateral meniscus. MRI findings of injury to the medial patellar retinaculum. The latter shows disrupted integrity against a background of pronounced adjacent soft tissue edema. Normal appearance of the medial collateral ligament. The cruciate ligaments are intact. MRI findings of partial injury to the lateral collateral ligament. The latter appears with diffusely increased diameter and increased signal intensity. Pronounced soft tissue and subcutaneous edema adjacent to the ligament. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact. As an additional finding, fragmentation is visualized in the region of the tibial tuberosity, as in Osgood-Schlatter disease. Quadriceps femoris tendon, patellar ligament – normal appearance. Popliteal fossa – unremarkable.

Conclusion: MRI findings of hemarthrosis. Contusion bone marrow edema in the lateral femoral condyle and in the right half of the patella. Injury to the lateral collateral ligament. Rupture of the medial patellar retinaculum. Lesion in the anterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 2b.

translation: Mild increase in intra-articular fluid of the knee joint. Cruciate and collateral ligaments are normal. Degeneration in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus is not accompanied by a tear. Lateral meniscus is normal. Chondral degeneration characterized by superficial chondral irregularities is observed in the lateral aspect of the medial femorotibial compartment. Chondral degeneration characterized by fissures reaching 50% of the chondral thickness is also observed in the medial aspect of the trochlear cartilage. The intraosseous bone island in the posterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle measures 5 mm in diameter. Bones and cartilaginous structures are otherwise normal. Proximal tibiofibular joint is normal. Tendinosis at the insertion level of the patellar tendon to the patella is short-segment and mild in degree. The extensor mechanism is otherwise preserved. Subcutaneous varicose venous structures posterior to the knee joint may be associated with venous insufficiency.

translation:
[DATE]: MR Knee Left 15ch
AA: Clinical information: See scanned request
Diagnostic question: See scanned request
Findings: Extensive horizontal tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with extension into the inferior meniscal surface almost reaching the free edge. Cruciate ligaments and lateral ligaments intact. Lateral meniscus intact. Baker's cyst measuring 3 x 2 x 1 cm, T2-hyperintense, possibly with recent rupture given extensive fluid infiltration superficial to the medial gastrocnemius muscle. Moderate distension of the suprapatellar recess. Suspicion of early medial femorotibial cartilage damage grade 2 with thinned appearance of cartilage on the anterior and central weight-bearing portion of the medial femoral condyle.
Conclusion:
- Extensive horizontal tear of the medial meniscus.
- Possibly early medial femorotibial cartilage damage grade 2, currently with moderate effusion.
- Small Baker's cyst, however with recent rupture.

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for 3 months after injury playing volleyball.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tear of the posterior root with dominant radial component. No extrusion or displaced fragment.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Top normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 16 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Complex tear of the posterior root of the medial meniscus with dominant radial component. No extrusion or displaced fragment.

translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI

Examination protocol: Coronal and sagittal proton density and coronal T1 images.

Findings:
The lateral meniscus is normal.
The medial meniscus shows 3.5 mm medial extrusion, a meniscal root tear, and grade II degeneration in the posterior horn and body.
The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, and lateral collateral ligament are normal.
Periligamentous edema is observed in the medial collateral ligament (grade I sprain).
The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal.
The patella is normally positioned.
There is no retinacular discontinuity.
Edema is observed in the prepatellar subcutaneous fat tissue.
A millimetric partial tear and signal change consistent with tendinosis are observed in the tendon at the proximal insertion level of the medial head of the gastrocnemius.
Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space.
Mild narrowing of the joint space in the medial tibiofemoral compartment, and focal thinning of the femoral and tibial cartilages adjacent to the joint are observed.
Subchondral millimetric cysts are observed in the medial tibial plateau.
Diffuse bone marrow edema is observed in the medial femoral condyle.
In the described area of edema, an 11x5 mm hypointense appearance on PD and T1 images is observed in the subchondral area, interpreted as favoring an osteochondral defect.
A Baker's cyst measuring 5x2 cm is observed in the popliteal fossa.
A periarticular ganglion cyst measuring 2x1.5 cm is observed in the posterior vicinity of the tibiofibular joint.

CONCLUSION:
Mild degenerative arthritis findings in the medial tibiofemoral compartment.
Diffuse bone marrow edema in the medial femoral condyle and osteochondral defect in the subchondral area.
Medial extrusion, root tear, and grade II meniscopathy of the medial meniscus.
Partial tear and tendinosis of the medial head of the gastrocnemius tendon.
Suprapatellar bursitis.
Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament.
Baker's cyst in the popliteal fossa.
Periarticular ganglion cyst in the vicinity of the tibiofemoral joint.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Suspected osteochondral injury right knee.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The medial meniscus is intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 11 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

There is fissuring of articular cartilage at the central femoral trochlea with focal full thickness cartilage denuding along the medial patellar facet. No evidence of displaced or unstable osteochondral fragment. Femorotibial articular cartilage is preserved.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Focal high-grade patellofemoral chondrosis as detailed above. No evidence of displaced or unstable osteochondral fragment.
2. No evidence of discrete meniscal, ligament, or tendon tear.

report: МР находка: Костите формиращи лявата колянна става се изобразяват с хомогенна структура и сигнален интензитет. Визуализират се малки остеофити по ставните краища на фемура и тибията, в областта на интеркондиларните еминенции, както и по долната повърхност на пателата. Артикулиращия хрущял на фемура и тибията от медиалната страна е изтънен, стеснена е медиалната ставна междина с наличие на „вакуум феномен“ в нея. Кръстните връзки са със запазена цялост. МР данни за увреда на медиалния менискус. Менискусът се представя с дифузно повишен интензитет на сигнала на фона на стеснената ставна междина. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. Нормално изобразяване на колатералните лигаменти. Хрущял на пателата, ретинакулуми – без особености. Лигамент на пателата и сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис – б.о. Поплитеална ямка – нормално изобразяване. Заключение: МР данни за гонартроза, по-изразена от медиалната страна на колянната става – 2 към 3 степен по класификацията на Kellgren and Lawrence. Увреда на медиалния менискус – 3 степен.
translation: MRI findings: The bones forming the left knee joint demonstrate homogeneous structure and signal intensity. Small osteophytes are visualized at the articular margins of the femur and tibia, in the region of the intercondylar eminences, as well as along the inferior surface of the patella. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia on the medial side is thinned, the medial joint space is narrowed with presence of a "vacuum phenomenon" within it. The cruciate ligaments are intact. MRI evidence of damage to the medial meniscus. The meniscus presents with diffusely increased signal intensity against the background of the narrowed joint space. Normal appearance of the lateral meniscus. Normal appearance of the collateral ligaments. Patellar cartilage, retinacula – unremarkable. Patellar ligament and quadriceps femoris tendon – unremarkable. Popliteal fossa – normal appearance. Conclusion: MRI evidence of gonarthrosis, more pronounced on the medial side of the knee joint – grade 2 to 3 according to the Kellgren and Lawrence classification. Damage to the medial meniscus – grade 3.

translation:
MRI RIGHT/LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
- In both knee joints, a congenitally high position of the patella is observed (Insall-Salvati ratio 1.5 right and 1.6 left). Additionally, bilateral mild edema is observed in the upper lateral portion of Hoffa's fat pad, immediately below the patellae, as well as in the prefemoral fat pad.
- The collateral and cruciate ligaments, as well as the medial and lateral menisci, appear normal bilaterally.
- The articular cartilage is within normal limits.
- The bone marrow shows normal signal.
- No significant intra-articular fluid collection.

IMPRESSION
The above findings are indicative of patellar tracking dysfunction and impingement syndrome in the anterior compartment.

report:
FINDINGS:

There is a large knee joint effusion.

There is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament near its femoral insertion. There are pivot shift bone marrow contusion with a subchondral impaction fracture involving the lateral femoral condyle with associated significant bone marrow edema. There are also bone contusion involving the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau without fracture.

There is high-grade tear of the medial collateral ligament with complete disruption of its fibers at its femoral attachment with also thickening and increased signal throughout the superficial component. There is no distal avulsion or proximal retraction of the distal superficial component. There is also complete tear of the deep meniscal femoral component with significant thickening of the meniscal tibial component.

There is a horizontal tear involving the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending to the inferior articular surface. There is no displaced meniscal fragment. There is a an oblique tear involving the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus at the insertion of the Wrisberg ligament compatible with a Wrisberg rip.

There is edema involving the myotendinous junction of the popliteus. The popliteus tendon itself is intact.

Otherwise the posterior cruciate ligament, the extensor mechanism, the semimembranosus, the distal biceps femoris, the lateral collateral ligament and the IT band are unremarkable.

CONCLUSION:

1. Complete tear of the ACL.

2. High-grade sprain of the medial collateral ligament without evidence of pseudocyst Stener.

3. Medial and lateral meniscal tear without displaced fragment.

4. Pivot shift bone marrow contusion with subchondral impaction fracture of the lateral femoral condyle.

5. Moderate knee joint effusion.

Otherwise the posterior cruciate ligament, the extensor mechanism, the semimembranosus, the distal biceps femoris, the lateral collateral ligament and the IT band are unremarkable.

CONCLUSION:

1. Complete tear of the ACL.

2. High-grade sprain of the medial collateral ligament without evidence of pseudocyst Stener.

3. Medial and lateral meniscal tear without displaced fragment.

4. Pivot shift bone marrow contusion with subchondral impaction fracture of the lateral femoral condyle.

5. Moderate knee joint effusion.

report: Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı minimal artmış. Distal femur proksimal tibya ve fibula diyafizometafizer kesimlerindeki artmış hematopoitik kemik iliği aktivitesi anemi ile birlikte olabilir. Medyal menisküs arka boynuzu-gövdesindeki dejenerasyona gövdesi düzeyindeki doku kaybının da eşlik ettiği kompleks yırtık ve medyale 5 mm ekstrüzyon eşlik ediyor. Ekstrüde disk iç yan bağı basılıyor ve iç yan bağın çevresi ödemli. Çapraz ve dış yan bağ normal. Popliteus tendinozisi insersiyosu düzeyinde ve hafif derecede. Diz eklemindeki trikompartmantal dejeneratif eklem hastalığı medyal patellar faset santralindeki tam kata ulaşan kondral fissür, medyal femoral kondilin ağırlık taşıyan yüzeyindeki segmenter tam kat kondral kayıp, eşlik eden subkortikal medüller fibrovasküler değişiklikler ve milimetrik boyutlu marjinal osteofitler ile karakterize. Gastroknemyus semimembranozus bursasındaki 4 cm maksimum boyutlu lobüle konturlu sıvı koleksiyonu sızdırmıyor. Prepatellar ve yüzeyel infrapatellar derin cilt altı bağ dokusu ödemli. translation: Intra-articular fluid volume is minimally increased. Increased hematopoietic bone marrow activity in the diaphyseal-metaphyseal regions of the distal femur, proximal tibia, and fibula may be associated with anemia. Cruciate and collateral ligaments are normal. Lateral meniscus is normal. Complex tear of the medial meniscus posterior horn-body, accompanied by degeneration and tissue loss at the body level, with 5 mm medial extrusion. The extruded disc compresses the medial collateral ligament, and there is periligamentous edema around the medial collateral ligament. Cruciate and lateral collateral ligaments are normal. Popliteus tendinosis at its insertion level, mild in degree. Tricompartmental degenerative joint disease of the knee, characterized by a full-thickness chondral fissure at the center of the medial patellar facet, segmental full-thickness chondral loss on the weight-bearing surface of the medial femoral condyle, accompanying subcortical medullary fibrovascular changes, and millimeter-sized marginal osteophytes. Lobulated-contoured fluid collection in the gastrocnemius-semimembranosus bursa with a maximum size of 4 cm, not leaking. Prepatellar and superficial infrapatellar deep subcutaneous connective tissue is edematous. Extensor mechanism is intact. Proximal tibiofibular joint is normal.

report:
Erhaltene Artikulation im rechten Kniegelenk. Deutliches Ödem in der medialen Femurkondyle sowie im medialen Tibiaplateau. Kleinzystische Veränderungen subcortikal an der Patellafacette (5/9). Ansonsten unauffälliges Knochenmarkssignal. Patella zentriert stehend.
Tief greifende chondrale Läsion an der lateralen Patellafacette mit ca. 5 x 7 mm (4/15 oder 7/22). Darunterliegende kleinzystische Veränderungen subcortikal. Weitere tief greifende chondrale Läsion auch an der medialen Patellafacette mit chondraler Ossifikationen mit ca. 6 x 6 mm (4/14 und 7/18). An den Femurkondylen der facies patellaris oberflächliche Chondropathie mit ausgedünntem Knorpelbelag. Auch femorotibial, führend medialseitig multiple tief greifende kontralaterale Läsionen, exemplarisch in der Hauptbelastungszone mit bis zu 4 mm (5/22) oder dorsal an der medialen Femurkondyle (5/24). Am medialen Tibiaplateau zudem kleine osteochondrale Läsion (5/20). Auch lateralseitig führend am dorsalen Tibiaplateau vollschichtige Chondropathie mit darunterliegenden kleinzystischen Veränderungen (1006/82). Die Kreuzbänder intakt. Diskrete Signalanhebung im Außenmeniskushinterhorn und im Bereich der anterioren Anheftungsstelle (6/22), DD bei mukoider Degeneration. Das Innenmeniskushinterhorn ebenfalls deutlich T2 signalalteriert mit komplexer in erster Linie degenerativer Rissbildung im Hinterhorn bis in die Pars intermedia (siehe z. B. 5/22). Der Innenmeniskus bereits gering exkludiert. LCL unauffällig. Schmaler Flüssigkeitssaum Umgebend zum MCL, DD bei Reizzustand. Moderater Gelenkerguss. Synoviale Proliferationen. Minimal Flüssigkeit an Baker Position (3/90). Ansonsten unauffällige Darstellung der umgebenden Weichteile.
translation:
Preserved articulation in the right knee joint. Marked edema in the medial femoral condyle as well as in the medial tibial plateau. Small subcortical cystic changes at the patellar facet (5/9). Otherwise unremarkable bone marrow signal. Patella centered in position.
Deep-reaching chondral lesion at the lateral patellar facet measuring approximately 5 x 7 mm (4/15 or 7/22). Underlying small subcortical cystic changes. Another deep-reaching chondral lesion also at the medial patellar facet with chondral ossifications measuring approximately 6 x 6 mm (4/14 and 7/18). At the femoral condyles of the patellar surface, superficial chondropathy with thinned cartilage covering. Also femorotibially, predominantly on the medial side, multiple deep-reaching contralateral lesions, exemplarily in the main weight-bearing zone up to 4 mm (5/22) or dorsally at the medial femoral condyle (5/24). At the medial tibial plateau additionally a small osteochondral lesion (5/20). Also on the lateral side, predominantly at the dorsal tibial plateau, full-thickness chondropathy with underlying small cystic changes (1006/82). The cruciate ligaments are intact. Discrete signal increase in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus and in the region of the anterior attachment (6/22), DD of myxoid degeneration. The posterior horn of the medial meniscus is also markedly T2 signal-altered with complex, primarily degenerative tear formation in the posterior horn extending into the pars intermedia (see e.g. 5/22). The medial meniscus is already slightly extruded. LCL unremarkable. Narrow fluid rim surrounding the MCL, DD of irritation. Moderate joint effusion. Synovial proliferations. Minimal fluid at Baker's position (3/90). Otherwise unremarkable appearance of the surrounding soft tissues.

Menisküs posterior komşuluğunda parameniskal kistler izlendi. Medial menisküs mediale doğru hafif ekstrude görünümdedir.Lateral menisküs normaldir.Medial kollateral ligamen, periligamentöz alanda hafif ödem görünümü izlendi ( grade I sprain ). Arka çapraz bağı posterior komşuluğunda büyüğü 14 mm çaplı birkaç adet kist izlendi.Ön çapraz bağ, lateral kollateral ligaman normaldir.Patellar kıkırdak medial fasette kıkırdakta hafif incelme ve bu düzeyde subkondrial milimetrik kist izlendi ( grade II kondromalazi ). Eklemde sıvı artışı saptanmamıştır. Diz eklemini oluşturan kemik yapıların sinyal intensiteleri doğaldır.Popliteal fossada yaklaşık 17 mm çaplı lobüle konturlu baker kisti izlendi.
translation:
LEFT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade III degeneration and horizontal tear at the body level of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Parameniscal cysts observed in the posterior vicinity of the meniscus. The medial meniscus appears slightly extruded medially. The lateral meniscus is normal. Mild edema in the periligamentous area of the medial collateral ligament (grade I sprain). Several cysts, the largest measuring 14 mm in diameter, observed in the posterior vicinity of the posterior cruciate ligament. The anterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Mild thinning of the cartilage at the medial facet of the patellar cartilage and a subchondral millimetric cyst at this level (grade II chondromalacia). No joint effusion detected. Signal intensities of the bony structures forming the knee joint are normal. A Baker's cyst with lobulated contours, approximately 17 mm in diameter, observed in the popliteal fossa.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:

Medial meniscus: Complex tear of the posterior horn. No extrusion. No displaced fragments. No peri-meniscal cysts.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Areas of full-thickness chondrosis involving the medial patellar facet extending to the median eminence. Associated subchondral bone marrow edema.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

Complex tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus as described.

Medial and patellofemoral compartment chondrosis. Small knee joint effusion.

report:
Antecedentes Clínicos:
Rodilla traumática aguda.
Hallazgos:
Edema óseo periférico asociado a fractura subcortical del platillo tibial medial, con edema las
partes blandas regionales.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios de rotura.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales y patelofemoral sin alteraciones.
No hay significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Fragmentación de la tuberosidad anterior de la tibia con discreto edema. Leve aumento de señal
del tendón rotuliano regional.
Tendón cuadricipital, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de
límites normales.
Ligamento patelofemoral medial dentro de límites normales.
Importante edema del tejido celular subcutáneo del aspecto anterior y lateral de la rodilla con
laminar cantidad de líquido profundo regional.
Impresión:
Edema óseo periférico asociado pequeña subcortical del platillo tibial medial.
Fragmentación de la tuberosidad anterior de la tibia con discreto edema óseo y leve tendinosis
rotuliana distal que podría representar reactivación de una enfermedad de Osgood Schlatter,
correlacionar con clínica.
Edema del tejido celular subcutáneo del aspecto anterior y lateral de rodilla con laminar cantidad
de líquido profundo regional.
translation:
Clinical History:
Acute traumatic knee.

Findings:
Peripheral bone edema associated with a subcortical fracture of the medial tibial plateau, with edema of the regional soft tissues.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
Menisci with preserved morphology and signal, no criteria for tear.
Cartilage of the femorotibial and patellofemoral compartments without alterations.
No significant joint effusion or popliteal cysts.
Fragmentation of the tibial tuberosity with mild edema. Mild increased signal of the regional patellar tendon.
Quadriceps tendon, pes anserinus tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Medial patellofemoral ligament within normal limits.
Significant edema of the subcutaneous tissue of the anterior and lateral aspect of the knee with a laminar amount of deep regional fluid.

Impression:
Peripheral bone edema associated with a small subcortical fracture of the medial tibial plateau.
Fragmentation of the tibial tuberosity with mild bone edema and mild distal patellar tendinosis that could represent reactivation of Osgood-Schlatter disease, correlate clinically.
Edema of the subcutaneous tissue of the anterior and lateral aspect of the knee with a laminar amount of deep regional fluid.

Multifragmentarna fraktura stražnjeg dijela lateralnog platoa tibije sa širenjem frakturne pukotine
u proksimalni tibiofibularni zglob i pomakom ulomaka za 4 mm.
Zone kontuzije kosti femoralnih kondila, manja lateralnog, veća medijalnog promjera 10 mm.
Lamelarni izljev uz distalni dio iliotibijalnog trakta, suspektna sitna avulzijska fraktura pri hvatištu
za tibiju.
Blaga subluksacija tibije dorzalno u femorotibijalnom zglobu.
Opsežan hemoragizirani izljev u zglobu i u Bakerovoj cisti veličine 7 cm.
Hondromalacija kondilarne i tibijalne hrskavice II stupnja, uz nekoliko traumatskih defekata
hrskavice lateralnog platoa tibije.
Potpuna ruptura prednjeg križnog ligamenta.
Potpuna ruptura stražnjeg križnog ligamenta.
Kompleksna ruptura prednjeg roga, trupa i stražnjeg roga lateralnog meniska. Avulzija hvatišta
prednjeg roga.
Degenerativno promijenjen medijalni menisk uz moguću rupturu prednjeg korijena i prednjeg roga.
Parcijalna ruptura lateralnog kolateralnog ligamenta pri hvatištu za femur i distenzija u
preostalom dijelu. Formirani veći rubni osteofiti FT i FP zgloba u sklopu OA promjena.
Distenzija medijalnog kolateralnog ligamenta.
Moguća parcijalna ruptura medijalnog i lateralnog retinakuluma patele, analiza limitirana
artefaktima pomicanja.
Ruptura tetive m. popliteusa.
Gubitak napetosti patelarnog ligamenta što vjerojatno odgovara parcijalnoj rupturi, uz tendinozu
na hvatištu.

Lamellar effusion along the distal part of the iliotibial tract, suspected small avulsion fracture at the tibial insertion.
Mild dorsal subluxation of the tibia in the femorotibial joint.
Extensive hemorrhagic joint effusion and in a Baker's cyst measuring 7 cm.
Grade II chondromalacia of the condylar and tibial cartilage, with several traumatic cartilage defects of the lateral tibial plateau.
Complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament.
Complete rupture of the posterior cruciate ligament.
Complex tear of the anterior horn, body, and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. Avulsion of the anterior horn insertion.
Degeneratively changed medial meniscus with possible tear of the anterior root and anterior horn.

Rupture of the popliteus tendon.
Loss of tension of the patellar ligament, likely corresponding to a partial tear, with tendinosis at the insertion.
Soft tissue edema.
Effusion around the visualized portions of the sciatic nerve, common peroneal nerve, and tibial nerve.

report:
Trouvailles :

Il y a un petit épanchement intra-articulaire avec un petit kyste poplité non-rupturé.

Il y a changements dégénératifs sévères au niveau patellofémoral avec perte de cartilage complet à la facette latérale et à la partie latérale de la trochlée du fémur avec changements réactifs sous-chondraux plus proéminents au niveau de la rotule. Il y a aussi changements dégénératifs légers à modérés du compartiment interne avec amincissement et perte de cartilage plus proéminent à la partie centrale du condyle fémoral interne. Il y a aussi un léger amincissement et fibrillation superficielle du cartilage du compartiment externe.

Il y a changements dégénératifs intra-substance impliquant le corps et la corne postérieure du ménisque interne. Il y a une déchirure horizontale surajoutée. La déchirure s’étend de la corne postérieure jusqu’au niveau du corps. La déchirure s’étend à la surface articulaire inférieure du ménisque. Il n’y a pas de fragment déplacé. Il y a un petit kyste para-méniscal adjacent à la corne postérieure. Le ménisque externe démontre changements dégénératifs intra-substance impliquant le corps sans déchirure linéaire bien définie.

Autrement, le ligament croisé antérieur, le ligament croisé postérieur, le mécanisme des extenseurs, le ligament collatéral interne, le semi-membraneux, le muscle et tendon du poplité, le biceps fémoris distal, le ligament collatéral externe et la bandelette ilio-tibiale sont sans particularité.

Conclusion :

1. Changements dégénératifs impliquant les trois compartiments plus proéminent au niveau patellofémoral tel que détaillé ci-haut.

2. Changements dégénératifs intra-substance des ménisques avec déchirure horizontale surajoutée du ménisque interne tel que détaillé ci-haut.

3. Petit épanchement intra-articulaire avec petit kyste poplité.
translation:
Findings:

There is a small intra-articular effusion with a small unruptured popliteal cyst.

There are severe degenerative changes at the patellofemoral compartment with complete cartilage loss at the lateral facet and the lateral portion of the femoral trochlea with subchondral reactive changes most prominent at the patella. There are also mild to moderate degenerative changes of the medial compartment with cartilage thinning and loss most prominent at the central portion of the medial femoral condyle. There is also mild thinning and superficial fibrillation of the cartilage of the lateral compartment.

There are intrasubstance degenerative changes involving the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is a superimposed horizontal tear. The tear extends from the posterior horn to the body. The tear extends to the inferior articular surface of the meniscus. There is no displaced fragment. There is a small parameniscal cyst adjacent to the posterior horn. The lateral meniscus demonstrates intrasubstance degenerative changes involving the body without a well-defined linear tear.

Otherwise, the anterior cruciate ligament, the posterior cruciate ligament, the extensor mechanism, the medial collateral ligament, the semimembranosus, the popliteus muscle and tendon, the distal biceps femoris, the lateral collateral ligament and the iliotibial band are unremarkable.

Conclusion:

1. Degenerative changes involving all three compartments, most prominent at the patellofemoral compartment as detailed above.

2. Intrasubstance degenerative changes of the menisci with superimposed horizontal tear of the medial meniscus as detailed above.

3. Small intra-articular effusion with small popliteal cyst.
