report: МР находка: Наличие на минимално количество ставен излив. Ставният хрущял на пателата е значително изтънен до липсващ. По горния и долния ръб на същата се виждат остеофитни наслагвания, а в нейната структура и зони на костномозъчен едем във връзка с дегенеративните изменения в ретропателарната става. Зад задната кръстна връзка се вижда овална лезия с костноеквивалентна сигнална характеристика и размери 10,5/4,7мм. Лезия с идентична структура се вижда вътреставно медиолатерално отпред пред предната кръстна връзка и големина 17,8/8мм. Трета подобна лезия се открива дорзално до медиалния фемурален кондил с големина 7мм. Находките съответстват на вътреставни мишки. В хрущяла на фемура вентрално и медиално под нивото на пателата се виждат дефекти, без данни за костномозъчен едем субхондрално. Ставният хрущял на тибията и фемура от медиалната страна на ставата се лекостепенно изтънен. По медиалната и латералната страна на кондилите и епикондилите на тибията и фемура се изобразяват остеофитни наслагвания. Субхондрално и дорзално по латералния кондил на тибията се намира малка дегенеративна киста с размер 5/2мм. Кръстните връзки са със запазена цялост. Нормално изобразяване на медиалния и латералния менискус. Колатерални лигаменти – б.о. Лигамент на пателата, сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис – б.о. Ретинакулуми – б.о. Меки тъкани – б.о. Заключение:  МР данни за дегенеративни промени в лявата колянна става, изразени предимно ретропателарно. Хондропатия на пателарния и фемуралния хрущял, значително по-изразена ретропателарно. Вътреставни мишки, съответстващи на откъснати фрагменти от хрущяла на пателата. Минимално количество ставен излив.
translation: MRI findings: Minimal joint effusion is present. The articular cartilage of the patella is significantly thinned to absent. Osteophytic deposits are seen along the superior and inferior margins of the patella, and within its structure there are zones of bone marrow edema related to the degenerative changes in the retropatellar joint. Behind the posterior cruciate ligament, an oval lesion with bone-equivalent signal characteristics measuring 10.5/4.7 mm is seen. A lesion with identical structure is seen intra-articularly, mediolaterally, anterior to the anterior cruciate ligament, measuring 17.8/8 mm. A third similar lesion is found dorsal to the medial femoral condyle, measuring 7 mm. The findings correspond to intra-articular loose bodies. Defects are seen in the femoral cartilage ventrally and medially below the level of the patella, without evidence of subchondral bone marrow edema. The articular cartilage of the tibia and femur on the medial side of the joint is mildly thinned. Osteophytic deposits are seen along the medial and lateral aspects of the condyles and epicondyles of the tibia and femur. A small degenerative cyst measuring 5/2 mm is located subchondrally and dorsally along the lateral tibial condyle. The cruciate ligaments are intact. Normal appearance of the medial and lateral meniscus. Collateral ligaments – unremarkable. Patellar ligament, quadriceps femoris tendon – unremarkable. Retinacula – unremarkable. Soft tissues – unremarkable. Conclusion: MRI findings of degenerative changes in the left knee joint, predominantly expressed retropatellarly. Chondropathy of the patellar and femoral cartilage, significantly more pronounced retropatellarly. Intra-articular loose bodies, corresponding to detached fragments of the patellar cartilage. Minimal joint effusion.

translation:

translation:

report:
MRI of left Knee with 
-Sag PD FS, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Cor T2 FS, Screen Save, Ax T2 FS, 3-Plane Loc


> Wearing of articular carilage and osteophytes of left knee and mild subchondral edema over femoral trochlea, reflecting osteoarthritis with grade 4 chondromalacia.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with extending into the surface, in favor of tear.
> No strong MR evidence of tear of lateral meniscus.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> A lobulated cystic lesion with internal septums in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles and downward extention, in favor of Baker's cyst, about 10 cm in length.
> The contour of ACL & PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Subcutaneous infiltration over anterior aspect of left knee.
> Fatty muscle transformatmion over left knee.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee.
2. Synovitis of left knee and large Baker's cyst.
3. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
4. Mild subcutaneous edema over anterior aspect of left knee and in favor of muscle atrophy with fatty transformation.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

report:
МР находка: МР данни за апофизит с остеонекроза на туберозитас тибие (болест на Osgood-Schlatter). Изобразяват се малки костни фрагменти в областта на туберозирас тибие. Вижда се костно мозъчен едем в областта на апофизата на тибията. Налице са едемни промени в инфрапателарната мастна подложка. Визуализира се задебеляване и едем на лигамента на пателата в залавното му място за тибията. МР данни за малък ставен излив. Бедрената кост и пателата са с нормална форма и сигнална характеристика. Артикулиращият ставен хрущял на фемура, тибията и пателата е съхранен. 
МР данни за дегенеративни промени в задния рог на медиалния менискус. Той е с висок сигнален интензитет, като в него се изобразява и хиперинтензна линия на скъсване. Тази линия се проследява до края на менискуса и до артикулиращия хрущял на тибията. Вижда се мултилокуларна киста на този менискус с размери 23/15/11мм. Нормално изобразяване на предния рог на медиалния менискус и на предния и задния рог на латералния менискус. МР данни за частична руптура на предната кръстна връзка с давност. Същата е с повишен сигнален интензитет и задебелен напречник. Нормално изобразяване на задната кръстна връзка. Колатерални лигаменти, ретинакулуми- б.о. Нормално изобразяване на сухожилието на мускулус квадрицепс феморис. Поплитеална ямка- б.о. Заключение: МР данни за болест на Osgood-Schlatter. Малък ставен излив. Thickening and edema of the patellar ligament at its tibial insertion are visualized. MR findings of a small joint effusion. The femur and patella are of normal shape and signal characteristics. The articular cartilage of the femur, tibia, and patella is preserved.
MR findings of degenerative changes in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. It shows high signal intensity, with a hyperintense tear line visualized within it. This line extends to the meniscal surface and to the articular cartilage of the tibia. A multilocular cyst of this meniscus is seen, measuring 23/15/11 mm. Normal appearance of the anterior horn of the medial meniscus and of the anterior and posterior horns of the lateral meniscus. MR findings of a chronic partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. It shows increased signal intensity and thickened diameter. Normal appearance of the posterior cruciate ligament. Collateral ligaments, retinacula – unremarkable. Normal appearance of the quadriceps femoris tendon. Popliteal fossa – unremarkable.
Conclusion: MR findings of Osgood-Schlatter disease. Small joint effusion. Tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 3. Meniscal cyst. Chronic partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.

report:
MRI of right Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc, Sag PD FS, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Cor T2 FS, Ax T2 FS, Ax DWI B800, Apparent Diffusion Coefficient (mm2/s), Screen Save



> Irregular thining of intra-articular cartilage of femoral trochela and patella and medial femoral condyle and mild subchondral bone marrow edema, reflecting grade 3-4 chondromalacia
   Some spur formation of right knee 
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst. Mild perifocal edema
> The contour of ACL & PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of  grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration or meniscal vascularity 
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Tendinosis of quadriceps tendon and mild subcutaneous infiltration over right knee.
> Small hyperintensity lesion in subchondral region of right distal femur, R/O fibrocystic chnage.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of right knee with grade 3-4 chondromalacia and subchondral edema.
2. Synovitis of right knee and suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae.
3. Large Baker's cyst with perifocal edema.
4. R/O small fibrocystic chnage in distal femur. (Srs/Img: 5/9-10)
5. Grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration.

report:
MRI of right knee in sagittal section (Proton density with fat saturation, T1WI, T2WI with fat saturation), axial section (T2WI with fat saturation) and coronal section (T2WI with fat saturation):

* Cortical discontinuity at lateral portion of patella with bone marrow edema is noticed, in favor of patellar fracture.

* Linear high signal intensity in the lateral meniscus with extension to its surface is noted, meniscal tear is suspected.

* Joint space narrowing at lateral compartment of right knee joint with spur formation and subchondral edema is noticed, in favor of osteoarthritis.

* Fluid accumulation in the suprapatellar bursa with fluid-fluid interface is noticed, in favor of hemoarthrosis.

* Subcutaneous edema at prepatellar region is noticed.

> The contour of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) and posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> No evidence of tear is noted in the medial meniscus.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.

Impressions: 
1. Patellar fracture with bone marrow edema
2. In favor of tear of lateral meniscus
3. No evidence of ACL injury
4. Osteoarthritis of right knee, prominent at lateral compartment
5. Hemoarthrosis

Suggest clinical correlation

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: [REDACTED].
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Full-thickness chondrosis at the proximal tibiofibular joint with marginal osteophytes and subchondral cystic change and intra-osseous ganglion cyst formation. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytes.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion with synovitis. No intra-articular bodies. Small multilobulated Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Extensive complex tear at the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with maceration and extrusion. Reactive edema at the joint line.
Medial compartment cartilage: Full thickness cartilage denudation throughout the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau with subchondral cystic change and marrow edema.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss at the anterior weightbearing surfaces. High grade chondrosis along the peripheral lateral joint. 

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the medial trochlea. High-grade fissuring at the median ridge with likely an early delaminating component extending along the medial patellar facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal fibers with bowing related to medial meniscus extrusion.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Mild popliteus tendonesis without tear. Ganglion cyst about the myotendinous junction. 

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: Mild proximal patellar tendinosis without tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 4 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Extensive complex tear at the body and posterior horn of medial meniscus with maceration and extrusion of the body.
2.	Tricompartmental chondrosis, severe in the medial compartment. 
3.	Mild proximal patellar tendinosis without tear.
4.	Mild popliteus tendonesis without tear.

hondromalacijskih promjena II-IV. stupnja, izraženije hrskavice medijalnog tibijalnog platoa gdje
je vidljivo početno formiranje subhondralnih cisti.
Zona rekonverzije koštane srži distalne metadijafize femura.
Prominentniji osteofit medijalnog platoa tibije straga uz hvatište stražnjeg križnog ligamenta.
Održan je kontinuitet križnih ligamenata.
Prednji križni ligament umjereno degenerativno promijenjen.
Umjerene degenerativne promjene oba meniska, lateralni promijenjene morfologije, bez znakova
rupture. Medijalni menisk pokazuje znakove horizontalne rupture stražnjeg roga.
Kolateralni ligamenti održani, entezopatske promjene proksimalnog LCL.
Entezitis medijalnog ruba tetive m. quadriceps. Edem suprapatelarnog masnog jastučića.
Blaža entezopatija patelarnog ligamenta.
Baker cista CC promjera 6 cm.
Ostali nalaz u granicama normale za dob
translation:
On a series of MR images of the left knee, there are OA changes of the femorotibial and femoropatellar joints with visible fissures and erosions of the cartilage, focally visible subchondral edema, in the setting of chondromalacia grade II–IV, more pronounced in the cartilage of the medial tibial plateau where initial formation of subchondral cysts is visible.
Zone of bone marrow reconversion of the distal metadiaphysis of the femur.
A more prominent osteophyte of the medial tibial plateau posteriorly at the insertion of the posterior cruciate ligament.
The continuity of the cruciate ligaments is preserved.
The anterior cruciate ligament is moderately degenerated.
Moderate degenerative changes of both menisci, the lateral meniscus of altered morphology, without signs of rupture. The medial meniscus shows signs of a horizontal tear of the posterior horn.
The collateral ligaments are intact, enthesopathic changes of the proximal LCL.
Enthesitis of the medial margin of the quadriceps tendon. Edema of the suprapatellar fat pad.
Mild enthesopathy of the patellar ligament.
Baker's cyst with a CC diameter of 6 cm.
The remaining findings are within normal limits for age.

translation:
MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
On evaluation of the lateral meniscus, articular cartilage, lateral collateral ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, and bone marrow, no pathological findings are observed.
The medial meniscus is identified with pathological signal at the body and posterior horn with vertical morphology.
The medial collateral ligament shows thickening at the femoral attachment, without edema.
The anterior cruciate ligament shows horizontalization.
On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, focal edema is observed in Hoffa's fat pad.
A small fluid collection is observed intra-articularly.

CONCLUSION:
1. Chronic tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
2. Vertical tear of the medial meniscus at the body and posterior horn.
3. Old healed partial injury of the medial collateral ligament.
4. The edema in Hoffa's fat pad is attributed to mild impingement syndrome of the patellar tendon against the anterior distal femur.

report:
MRI of left Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, AX T2W FS, CO T2W FS

> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, and unclear contour of meniscal root, in favor of tear.
> The contour of PCL is not in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, in favor of tear.
> Enlarged size of ACL and increased interstitial signal intensity on F/S T2WI and mild laxity contour , R/O mucoid degeneration or grade 1 injury.
Joint effusion with mildly increased signal on T1WI and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; in favor of severe hypertrophy of the synovium of right knee, indicative of severe synovitis.
> Loculated fluid with isointensity to muscle on T1WI and hyperintensity on F/S T2WI over anterior lateral aspect of left knee, in favor of residual subcutaneous hematoma.
> Mottled mild hyperintensity foci in proximal tibia ( major at tibial tuberosity) and distal femur and fibula, which shows low signal intensity on T1WI and high signal intensity on T2WI, in favor of residural red bone marrow.
> Increased singal intensity of patellar cartilage with deep fissures, in favor of grade III patellar chondromalacia.
  Wearing of articular cartilage of femoral trochela with subchondral edema and cyst.

Impression: 
1. Tear of posterior horn of left medial meniscus.
2. PCL tear.
3. Grade 1 injury of ACL.
4. Synovitis of left knee joint with suprapetellar bursitis.
5. Subcutaneous edema in left anterior knee with residual subcutaneous hematoma in left lateral knee.
6. Osteoarthritis of left knee with grade 3-4 chondromalacia of patellofemoral joint.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

translation:
MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
On evaluation of the lateral meniscus, the posterior cruciate ligament, and the collateral ligaments, no pathological findings are observed.
On evaluation of the medial meniscus, subluxation and degeneration of its body are observed with presence of torn meniscal material which has folded exactly proximal to the anterior horn.
The articular cartilage has satisfactory appearance.
The extensor mechanism does not show pathological findings.
Pathological edema is observed between the lateral femoral condyle and the iliotibial band.
A small intra-articular fluid collection is observed which communicates with a small Baker's synovial cyst adjacent to the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle.
The anterior cruciate ligament is not identified.

IMPRESSION:
1. Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
2. Flap tear of the medial meniscus as described.
3. Findings of iliotibial band impingement syndrome.

MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

Subchondral insufficiency fracture central weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle as well as the adjacent tibia with moderate bone marrow edema. No articular surface collapse or osteonecrosis. 
Subcortical cyst identified in the head of the fibula. Mild to moderate osteophyte formation within all 3 compartments of the knee.

A 21x15 mm multiloculated cyst is seen in the posteromedial vicinity of the meniscus (parameniscal cyst). A bucket-handle tear is seen in the lateral meniscus. A partial tear is seen in the proximal portion of the posterior cruciate ligament. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration is seen in the anterior cruciate ligament. The lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. No joint effusion is detected. The signal intensities of the bony structures forming the knee joint are normal. Conclusion: Grade III meniscopathy in the medial meniscus with an accompanying horizontal tear. Parameniscal cyst adjacent to the meniscus. Bucket-handle tear in the lateral meniscus. Partial tear of the posterior cruciate ligament. Myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament.

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE]  [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for 7 months. No known injury.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Acute subchondral insufficiency fracture at the weightbearing medial femoral condyle. Confluent subchondral bone marrow edema at the medial femoral condyle. Mild/early subchondral insufficiency fracture at the anteromedial tibial plateau. Normal background marrow signal. Proximal patellar enthesophytes.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with synovitis. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Diffuse complex degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus. Superiorly displaced meniscal flap at the medial joint line and at the posterior horn. Severe meniscal extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Large confluent regions of full-thickness articular cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint. High-grade cartilage loss at the posterior medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Small complex tear of the lateral meniscal body, characterized by a dominant horizontal component.

report:
MRI of left Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, AX T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS



> Wearing of articular cartilage of left knee with mild subchondral bone marrow edema, more porminent at medial facet of patella and medial femorotibial joint.
  Osteophyte of left knee and patellar enthesophyte
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with extending into the surface, in favor of tear; degeneration of lateral meniscus.
> The contour of ACL and PCL and LCL-biceps tendon in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of grade 1 injury or degeneration.
> Interstitial increased signal of popliteus tendon and quadriceps tendonon F/S T2WI, in favor of tendinosis.
  Popliteus tenosynovitis and muscle edema.
> Joint effusion with intermediate signal on T1WI in comparison with adjacent muscle and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Subcutanoeus edema over anterior aspect of left knee.
> Mild increased fat stranding surrounding common fibular nerve with increased internal signal on F/S T2WI, R/O neuritis.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee, more prominent at medial compartment with grade 4 chondromalacia.
2. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
3. Grade 1 injury or degeneration of ACL and PCL and LCL-biceps complex.
4. Tendinosis of quadriceps tendon and patellar tendon and popliteus tendon; popliteus muscle edema.
5. Moderate synovitis-joint effusion of left knee and suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae; deep infrapatellar bursitis.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

report: SAĞ DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Lateral menisküs anterior-posterior hornu ve gövde kesimde grade II dejenerasyon izlenmiştir. Medial menisküs diz eklem mesafesinde 8.5 mm mediale ekstrüdedir. Menisküs anterior-posterior hornu ve gövde kesimde grade III dejenerasyon ve eşlik eden kompleks yırtıklar izlenmiştir. Arka çapraz bağ, lateral kollateral ligaman normaldir.Anterior çapraz bağda miksoid dejenerasyona sekonder sinyal değişikliği izlenmiştir. Medial kollateral ligamanda periligamentöz ödem izlenmiştir. Distal kuadriseps normaldir. Retinaküler devamsızlık yoktur.Patella medial fasette subkondral alanda ödem, kartilajda bütünlük kaybı izlenmiştir. Suprapatellar bursa ve diz eklem mesafesinde sıvı mevcuttur.Tibiofemoral eklem medialde eklem aralığında daralma, ekleme komşu tibia medial platoda subkondral 11x6 mm boyutlu osteokondral defekt izlenmiştir. Bu düzey femoral ve tibial kartilajlarda destrüksiyon izlenmektedir.Popliteal fossada 4x2 cm boyutlu Baker kisti izlenmiştir. SONUÇ:Gonartroz .Medial menüsküste medial ekstrüzyon, grade III meniskopati, horizontal yırtık, lateral menisküste grade II meniskopati.Medial kollateral ligamanda grade I sprain.Anterior çapraz bağda miksoid dejenerasyon.Suprapatellar bursit, diz ekleminde sinovit.Popliteal fossada Baker kisti.Patella medial fasette grade III kondromalazi.
translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior and posterior horns and body of the lateral meniscus. The medial meniscus is extruded 8.5 mm medially at the knee joint space. Grade III degeneration and accompanying complex tears are observed in the anterior and posterior horns and body of the medial meniscus. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. Periligamentous edema is observed in the medial collateral ligament. The distal quadriceps is normal. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Edema in the subchondral area and loss of cartilage integrity are observed at the medial facet of the patella. Fluid is present in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Joint space narrowing is present in the medial tibiofemoral compartment. A subchondral osteochondral defect measuring 11x6 mm is observed in the medial tibial plateau adjacent to the joint. Destruction of the femoral and tibial cartilages is observed at this level. A Baker's cyst measuring 4x2 cm is observed in the popliteal fossa.
CONCLUSION: Gonarthrosis. Medial extrusion of the medial meniscus, grade III meniscopathy, horizontal tear. Grade II meniscopathy of the lateral meniscus. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. Suprapatellar bursitis, synovitis of the knee joint. Baker's cyst in the popliteal fossa. Grade III chondromalacia of the medial facet of the patella.

report: [DATE]: * MR Knie Rechts 15ch AA : Klinische Inlichtingen: Kniepijn rechts. Diagnostische vraagstellling: Evaluatie. Verder : "F ull thickness " kraakbeenverlies denudatie mediale patellaire facet en crista patellae (overgrijpend op het laterale facet, deels ondermijnd)-geassocieerde aanscherping van de gewrichtsranden . Besluit/conclusie: Gonartrose ( zoals hoger beschreven ) met een degeneratieve scheur mediale meniscus-secundair hieraan subchondrale insuffici ëntiefractu ren mediale femorotibiale gewrichtscompartiment.
translation: [DATE]: * MRI Right Knee 15ch AA : Clinical Information: Right knee pain. Diagnostic question: Evaluation. Scan protocol (DRB): sagittal intermediate-weighted sequences without and with fat suppression, axial/coronal PD-weighted sequences with fat suppression, coronal T1-weighted sequences. Findings: - No significant distension of the suprapatellar bursa, limited to mildly increased amount of fluid in the semimembranosus/gastrocnemius-semimembranosus bursa. - Chondromalacia of the medial femorotibial compartment with global cartilage loss as well as grade 4 cartilage defects, subchondral insufficiency fracture both tibial and femoral (with significant perilesional edema and periosteal soft tissue infiltration extending to the metaphysis). - Complex (partial to sub)total tear/maceration of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus (near the posterior meniscal root) with extra-articular extrusion of the body portion, also characterized by an undersurface tear and locoregional mucoid degeneration. - Grade 1 sprain pattern of the MCL, secondary to the above-described findings. Furthermore: "Full thickness" cartilage loss/denudation of the medial patellar facet and patellar ridge (extending to the lateral facet, partially undermined) - associated sharpening of the joint margins. Conclusion: Gonarthrosis (as described above) with a degenerative tear of the medial meniscus - secondary to this, subchondral insufficiency fractures of the medial femorotibial compartment.

kolateralnog ligamenta, stražnjeg križnog ligamenta, iliotibijalnog traktusa, početne
entezopatske promjene tetive m. kvadricepsa i patelarnog ligamenta.
Promijenjen intenzitet signala i morfologija prednjeg križnog ligamenta u prilog parcijalnoj rupturi
anteromedijalnog snopa.
Linearno horizontalno intrasupstancijsko povišenje intenziteta signala stražnjeg roga i dijela
tijela medijalnog meniska koja prelazi tibijalnu zglobnu plohu - kompleksna ruptura s
horizontalnom i radijalnom komponentom. Manja ruptura prednjeg korijena medijalnog meniska uz
vidljive dvije manje parameniscealne ciste.
Diskretno linearno povišenje intenziteta signala stražnjeg roga lateralnog meniska - ddg.
degenerativne promjene, bez znakova rupture.
Parcijalna ruptura dubokog sloja MCL uz formiranje ganglion cisti.
Reducirana je debljina artikulacijske hrskavice femoropatelarnog zgloba uz zone hondromalacije
II. i IV. stupnja medijalne i lateralne fasete patele te formirane site osteofite u smislu OA promjena.
Hondromalacija II. stupnja femorotibijalnog zgloba.

translation:
On the series of MR images of the right knee, normal morphology and signal intensity of the lateral collateral ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, and iliotibial tract are found, along with early enthesopathic changes of the quadriceps tendon and patellar ligament.
Altered signal intensity and morphology of the anterior cruciate ligament consistent with partial tear of the anteromedial bundle.
Linear horizontal intrasubstance increased signal intensity of the posterior horn and part of the body of the medial meniscus extending to the tibial articular surface – complex tear with horizontal and radial components. Minor tear of the anterior root of the medial meniscus with two small parameniscal cysts visible.
Discrete linear increased signal intensity of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus – differential diagnosis: degenerative changes, without signs of tear.
Partial tear of the deep layer of the MCL with formation of ganglion cysts.
Reduced thickness of the articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint with zones of chondromalacia grade II and IV of the medial and lateral patellar facets and small osteophytes formed consistent with OA changes.
Grade II chondromalacia of the femorotibial joint.
No popliteal (Baker's) cyst is found.
Other visualized bony, soft tissue, and neurovascular structures are of normal morphology and signal intensity.

The examination was performed with T1, T2 gradient echo and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

A small fluid collection is observed in the knee joint. Tetkike dahil kemik yapıların korteks bütünlükleri meduller sinyal intensiteleri doğaldır.Distal kuadriseps ve patellar tendonlar normaldir.Arka çapraz bağ, lateral ve medial kollateral ligaman normaldir.Anterior çapraz bağda travmaya sekonder olabilecek sinyal artışı dikkati çekti .Medial menisküs sinyal intensitesi ve bütünlüğü doğaldır. Lateral menisküs posterior hornunda grade II dejenerasyon dikkati çekti .Eklem mesafesinde ve suprapatellar bursada artmış effüzyon , suprapatellar plikaya ait görünüm dikkati çekti. translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: A suspicious hypointense fracture line on T1 and T2W sequences in the tibial plateau with surrounding diffuse bone marrow edema on T2W sequences was noted. The cortical integrity and medullary signal intensities of the bones included in the examination are normal. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. Signal increase possibly secondary to trauma was noted in the anterior cruciate ligament. The signal intensity and integrity of the medial meniscus are normal. Grade II degeneration was noted in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. Increased effusion in the joint space and suprapatellar bursa, and appearance consistent with a suprapatellar plica was noted. No space-occupying lesion was detected in the popliteal fossa.

translation:
TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
- On evaluation of the medial compartment, small marginal osteophytes are observed, along with thinning and microerosions of the articular cartilage of the femoral and tibial condyle (ICRS Grade II), as well as subchondral sclerosis and barely perceptible bone marrow edema of the medial tibial condyle. The medial meniscus shows extrusion and a degenerative tear of the posterior horn.
- On evaluation of the lateral compartment, no significant pathological findings are observed.
- On evaluation of the anterior (patellofemoral) compartment, a small focus of bone marrow edema is noted in the lateral facet of the patella, accompanied by complete loss of the overlying articular cartilage over a length of 9 mm (ICRS Grade IV).
- The anterior cruciate ligament shows myxoid degeneration, without tear.
- The posterior cruciate ligament and the collateral ligaments appear normal.
- Intra-articularly, a moderate joint effusion is observed with the presence of a few osteochondral loose bodies measuring up to 9 mm in diameter. The intra-articular effusion communicates with a Baker's cyst of craniocaudal diameter, within which a loose body measuring 3.5 mm in diameter is identified.
- A small enchondroma measuring 1.3 cm in diameter is observed in the tibial epiphysis.

CONCLUSION:
1) Findings indicative of degenerative osteoarthritis of the anterior and medial compartments with degenerative tear of the medial meniscus.
2) Myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament.
3) Moderate intra-articular fluid collection with osteochondral loose bodies.

report:
Constatations:

Épanchement intra-articulaire modéré, avec suspicion d'un niveau graisseux au versant externe suggérant un degré de lipohémarthrose. Pas de kyste de Baker significatif avec un liséré de liquide au sein du creux poplité et de la portion supérieure de la patte d'oie. 

Il y a un émoussement du rebord postérieur de la corne postérieure du ménisque interne suspect d'une déchirure longitudinale verticale périphérique potentielle. Il y a également une extrusion relativement significative du corps méniscal, le plus probablement en lien avec une déchirure complète du ligament collatéral interne. 

Il y a une déchirure complète du ligament colléral interne distal avec rétraction proximale des fibres déchirées, associées à de multiples zones d'irrégularités, épaississements et signal anormal intra-substance. Il y également une atténuation et signal intra-substance à son origine. La partie distale du ligament collatéral interne déchirée se situe légèrement sous les tendons de la patte d'oie constituant une lésion de type ''pseudo Stener''. Il y a également une déchire complète de la composante profonde ménisco-fémorale et une déchirure partielle de la composante ménisco-tibiale. 

Pas d'atteinte chondrale transfixiante fémorotibiale interne.

Le ménisque externe est intact sans déchirure. Il y a une petite fracture au versant supérieur de la tête du péroné potentiellement à l'insertion du ligament poplité arqué. Minime déplacement et œdème associés. L'insertion distale du ligament collatéral externe et du tendon du biceps est préservé de même que l'origine. Il y a également une petite ossification au versant postérieur de la tête du péroné mesurant 5 mm, d'origine indéterminée. 

Il y a des irrégularités de l'os sous-chondral à la surface portante du condyle fémoral externe d'allure plutôt chronique. Pas d'atteinte chondrale transfixiante fémorotibiale externe. Toutefois, petit foyer d'œdème au versant postérieur du condyle fémoral externe avec léger hypersignal chondral, contusion versus lésion oséto-chondrale (atypique) versus changement de stress en lien avec l’origine du gastrocnémien externe. 

Kyste ganglionnaire à l'origine des deux gastrocnémiens.

Il y a une déchirure d'allure complète à l'insertion distale du ligament croisé postérieur et/ou avulsion du LCP. Le ligament est rétracté proximalement, épaissi et de signal anormal. Il y a une atténuation significative du ligament croisé antérieur sans composante transfixiante toutefois notée, en lien avec une déchirure partielle. Il y a des contusions probablement associées au plateau tibial externe, plus marquées en postérieur +/- impaction/fracture sous-chondrale.

Petit kyste ganglionnaire à l'empreinte distale du ligament croisé antérieur.

L'alignement patello-fémoral demeure dans les limites normales. Séquelles de maladie Osgood Schlatter avec fragmentation d'allure chronique de la tubérosité tibiale et léger épaississement du tendon rotulien. Le tendon du quadriceps distal est intact sans déchirure. Pas d'atteinte chondrale transfixiante patello-fémorale. La graisse de Hoffa est sans grande particularité.

Il y a un œdème diffus significatif sous-cutané et inter-musculaire. Il y a également un œdème des muscles poplité et plantaire en lien avec une entorse.

Conclusion:

Déchirure complète du ligament collatéral interne distal avec déplacement de la portion distale sous les tendons de la patte d'oie en lien avec une lésion de type 'pseudo Stener''. Il y a également une déchirure complète de la composante profonde ménisco-fémorale et partielle de la composante ménisco-tibiale.

Déchirure d'allure complète du ligament croisé postérieur distal et/ou avulsion du LCP. Déchirure partielle probable du ligament croisé antérieur.

Fracture au versant supérieur de la tête du péroné probablement à l'insertion du ligament poplité arqué. Œdème associé.

De plus, contusions probable du plateau tibial externe +/- impaction/fracture sous-chondrale et du versant postérieur du condyle fémoral externe. 

Émoussement du rebord postérieur de la corne postérieure du ménisque interne suspect d'une déchirure longitudinale verticale périphérique potentielle.

Épanchement intra-articulaire modéré avec composante de lipohémarthrose suspectée.

Dans ce contexte, un complément d'investigation par tomodensitométrie est recommandé pour mieux évaluer les structures osseuses. De plus, une consultation en chirurgie orthopédique est également, fortement recommandée. 

Le rapport a été transcrit en priorité.
translation:
Findings:

Moderate intra-articular effusion, with suspicion of a fat-fluid level on the lateral side suggesting a degree of lipohemarthrosis. No significant Baker's cyst, with a thin rim of fluid within the popliteal fossa and the proximal portion of the pes anserinus.

There is blunting of the posterior margin of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, suspicious for a potential peripheral vertical longitudinal tear. There is also relatively significant extrusion of the meniscal body, most likely related to a complete tear of the medial collateral ligament.

There is a complete tear of the distal medial collateral ligament with proximal retraction of the torn fibers, associated with multiple zones of irregularity, thickening, and abnormal intrasubstance signal. There is also attenuation and intrasubstance signal at its origin. The torn distal portion of the medial collateral ligament is situated slightly beneath the pes anserinus tendons, constituting a "pseudo-Stener" type lesion. There is also a complete tear of the deep meniscofemoral component and a partial tear of the meniscotibial component.

No full-thickness chondral defect of the medial femorotibial compartment.

The lateral meniscus is intact without tear. There is a small fracture on the superior aspect of the fibular head, potentially at the insertion of the arcuate popliteal ligament. Minimal displacement and associated edema. The distal insertion of the lateral collateral ligament and the biceps tendon is preserved, as is the origin. There is also a small ossification on the posterior aspect of the fibular head measuring 5 mm, of indeterminate origin.

There are subchondral bone irregularities at the weight-bearing surface of the lateral femoral condyle, appearing rather chronic. No full-thickness chondral defect of the lateral femorotibial compartment. However, a small focus of edema on the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle with mild chondral hyperintensity, contusion versus osteochondral lesion (atypical) versus stress change related to the origin of the lateral gastrocnemius.

Ganglion cyst at the origin of both gastrocnemii.

There is a tear appearing complete at the distal insertion of the posterior cruciate ligament and/or PCL avulsion. The ligament is proximally retracted, thickened, and of abnormal signal. There is significant attenuation of the anterior cruciate ligament without a full-thickness component noted, however, consistent with a partial tear. There are contusions likely involving the lateral tibial plateau, more marked posteriorly +/- impaction/subchondral fracture.

Small ganglion cyst at the distal footprint of the anterior cruciate ligament.

Patellofemoral alignment remains within normal limits. Sequelae of Osgood-Schlatter disease with chronic-appearing fragmentation of the tibial tuberosity and mild thickening of the patellar tendon. The distal quadriceps tendon is intact without tear. No full-thickness chondral defect of the patellofemoral compartment. Hoffa's fat pad is unremarkable.

There is significant diffuse subcutaneous and intermuscular edema. There is also edema of the popliteus and plantaris muscles consistent with a sprain.

Conclusion:

Complete tear of the distal medial collateral ligament with displacement of the distal portion beneath the pes anserinus tendons, consistent with a "pseudo-Stener" type lesion. There is also a complete tear of the deep meniscofemoral component and a partial tear of the meniscotibial component.

Tear appearing complete of the distal posterior cruciate ligament and/or PCL avulsion. Probable partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.

Fracture of the superior aspect of the fibular head, probably at the insertion of the arcuate popliteal ligament. Associated edema.

Additionally, probable contusions of the lateral tibial plateau +/- impaction/subchondral fracture and of the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle.

Blunting of the posterior margin of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, suspicious for a potential peripheral vertical longitudinal tear.

Moderate intra-articular effusion with suspected lipohemarthrosis component.

In this context, further investigation with CT is recommended to better evaluate the bony structures. Additionally, an orthopedic surgery consultation is also strongly recommended.

The report was transcribed as a priority.

translation:
Clinical History:
Left knee pain.

Findings:
No significant bone marrow signal abnormalities.
Cruciate ligaments and lateral collateral ligament are unremarkable.
Thickening with predominantly low signal of the superficial and deep components of the medial ligamentous complex in its proximal third, with minimal peripheral bone marrow edema of the medial femoral condyle in a reactive pattern. Mild edema of the adjacent soft tissues, especially deep to the pes anserinus tendons. The remaining components of the medial complex are unremarkable.
Increased central signal of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus that may contact the inferior articular surface at the level of the body peripherally, without displacement of segments.
The lateral meniscus is of preserved morphology and signal, without signs of tear.
Cartilage of the femorotibial compartments is unremarkable. Focal full-thickness chondral ulcer of the central region of the femoral trochlea with secondary bone changes. Diffuse superficial patellar chondropathy.
No significant joint effusion or pathological popliteal cysts.
Edema of the suprapatellar retroquadriceps fat pad.
Mild increased signal of the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon and the proximal insertion of the patellar tendon, without signs of tear.
Pes anserinus tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band are within normal limits.

Impression:
Sequelar thickening of the superficial and deep components of the medial ligamentous complex in its proximal third, with minimal peripheral bone marrow edema of the medial femoral condyle in a reactive pattern. Edema of the adjacent soft tissues, deep to the pes anserinus tendons, may represent findings of an associated regional friction syndrome.
Probable peripheral tear of the medial meniscus, correlate clinically.
Grade 3 chondropathy of the central region of the femoral trochlea.
Edema of the suprapatellar retroquadriceps fat pad, nonspecific finding. Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis and proximal patellar tendinosis.

translation:
LEFT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus. Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior and posterior horns and body of the lateral meniscus. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. No joint effusion is detected. Signal change consistent with medullary bone marrow edema is observed in the left section of the patella. A Baker's cyst measuring 6.5x1 cm is observed in the popliteal fossa.
Conclusion: Grade II meniscopathy in the medial and lateral menisci. Myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. Focal bone marrow edema in the patella. Baker's cyst in the popliteal fossa.

report: МР находка: МР данни за лезия на задния рог налатералния менискус. Задният рог е фрагментиран. Вижда се дегератина промяна с малки кистични включвания в предния рог на латералния менискус. МР данни за лезия и на задния рог на медиалния меникус. В задният рог на този менискус се изобразява хиперинтензна линия с радиерен ход, съответсваща на скъсване. Скъсването видимо достига до задния край на менискуса, но не и до ставните краища на фумра и тибията. Няма данни за ставен излив. Костите, формиращи колянната става са с нормална форма и интензитет на сигнала. Ставният хрущял на фемура, тибията и пателата изглежда съхранен. Предната кръстна връзка е с уголемен напречник и повишен интензитет на сигнала. Находката е както при частично скъсване на връзката с давност. Нормално изобразяване на задната кръстна връзка. Колатерални лигаменти – б.о.  Патела, ретинакулуми – б.о. Сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис и лигамент на пателата – б.о. Поплитеална ямка – б.о. Заключение: МР данни за лезия – 3 стадия на латералния менискус и 2а стадий на задния рог на медиалния менискус. Частично скъсване на предната кръстна връзка.
translation: MRI findings: MRI evidence of a lesion of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. The posterior horn is fragmented. Degenerative change with small cystic inclusions is seen in the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus. MRI evidence of a lesion of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus as well. In the posterior horn of this meniscus, a hyperintense line with a radial course is visualized, corresponding to a tear. The tear visibly reaches the posterior edge of the meniscus, but not the articular surfaces of the femur and tibia. No evidence of joint effusion. The bones forming the knee joint are of normal shape and signal intensity. The articular cartilage of the femur, tibia, and patella appears preserved. The anterior cruciate ligament is thickened with increased signal intensity. The finding is consistent with a chronic partial tear of the ligament. Normal appearance of the posterior cruciate ligament. Collateral ligaments – unremarkable. Patella, retinacula – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon and patellar ligament – unremarkable. Popliteal fossa – unremarkable. Conclusion: MRI evidence of a lesion – grade 3 of the lateral meniscus and grade 2a of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.

Cruciate and collateral ligaments within preserved limits. Polylobulated cystic ganglion in the posterior region of the knee with an intra-articular and extra-articular component, without signs of definite complication.
Grade 2-3 delaminative chondral ulcer, not displaced, of the lateral facet of the patella.
Signs of lateral patellar hyperpressure syndrome.
Minimal joint effusion. Small uncomplicated popliteal cyst.
Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis.
Probable iliotibial band friction phenomena.

translation:
MRI OF THE KNEE

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed on a 3T magnetic resonance scanner with PDFS and T1 sequences.

FINDINGS
- Extensive bone marrow edema is noted in the proximal tibial epiphysis/metaphysis, particularly in the medial compartment, where a subchondral linear area of increased signal is identified, approximately 4 mm in width, compatible with a subchondral fracture. No depression of the articular surface is observed correspondingly.
- Pathological signal and fluid infiltration is seen around the medial collateral ligament, most likely reactive in etiology.
- Mild edematous appearance of the popliteus muscle, possibly in the context of a low-grade muscle strain.
- The cruciate ligaments, the medial and lateral menisci, and the lateral collateral ligament appear normal.
- Normal appearance of the iliotibial band, the popliteofibular ligament, the posterolateral corner, and the proximal tibiofibular joint.
- Normal appearance of the posteromedial corner and the pes anserinus as well as the articular cartilage.
- Small intra-articular fluid collection. Presence of a suprapatellar synovial plica.
- The remaining bone marrow is within normal signal limits.
- On examination of the anterior compartment, hypoplasia of the medial articular surface of the trochlea is identified, along with edematous appearance and coexistence of microcystic areas in the prefemoral fat pad, a finding that requires correlation for the possibility of prefemoral impingement. Small fluid collection in the prepatellar bursa.

translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings:
The lateral meniscus is normal. The medial meniscus is extruded 5.5 mm medially from the joint space. A decrease in meniscal volume and grade II degeneration in the posterior horn and body are observed. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral collateral ligament, and medial collateral ligament are normal. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. A subchondral millimetric cyst and signal change consistent with edema in its vicinity are observed at the anterior aspect of the tibial intercondylar eminence. A subchondral osteochondral defect measuring 6.5 x 4.5 mm is observed at the anterior aspect of the femoral intercondylar area. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Minimal fluid increase is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Osteophytic spurring is observed at the corners of the bony structures at the tibiofemoral joint level. Joint space narrowing is observed in the medial tibiofemoral joint. Focal thinning is observed in the femoral and tibial cartilages adjacent to the joint.
CONCLUSION: Gonarthrosis. Medial extrusion, volume loss, and grade II meniscopathy of the medial meniscus. Myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. Subchondral bone marrow edema of the tibial intercondylar eminence. Focal osteochondral defect in the femoral intercondylar notch.

MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1 proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression and T2 gradient echo.

FINDINGS
In the lateral compartment of the knee, there is simple degeneration, without tear of the meniscus.
In the medial compartment of the knee, a degenerative tear is observed in the posterior horn of the meniscus and subluxation thereof. Additionally, bone marrow edema is observed in the medial femoral condyle and epicondyle, as well as articular cartilage erosion ICRS grade III of the medial femoral condyle and epicondyle. Intra-articular fluid collection communicates with a Baker's synovial cyst with a craniocaudal diameter of 6.5 cm in the medial popliteal fossa.

CONCLUSION
The findings are consistent with an insufficiency fracture (synonymous with spontaneous osteonecrosis) of the medial femoral condyle.

RIGHT KNEE MRI.

There is a finding consistent with periligamentous edema around the medial collateral ligament (grade I sprain). Grade II degeneration of the lateral meniscus. There is increased signal in the anterior cruciate ligament consistent with myxoid degeneration. Thickening and increased signal at the proximal level of the posterior cruciate ligament. Marked thickening and increased signal in the meniscofemoral ligament. The patella is normally positioned. The retinacula are normal. The patellar tendon is normal. Mild osteophytic spurring of the bony structures forming the knee joint, mild narrowing of the joint space in the medial tibiofemoral compartment, and mild thinning of the adjacent cartilage (findings of degenerative arthritis). Subchondral millimetric cysts at the level of the ACL insertion on the intercondylar tubercle of the tibia. Mild joint effusion in the knee joint. Findings consistent with a partial tear at the femoral attachment of the medial head of the gastrocnemius, with a cystic appearance in this area. A Baker's cyst approximately 16 mm in diameter in the popliteal fossa.

report:
Interprétation : 

Il y a un minime liséré de liquide au sein du récessus suprapatellaire, sans épanchement intra-articulaire significatif. Il y a un petit kyste de Baker, sans complication significative, mesurant 2,8 cm de diamètre CC.

Il y a une déchirure longitudinale horizontale impliquant la corne postérieure et le corps du ménisque interne, s’étendant à la racine postérieure, à la jonction avec la corne antérieure et le long de la surface articulaire inférieure. Il y a de petits kystes paraméniscaux associés au versant postérieur. 

Il y a un épaississement des fibres superficielles du ligament collatéral interne avec un œdème léger à modéré au pourtour suggérant une entorse de grade 1. 

Il y a une atténuation légère à modérée des surfaces chondrales au compartiment fémorotibial interne , sans atteinte transfixiante. Il y a de petits ostéophytes marginaux. 

Le ménisque externe et le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe sont intacts et sans déchirure.

Il y a une légère atténuation diffuse des surfaces chondrales au compartiment fémorotibial externe avec un foyer de chondropathie sévère à la surface non-portante au versant postérieur du condyle fémoral externe avec une perte focale transfixiante de la surface cartilagineuse et un début de changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés. Il y a de minimes ostéophytes marginaux.

Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts et sans déchirure. Il y a de minimes kyste ganglionnaires intra-osseux sous l’insertion distale du ligament croisé antérieur. 

L’alignement patellofémoral parait dans les limites de la normale. Il y a plusieurs artéfacts de susceptibilité magnétique au versant antérieur du tendon patellaire, le plus probablement de nature post-interventionnel/chirurgical; à corréler cliniquement. 

Les tendons du quadriceps distal et patellaire sont grossièrement intacts et sans déchirure. 

Il y a un léger épaississement prépatellaire qui pourrait être en lien avec des séquelles de bursite.

Il y a une légère atténuation des surfaces chondrales au compartiment patellofémoral, principalement à la surface trochléaire avec des foyers de chondropathie sévère le long de l’échancrure intercondylienne et de la facette trochléaire externe avec fissures transfixiantes et des changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés. Il y a de petits ostéophytes marginaux. 

Il y a des microkystes ganglionnaires millimétriques en lien avec l’articulation tibiofibulaire proximale.

Conclusion :

Déchirure longitudinale horizontale de la corne postérieure et du corps du ménisque interne telle que décrite ci-haut avec de petits kystes paraméniscaux associés au versant postérieur.

Entorse de grade 1 du ligament collatéral interne. 

Changements dégénératifs/chondropathie tricompartimentale avec des foyers de chondropathie sévère à la surface non-portante au versant postérieur du condyle fémoral externe et le long de la surface trochléaire au compartiment patellofémoral. 

Pas d'épanchement intra-articulaire significatif.

Petit kyste de Baker non-compliqué.

Autres trouvailles telles que décrites ci-haut.
translation:
Interpretation:

There is a minimal rim of fluid within the suprapatellar recess, without significant intra-articular effusion. There is a small Baker's cyst, without significant complication, measuring 2.8 cm in CC diameter.

There is a horizontal longitudinal tear involving the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus, extending to the posterior root, to the junction with the anterior horn and along the inferior articular surface. There are small parameniscal cysts associated on the posterior aspect.

There is thickening of the superficial fibers of the medial collateral ligament with mild to moderate surrounding edema suggesting a grade 1 sprain.

There is mild to moderate attenuation of the chondral surfaces in the medial femorotibial compartment, without full-thickness involvement. There are small marginal osteophytes.

The lateral meniscus and the lateral collateral ligament complex are intact and without tear.

There is mild to moderate diffuse attenuation of the chondral surfaces in the lateral femorotibial compartment with a focus of severe chondropathy at the non-weight-bearing surface on the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle with focal full-thickness loss of the cartilage surface and early associated reactive subchondral changes. There are minimal marginal osteophytes.

The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact and without tear. There are minimal intraosseous ganglion cysts beneath the distal insertion of the anterior cruciate ligament.

The patellofemoral alignment appears within normal limits. There are several magnetic susceptibility artifacts on the anterior aspect of the patellar tendon, most likely of post-interventional/surgical nature; to correlate clinically.

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are grossly intact and without tear.

There is mild prepatellar thickening which could be related to sequelae of bursitis.

There is mild attenuation of the chondral surfaces in the patellofemoral compartment, mainly at the trochlear surface with foci of severe chondropathy along the intercondylar notch and the lateral trochlear facet with full-thickness fissures and associated reactive subchondral changes. There are small marginal osteophytes.

There are millimetric ganglion microcysts related to the proximal tibiofibular joint.

Conclusion:

Horizontal longitudinal tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus as described above with small parameniscal cysts associated on the posterior aspect.

Grade 1 sprain of the medial collateral ligament.

Tricompartmental degenerative changes/chondropathy with foci of severe chondropathy at the non-weight-bearing surface on the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and along the trochlear surface in the patellofemoral compartment.

No significant intra-articular effusion.

Small uncomplicated Baker's cyst.

Other findings as described above.

  on T1WI and hyper-signal intensity on T2WI compatible with Baker's cyst ans associated with 
  adjacent soft tissue infiltrations.

  1 injury.

  anterior horn of lateral meniscus on proton density sequence, R/O tear.
> Massive effusions in suprapatellar bursa and with suspicious some irregular multiple villous 
  lipomatous synovial proliferations, in favor of massive effusion with synovitis with/without 
  lipoma arborescence.
> Subcutaneous infiltration is noted at infrapatellar area to pretibial area.
> Presence of fissure of medial aspect lateral facet of patella extending to subchondral 
  bone in favor of grade 2 chondromalacia.
> The contour of PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Both medial and lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> No evidence of bone contusion is noted.

1. Compatible with a Baker's cyst associated with adjacent soft tissue infiltrations.
2. Massive effusion with synovitis and with/without lipoma arborescence.

Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.

There is a mass lesion in the posterior knee, measuring about 5.8x2.0x1.8 cm in size, arising between medial gastronemius tendon and the semimembranous tendon head with iso-signal intensity on T1WI and hyper-signal intensity on T2WI compatible with Baker's cyst ans associated with adjacent soft tissue infiltrations.
The contour of ACL is in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, in favor of grade 1 injury.
There are increased intrasubsance signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus and anterior horn of lateral meniscus on proton density sequence, R/O tear.
Massive effusions in suprapatellar bursa and with suspicious some irregular multiple villous lipomatous synovial proliferations, in favor of massive effusion with synovitis with/without lipoma arborescence.
Subcutaneous infiltration is noted at infrapatellar area to pretibial area.
Presence of fissure of medial aspect lateral facet of patella extending to subchondral bone in favor of grade 2 chondromalacia.
The contour of PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
Both medial and lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
No evidence of bone contusion is noted.

Impression:
1. Compatible with a Baker's cyst associated with adjacent soft tissue infiltrations.
2. Massive effusion with synovitis and with/without lipoma arborescence.
3. In favor of grade 2 chondromalacia of medial aspect lateral facet of patella.
4. Suspected tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus and anterior horn of lateral meniscus.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.

report:
FINDINGS:

Fractures:
None.

Joint alignment:
Normal.

Degenerative changes:
Focal high to full-thickness cartilage loss in the lateral femoral condyle and tibia posteriorly. This is most likely related to a prior osteochondral injury.

Mild cartilage loss in the patellofemoral cartilage with thinning of the patellar cartilage inferiorly.

Bone marrow signal:
Normal. Subchondral cysts involving the lateral tibial plateau.

Anterior cruciate ligament: Mild signal abnormality involving the ACL ligament at the posterior insertion to the femur, likely related to a mild sprain.
Posterior cruciate ligament: Normal.
Medial collateral ligament: Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament complex: The fibular collateral ligament, IT band and biceps femoris are intact. Signal abnormality involving the popliteus tendon insertion at the lateral femoral condyle, most likely tendinosis. The popliteomeniscal fascicles are not well seen and likely torn, with associated mild medial displacement of the popliteus tendon below the popliteus hiatus.

Medial meniscus: Normal.
Lateral meniscus: Complex multidirectional tear involving the posterior, body and anterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is volume loss in the body and a large displaced fragment in the intercondylar notch. There is complete loss of tissue in the posterior horn, likely a complete radial tear. There is unusual U shaped fragment adjacent to the posterior root ligament.

Extensor mechanism: Normal.
Patellar retinacula: Normal.
Pes anserinus: Normal.

Posteromedial and posterolateral corner: Normal.

Joint effusion: Small to moderate right knee joint effusion, with synovial thickening. There is a small loose body in the suprapatellar recess measuring approximately 3 mm.
Baker cyst: None.

Other significant findings:
None.

CONCLUSION:
*Complex multidirectional tear of the body, posterior and anterior horn of the lateral meniscus, with a large unusually shaped displaced fragment in the intercondylar notch. Recommend an orthopedic surgery consultation.
*Mild signal abnormality of the ACL, likely from a sprain, without evidence of tear.
*Focal high to full-thickness cartilage loss in the lateral compartment posteriorly, most significantly the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle.

Na seriji MR presjeka lijevog koljena nalazi se kompleksna, predominantno horizontala ruptura
prednjeg roga, trupa i stražnjeg roga medijalnog meniska. Uz prednji rog meniska formirana je
parameniscealna cista promjera 13 mm. Distenzija meniskokapsularnih sveza uz stražji rog
meniska.
Lateralni menisk je primjerene morfologije i intenziteta signala.
Blaža mukoidna degeneracija prednjeg križnog ligamenta, bez znakova rupture.
Primjeren nalaz stražnjeg križnog ligamenta.
Lezija I. stupnja medijalnog kolateralnog ligamenta.
Primjeren nalaz lateralnog kolateralnog ligamenta.
Entezopatske promjene tetive kvadricepsa uz moguću manju parcijalnu rupturu u medijalnom
dijelu vlakana.
Prikazane artikulacijske hrskavice urednih su intenziteta signala.
Ostale prikazane koštane, mekotkivne i neurovaskularne strukture uredne su morfologije i
intenziteta signala.
translation:
On the series of MR images of the left knee, there is a complex, predominantly horizontal tear of the anterior horn, body, and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. A parameniscal cyst measuring 13 mm in diameter is formed adjacent to the anterior horn of the meniscus. Distension of the meniscocapsular ligaments adjacent to the posterior horn of the meniscus.
The lateral meniscus is of normal morphology and signal intensity.
Mild mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament, without signs of tear.
Normal appearance of the posterior cruciate ligament.
Grade I lesion of the medial collateral ligament.
Normal appearance of the lateral collateral ligament.
Enthesopathic changes of the quadriceps tendon with possible minor partial tear in the medial portion of the fibers.
The visualized articular cartilages are of normal signal intensity.
The other visualized osseous, soft tissue, and neurovascular structures are of normal morphology and signal intensity.

translation:
Clinical History:
Bilateral patellar chondromalacia.
Findings:
No significant bone marrow signal abnormalities.
Partial cystic transformation of the ACL, without signs of tear. PCL and lateral collateral ligament without abnormalities. Mild sequelae thickening of the superficial component of the medial collateral ligament with peripheral enthesophyte of the medial femoral condyle.
Lateral meniscus with preserved morphology and signal, without criteria for tear.
Peripheral vertical linear image of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus that could represent a small complete, non-displaced tear.
Superficial chondropathy of the weight-bearing zone of the femorotibial compartments and of the femoral trochlea. Full-thickness chondral ulcers with secondary bone changes of the apex and lateral facet of the patella.
Minimal joint effusion. No popliteal cysts.
Quadriceps tendon with increased signal at its distal insertion. Increased signal of the proximal third of the patellar tendon, without signs of tear. Pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Impression:
Partial cystic transformation of the ACL, without criteria for tear.
Sequelae thickening of the proximal third of the medial collateral ligament.
Probable peripheral tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, non-displaced.
Superficial chondropathy of the weight-bearing zone of the femorotibial compartments. Chondropathy grade 3 and 4 lesions of the patella.
Minimal joint effusion.
Mild distal quadriceps and proximal patellar tendinosis.

report:
Clinical information: Left knee pain for 8 weeks, atraumatic. No improvement with physiotherapy/rehabilitation. Positive meniscus tests. Concern for LCL tear versus lateral meniscal tear. Rule out internal derangement of the knee.

Technique: Unenhanced multiplanar multiphase MRI of the left knee performed at 3.0 Tesla MRI scanner.

Findings:
There is a radial tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus measuring 4.5 x 3.5 mm. There is an fraying of the residual posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There are no displaced meniscal fragments. There is a moderate mucoid degeneration of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is no acute tear of the lateral meniscus.

The cruciate ligaments are intact. There is a moderate thickening with associated T2 hyperintensity of the proximal medial collateral ligament. Otherwise the collateral ligaments are intact. The extensor mechanism of the knee is unremarkable.

There are no deep cartilage defects in the medial and lateral femorotibial joint compartment. 

There is an mild chondrosis at the medial and lateral patellar facet with focal superficial cartilage irregularities at the lateral patellar facet. There are no cartilage defects, no subchondral bone marrow edema.

There is no joint effusion. There is no Baker's cyst. 

The joint articulations are well-maintained. 

There is a lobulated ganglion cyst extending along the popliteus tendon measuring 4.5 x 1.4 cm in the axial plane.

The infrapatellar fat pad is unremarkable. The visualized muscle bulk is intact.

Conclusion:
1. Radial tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. No displaced meniscal fragments. 
2. No acute ligamentous injury, especially no tear of the lateral collateral ligament.
3. Mild patellofemoral chondrosis.

report: МР находка: МР данни за медиална гонартроза. Ставният хрущял на фемура и тибията от медиалната страна е изтънен и е с неравни контури. Наличие на ставна течност на мястото на лизирания хрущял. Виждат се малки зони на субхондрален костно-мозъчен едем в медиалния кондул на фемура и тибията. Виждат се остеофити от медиалната страна на ставата. Ставните хрущяли от латералната страна на ставата и на пателата са съхранени. МР данни за ставен излив. Вижда се голяма Бекерова киста с размер 60/22мм. Визуализират се дегенеративни промени в задния рог на медиалния менискус. Задният рог на този меникус е уголемен и е с повишен сигнален интензитет. В него се намират хиперинтензни линии, съответстващи на скъсване. Скъсването достига до задния край на меникускуса и до ставните повърхности на фемура и на тибията. Дегенеративни промени се откриват и в прения рог на латералния менискус, без видимо скъсване в него. Предната кръстна връзка е с изтънн напречник – находка съответсваща на частично скъсване с давност. Налричие на малка зона на отоко на костния мозък в тибията под залавното място на предната кръстна връзка. Колатералните лигаменти са със запазена цялост. Ретинакулуми – б.о. Сухожилие на м квадрицепс феморис и лигамент на пателата – нормално изобразяване. Заключение: МР данни за медиална гонартроза. Детенеративни промени в меникусите. Фрагментиран е задният рог на медиалния менискус. Частично скъсване с давност на предната кръстна връзка. Ставен излив. Бекерова киста.
translation: MR findings: MR findings consistent with medial gonarthrosis. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia on the medial side is thinned and has irregular contours. Presence of joint fluid at the site of the lysed cartilage. Small zones of subchondral bone marrow edema are seen in the medial condyle of the femur and tibia. Osteophytes are seen on the medial side of the joint. The articular cartilage on the lateral side of the joint and on the patella is preserved. MR findings of joint effusion. A large Baker's cyst measuring 60/22 mm is seen. Degenerative changes are visualized in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. The posterior horn of this meniscus is enlarged and has increased signal intensity. Hyperintense lines are found within it, corresponding to a tear. The tear extends to the posterior edge of the meniscus and to the articular surfaces of the femur and the tibia. Degenerative changes are also found in the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus, without a visible tear in it. The anterior cruciate ligament has a thinned diameter – a finding consistent with a chronic partial tear. Presence of a small zone of bone marrow edema in the tibia beneath the insertion site of the anterior cruciate ligament. The collateral ligaments are intact. Retinacula – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon and patellar ligament – normal appearance. Conclusion: MR findings consistent with medial gonarthrosis. Degenerative changes in the menisci. The posterior horn of the medial meniscus is fragmented. Chronic partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. Joint effusion. Baker's cyst.

report:
Na seriji MR presjeka desnog koljena nalazi se uredna morfologija i intenziteti signala lateralnog
kolateralnog ligamenata, prednjeg i stražnjeg križnog ligamenta, iliotibijalnog traktusa, patelarne
tetive i tetive m. kvadricepsa.
Kompleksna ruptura korpusa i stražnjeg roga medijalnog meniska, s "flap" komponentom koja se
prebacuje iznad stražnjeg roga meniska u području korijena. Korpus meniska periferno je
potisnut.
Lateralni menisk uredne je morfologije i intenziteta signala.
Reaktivni periligamentarni edem uz medijalni kolateralni ligament.
Fisure i defekti pune debljine hrskavice obje fasete patele (hondromalacija 3. stupnja prema
ICRS klasifikaciji),  uz sitne rubne osteofite - OA promjene.
Ostale prikazane artikulacijske hrskavice prožete su plitkim fisurama (hondromalacija 2. stupnja
prema ICRS klasifikaciji), uz sitne rubne osteofite FT zgloba - OA promjene.
Koštani edem medijalnog kondila tibije.
Enhondrom u lateralnom aspektu distalne metafize femura promjera 13 mm.
Opsežan izljev u koljenu, masivna poplitealna (Bakerova) cista uz koju se nalazi subfascijalna
slobodna tekućina uz stražnji rub m. gastroknemijusa. Opisano je suspektno na rupturu
Bakerove ciste, bez potpune drenaže njenog sadržaja.
Varikoziteti potkožnih vena poplitealno.
Ostale prikazane koštane, mekotkivne i neurovaskularne strukture uredne su morfologije i
intenziteta signala.
translation:
On the series of MR images of the right knee, there is normal morphology and signal intensity of the lateral collateral ligament, anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments, iliotibial tract, patellar tendon, and quadriceps tendon.
Complex tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with a flap component that displaces over the posterior horn of the meniscus in the region of the root. The body of the meniscus is peripherally displaced.
The lateral meniscus is of normal morphology and signal intensity.
Reactive periligamentous edema along the medial collateral ligament.
Fissures and full-thickness cartilage defects of both patellar facets (chondromalacia grade 3 according to ICRS classification), with small marginal osteophytes - OA changes.
The other visualized articular cartilages are permeated by shallow fissures (chondromalacia grade 2 according to ICRS classification), with small marginal osteophytes of the femorotibial joint - OA changes.
Bone edema of the medial tibial condyle.
Enchondroma in the lateral aspect of the distal femoral metaphysis measuring 13 mm in diameter.
Extensive knee joint effusion, massive popliteal (Baker's) cyst with subfascial free fluid along the posterior margin of the gastrocnemius muscle. The findings are suspicious for rupture of the Baker's cyst, without complete drainage of its contents.
Varicosities of the subcutaneous veins in the popliteal region.
The other visualized osseous, soft tissue, and neurovascular structures are of normal morphology and signal intensity.

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Mild degenerative subchondral cystic changes and edema are present at the lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau. Mild cystic changes are present at the tibial spines. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Cartilage appears intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: There is a large, complex tear involving the anterior horn and body, extending to the posterior horn, with moderate extrusion.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Moderate to severe cartilage loss is present, most prominent at the posterior aspect. Small osteophytes.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is mild cartilage thinning and fissuring at the patella diffusely. Moderate cartilage thinning and fissuring is present at the trochlea diffusely, with a chondral flap at the lateral trochlear facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): There is severe mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament, with evidence of chronic partial tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Lateral meniscal tear with extrusion.
2. Chondrosis in the patellofemoral and lateral tibiofemoral compartment.
3. Severe mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament with evidence of chronic partial tear.
4. Moderate Baker cyst.
