> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of right knee with synovitis.
2. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
3. Mild anserine bursitis and small Baker's cyst.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Focal marrow edema with cyst formation at the posterior medial tibial plateau subjacent to the PCL attachment. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.

Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.

1.	Patellofemoral chondrosis.

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Few day history of knee pain following skiing injury.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Osteochondral impaction injury at the posterolateral tibial plateau. Low-grade osseous contusion along the posteromedial tibial plateau. Background marrow signal is otherwise normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate hemarthrosis. Disruption of the posterolateral joint capsule with edema tracking along the posterior knee interfascial planes. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Oblique undersurface tear involving the body and posterior horn medial meniscus without extrusion or displaced fragment.
Medial compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the central weightbearing medial femoral condyle towards the intercondylar notch.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Focal high-grade near full-thickness cartilage loss along the median ridge-medial patellar facet junction with overhanging edges. Trochlear cartilage remains intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Complete ACL tear with torn fibers along the anterior intercondylar notch.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Grade 1 sprain characterized by periligamentous edema without fiber disruption.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: There is low-grade partial-thickness tearing involving the distal conjoint tendon and partial tearing of the popliteofibular ligament.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Suspected partial tearing of the MPFL at the medial patellar attachment with superimposed disruption of the medial patellar retinaculum.
Patellofemoral tracking: Edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. There is marked lateral patellar translation and mild lateral patellar tilt. Patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Complete ACL tear with associated osteochondral impaction injury of the posterolateral tibial plateau and osseous contusion at the posteromedial tibial plateau. 
2.	Lateral patellar subluxation possibly sequela of lateral patellar dislocation with partial disruption of the MPFL and medial patellar retinaculum. Additional near full-thickness focal cartilage defect at the median ridge and medial patellar facet possibly posttraumatic.
3.	Oblique undersurface tear posterior horn and body medial meniscus without displaced fragment or extrusion.
4.	Grade 1 sprain of the MCL.
5.	Grade 1 to low-grade 2 sprain of the distal conjoint tendon and popliteofibular ligament at the posterolateral corner. 
6.	Moderate hemarthrosis.

report:
Interprétation :

Minime épanchement intra-articulaire. Liséré de liquide au sein du récessus poplité sans kyste de Baker significatif. 

Le ménisque interne et le ligament collatéral interne sont intacts sans déchirure.

Légère atténuation diffuse des surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne sans atteinte transfixiante, en lien avec de légers changements dégénératifs/chondropathie. Ébauche d’ostéophytes marginaux.

Le ménisque externe de même que le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe sont intacts sans déchirure. Les surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment fémoro-tibial externe sont relativement préservées sans atteinte transfixiante.

Il y a une infiltration kystique ganglionnaire au sein du ligament croisé antérieur sans déchirure transfixiante. Également, petits kystes para-ligamentaires. Le ligament croisé postérieur est intact sans déchirure.

Il y a une patella alta. Il y a un foyer d’œdème au versant supéro-externe de la graisse de Hoffa en lien avec un syndrome de friction du tendon patellaire et du condyle fémoral externe. Légère tendinose du tendon patellaire sans déchirure.  Légère tendinose du tendon du quadriceps distal, sans déchirure.

Il y a une atténuation modérée des surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment patellofémoral avec fissures chondrales de haut grade le long de la facette patellaire externe et de l’apex patellaire en lien avec des changements dégénératifs/chondropathie modérée. De plus, foyer de chondropathie focale sévère à la facette patellaire interne avec fissures chondrales transfixiantes et petit foyer de changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés. Ébauche d’ostéophytes marginaux.

Conclusion :

Il n’y a pas de dérangement interne (pas de déchirure méniscale ou ligamentaire significative).

Minime épanchement intra-articulaire.

Infiltration kystique ganglionnaire du ligament croisé antérieur sans déchirure transfixiante.

Changements dégénératifs/chondropathie légère au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne et modérée au compartiment patellofémoral avec foyer de chondropathie sévère le long de la facette patellaire interne.

Patella alta. Signes d’un syndrome d’accrochage du tendon patellaire et du condyle fémoral externe (Hoffa’s fat pad impingement).
translation:
Interpretation:

Minimal intra-articular effusion. Thin rim of fluid within the popliteal recess without a significant Baker's cyst.

The medial meniscus and the medial collateral ligament are intact without tear.

Mild diffuse attenuation of the cartilage surfaces in the medial femorotibial compartment without full-thickness defect, consistent with mild degenerative changes/chondropathy. Early marginal osteophytes.

The lateral meniscus as well as the lateral collateral ligament complex are intact without tear. The cartilage surfaces in the lateral femorotibial compartment are relatively preserved without full-thickness defect.

There is ganglion cyst infiltration within the anterior cruciate ligament without full-thickness tear. Additionally, small paraligamentous cysts. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact without tear.

There is patella alta. There is a focus of edema at the superolateral aspect of Hoffa's fat pad consistent with impingement syndrome of the patellar tendon and the lateral femoral condyle. Mild tendinosis of the patellar tendon without tear. Mild tendinosis of the distal quadriceps tendon, without tear.

There is moderate attenuation of the cartilage surfaces in the patellofemoral compartment with high-grade chondral fissures along the lateral patellar facet and the patellar apex consistent with moderate degenerative changes/chondropathy. Additionally, a focus of severe focal chondropathy at the medial patellar facet with full-thickness chondral fissures and a small focus of associated reactive subchondral changes. Early marginal osteophytes.

Conclusion:

There is no internal derangement (no significant meniscal or ligamentous tear).

Minimal intra-articular effusion.

Ganglion cyst infiltration of the anterior cruciate ligament without full-thickness tear.

Mild degenerative changes/chondropathy in the medial femorotibial compartment and moderate in the patellofemoral compartment with a focus of severe chondropathy along the medial patellar facet.

Patella alta. Signs of impingement syndrome of the patellar tendon and the lateral femoral condyle (Hoffa's fat pad impingement).

report:
FINDINGS:

There is a large knee joint effusion. There is significant soft tissue swelling surrounding the knee.

There is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is thickening and increased signal involving the distal posterior cruciate ligament with partial tear (approximately 50% of the fibers) of the posterior medial fibers. There is mild thickening and increased signal involving the proximal and mid aspect of the PCL.

There is complete radial tear of the posterior root of the lateral meniscus. The medial meniscus is unremarkable.

There is complete tear of the medial collateral ligament with distal avulsion of the superficial component which is retracted proximally and superficial to the pes anserine tendons compatible with a pseudoStener lesion. There is also high-grade injury involving the deep meniscal femoral and meniscal tibial component of the MCL with thickening of the posterior oblique ligament.

There is almost complete tear of the lateral collateral ligament at its femoral attachment. There are thinned out fibers that appear physically continuous. This is likely a functionally complete tear. There is also almost complete tear of the popliteus tendon as it courses around the lateral femoral condyle with significant thinning and laxity of the tendon. There is disruption of the popliteal fibular ligament. The distal biceps femoris insertion remains intact.

There is significant bone marrow edema at the posterior tibial plateau fractures. There is also bone contusion involving the anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and minimal contusion at the medial femoral condyle.

There is an enchondroma in the distal femur.

CONCLUSION:

1. Complete tear of the ACL with a moderate grade injury of the PCL.

2. High-grade injury involving the medial collateral ligament including distal avulsion of the superficial MCL with pseudo Stener lesion.

3. High-grade tear of the lateral collateral ligament which is likely functionally complete.

4. Almost complete tear of the popliteus tendon. Injury to the popliteal fibular ligament.

5. Complete radial tear involving the posterior root of the lateral meniscus.

6. Significant bone marrow edema surrounding the known tibial plateau fracture with a bone contusion in the lateral femoral condyle.

7. large knee joint effusion.

report: МР находка: Костите, формиращи колянната става са с нормална форма и сигнална характеристика. Артикулиращия хрущял на фемура и тибията е запазен. Наличие на ставен излив. МР данни за частична увреда на предна кръстна връзка. Тя се представя оточна, с повишен интензитет на сигнала и уголемен напречник. Задната кръстна връзка е интактна. Вижда се лезия с вертикален към кос ход в задния рог на медиалния менискус. Лезията достига ставните повърхности на фемура и тибията. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. Латералния колатерален лигамент се представя с уголемен напречник и повишен интензитет на сигнала в проксималната си част в близост до залавното към фемура място, както при едем, без данни за руптура. Лезия в задния рог на медиалния менискус – 3 степен. Посттравматичен мекотъканен едем, както и по хода на латералния колатерален лигамент.
translation: MRI findings: The bones forming the knee joint are of normal shape and signal characteristics. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia is preserved. Presence of joint effusion. report: There is a significant, incompletely imaged knee joint effusion that is communicating with a large, tense looking non ruptured Baker's cyst that is measuring just over 8 cm in maximal craniocaudal dimension.  Degenerative maceration is noted throughout the posterior half of the medial meniscus, with medial extrusion at the level of the body, together with a small inferiorly displaced fragment that is best appreciated in the coronal plane. There is resultant bowing of an otherwise intact superficial MCL.  An undisplaced tear through the body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus is also present, along with mucoid degeneration at the corresponding anterior horn.  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments, popliteus, distal iliotibial band and the extensor tendons. No fracture or marrow infiltration.  Reasonably well-maintained lateral weightbearing and patellofemoral articular cartilage surfaces, diffuse grade 2 thinning of medial weightbearing articular cartilage noted. Focal subcortical cystic change noted at the tibial aspect of the medial tibiofemoral joint line, presumed reactive in nature given the overlying extensive degenerative maceration.  Grossly unremarkable remaining imaged extra-articular soft tissues.

Findings: Thickened and very irregular appearance of the anterior cruciate ligament, with increased T2 signal on DST with disruption of fibers in the proximal third. translation:
Medial compartment:
Normal bone marrow signal. Mild superficial cartilage irregularities at the medial femoral condyle (Series 4 / Image 19). No deep or full-thickness cartilage defect. No subchondral bone edema. Intact medial meniscus. Intact MCL.

Lateral compartment:
Normal bone marrow signal. Intact cartilage. Intact lateral meniscus. Intact LCL.

Patellofemoral compartment and trochlea:
Normal bone marrow signal. Focal deep cartilage defect at the medial patellar facet in the middle portion (Series 7 / Image 10). No full-thickness cartilage defect, no subchondral edema. Normal appearance of the quadriceps and patellar tendons. Normal appearance of Hoffa's fat pad.

Cruciate ligaments:
Intact cruciate ligaments.

Musculature and remaining soft tissues:
No joint effusion. Mediopatellar plica (Type B according to Sakakibara).

report:
Trouvailles : 

Il n’y a pas d’épanchement significatif ni de kyste poplité.

Il y a un épaississement et une augmentation de signal impliquant la composante superficielle du ligament collatéral interne avec une déchirure des fibres antérieures partielles. La blessure est d’apparence subaiguë. Les composantes profondes méniscofémorale et méniscotibiale puis l’insertion distale demeurent intactes. 

Il y a une déchirure du ligament croisé antérieur, près de son insertion fémorale. Il y a des fibres physiquement continues, mais d’apparence laxe. Ceci est suggestif d’une blessure complète fonctionnelle. Le croisé postérieur est sans particularité. 

Autrement, le cartilage articulaire, le signal de la moelle osseuse, le ménisque interne, le ménisque externe, le mécanisme des extenseurs, le semi-membraneux, le muscle et le tendon du poplité, le biceps femoris distal, le ligament collatéral externe et la bandelette iliotibiale sont sans particularité. 

Conclusion :

Déchirure fonctionnelle complète du ligament croisé antérieur. 

Entorse subaiguë de moyen grade impliquant le ligament collatéral interne. 

Aucune déchirure méniscale.
translation:
Findings:

There is no significant effusion and no popliteal cyst.

There is thickening and increased signal involving the superficial component of the medial collateral ligament with a partial tear of the anterior fibres. The injury appears subacute. The deep meniscofemoral and meniscotibial components and the distal insertion remain intact.

There is a tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, near its femoral insertion. There are physically continuous fibres, but they appear lax. This is suggestive of a functionally complete injury. The posterior cruciate ligament is unremarkable.

Otherwise, the articular cartilage, bone marrow signal, medial meniscus, lateral meniscus, extensor mechanism, semimembranosus, popliteus muscle and tendon, distal biceps femoris, lateral collateral ligament and iliotibial band are unremarkable.

Conclusion:

Functionally complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.

Subacute moderate-grade sprain involving the medial collateral ligament.

No meniscal tear.

MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Osseous contusions involving the sulcus terminalis and posterolateral tibial plateau as well as the posterior medial tibial plateau. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Complete tear of the midsubstance.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Low grade 2 sprain pattern with partial tear of the deep fibers.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

Recent pivot shift contusions with complete rupture of the midsubstance of the ACL and low grade 2 sprain of the medial collateral ligament.

Anterior çapraz bağda mukoid dejenerasyon ile uyumlu sinyal değişikliği mevcuttur.Lateral kollateral ligamanda  grade II sprain ile uyumlu sinyal artışı mevcuttur.Lateral menisküs sinyal intensitesi ve bütünlüğü doğaldır. Medial menisküs posterior hornunda inferior artiküler yüz ile ilişkili yırtık izlenmiştir. Anterior hornda grade II dejenerasyon dikkati çekmiştir.Suprapatellar bursada lateral reses düzeyinde plikaya ait görünüm dikkati çekmiştir. Suprapatellar bursada ve eklem mesafesinde efüzyon izlenmiştir.Prepatellar yumuşak dokuda ödemli görünüm dikkati çekmiştir.Popliteal fossada yer işgal eden lezyon saptanmadı.
translation: RIGHT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: The integrity and signal intensities of the bony structures forming the knee joint are normal. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The posterior cruciate ligament and medial collateral ligament are normal. There is signal alteration in the anterior cruciate ligament consistent with mucoid degeneration. There is increased signal in the lateral collateral ligament consistent with grade II sprain. The signal intensity and integrity of the lateral meniscus are normal. A tear involving the inferior articular surface is observed in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Grade II degeneration is noted in the anterior horn. A plica-like appearance is noted at the level of the lateral recess in the suprapatellar bursa. Effusion is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and joint space. An edematous appearance is noted in the prepatellar soft tissue. No space-occupying lesion was detected in the popliteal fossa.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 8 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Horizontal oblique flap tear posterior horn and body medial meniscus with extrusion of the flap of meniscal tissue into the coronary recess.

report:
MRI of right Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS



Linear fracture of low pole of patella without significant displaced bony gragment, causing bone marrow edmea; the possibility of avulsion fracture of patellar tendon attchment can't excluded. 
Subcutanoeus infiltration over anterior aspect of right knee to pretibial region
Osteoarthritis of right knee with spur formation and wearing of articular cartilage and subchondral edema in posterior femoral condyle and anterior aspect of lateral femoral condyle.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with extending into the surface, in favor of tear.
> Linear signal intensity in lateral meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of grade 2 intrasubstance signal, maybe due to degeneration.
> The contour of PCL is not in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of tear.
> The contour of ACL appears to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Increased fat stranding and minimal fluid accumulation located along the pes anserinus, R/O Anserine bursitis
> The contour of medial patellar retinaculum is not in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of tear.

Impression: 
1. Linear fracture of right low pole patella with bone marrow edema; R/O tear of medial patellar retinaculum with suspicious of avulsion fracture.
2. Tear of PCL.
3. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus; in favor of degeneration of lateral meniscus.
4. Osteoarthritis of right knee and synovitis and mild suprapteallar bursitis.
5. Subcutanenous contusion over right knee, especially at prepatellar to infrapatellar region.
6. Anserine bursitis.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

translation:
Preserved signal intensity of the femoral and tibial cartilage in the area of the lateral condyles.
Reduced width of the medial part of the joint space of the femorotibial joint with initial degenerative changes of the adjacent cartilage (chondromalacia grade I).
Small zone of bone edema of the intercondylar eminence, at the insertion of the anterior cruciate ligament.
Other bone structures of appropriate signal intensity.
Moderate amount of effusion in the joint space.
Discontinuity of the anterior cruciate ligament consistent with a complete rupture in the middle third.

report:

Gonalgia derecha.

Formación quística subcortical del aspecto anterior del platillo tibial medial de 7 x 6 mm en sus
ejes mayores, sin significado patológico específico.
No hay otras alteraciones de señal de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos impresionan de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Condropatía superficial de la zona de carga de los compartimentos femorotibiales. Cartílago
troclear sin alteraciones. Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial del cartílago rotuliano su faceta
lateral sin cambios óseos secundarios.
Mínimo derrame articular. No hay quistes poplíteos patológicos.
Edema del paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital suprarrotuliano.
Tendones cuadricipital, la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites
normales.
Aumento de señal de la inserción proximal del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura.
Impresión:
Condropatía superficial de la zona de carga de los compartimentos femorotibiales.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 de la rótula.
Mínimo derrame articular.
Edema del paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital suprarrotuliano, hallazgo inespecífico, podría
representar fenómenos de mal alineamiento rotuliano.
Leve tendinosis rotuliana proximal.
translation:
Clinical History:
Right knee pain.

Findings:
Subcortical cystic formation at the anterior aspect of the medial tibial plateau, measuring 7 x 6 mm in its longest axes, without specific pathological significance.
No other bone marrow signal abnormalities.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
Menisci appear with preserved morphology and signal, without signs of tear.
Superficial chondropathy of the weight-bearing zones of the femorotibial compartments. Trochlear cartilage without alterations. Partial-thickness chondral ulcers of the patellar cartilage at its lateral facet without secondary bone changes.
Minimal joint effusion. No pathological popliteal cysts.
Edema of the suprapatellar retroquadriceps fat pad.
Quadriceps tendon, pes anserinus, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Increased signal at the proximal insertion of the patellar tendon, without signs of tear.

Impression:
Superficial chondropathy of the weight-bearing zones of the femorotibial compartments.
Grade 2 chondropathy of the patella.
Minimal joint effusion.
Edema of the suprapatellar retroquadriceps fat pad, a nonspecific finding that could represent patellar malalignment phenomena.
Mild proximal patellar tendinosis.

translation:
MRI LEFT KNEE
TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1 sequences in the coronal plane and PDFS in three planes.
FINDINGS:
- The medial and lateral meniscus, both collateral ligaments, and the cruciate ligaments appear normal.
- No findings are observed on examination of the extensor mechanism.
- The articular cartilage in the medial and lateral compartment is within normal limits.
- Small intra-articular fluid collection in communication with a small Baker's synovial cyst in the medial popliteal fossa.
- Bone marrow signal is within normal limits.

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]

MRI RIGHT KNEE
TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1 sequences in the coronal plane and PDFS in three planes.
FINDINGS:
- The medial and lateral meniscus, the collateral ligaments, and the cruciate ligaments appear normal.
- On examination of the extensor mechanism, mild tendinopathy is observed at the lateral portion of the quadriceps tendon insertion.
- Small intra-articular fluid collection with focal synovitis (cephalocaudal diameter 3 cm) suprapatellar, requiring rheumatological evaluation.
- Bone marrow and articular cartilage signal are within normal limits.

translation: Nearly completely resolved bone bruise of the medial femoral condyle with a subchondral insufficiency fracture demonstrated on the prior examination [DATE]. Normal articulation of the knee joint. Known advanced chondropathy of the trochlea and the lateral compartment with partly broad, deep-reaching components (4/22). report:
MRI of Left Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc, Sag PD FS, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Cor T2 FS, Ax T2 FS, Screen Save

*  Increased signal intensity in ACL on F/S T2WI, R/O grade 1 injury.
*  Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with extending into the surface and meniscal root and protrusion of medial meniscus, in favor of tear.
   There are linear signal intensity in lateral meniscus, without significant extends into the surface , R/O grade 2 intrasubstance signal.
* Fluid accmulation around medial head of gastrocnemius muscle and synovial bursa, r/o gastrocnemius bursitis.
* Fluid accumulation in the posterior articular capsule to retrocruciate ligament recess.
* Increased fat stranding and minimal fluid accumulation located along the pes anserinus, reflecting Anserine bursitis
* Increased signal intensity in F/S T2WI at tibial medial condyle, bone marrow edema is considered.
* A lobulated cystic lesion in popliteal fossa with a small recess of the knee joint capsule lies medially between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of small Baker's cyst.
* Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
* Subchondral cysts noted in the intercondylar eminence of proximal tibia and spur formation, in favor of degeneration.
> No significant myositis noted at distal thights to proximal legs.
> The contour of PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Wearing of articular cartilage of medial compartment and spur formation and mild subchondral bone marrow edema over medial tibial plateau, reflecting osteoarthritis.
Impression:
1. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus; R/O grade 2 intrasubstance signal in lateral meniscus.
2. Osteoarthritis of left knee ( more severe at medial compartment) with synovitis and small Baker's cyst
3. Anserine bursitis
4. Grade 1 injury of ACL.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.

kompleksnom rupturom trupa i značajnom ektruzijom pod MCL koja mjeri za oko 9mm te

Lateralni menisk je izmjenjenog intenziteta signala u smislu miksoidne degeneracije uz vidlju
kompleksnu rupturu prednjeg roga i anteriornog dijela korpusa. Parameniscealna cista uz prednji

translation:
Complete loss of cartilage in the anterior and middle thirds of the medial tibial plateau and femoral condyle with edema of the adjacent subchondral bone and one subchondral cyst each – chondromalacia grade IV. In the posterior third, the cartilage is thinned.
Multifocal erosions of the articular cartilages, locally with subchondral cysts as part of advanced degenerative changes.
Osteophytes of the articular surfaces of the patella, femoral trochlea, both tibial plateaus, and femoral condyles (on the ventral and dorsal sides).
Narrowing of the joint space of the femorotibial and patellofemoral joints.
Knee joint effusion.
The anterior cruciate ligament shows altered signal intensity consistent with advanced mucoid degeneration, visualized in continuity.
The posterior cruciate ligament shows altered signal intensity consistent with mild degenerative changes, without signs of rupture.
The medial meniscus shows altered signal intensity consistent with myxoid degeneration with a complex tear of the body and significant extrusion under the MCL measuring approximately 9 mm, with caudal and cranial migration of approximately 8 mm.
The lateral meniscus shows altered signal intensity consistent with myxoid degeneration with a visible complex tear of the anterior horn and the anterior part of the body. A parameniscal cyst adjacent to the anterior horn measuring 8 mm.
The lateral and medial collateral ligaments show normal signal and are visualized in continuity.
The popliteus tendon shows altered signal intensity at the proximal insertion consistent with tendinosis.
Enthesopathic changes at the insertions of the quadriceps tendon and patellar ligament on the patella.
Popliteal cyst, AP size 3 cm.

report: МР находка: Няма  данни за ставен излив. Костите формиращи коленните стави са с нормална форма. Тип 2 патели. В пателата на дясната колянна става се вижда слабо изразен костномозъчен едем. Изобразява се малка лезия на хрущяла на дясната патела, по нейната медиална ставна повърхност. Ставните хрущяли на фемурите, тибиите и на лявата патела са интактни. МР данни за начални дегенеративни промени в задния рог на медиалния менискус на лявата колянна става. Задният рог на този менискус е със слабо повишен интензитет на сигнала, без да се дефинира скъсване. Нормално изобразяване на кръстните връзки. Ретинакулуми на пателите – без особености. Колатерални лигаменти – без особености. Лигамент на пателите, сухожилия на мм. квадрицепс феморис – без особености.  Поплитеални ямки – б.о.  Изобразени мускулни групи – б.о. Заключение: МР данни за хондромалация на дясната патела –  grade 4. Не се намират други изменения в дясната колянна става.  Начални дегенеративни промени в задния рог на медиалния менискус на лявата колянна става, без видимо скъсване.
translation: MRI findings: No evidence of joint effusion. The bones forming the knee joints are of normal shape. Type 2 patellae. Mild bone marrow edema is seen in the patella of the right knee joint. A small cartilage lesion is visualized on the right patella, along its medial articular surface. The articular cartilage of the femora, tibiae, and the left patella is intact. MRI evidence of early degenerative changes in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus of the left knee joint. The posterior horn of this meniscus shows mildly increased signal intensity, without a defined tear. Normal appearance of the cruciate ligaments. Patellar retinacula – unremarkable. Collateral ligaments – unremarkable. Patellar ligament, quadriceps femoris tendons – unremarkable. Popliteal fossae – unremarkable. Visualized muscle groups – unremarkable. Conclusion: MRI evidence of chondromalacia of the right patella – grade 4. No other abnormalities are found in the right knee joint. Early degenerative changes in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus of the left knee joint, without visible tear.

translation:

Bone edema of the anterolateral part of the tibia and the lateral femoral condyle.

report: Diz eklemindeki trikompartmantal dejeneratif eklem hastalığı medyal femoral tibyal kompartmanda en belirgin ve tam kata ulaşan eklem kıkırdağı kaybı ve dejenerasyonu, subkondral medüller fibrokistik ve fibrovasküler değişiklikler ve marjinal osteofitlerle karakterize. Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı orta derecede artmış. Ön çapraz bağdaki mukoid dejenerasyon dışında çapraz bağlar normal. İç yan bağın derin bileşeni ödemli Medyale 6 mm ekstrude medyal menisküsün arka boynuzundaki kompleks dejeneratif yırtık süperiyor ve inferiyor eklem yüzeylerine ulaşıyor. Lateral menisküstaki yapı içi dejenerasyon eklem yüzeylerine yırtk biçiminde ulaşmıyor. Patellar tendonozis.
translation: Tricompartmental degenerative joint disease of the knee, most prominent in the medial femorotibial compartment, characterized by full-thickness articular cartilage loss and degeneration, subchondral medullary fibrocystic and fibrovascular changes, and marginal osteophytes. The intra-articular fluid volume is moderately increased. The cruciate ligaments are normal except for mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. The deep component of the medial collateral ligament is edematous. Complex degenerative tear in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, which is extruded medially by 6 mm, extending to both the superior and inferior articular surfaces. Intrasubstance degeneration in the lateral meniscus does not extend to the articular surfaces as a tear. Patellar tendinosis.

translation:
LEFT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings:
Grade III degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus. A radial tear is observed in the body of the meniscus. Grade II degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus. Increased T2 signal is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament, interpreted in favor of grade I sprain. Periligamentous edema is observed in the medial collateral ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Increased fluid is observed in the gastrocnemius bursa. A linear nondisplaced fracture line and signal change consistent with edema in the adjacent bone marrow are observed in the medial femoral condyle. A Baker's cyst measuring 2.5x1 cm is observed in the popliteal fossa.
CONCLUSION: Nondisplaced fracture of the medial femoral condyle and adjacent bone marrow edema. Grade III meniscopathy and radial tear of the medial meniscus. Grade II meniscopathy of the lateral meniscus. Grade I sprain of the anterior cruciate ligament. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Suprapatellar bursitis. Baker's cyst in the popliteal fossa.

translation: The amount of intra-articular fluid in the knee joint is normal. The cruciate and collateral ligaments are normal. The posterolateral corner structures are intact. A complex tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, predominantly longitudinal, horizontal, and oblique in orientation, extending from the inferior to the superior articular surface, is surrounded laterally and posteriorly by millimetric parameniscal cysts. The lateral meniscus is normal. The articular cartilages and bones are normal except for a focal superficial hyperostosis representing a "cortical desmoid" remnant at the posteromedial aspect of the distal femur. At this region, the medial gastrocnemius insertion is mildly edematous and contains a millimetric tear. The extensor mechanism is intact (the quadriceps tendon and patellar tendon, the patella and its position, the femoral trochlear groove, and the patellofemoral ligaments are normal).

report:
MRI  KNEE  -  LEFT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Fall onto left knee while downhill skiing 3 months ago. Immediate bruising. Has had residual swelling and medial joint line pain. X-ray is negative for OA. Please evaluate for meniscal or ligamentous pathology.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout images were reviewed.

Radial tear posterior horn and adjacent posterior root of the medial meniscus with slight peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The anterior horn is intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

ACL, PCL MCL and LCL are intact.

MCL and LCL are intact. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear.

Low-grade partial thickness tear of the medial patellofemoral ligament. No patellofemoral subluxation. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 8 mm, within normal limits.

Nonspecific subchondral insufficiency fracture peripheral weightbearing aspect medial femoral condyle, measuring 8 mm anterior to posterior and 6 mm medial to lateral. Exuberant surrounding marrow edema. No evidence of displaced 1 stable osteochondral fragment.

Focal fissuring of articular cartilage central weightbearing aspect medial femoral condyle as well as central to medial femoral trochlea and along the patellar apex and medial patellar facet.

Incidental finding 0.8 x 1.1 x 1.3 cm lowT1 signal intensity and high T2 signal intensity lesion, likely to represent an enchondroma.

3.5 x 1.3 x 2.7 cm the Baker's cyst. Trace fluid in the pes anserine bursa.

Small volume joint effusion.

INTERPRETATION:

1. Radial tear posterior root and posterior horn of the medial meniscus slight extrusion. 
2. Nonspecific subchondral insufficiency fracture medial femoral condyle with exuberant surrounding marrow edema.
3. Medial femorotibial and patellofemoral chondrosis most pronounced involving the patellofemoral compartment suggesting evolving mild patellofemoral predominant osteoarthritis of the left knee. 
4. Low-grade partial thickness tear of the medial patellofemoral ligament without patellofemoral subluxation. 
5. Mild pes anserine bursitis.
6. Incidental finding of enchondroma.

report:
Bez signifikantnog izljeva u koljenu.
U medijalnom kompartmentu femorotibijalnog zgloba uslijed osteoartritičnih promjena vidi se
stanjenje hrskavice, redukcija intraartikularnog prostora te rubnim osteofitom femoralnog
kondila i tibijalnog platoa s koštanim edemom te sa malom subhondralnom cistom tibijalnog
platoa i početnim formiranjem ciste femoralnog kondila.
Također uslijed deg. promjena osteofit medijalnog dijela medijalnog kondila femura koji prominira
u interkondilarnu fosu i utiskuje se u prednji križni ligament. Osteofiti kranijalnog i kaudalnog
pola posteriornog dijela patele, lateralnog platoa tibije, lateralnog femoralnog kondila i rubno
obje strane trohleje femura. Masivni ostoefit tibije u proksimalnom tibiofibularnom zglobu te
manji osteofiti glavice fibule.
Hiperintenzitet lateralnog interkondilarnog tuberkula tibije uslijed početnog formiranja
subhondralne ciste.
Intraosealne ciste lateralnog kondila femura uz hvatište kolateralnog ligamenta.
Kompleksna ruptura tijela medijalnog meniska uz degenerativne promjene stražnjeg roga.
Degenerativne promjene oba roga lateralnog meniska.
Uznapredovala mukoidna degeneracija prednjeg križnog ligamenta koji je horizontalnije položen i
stanjen u razni opisanog osteofita medijalnog femoralnog kondila, suspektna kompletna ruptura
u srednjoj trećini.
Pri hvatištu patelarne tetive za patelu u posteriornom dijelu vlakana hiperintenzitet koji može
odgovarati patelarnoj tendinopatiji.
Nalazi se uredna morfologija i intenziteti signala kolateralnih ligamenata, stražnjeg križnog
ligamenta, iliotibijalnog traktusa i tetive m. kvadricepsa.
Hondromalacija III. stupnja lateralne strane trohleje femura.
Hondromalacija II. stupnja centralnog dijela hrskavice patele i lateralnog kondila femura. Odgovara degenerativnim promjenama FP zgloba.
Ne nalazi se poplitealne (Bakerove) ciste.
Ostale prikazane koštane, mekotkivne i neurovaskularne strukture uredne su morfologije i
intenziteta signala
translation:
No significant knee effusion.
In the medial compartment of the femorotibial joint, due to osteoarthritic changes, there is cartilage thinning, reduction of the intra-articular space, and marginal osteophytes of the femoral condyle and tibial plateau with bone edema, as well as a small subchondral cyst of the tibial plateau and early cyst formation of the femoral condyle.
Also, due to degenerative changes, an osteophyte of the medial part of the medial femoral condyle protrudes into the intercondylar fossa and impinges on the anterior cruciate ligament. Osteophytes of the cranial and caudal poles of the posterior part of the patella, the lateral tibial plateau, the lateral femoral condyle, and marginally on both sides of the femoral trochlea. A massive osteophyte of the tibia at the proximal tibiofibular joint and smaller osteophytes of the fibular head.
Hyperintensity of the lateral intercondylar tibial tubercle due to early subchondral cyst formation.
Intraosseous cysts of the lateral femoral condyle at the insertion of the collateral ligament.
Complex tear of the body of the medial meniscus with degenerative changes of the posterior horn.
Degenerative changes of both horns of the lateral meniscus.
Advanced mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament, which is more horizontally oriented and thinned at the level of the described osteophyte of the medial femoral condyle, with suspected complete tear in the middle third.
At the insertion of the patellar tendon to the patella, in the posterior part of the fibers, there is hyperintensity that may correspond to patellar tendinopathy.
The collateral ligaments, posterior cruciate ligament, iliotibial tract, and quadriceps tendon show normal morphology and signal intensity.
Grade III chondromalacia of the lateral side of the femoral trochlea.
Grade II chondromalacia of the central part of the patellar cartilage and the lateral femoral condyle. This corresponds to degenerative changes of the patellofemoral joint.
No popliteal (Baker's) cyst is present.
The other visualized osseous, soft tissue, and neurovascular structures are of normal morphology and signal intensity.

Normal.

The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Joint effusion is seen in the knee joint. Signal intensities of the bony structures forming the knee joint are normal. Grade 2-3 degeneration areas are observed in the medial aspect of the patellar cartilage. A Baker's cyst measuring 3 cm in diameter is observed in the popliteal region. Fibrillation is present in the trochlear cartilage. Conclusion: Patellar chondromalacia, joint effusion, Baker's cyst, medial meniscus degeneration.

report:
U području metafize tibije, lateralno od središnje linije, vidi se polimikrolobulirana intramedularna
tvorba neagresivnih karakteristika, heterogenih, predominantno viših T2 intenziteta signala koji
će prvenstveno odgovarati hondroidnom porijeklu. Lezija je ukupnih dimenzija 19x22x30mm
(APxLLxCC), bez vidljive periostalne reakcije i bez vidljivog zahvaćanja kortikalisa - prvenstveno
će odgovarati enhondromu.
Denudacija hrskavice patele u centralnom dijelu kranijalno na arealu veličine oko 6mm (CC) sa
vidljivim manjim subhondralnim edemom u smislu hondromalacije IV. stupnja.
Stanjena hrskavica oba femoralna kondila i tibijalnog platoa uz mjestimične zone hondormalacije
II. stupnja - početne OA promjene.
Bez izljeva.
Medijalni menisk je izmjenjenog intenziteta signala u smislu blaže miksoidne degeneracije.
Uz anteriorni dio trupa sitne ganglion ciste koje najvjerojatnije pripadaju medijalnom patelarnom
retinakulumu koji je promijenjene strukture, vjerojatno ranija ozljeda.
Vidi se kompleksna ruptura trupa lateralnog meniska koja seže do obje artikualcijske površine.
Stražnja i prednja ukrižena sveza su primjerenog intenziteta signala, bez vidjivih znakova
rupture.
Oba kolateralna ligamenta su primjerenog intenziteta signala, bez znakova rupture.
Tendinopatija tetive m.popliteus umjerenog stupnja. Tetive pes anserinusa i iliotibijalni trakt
primjerenog prikaza, bez znakova rupture.
Izmjenjen intenzitet signala tetive kvadricepsa i patelarnog ligamenta na mjestu hvatišta na
pateli u smislu entezopatskih promjena. Edem suprapatelarnog masnog jastučića. U području
koljena vidljiv edem potkožja.
translation:
In the region of the tibial metaphysis, lateral to the midline, there is a polymicrolobulated intramedullary lesion of non-aggressive characteristics, heterogeneous, predominantly high T2 signal intensity, most likely corresponding to chondroid origin. The lesion measures 19x22x30mm (APxLLxCC) in total dimensions, without visible periosteal reaction and without visible cortical involvement - most likely corresponding to an enchondroma.
Cartilage denudation of the patella in the central part cranially over an area of approximately 6mm (CC) with visible minor subchondral edema consistent with grade IV chondromalacia.
Thinned cartilage of both femoral condyles and the tibial plateau with focal zones of grade II chondromalacia - early OA changes.
No effusion.
The medial meniscus shows altered signal intensity consistent with mild myxoid degeneration.
Along the anterior part of the body, small ganglion cysts most likely belonging to the medial patellar retinaculum which is of altered structure, probably prior injury.
There is a complex tear of the body of the lateral meniscus extending to both articular surfaces.
The posterior and anterior cruciate ligaments are of normal signal intensity, without visible signs of rupture.
Both collateral ligaments are of normal signal intensity, without signs of rupture.
Moderate tendinopathy of the popliteus tendon. The pes anserinus tendons and iliotibial tract are of normal appearance, without signs of rupture.
Altered signal intensity of the quadriceps tendon and patellar ligament at the insertion site on the patella consistent with enthesopathic changes. Edema of the suprapatellar fat pad. Subcutaneous edema visible in the knee region.

report:
COMPARISON:Prior right knee MRI from [Date].

CLINICAL HISTORY:Suspected osteoarthritis/internal derangement right knee.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Diminutive appearance of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus consistent with complex tear, progressed since <[YEAR]>. Diminutive appearance of the medial meniscal body consistent with complex tear. There is peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The anterior horn is intact.

Intrasubstance degeneration posterior horn of the lateral meniscus without discrete tear. No lateral meniscal extrusion.

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament without tibial translation, new since previous study. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

The medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact. The fibular collateral ligament is intact. The popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments are intact. The interval and is intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No patellofemoral subluxation. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 10 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. Mild edema of the suprapatellar fat pad suggesting patellofemoral maltracking.

There is mild to moderate generalized patellofemoral chondrosis, progressed since previous study. There is extensive fissuring and thinning of medial femorotibial articular cartilage with small focal areas of full-thickness cartilage denuding, progressed since <[YEAR]>. Within the lateral formidable compartment, there is thinning of articular cartilage involving the central weightbearing aspect of the left femoral condyle and overlying the lateral tibial plateau, progressed since previous study.

Small knee joint effusion. Baker's cyst, measuring 30 x 19 x 65 mm.

Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Progressive complex tearing of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus and progressive tricompartment chondrosis most pronounced involving the medial femorotibial compartment, consistent with progressive moderate to severe medial compartment predominant tricompartment osteoarthritis of the right knee.
2. Since <[YEAR]>, interval development of low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament without tibial translation.
3. 30 x 19 x 65 mm Baker's cyst.

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee buckling. Osteoarthritis. ACL sprain. Medial meniscus tear. 
Comparison: [REDACTED]. 

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar and multisequence MRI of the right  knee without IV contrast.   

FINDINGS: 

JOINT EFFUSION:  Small joint effusion. Small leaking popliteal cyst. 

ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

POSTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

MEDIAL MENISCUS: Large horizontal undersurface tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is also low-grade tearing of the posterior root attachment. Mild peripheral meniscal extrusion. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:  Subchondral fracture line is noted along the weightbearing segment of the medial femoral condyle, with probable nondisplaced osteochondral lesion. This measures 15 mm AP and 10 mm transverse. Moderate degree of associated bone marrow edema.

There is also mild medial compartment osteoarthritis, with subchondral cystic changes of the tibial plateau. 

LATERAL MENISCUS:  Intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:  Within normal limits. 

MEDIAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT:  Edema along the medial collateral ligament suggestive of grade 1 sprain pattern. No discrete tear. 

LATERAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT COMPLEX:  Intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: Low-grade fissuring of the patellar cartilage. No high-grade or full-thickness cartilage defect. No subchondral edema. 

EXTENSOR APPARATUS:  Superior and inferior patellar enthesophytes. Small interstitial tear in the proximal patellar tendon. 

BONE MARROW:  As above. 
 
OTHER:  None. 


IMPRESSION:

1. Large horizontal undersurface tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Mild peripheral meniscal extrusion.

2. Subchondral fracture line of the medial femoral condyle, likely in the context of nondisplaced osteochondral lesion.

3. Mild medial compartment osteoarthritis.

4. Grade 1 sprain pattern of the medial collateral ligament. Intact cruciate ligaments.

5. Small knee joint effusion and leaking popliteal cyst.

translation:
TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

RIGHT KNEE
In the medial compartment, degeneration and mild subluxation of the medial meniscus are identified. The articular cartilage and bone marrow have normal appearance.
On evaluation of the lateral compartment, a degenerative tear and subluxation of the meniscus are observed, a full-thickness cartilage defect measuring 2.5 mm in diameter in the context of a chondral fracture, thinning-erosion of the articular cartilage of the lateral tibial plateau (ICRS grade III), and subarticular bone marrow edema particularly evident at the tibial epiphysis. The findings are consistent with degenerative osteoarthritis.
On evaluation of the anterior compartment, ICRS grade III degeneration of the articular cartilage of the patella at the medial facet is observed, while the quadriceps and patellar tendons appear within normal limits.
Intra-articularly, a large joint effusion is observed with a large cartilaginous loose body at the lateral recess measuring 12x10 mm.
The anterior cruciate ligament shows myxoid degeneration. The remaining ligamentous structures are intact.
In the medial popliteal fossa, a Baker's cyst is observed with locally viscous content, craniocaudal diameter of 4 cm, and signs of microtears of its wall with presence of free fluid in the gastrocnemius bursa.

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]

LEFT KNEE
In the medial compartment, degeneration and mild subluxation of the medial meniscus are observed without other findings.
In the lateral compartment, full-thickness degeneration and erosion of the articular cartilage of the lateral tibial plateau (ICRS grade IV) are observed. The lateral meniscus shows a degenerative tear and mild subluxation. Mild erosion is also present in the articular cartilage of the lateral femoral condyle. Small extent bone marrow edema is observed at the tibial epiphysis ipsilaterally. The findings are consistent with degenerative osteoarthritis.
On evaluation of the anterior compartment and the extensor mechanism, small extent erosion (ICRS grade II) at the medial articular surface of the patella is observed. A moderate intra-articular joint effusion is present with three osteochondral loose bodies at the posterior aspect posterior to the posterior cruciate ligament. The ligamentous structures are intact.

translation:
On the series of MR images of the left knee, there is lateral patellar dislocation in the patellofemoral joint. Reduced cartilage thickness of the medial patellar facet with a larger cartilage defect in the medial portion and smaller zones of subchondral bone edema/subchondral cysts - chondromalacia grade IV. Altered signal intensity of the cartilage of the lateral patellar facet consistent with chondromalacia grade I-II.
Altered signal intensity of the trochlear cartilage - chondromalacia grade I.
Marginal osteophytes have formed on the articular bodies of the medial side of the patellofemoral joint.
Wiberg type 2 patella.
Trochlear dysplasia - reduced size of the medial facet with a shallow trochlea. The TT-TG distance is increased and measures approximately 16 mm.
The Insall-Salvati ratio is 1.3 (normal).
The medial patellar retinaculum is of reduced tension without a clearly visible disruption of continuity.
At the insertion of the lateral patellar retinaculum on the patella, there are small subcortical cysts consistent with enthesopathic changes or a condition after a previous partial rupture.
Minor prepatellar subcutaneous edema. Early OA changes of the femorotibial joint.
The anterior cruciate ligament is thickened, with increased signal intensity, probably consistent with degenerative changes, possibly also a condition after a previous partial rupture, with visible intraosseous ganglion cysts at the tibial insertion measuring up to 7 mm in diameter.
The posterior cruciate ligament has appropriate signal intensity and maintained continuity; an intraosseous ganglion cyst measuring 4 mm in diameter is located at the femoral insertion.
The anterior root and horn of the lateral meniscus have increased signal intensity, without clear signs of rupture, primarily consistent with degenerative changes.
The medial meniscus shows no signs of rupture or degeneration.
The lateral collateral ligament has appropriate signal intensity and maintained continuity.
The medial collateral ligament has appropriate signal intensity and maintained continuity.
Normal appearance of the popliteus tendon, iliotibial tract, and pes anserinus.
Mildly increased signal intensity of the patellar ligament at the insertion on the inferior pole of the patella, consistent with enthesopathic changes.
The quadriceps tendon has appropriate signal intensity and maintained continuity.
No significant joint effusion.
Minor effusion in the popliteal bursa.
Along the posterior margin of the medial femoral condyle, medially, there is an ossification measuring 3x5 mm axially (AP x LL) which may correspond to an accessory bone or a bone fragment with sclerotic margins consistent with a loose joint body.

translation: LEFT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus. The lateral meniscus is normal. The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. Loss of integrity and subchondral bone marrow edema are observed in the medial facet of the patellar cartilage (type IV chondromalacia). Subchondral bone marrow edema is observed at the level of the medial femoral condyle. Thinning and signal changes consistent with grade I-II chondromalacia are present in the femoral cartilage at this level. A lobulated contoured cystic lesion approximately 14x6 mm in size is present in the lateral head of the gastrocnemius muscle with mild edematous appearance in its vicinity. No joint effusion is detected.

Knee contusion.

The lateral meniscus is of preserved morphology and signal, without categorical criteria for tear.
Peripheral vertical signal increase in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus, which could represent at least a partial peripheral lesion with regional soft tissue edema.

translation:
LEFT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: The lateral meniscus is normal. There is a horizontal tear in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus related to the femoral articular surface. A radial tear was also observed in the body of the meniscus. The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Significant effusion was observed in the joint. Signal intensities of the bony structures forming the knee joint are normal. There is significant subchondral edematous signal change in the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.
Conclusion: Joint effusion, edema in the medial femoral condyle and tibia, tear in the medial meniscus.

translation:
MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
From the evaluation of the menisci, the cruciate and collateral ligaments, and the bone marrow, no significant findings are observed.

From the evaluation of the articular cartilage, a small focus of swelling is noted on the medial articular surface of the patellar cartilage, corresponding to chondromalacia. No erosions are observed.

From the evaluation of the remaining extensor mechanism, a focus of edema is recognized in the region of the superior Hoffa's fat pad, where a small synovial plica is also noted infrapatellarly. The finding is consistent with impingement of the inferior pole of the patella against the femur.

A small fluid collection is observed intra-articularly.

In the lateral compartment, edema is observed adjacent to the lateral femoral epicondyle, approximately 3 cm in craniocaudal diameter. The finding is attributed to iliotibial band friction syndrome.

ligament. Manji rubni osteofiti FT zgloba u smislu OA promjena.

Prikazane koštane strukture primjerenih intenziteta signala i morfologije.
Prikazana zglobna tijela primjereno su uzglobljena.
Prikaže se hondromalacija I-II° kondilarne i tibijalne hrskavice.
Hondromalacija II° medijalne i lateralne fasete patele.
Prednji i stražnji križni ligamenti su održanog kontinuiteta i primjerenih intenziteta signala. Uz
hvatište prednjeg križnog ligamenta za tibiju vidi se intraosealna cista promjera 3 mm.
Medijalni i lateralni kolateralni ligamenti su primjerenih intenziteta signala, održanog kontinuiteta.
Uredan prikaz tetive popliteusa, iliotibijalnog trakta i pes anserinus.
Blago povišen intenzitet signala tetive kvadricepsa i ligamenta patele na hvatištu za patelu u
smislu blažih entezopatskih promjena.
Degenerativne promjene hvatišta tetive medijalne glave m. gastrocnemius za femur.
Patelarni retinakulumi održani.
Bez signifikantnog izljeva u zglob.
Poplitealna cista promjera 4 mm.
translation:
Oblique tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus communicating with the tibial articular surface, with meniscal extrusion of approximately 2 mm and mild periligamentous edema along the medial collateral ligament. Small marginal osteophytes of the femorotibial joint consistent with OA changes.
Lateral meniscus without signs of tear or degeneration.
The visualized osseous structures are of appropriate signal intensity and morphology.
The visualized articular bodies are appropriately articulated.
Chondromalacia grade I-II of the condylar and tibial cartilage is demonstrated.
Chondromalacia grade II of the medial and lateral patellar facets.
The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are of intact continuity and appropriate signal intensity. At the tibial insertion of the anterior cruciate ligament, an intraosseous cyst measuring 3 mm in diameter is seen.
The medial and lateral collateral ligaments are of appropriate signal intensity, with intact continuity.
Normal visualization of the popliteus tendon, iliotibial tract, and pes anserinus.
Mildly increased signal intensity of the quadriceps tendon and patellar ligament at the patellar insertion consistent with mild enthesopathic changes.
Degenerative changes at the femoral insertion of the medial head of the gastrocnemius tendon.
Patellar retinacula are intact.
No significant joint effusion.
Popliteal cyst measuring 4 mm in diameter.

translation:
Technique: The examination was performed with T1, T2/proton density pulse sequences with fat suppression.

Findings:
- In the medial and lateral compartments of the knee joint as well as in the patellofemoral joint, there is joint space narrowing, thinning (up to complete loss) of the cartilage, presence of multiple large marginal osteophytes, and small foci of subarticular bone marrow edema in the tibial epiphysis, the articular surface of the patella, and the anterior surface of the distal femur. A significant joint effusion is also observed, along with intra-articular osteochondral fragments, the largest measuring 1.8 cm in diameter, located suprapatellarly.
- A degenerative tear of the lateral meniscus and a degenerative tear with subluxation of the medial meniscus are observed.
- Small osteophytes also project into the intercondylar notch with associated indistinctness of the anterior cruciate ligament, in the setting of a complete tear.
- No pathological findings are identified in the posterior cruciate ligament and the collateral ligaments.
- The remaining bone marrow demonstrates normal signal.

Conclusion: Degenerative changes of osteoarthritis with associated secondary osteochondromatosis (findings possibly in the setting of CPPD).

As above

Normal.

None

CONCLUSION:

Horizontal tear of the lateral meniscal body. No displaced meniscal flap.

Tricompartmental chondropathy as described above.

Distal quadriceps tendinosis, without tear.

translation:
Clinical History:
Internal meniscal syndrome of the left knee.
Findings:
No significant bone marrow signal abnormalities.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
The lateral meniscus is of preserved morphology and signal, without signs of tear.
Increased central signal of the posterior horn and part of the body of the medial meniscus that does not appear to contact the articular surface, without features of a tear.
Cartilage of the femorotibial compartments and femoral trochlea without alterations.
Diffuse superficial patellar chondropathy with medial predominance.
Increased signal of the superolateral aspect of Hoffa's fat pad.
No evident joint effusion or pathological popliteal cysts.
Quadriceps tendon, patellar tendon, pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Increased signal of the insertional region of the medial gastrocnemius in its peripheral region, with mild edema of the regional soft tissues. A laminar amount of fluid is also observed between the pes anserine tendons and the medial femoral condyle.
Impression:
Superficial patellar chondropathy.
Signs of lateral patellar hyperpressure syndrome.
Probable insertional tendinosis of the medial gastrocnemius associated with posteromedial friction phenomena of the knee.

translation:

Knee sprain. Traumatic knee.
Findings:
No significant bone marrow signal abnormalities.
Cruciate ligaments and lateral collateral ligament without abnormalities.
Thickening and increased signal of the superficial component of the medial collateral ligament with loss of continuity of its proximal fibers, with regional soft tissue edema and a mild amount of regional fluid. The remaining components of the medial complex are within normal limits.

translation:
LEFT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings:
Grade III degeneration and a horizontal tear are observed in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. The medial meniscus appears extruded medially. Grade I degeneration is observed in the lateral meniscus. Diffuse signal increase is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament (myxoid degeneration). Focal signal increases are observed in the posterior cruciate ligament (grade I sprain). The lateral collateral ligament is normal. An edematous appearance is present around the medial collateral ligament (grade I sprain). Widespread fluid increase is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and within the knee joint. A subarticular fracture line and widespread edema in the adjacent bone are observed at the level of the medial femoral condyle facing the tibiofemoral joint surface. The joint space is narrowed at this level. Subchondral millimetric cysts are observed at the tibial insertion site of the posterior cruciate ligament. An edematous appearance is present in the subcutaneous fatty tissue at the prepatellar level of the knee joint.

report: SOL DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Lateral menisküste grade I dejenerasyon izlenmiştir. Medial menisküste grade III dejenerasyon ve  gövde düzeyinde horizontal yırrtık izlendi. Medial kollateral ligamen çevresinde grade I sprain ile uyumlu periligamentöz ödem izlendi. Ön çapraz bağda diffüz sinyal artışı, arka çapraz bağda yer yer fokal sinyal artışları izlendi.Lateral kollateral ligaman normaldir.Patellar tendon normaldir. Retinakulumlar normaldir . Patella normal yerleşimlidir.Patellofemoral eklem mesafesinde , suprapatellar bursada ve diz eklemi içerisinde sıvı artışları mevcuttur. Tibiofemoral eklem mesafesinde medialde daralma komşu femoral ve tibial kartilajlarda incelmeler izlendi(dejeneratif artrit bulguları). Femur medial kondil posterior düzeyinde subkondral milimetrik kistler izlenmiştir.Prepatellar düzeyde cilt altı yağlı dokuda ödematöz görünüm mevcuttur.
translation: LEFT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: Grade I degeneration is observed in the lateral meniscus. Grade III degeneration and a horizontal tear at the body level are observed in the medial meniscus. Periligamentous edema consistent with grade I sprain is observed around the medial collateral ligament. Diffuse signal increase is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament, and focal signal increases are observed in places in the posterior cruciate ligament. The lateral collateral ligament is normal. The patellar tendon is normal. The retinacula are normal. The patella is normally positioned. Fluid increases are present in the patellofemoral joint space, in the suprapatellar bursa, and within the knee joint. Narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral joint space with thinning of the adjacent femoral and tibial cartilage is observed (findings of degenerative arthritis). Subchondral millimetric cysts are observed at the posterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle. An edematous appearance is present in the subcutaneous fatty tissue at the prepatellar level.

report: Kuadriseps yağ yastığı ödemi hafif dereceli ve ön diz ağrısı ile birlikte olabilir. Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı normal. Çapraz ve yan bağlar normal. Posterolateral ve posteromedyal köşe yapıları korunmuş. Lateral menisküs normal. Mediyal menisküs arka boynuzu - gövdesindeki dejenerasyon alt eklem yüzeyi ile ilişkilenen horizantal oblik longitüdinal yırtık ve gövdesi düzeyinde serbest kenardaki milimetrik radyal yırtık ile birlikte. Eklem kıkırdakları ve kemikler normal. Ekstensör mekanizma korunmuş (kuadriseps tendonu ve patellar tendon, patella ve yerleşimi, femoral troklear oluk ve patellofemoral bağlar normal). Gastroknemyus-semimembranozus (GK-SM) bursasındaki sıvı lokülasyonunun kalınlığı 5 mm'yi geçmiyor. report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain with walking up and down stairs.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with lipomatous synovial hypertrophy in the suprapatellar recess. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Bucket-handle variant tear of the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with a large displaced flap fragment into the intercondylar notch.
Medial compartment cartilage: High grade partial thickness cartilage loss along the medial weightbearing surfaces with deep cartilage fissuring cartilaginous flap formation.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild cartilage thinning and heterogeneity.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness cartilage loss along the medial patella with subchondral cystic change. High-grade partial thickness cartilage loss along the central trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: Mild proximal tendinosis without tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Bucket-handle variant tear of the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with a large displaced flap fragment into the intercondylar notch.
2.	Tricompartmental chondrosis, worse in the patellofemoral and medial compartments.
3.	Moderate joint effusion with lipomatous synovial hypertrophy.
4.	Mild distal quadriceps and proximal patellar tendinosis without tearing.

translation: LEFT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: Grade I degeneration was observed in the lateral meniscus. Grade III degeneration and complex tear in the medial meniscus, with an appearance consistent with volume loss at the body level, were observed. The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, and lateral ligament are normal. A ganglion cyst with lobulated contours containing thin septations, approximately 20x10 mm in size in the posterior vicinity of the posterior cruciate ligament and 8x8 mm in size in the posteromedial vicinity, was observed. Mild fluid increase was observed around the medial collateral ligament. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Fluid increase was observed in the suprapatellar bursa and at the knee joint level. An edematous appearance is present in the subcutaneous fat tissue surrounding the knee joint. Narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral joint space, subchondral edema, and cartilage thinning were observed. An appearance consistent with a Baker's cyst with septations and lobulated contours, measuring 76x20 mm, is present in the popliteal fossa.

translation:

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
On evaluation of the cruciate and collateral ligaments, no significant findings are observed.
The lateral meniscus has borderline discoid morphology and mild degeneration.

translation:
KNEE MRI

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences. [DATE].

FINDINGS
The bone marrow edema in the lateral femoral condyle is no longer observed. A small focus of new edema (9 mm) is observed in the anterior medial tibial condyle, in the same context of a microtrabecular insufficiency fracture. Re-evaluation shows degeneration without tear of the medial meniscus, while articular cartilage and ligamentous structures are depicted within normal limits. On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, edema of the medial parapatellar and suprapatellar fat pad is observed, with a craniocaudal diameter of approximately 3 cm, attributed to mild impingement of the patella and the quadriceps tendon against the anterior femur.

CONCLUSION
Complete resolution of bone marrow edema of the lateral femoral condyle and a barely recognizable new focus of edema in the anterior medial tibial condyle.

translation:
TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo sequences.

FINDINGS
- Extensive bone marrow edema is observed in the medial femoral condyle and on the medial tibial plateau, with a subarticular low-signal lesion on all sequences. A similar, smaller lesion is observed in the medial tibial condyle. There is only subtle flattening of the articular surface of the medial femoral condyle. The remaining articular surfaces are intact.
- Abnormal signal is observed in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with contour abnormality and subluxation.
- Osteoarthritis is observed with erosion of the articular cartilage of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau, as well as with the presence of osteophytes. Early osteoarthritis is observed in the lateral patellofemoral compartment.
- Thickening and abnormal signal of the medial collateral ligament at its midportion and toward its femoral insertion, likely reactive to the displacement of the medial meniscus.
- Moderate amount of intra-articular fluid with mild synovitis.

CONCLUSION
1. Findings consistent with insufficiency fracture of the medial femoral and tibial condyles (synonym: "spontaneous osteonecrosis").
2. Degenerative tear of the medial meniscus with joint effusion.

report:
Findings:  Small knee joint effusion. No intra-articular loose bodies. No sinister bone marrow changes.  10 mm x 6 mm by 16mm well-defined lobulated intramedullary lesion in the distal metadiaphysis of the right femur display low signal on T1 and high signal on PD sequences. Multiple hypointense foci within the lesion representing calcification. No perilesional edema, endosteal scalloping or cortical destruction. Findings are in keeping with a low-grade chondroid lesion (enchondroma).  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments.  Intact lateral meniscus. Radial tearing of the inner free of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus.  Normal appearance of the distal biceps femoris tendon, popliteus tendon, pes anserine tendons and distal iliotibial band.  Intact quadriceps and patellar tendons. Severe patellofemoral degenerative changes with high-grade chondral thinning and full-thickness chondral loss along the lateral retropatellar facet and corresponding lateral femoral trochlea surface with underlying stress changes. The patella is lateralized relative to the femoral trochlear groove. Evidence of trochlear dysplasia with a shallow trochlear groove.  Relatively well-maintained medial and lateral tibiofemoral hyaline articular cartilage. Tricompartmental osteophyte formation noted.  
Conclusion:  Radial tearing of the inner free edge of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Severe patellofemoral degenerative changes with evidence of trochlear dysplasia and lateralization of the patella relative to the trochlear groove.
