translation:
MRI right knee

Clinical information / radiological question: Pain on flexion. Chondromalacia patellae? Additionally also meniscal injury? See scanned request.

Procedure: Sagittal, coronal and axial intermediate-weighted sequences with fat saturation, sagittal intermediate-weighted sequences without fat saturation, coronal T1-weighted images.

Findings:
Normal appearance of the quadriceps tendon and patellar tendon. Normal delineation of the patellar cartilage with a limited zone of cartilage thinning / limited fissuring in the medial patellar facet. Loculated cysts bulging into Hoffa's fat pad, from the tibial insertion of the anterior cruciate ligament, extending further medially and caudally, around the medial tibial plateau, superficial and deep to the distal patellar tendon on the lateral side. Intact appearance of the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments. The signal intensities of the menisci appear within normal limits. Normal appearance of the medial and lateral collateral ligaments and the iliotibial tract. Normal appearance of the pes anserinus. Normal signal intensities of the tibial nerve and the common peroneal nerve.

Conclusion:
Loculated ganglion cyst of Hoffa's fat pad with extension as described above.

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Chronic atraumatic knee pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Small tricompartmental marginal osteophytes. Intraosseous ganglion cyst formation along the anterior medial tibial plateau.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion with synovitis. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Inner margin tearing of the body segment. Root attachments are intact. No parameniscal cyst.
Medial compartment cartilage: Scattered foci of high-grade cartilage loss along the weightbearing femoral condyle. High-grade cartilage loss at the periphery and anterior aspects of the tibial plateau with underlying subchondral cystic change/edema.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade chondrosis along the posterior weightbearing aspect of the femoral condyle along the intercondylar notch. Mild chondrosis along the posterior tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade partial thickness cartilage thinning along the inferior aspect of the lateral patellar facet with small areas of high-grade fissuring involving the medial facet. Foci of high-grade and full thickness cartilage loss along the medial and central trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis with some low-grade interstitial tearing along the medial distal fibers.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Tricompartmental osteoarthritis, mild to moderate in the medial compartment.
2.	Inner margin tearing of the medial meniscal body.
3.	Mild insertional quadriceps tendinosis with some low-grade interstitial tearing.

* Osteophytes of left knee with wearing of articular cartilage, more prominent at lateral compartment, reflecting osteoarthritis.
  Focal linear hypointensity material in anterior intercondylar notch (Srs/Img: [ID].
* Irregular contour and increased signal intensity of the intra-articular cartilage of patella lateral and inferior part, in favor of grade 2 chondromalacia.
> Mild interstitial increased signal of ACL on F/S T2WI, in favor of mild degeneration. 
  PCL and MCL and LCL appear to be within normal.
* Joint effusion with mild increased signal intensity on T1WI and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae ; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis. 
  Fat stranding of infrapatellar fat pad, with a increase signal intensity inside on PD F/S image, connected to suprapatellar bursa.
* Small size of lateral meniscus with linear signal intensity in posterior horn of lateral meniscus, with extending into the surface, in favor of tear.
> Subcutaneous edema over left knee, prominent in prepatella region.
  Focal heterogeneous hyperintense foci at anterior and lateral peripatellar subcutaneous fat on T2WI and PD image (Srs/Img: 11/8-10), in favor of post-operative change  (s/p left knee arthroscope for 8 years)
> Small superficial nodular-like foci in infrapatellar region (Srs/Img: [ID]; 7,8/7), nature unknown?R/O granuloma or scar formation
IMP:
1. C/W osteoarthritis of left knee, more severe at lateral compartment, with grade 3-4 chondral injury and loose body / detached cartilage.
2. Degeneration of lateral meniscus and R/O tear of posterior horn of lateral meniscus; differential diagnosis of  post-operative change ( partial menisectomy).
3. Synovitis- mild joint effusion of left knee with patellar plicae.
4. Grade 1 injury or degeneration of ACL.   
5. R/O granuloma or scar formation over superficial skin.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management

report: ΤΕΧΝΙΚΗ : H εξέταση εγίνε με τομογράφο 3 Tesla και ακολουθίες παλμών Τ1 και πυκνότητας πρωτονίων με καταστολή του σήματος του λίπους. ΕΥΡΗΜΑΤΑ : - Εκφυλιστική ρήξη και βαθμός υπεξαρθρήματος σημειώνεται στον έσω μηνίσκο. Παρατηρείται μικρή εστία οστεομυελικού οιδήματος στην οφρύ του έσω κνημιαίου κονδύλου στα πλαίσια μικρής έκτασης μικροδοκιδώδους κατάγματος ανεπάρκειας. Στο έσω διαμέρισμα συνυπάρχει σχισμοειδής διάβρωση του αρθρικού χόνδρου στον έσω μηριαίο κόνδυλο. - Ο λοιπός αρθρικός χόνδρος σε έξω και πρόσθιο διαμέρισμα, έχει φυσιολογική απεικόνιση. - Μικρή συλλογή υγρού παρατηρείται ενδαρθρικά σε επικοινωνία με μικρή συνοβιακή κύστη BAKER. - Προεπιγονατιδικά αναγνωρίζεται οίδημα και μικρής έκτασης ορογονοθυλακίτιδα. - Τα συνδεσμικά στοιχεία και ο έξω μηνίσκος απεικονίζονται εντός του φυσιολογικού.

report:
FINDINGS:

Fractures:
Known mildly comminuted undisplaced avulsion fracture of the tibial tuberosity involving the distal ACL insertion, anteriorly the anterior horn root insertion of the lateral meniscus, as well as posteriorly the tibial insertion of both the posterior horn of medial and lateral menisci. The fracture involves the central portion of the medial tibial plateau articular surface anteriorly and posteriorly with articular surface collapse of 3 mm anteriorly and 5 mm posteriorly, as well as a step deformity of up to 2 mm posteriorly.
Small mildly displaced avulsion fracture of the lateral corner of lateral tibial plateau [Segond fracture].
Small mild osteochondral impaction at the anterior lateral weightbearing aspect of lateral femoral condyle.
There is associated bone marrow edema associated with these fractures.

Joint alignment:
Mild widening of the medial femorotibial joint space. Otherwise preserved articular alignment.

Degenerative changes:
None.

Bone marrow signal:
Additional small area of bone marrow edema on the medial side of medial femoral condyle without evidence of associated fracture.

Anterior cruciate ligament: The distal bony avulsion with laxity of the ACL, showing some internal high T2 signal changes compatible with additional low-grade partial ligamentous tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament: Intact with mild laxity.
Medial collateral ligament: Complete tear of the superficial portion at the mid to distal third. Moderate grade partial tear of the deep meniscal femoral and meniscal tibial components with partial meniscocapsular separation of the medial meniscal body.
Lateral collateral ligament complex: Low-grade sprain of the proximal lateral collateral ligament. The other associated structures are intact.

Medial meniscus: Mild nonspecific signal changes of the meniscal body, with evidence of small horizontal oblique tear extending to the femoral surface. No other significant tear. Bony avulsion of the posterior horn root insertion as detailed above.
Lateral meniscus: Mild nonspecific signal changes at the anterior horn compatible with low-grade tearing. Evidence of small Wrisberg rip-type longitudinal tear of the periphery of the posterior horn. Complete tear of the inferior meniscal popliteal fascicle compatible with posterior lateral corner injury. There is a bony avulsion of the anterior horn and posterior horn root insertion sites.

Extensor tendons: Normal.
Patellar retinacula: Moderate grade partial tear of the medial retinaculum.
Pes anserinus: Normal.

Posteromedial and posterolateral corner: Diffuse signal change and mild thickening of the distal semimembranosus tendon compatible with low to moderate grade partial tearing.
Complete tear of the inferior meniscal popliteal fascicle compatible with posterior lateral corner injury.

Joint effusion: Large joint effusion.
Baker cyst: None.

Other significant findings:
None.

CONCLUSION:
*Comminuted mildly displaced avulsion fracture of the tibial spine with mild comminution, including the distal insertion of the ACL, the anterior horn root insertion of the lateral meniscus, and posterior horn root insertion zone of the medial and lateral menisci. Intra-articular fracture extension involving the central portion of the medial tibial plateau with small gap/step as described.
*Small mildly displaced lateral corner fracture of the lateral tibial plateau [Segond fracture].
*Small osteochondral impaction fracture of the lateral corner of lateral femoral condyle.
*High-grade tear of the medial collateral ligament.
*Low-grade partial tear/sprain of the anterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament.
*Additional low-grade tears involving the medial and lateral menisci as described.
*Moderate grade partial tear of the medial patellar retinaculum.
*Posteromedial and posterolateral corner injuries as described.
*Large joint effusion.

Indication: Left knee pain

MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Oblique undersurface tear of the posterior body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extrusion into the meniscotibial recess and reactive marrow edema at the periphery of the medial tibial plateau.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Borderline tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 16 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:


1. Oblique undersurface tear of the posterior body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extrusion into the meniscotibial recess.

2. Small Baker's cyst.

Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
Menisci with preserved morphology and signal, without categorical criteria for an evident tear.
Partial-thickness chondral ulcers of the weight-bearing zone of the femorotibial compartments without secondary bone changes.
Focal full-thickness chondral ulcer at the junction of the lateral facet with the central region of the femoral trochlea.
Partial-thickness chondral ulcers with diffuse distribution of the patella.
No significant joint effusion or popliteal cysts.
Patellar tendon, pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris and iliotibial band within normal limits. Increased signal at the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon, without categorical criteria for tear.
Increased signal of the superolateral aspect of Hoffa's fat pad.
No other relevant findings to note, especially in the popliteal region.
Impression:
Chondropathy grade 4 lesions of the femoral trochlea. Chondropathy grade 2 lesions of the patella and of the weight-bearing zone of the femorotibial compartments.
Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis.
Subtle signs of lateral patellar hyperpressure syndrome.

translation:
MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, STIR, proton density/T2, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
On evaluation of the menisci, the cruciate and collateral ligaments, the articular cartilage, and the bone marrow, no pathological findings are observed.
On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, edema of the prefemoral fat pad is observed, measuring approximately 1.5 cm in transverse diameter at its lateral aspect, as well as lesser extent edema at the superior lateral aspect of Hoffa's fat pad.

CONCLUSION
The findings are consistent with impingement syndrome of the patella and patellar tendon against the femur.

Und Kollateralbänder intakt minimaler Flüssigkeitssaum um das MCL, DD bei geringer Reizung (5/19). translation: Preserved articulation in the left knee joint. Collateral ligaments intact, minimal fluid rim around the MCL, differential diagnosis of mild irritation (5/19). Known, slightly progressive nodular T2 mildly hypointense lesion in the medial recess (3/40 or 7/13), currently measuring 11 x 7 x 9 mm. No significant joint effusion. report:
Na učinjenim sekvencama vide se formirani medijalni i lateralni osteofiti u području kondila tibije i
femura, reducirana debljine zglobne hrskavice femura i patele, izraženije lateralno uz gubitak
širine zglobnog prostora te uz vidljivu fisuru u području medijalnog dijela platoa tibije, što
odgovara osteoartrotskim promjenama.
Također je vidljiva redukcija zglobne hrskavice pokrovnih ploha femoropatelarnog zgloba uz
suženje zglobnog prostora, što odovara osteoartrotskim promjenama.
U oba meniska vide se središnje zone blaže povišenog signala u T2 sekvenci što odgovara
degenerativnim promjenama meniska, bez znakova rupture. Također se vidi ekstruzija lateralnog
meniska koja se djelomično utiskuje u iliotibijalni trakt, uz zadebljanje hvatišta lateralnog
kolateralnog ligemetna u smislu entezopatskih promjena.
Prati se samo tanji snop vlakana prednjeg križnog ligamenta, dig.dg. može odgovarati stanju po
parcijalnoj rupturi ili degenerativnim promjenama.
Vidi se manja količina tekućine u posteriornom dijelu zglobnog prostora te manja količina u
suprapatelarnoj burzi te u infrapatelarnoj burzi uz hvatište patelarnog ligamenta na tuberositas
tibije.
Izmjenjen je intenzitet signala hvatišta tetive m. quadriceps femoris na kranijalni pol patele u
smislu tendinopatskih promjena, kao i intenzitet signala hvatišta patelarnog ligamenta u smislu
entezopatskih promjena.
Nalazi se uredna morfologija i intenziteti signala medaijlnog kolateralnog ligamenta i stražnjeg
križnog ligamenta.
translation:
On the performed sequences, formed medial and lateral osteophytes are seen in the region of the tibial and femoral condyles, with reduced thickness of the articular cartilage of the femur and patella, more pronounced laterally, with loss of joint space width and a visible fissure in the medial portion of the tibial plateau, corresponding to osteoarthritic changes.
There is also reduction of the articular cartilage of the femoropatellar joint surfaces with narrowing of the joint space, corresponding to osteoarthritic changes.
In both menisci, central zones of mildly elevated signal on T2 sequence are seen, corresponding to degenerative meniscal changes, without signs of rupture. Extrusion of the lateral meniscus is also seen, which partially impinges on the iliotibial tract, along with thickening of the insertion of the lateral collateral ligament in the sense of enthesopathic changes.
Only a thinner bundle of fibers of the anterior cruciate ligament is traced; the differential diagnosis may correspond to a state after partial rupture or to degenerative changes.
A small amount of fluid is seen in the posterior part of the joint space, as well as a small amount in the suprapatellar bursa and in the infrapatellar bursa at the insertion of the patellar ligament on the tibial tuberosity.
Altered signal intensity of the insertion of the quadriceps femoris tendon at the cranial pole of the patella is noted, in the sense of tendinopathic changes, as well as altered signal intensity of the insertion of the patellar ligament in the sense of enthesopathic changes.
Normal morphology and signal intensities of the medial collateral ligament and the posterior cruciate ligament are found.

translation:
Clinical History:
Obs. Ruptured Baker's cyst versus gastrocnemius tear.
Findings:
Medullary bone lesion of the distal femoral metaphysis measuring approximately 18 x 12 mm in its longest axes, without signs suggesting local aggressiveness. No other bone marrow signal abnormalities.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
Menisci with preserved morphology and signal, without criteria for tear.
Full-thickness chondral ulcer of the posterior weight-bearing zone of the lateral femoral condyle measuring approximately 5 x 12 mm in its mediolateral and anteroposterior axes respectively.
Superficial chondropathy of the central region of the weight-bearing zone of the medial femoral condyle. The remaining femorotibial and patellofemoral cartilages without alterations.
Mild to moderate joint effusion.
Small popliteal cyst. This is associated with thickening and increased signal of the medial gastrocnemius tendon at its proximal insertion with partial tear at its myotendinous junction with regional partial reparative phenomena. It appears to extend approximately 23 mm in its craniocaudal axis and approximately 7 mm in its largest transverse axis. This is associated with edema of the regional musculature and a mild amount of intermuscular fluid extending cranially and caudally. The remaining regional musculature and tendons without alterations.
Quadriceps tendon, patellar tendon, pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris tendon and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Impression:
Grade 3 chondropathy of the weight-bearing zone of the lateral femoral condyle.
Mild to moderate joint effusion. Small popliteal cyst with probable leakage.
Tendinosis with partial tear of the myotendinous junction of the medial gastrocnemius associated with edema of the musculature and a mild amount of intermuscular fluid extending cranially and caudally.

translation:
Technique: The examination was performed with T1 and proton density sequences with fat signal suppression applied.

Findings:
- A degenerative tear of the medial meniscus is observed with associated subluxation.
- Myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament is identified.
- On evaluation of the lateral meniscus, the posterior cruciate ligament, and the collateral ligaments, no pathological findings are observed.
- Areas of full-thickness and partial-thickness cartilage loss of the medial femoral condyle and the medial tibial condyle are observed, as well as areas of partial-thickness cartilage tear of the medial surface of the patella, 2 and 2.5 mm, in the setting of osteoarthritis. Marginal osteophytes coexist in the medial and lateral compartments.
- On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, a shallow trochlea is noted with an intercondylar angle of 160 degrees and lateral subluxation of the patella.
- Benign hyperplasia of the red marrow element.
- Moderate amount of intra-articular fluid collection, particularly in the suprapatellar bursa.

translation:
TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, PD FS, T2me2d sequences.

FINDINGS:
- Significant narrowing of the lateral compartment is observed, with full-thickness loss of the articular cartilage, presence of marginal osteophytes, as well as loss and fragmentation of the lateral meniscus.
- Lesser degree of narrowing is noted in the medial compartment with accompanying smaller marginal osteophytes.
- Small osteophytes project centrally in the intercondylar notch in contact with the anterior cruciate ligament, which shows thinning of its fibers, without however evidence of tear.
- Subchondral erosions are also revealed in the cartilage of the patella.
- Significant amount of intra-articular effusion as well as presence of a large Baker's cyst, with a cephalocaudal dimension of 6.3 cm, extending cephalad anterior to the semimembranosus muscle with multicystic character.
- Numerous nodular free bodies of bony texture coexist intra-articularly, as well as within the Baker's cyst.
- The collateral ligaments and the cruciate ligament appear normal, as well as the medial meniscus.

CONCLUSION: Extensive degenerative changes mainly in the lateral compartment and to a lesser degree in the medial compartment and in the patellofemoral articulation, with accompanying secondary osteochondromatosis.

Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Bone marrow edema at the lateral femoral condyle and anterior medial tibial plateau, consistent with osseous contusions. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

Trace joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: High grade fissure medial tibial plateau. 

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss with full-thickness fissuring at the central trochlea. High-grade fissure median ridge and and medial facet with delamination.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Osseous contusions at the lateral femoral condyle and anterior medial tibial plateau.
2.	Moderate patellofemoral and mild medial compartment chondrosis.

Edema signal and fraying of the popliteus muscle (5/29).

report: Diz eklemindeki trikompartmantal dejeneratif eklem hastalığı medyal femoral tibyal kompartmanda en belirgin ve tam kata ulaşan eklem kıkırdağı kaybı ve dejenerasyonu, subkondral medüller fibrokistik ve fibrovasküler değişiklikler ve marjinal osteofitlerle karakterize. Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı hafif derecede artmış. Ön çapraz bağda mukoid dejenerasyon. Arka çapraz ve yan bağlar normal. Tibyal platonun lateralinde eklem yüzeyinde 2 mm çökmeye neden olmuş kırığı yaygın kemik iliği ödemi çevreliyor. Tibyal platonun mediyalindeki subkondral kırık kemik iliği ödemi ile birlikte. Fibula başındaki nondeplase inkomplet kırığı kemik iliği ödemi çevreliyor. Mediyal menisküsün arka kökünde tam kat yırtık izleniyor. Mediyal menisküsün gövdesindeki ve arka boynuzundaki üst ve alt eklem yüzeylerine ulaşan kompleks dejeneratif yırtık arka boynuzda doku kaybı ile birlikte. Lateral menisküsün arka boynuzunda alt eklem yüzeyiyle ilişkilenen horizontal oblik yırtık ve serbest kenarda gövdede radyal yırtık izleniyor. Prepatellar cilt altı bağ dokusu ödemli. Ekstensör mekanizma korunmuş.
translation: Tricompartmental degenerative joint disease of the knee, most prominent in the medial femorotibial compartment, characterized by full-thickness articular cartilage loss and degeneration, subchondral medullary fibrocystic and fibrovascular changes, and marginal osteophytes. The intra-articular fluid volume in the knee joint is mildly increased. Mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate and collateral ligaments are normal. A fracture of the lateral tibial plateau causing 2 mm depression of the articular surface is surrounded by extensive bone marrow edema. Subchondral fracture of the medial tibial plateau with bone marrow edema. A nondisplaced incomplete fracture of the fibular head is surrounded by bone marrow edema. A full-thickness tear is seen at the posterior root of the medial meniscus. A complex degenerative tear in the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus, reaching both the superior and inferior articular surfaces, with tissue loss in the posterior horn. A horizontal oblique tear communicating with the inferior articular surface in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, and a radial tear at the free edge in the body are seen. The prepatellar subcutaneous connective tissue is edematous. The extensor mechanism is intact.

report: SAĞ DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Medial menisküs posterior hornunda grade III dejenerasyon ve horizontal yırtık ile uyumlu sinyal değişiklikleri izlenmektedir. Medial menisküs ekstrüde izlendi. Lateral menisküs normaldir. Ön çapraz bağ ve arka çapraz bağ  normaldir. Lateral kollateral ligaman doğaldır. Medial  kollateral ligaman çevresinde hafif sıvı artışı izlendi(grade I sprain).Prepateller düzeyde cilt altı yağlı dokuda belirgin ödematöz değişiklikler, sinyal artışları izlenmektedir. Patellar kemik doğaldır. Pateller kıkırdakta yer yer hafif incelmeler  izlenmektedir (Tip II kondromalazi). Patellar tendonda tendinozis bulguları mevcuttur.Lateral ve medial reseslerde sıvı artışı izlendi.Lateral retinakulumda  sinyal artışı mevcuttur. Femur medial kondil düzeyinde  kemik iliği ödemi ve bu düzeyde subkondral milimetrik kistler izlenmektedir. Diz eklemini çevreleyen komşu kemik yapılarda osteofitik sivrileşmeler , eklem mesafesinde azalma izlendi. Ayrıca femoral ve tibial kartilajlarda yer yer incelme ve bütünlük kaybı subkondral skleroz izlendi(dejeneratif artrit bulguları).
translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Signal changes consistent with grade III degeneration and horizontal tear are observed in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. The medial meniscus appears extruded. The lateral meniscus is normal. The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament are normal. The lateral collateral ligament is normal. Mild fluid increase is observed around the medial collateral ligament (grade I sprain). Marked edematous changes and signal increases are observed in the subcutaneous fatty tissue at the prepatellar level. The patellar bone is normal. Mild thinning is observed in places in the patellar cartilage (Type II chondromalacia). Findings of tendinosis are present in the patellar tendon. Fluid increase is observed in the lateral and medial recesses. Signal increase is present in the lateral retinaculum. Bone marrow edema at the level of the medial femoral condyle and subchondral millimetric cysts at this level are observed. Osteophytic spurs in the adjacent bone structures surrounding the knee joint and joint space narrowing were observed. Additionally, thinning and loss of integrity in places in the femoral and tibial cartilages, and subchondral sclerosis were observed (findings of degenerative arthritis).

Μικρότερης έκτασης οίδηµα αναγνωρίζεται επίσης και στον έξω µηριαίο και κνηµιαίο κόνδυλο. - Σηµειώνεται οίδηµα ιγνυακού µυός. - Μέτρια συλλογή υγρού αναγνωρίζεται ενδοαρθρικά. - Από τον έλεγχο του εκτατικού µηχανισµού και του αρθρικού χόνδρου δεν αναγνωρίζονται παθολογικά ευρήµατα. - Υποδόριο οίδηµα, πιο έκδηλο στην έσω πλευρά του γόνατος. Συµπερασµα: Μετατραυµατικά ευρήµατα κάκωσης οπίσθιας-έξω γωνίας του γόνατος (PLC) µε αποσπαστικό κάταγµα κεφαλής περόνης, µερική ρήξη πρόσθιου χιαστού, ρήξη ιγνυοπερονικού συνδέσµου, θλάση ιγνυακού µυός και οστικούς µώλωπες.
translation:
TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
- An avulsion fracture of the fibular head is noted, with cranial displacement of the head and its attached anatomical structures (biceps femoris muscle and lateral collateral ligament) by 2.5 cm, with accompanying edema of the surrounding soft tissues. The popliteofibular ligament is not identified.
- Pathological signal with accompanying small intraligamentous tears is identified in the inferior portion of the anterior cruciate ligament.
- Degeneration of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus is observed.
- The lateral meniscus, the posterior cruciate ligament, and the medial collateral ligament are within normal limits.
- Bone marrow edema, in the context of post-traumatic bone bruises, is identified in the anterior medial tibial plateau and condyle as well as in the opposing medial femoral condyle and epicondyle. Lesser extent edema is also identified in the lateral femoral and tibial condyle.
- Edema of the popliteus muscle is noted.
- A moderate intra-articular fluid collection is identified.
- On evaluation of the extensor mechanism and the articular cartilage, no pathological findings are identified.
- Subcutaneous edema, more prominent on the medial side of the knee.

CONCLUSION
Post-traumatic findings of posterolateral corner (PLC) injury of the knee with avulsion fracture of the fibular head, partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, tear of the popliteofibular ligament, popliteus muscle contusion, and bone bruises.

report:
MRI LEFT KNEE

INDICATION: Assess for ligamentous injury post trauma 


Routine MRI of the left knee shows focal degenerative signal in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with faint extension to the inferior articular surface consistent with nondisplaced tear. No lateral meniscal tear. ACL and PCL are intact. Extensor mechanism intact. Collateral ligaments are intact.

No joint effusion. No Baker's cyst. There is slight chondrosis in the medial tibial plateau with no underlying bony edema. Moderate chondrosis in the lateral tibial plateau with no underlying bony edema. No full-thickness cartilage defects. Patellofemoral joint shows focal severe chondrosis at the apex of the trochlear groove.

IMPRESSION:

Focal degenerative signal in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with tiny inferior surfacing tear, nondisplaced. No lateral meniscal tear. No ligament tear.

Cartilage thinning in the medial lateral tibial plateaus. Tiny focus of severe chondrosis at the apex of the trochlea with 2 mm underlying subchondral edema.

translation:
TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
- On evaluation of the structures of the posterolateral corner of the knee, bone marrow edema is noted in the fibular head, with accompanying fluid and fracture lines.
- Increased signal and disruption of the fiber architecture of the anterior cruciate ligament are noted at the level of its insertion on the intercondylar notch of the femur.
- Edema is also identified around the medial collateral ligament at the femoral insertion.
- A small joint effusion is observed intra-articularly.
- The popliteofibular ligament, lateral collateral ligament, and posterior cruciate ligament are intact without evidence of tear.
- No pathological findings from the evaluation of the medial and lateral meniscus.
- The articular cartilage is within normal limits.
- No significant pathological findings are observed from the evaluation of the extensor mechanism.
- Benign bone marrow hyperplasia.

CONCLUSION
Findings of posterolateral corner injury, with multifocal fracture of the fibular head without signs of healing and partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. Medial collateral ligament injury (sprain grade I).

4. Mild synovitis and joint effusion in right knee; large Baker's cyst with mild perifocal edema.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

- In the medial compartment, the only finding noted is the presence of small marginal osteophytes of the femoral condyle.

- On evaluation of the anterior compartment, small bone marrow edema is observed in the lateral facet of the patella accompanied by loss of the overlying articular cartilage (ICRS Grade IV), with coexisting bone marrow edema in the corresponding area of the lateral femoral condyle.
- The collateral and cruciate ligaments appear normal.
- A moderate amount of fluid is observed, associated with a Baker's cyst of craniocaudal diameter 3.2 cm adjacent to the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle.
- Mild edema is observed in the subcutaneous fat anterior to the patellar tendon, without clinical significance.

CONCLUSION
Degenerative osteoarthritis of the lateral patellofemoral compartment.

report:

Indication: 64-year-old with progressive left knee pain related to "wear and tear". Evaluate for cartilage loss. Evaluate for meniscus tear.
Comparison: No recent left lower extremity imaging available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee is acquired in 3 anatomic planes at 1.2 Tesla using a local extremity receiver coil and a noncontrast protocol.

FINDINGS:

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Osseous and articular alignment at the left knee are normal.
No fracture. No focal osseous contusion.
No evidence for a recent pivot shift mechanism.

JOINT SPACE:
There is a small left knee effusion.
There is a minimal, partially ruptured Baker's cyst.
No intra-articular bodies.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a complex tear of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with a dominant oblique undersurface component and a smaller inner margin radial component at the junction posterior horn and posterior root. There is moderate subsequent medial meniscus extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss all along the weightbearing region of the medial femoral condyle, with focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial femoral margin.
There is partial-thickness cartilage loss at the medial tibial margin.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: The lateral meniscus shows normal morphology and signal with no tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage throughout the lateral tibiofemoral compartment is normal.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
There is a small region of focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the patellar median ridge, with more diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss extending along the medial patellar facet.
There is diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss with deep chondral fissuring at the central femoral trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal morphology and signal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): The MCL is bowed from medial meniscus extrusion, but intact.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: The fibular-collateral ligament and anterolateral ligament are normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Intact stabilizers.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Moderate degenerative hypertrophic distal quadriceps tendinopathy, with intrasubstance degeneration at its patellar attachment and mild enthesopathy. No high-grade quadriceps tear.
Patella tendon: Normal morphology and signal with no tear or degeneration.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No significant soft tissue edema in Hoffa's fat.
A TT-TG distance is normal at 7 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
The distal iliotibial band and biceps femoris are normal.
The distal semimembranosus is normal.

SOFT TISSUES:
Neurovascular structures in the popliteal fossa are normal.
Subcutaneous soft tissues are normal. No soft tissue mass.

IMPRESSION:

1. Extensive complex medial meniscus tear with a dominant oblique undersurface component at its body and posterior horn, moderate medial meniscus extrusion, and high-grade cartilage loss on the medial femoral condyle with low-grade cartilage loss at the medial tibial margin.

2. Focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the patellar median ridge with high-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss at the central femoral trochlea.

3. Moderate degenerative hypertrophic distal quadriceps tendinopathy, with mild enthesopathy.

4. Small left knee effusion with a minimal ruptured Baker's cyst.

translation:
MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

Technique: The examination was performed with T1, PD fs, and T2* pulse sequences.

Findings:
- Presence of a small amount of intra-articular fluid collection.
- There is significant narrowing of the medial compartment joint space, with complete loss of articular cartilage and extensive architectural disruption of the medial meniscus (meniscal maceration). The lateral meniscus shows diffusely increased signal, likely in the context of degeneration.
- Normal appearance of the cruciate and collateral ligaments.
- Bone marrow edema is observed in the lateral tibial condyle, likely in the context of an insufficiency reaction (without clear evidence of fracture) or traumatic origin (correlation with clinical history).
- On evaluation of the patellofemoral joint, architectural disruption of the trochlear cartilage is identified, with thinning and focal defect in the lateral aspect, and correspondingly in the central aspect of the patella, with subchondral cysts at the same level (Grade II and IV respectively).

CONCLUSION: Findings consistent with severe knee osteoarthritis.

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]

MRI OF THE LEFT KNEE

Technique: The examination was performed with T1, PD fs, and T2* pulse sequences.

Findings:
- Presence of intra-articular fluid collection, predominantly in the medial compartment of the joint, with an accompanying Baker's cyst measuring 6 cm in craniocaudal dimension.
- There is narrowing of the medial compartment joint space, with significant thinning-loss of articular cartilage, severe degeneration of the medial meniscus, architectural disruption and extrusion thereof. A region of bone marrow edema is also observed in the medial femoral condyle, in the subarticular portion of the medial tibial condyle, as well as several subarticular cysts in the posterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle. A small bony structure is noted at the medial supracondylar ridge, as in secondary osteochondromatosis.
- Increased signal and thickening of the insertion of the semimembranosus and semitendinosus tendons are observed, in the context of degeneration.
- On evaluation of the lateral meniscus, cruciate ligaments, and collateral ligaments, no significant pathological findings are identified.
- On evaluation of the patellofemoral joint, architectural disruption of the trochlear cartilage is identified, with thinning and focal defect in the lateral aspect, thickness >50% (Grade III).

CONCLUSION: Findings consistent with severe knee osteoarthritis.

report:
FINDINGS:

There is a small knee joint effusion with no popliteal cysts.

There are moderate degenerative changes in the medial compartment with moderate cartilage thinning most pronounced at the central weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau. There is diffuse mild thinning and superficial fraying in the lateral and patellofemoral compartments. There are no regions of full-thickness cartilage loss.

There is intrasubstance degeneration involving the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a longitudinal oblique tear involving the posterior horn extending to the inferior articular surface. There is an intra and para meniscal cyst at the level of the posterior root. There is no displaced meniscal fragment. The lateral meniscus is unremarkable.

Otherwise the anterior cruciate ligament, the posterior cruciate ligament, the extensor mechanism, the medial collateral ligament, the pes anserine tendons, the semimembranosus, the popliteus, the distal biceps femoris, the lateral collateral ligament and the IT band are unremarkable.

CONCLUSION:

1. Mild to moderate degenerative changes most pronounced in the medial compartment as detailed above. No evidence of intra-articular body.

2. Intrasubstance degeneration of the medial meniscus with an oblique tear and para meniscal cyst. No displaced meniscal fragment.

3. Knee joint effusion with no popliteal cysts.

report:
COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Medial and anterior pain left knee. Large effusion. Locking. Suspected medial meniscal tear.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The lateral meniscus is intact. Inferiorly surfacing oblique tear posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus, which is peripherally extruded. There is a flipped meniscal fragment in the medial meniscal tibial recess, measuring 12 x 3 x 6 mm. The medial meniscal posterior root and anterior horn are intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

Medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, and fibular collateral ligament are intact. There is strain/low-grade partial thickness tear of the popliteus muscle and proximal to the musculotendinous junction. The popliteus tendon at the lateral femoral condylar insertion shows mild tendinosis without tear. The biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. Iliotibial band is intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 9 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Preserved medial and lateral femorotibial articular cartilage. Preserved patellofemoral articular cartilage. Trace knee joint fluid. Tiny Baker's cyst. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Inferiorly dissecting oblique tear posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with flipped 12 x 3 x 6 mm meniscal fragment in the medial meniscal tibial recess and medial meniscal extrusion.
2. Strain/low-grade partial-thickness tear of the popliteus muscle as well as popliteus insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.

translation:
LEFT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior and posterior horns and body of the lateral meniscus. Grade III degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. Signal change consistent with tendinosis is observed at the proximal insertion level of the medial crus of the gastrocnemius. A 1 cm diameter cyst is observed in the subchondral area of the posterior medial tibial plateau. The distal quadriceps is normal. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Edema in the subchondral area and significant cartilage thinning are observed at the lateral patellar facet. Increased fluid is observed in the pes anserine bursa. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Joint space narrowing and osteophytic spurring at the corners of the bony structures adjacent to the joint are observed in the medial tibiofemoral joint. Cartilage thinning is observed at the femoral and tibial levels at this level, more pronounced at the tibial level.
CONCLUSION: Gonarthrosis. Grade III meniscopathy in the medial meniscus, grade II meniscopathy in the lateral meniscus. Myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. Grade II chondromalacia of the lateral patellar facet. Suprapatellar bursitis, pes anserine bursitis. Tendinosis of the medial crus of the gastrocnemius.

Lateral menisküste korpus ön boynuz bileşkesinde üst eklem yüzeyi ile ilişkili yırtık izlenmektedir. Bu düzeyde apekste bir miktar küntleşme de vardır. Arka boynuzda  sadece milimetrik radial yırtık izlenmektedir. Yan bağlar normaldir. Arka çapraz bağ normaldir. Ön çapraz bağ rüptüre görünümdedir. Anterior liflerde ödematöz sinyal değişiklikleri vardır. Lateral femorotibial eklem yüzlerinde fokal kondral milimetrik kayıplar, kondral ödem alanları subkobdral hafif ödematöz fokal sinyal değişiklikleri izlenmektedir. Medial femorotibial eklemde femoral tarafta yüzeyel kondral kayıp subkondral hafif ödematöz sinyal değişiklikleri kondral fissür oluşumları izlenmektedir. Popliteus tendonu intraartiküler parçasında tendonozis vardır. Patellofemoral eklem pateller taraf lateral fasette yüzeyel kondral kayıp  bu lokalizasyonda fibrilasyon vardır .Medialde fokal kondral ödem izlenmektedir. Troklear tarafta  interkondiler sulkus düzeyinde ve  medial kondil anteriorunda yüzeyel kondral kayıplar, kondral hafif ödematöz sinyal değişiklikleri izlenmektedir. translation: There is mild intra-articular effusion in the knee joint. The extensor mechanism is normal. There is deep infrapatellar bursitis. There is a superior and medial patellar plica. There is no significant interposition of the medial plica into the patellofemoral joint space. The medial meniscus is normal. A tear involving the superior articular surface is seen at the body–anterior horn junction of the lateral meniscus. There is also some blunting at the apex at this level. Only a millimetric radial tear is seen in the posterior horn. The collateral ligaments are normal. The posterior cruciate ligament is normal. The anterior cruciate ligament appears ruptured. There are edematous signal changes in the anterior fibers. Focal millimetric chondral losses, areas of chondral edema, and mild subchondral edematous focal signal changes are seen on the lateral femorotibial joint surfaces. Superficial chondral loss, mild subchondral edematous signal changes, and chondral fissure formations are seen on the femoral side of the medial femorotibial joint. There is tendinosis in the intra-articular portion of the popliteus tendon. There is superficial chondral loss on the lateral facet of the patellar side of the patellofemoral joint, with fibrillation at this location. Focal chondral edema is seen medially. Superficial chondral losses and mild chondral edematous signal changes are seen on the trochlear side at the level of the intercondylar sulcus and anterior to the medial condyle. There is a Baker's cyst in the popliteal fossa.

translation: The amount of intra-articular fluid in the knee joint is normal. The cruciate and collateral ligaments are normal. The medial and lateral menisci are normal. A fibrosclerotic lesion with a 3 mm diameter intraosseous bone island is seen in the proximal tibial metaphysis. Mild-degree medial femorotibial joint osteoarthritis characterized by focal thinning reaching 50% of the cartilage thickness in the weight-bearing portion of the femoral condyle. The articular cartilages and bones are otherwise normal. The extensor mechanism is intact. The proximal tibiofibular joint is normal.

report: МР находка: МР данни за дегенеративна промяна и лезия на на латералния менискус. Латералният менискус е с висок интензитет на сигнала. В него се вижда хиперинтензна линия с кос ход, съответстваща на скъсване. Засегнати са предният рог и средната трета на менискуса. Предният рог на латералния менискус е фрагментиран, като част от него е изместен встрани от ставната междина. Свързана с предния рог на менискуса се изобразява мултилокуларна киста с големина 20/8мм. В тибията, до залавното място на предната кръстна връзка също се намира малка киста, вероятно свързана с описаната по-голяма киста до менискуса. Осколо субхондралната киста в тибията се визуализира отграничен едем на костния мозък. МР данни за дегенеративна промяна и скъсване в задния рог на медиалния менискус. Скъсването достига до зания край на менискуса и до ставния хрущял на тибията. Ставният хрущял та фемора и на тибията е запазен. Изобразява се малък дефект в ставния хрущял на пателата – 3-та степен.  Кръстните връзки са със запазена цялост и сигнална характеристика. Колатерални лигаменти – без особености. Пателарен лигамент и двата ретинакулума са с нормално представяне. Сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис – без особености. Поплитеална ямк а – б.о. Наличие на малък ставен излив. Заключение:  МР данни за дегенеративна промяна и лезия на латералния менискус. Предният рог на латералния менискус е фрагментиран. МР данни за мултилокуларна киста, свързана с предния рог на латералния менискус. Лезия на задния рог на медиалния менискус– 3b степен. Хондромалация на пателата – 3-та степен. Малък ставен излив.
translation: MRI findings: MRI findings of degenerative change and lesion of the lateral meniscus. The lateral meniscus shows high signal intensity. A hyperintense oblique line is seen within it, corresponding to a tear. The anterior horn and the middle third of the meniscus are affected. The anterior horn of the lateral meniscus is fragmented, with part of it displaced laterally from the joint space. A multilocular cyst measuring 20/8 mm is seen in association with the anterior horn of the meniscus. A small cyst is also found in the tibia, near the insertion site of the anterior cruciate ligament, likely related to the larger cyst described near the meniscus. Around the subchondral cyst in the tibia, circumscribed bone marrow edema is visualized. MRI findings of degenerative change and tear in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. The tear extends to the posterior edge of the meniscus and to the articular cartilage of the tibia. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia is preserved. A small defect is seen in the articular cartilage of the patella – grade 3. The cruciate ligaments are intact with preserved signal characteristics. Collateral ligaments – unremarkable. The patellar ligament and both retinacula appear normal. Quadriceps femoris tendon – unremarkable. Popliteal fossa – unremarkable. Small joint effusion is present. Conclusion: MRI findings of degenerative change and lesion of the lateral meniscus. The anterior horn of the lateral meniscus is fragmented. MRI findings of a multilocular cyst associated with the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus. Lesion of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 3b. Chondromalacia of the patella – grade 3. Small joint effusion.

Fabella.

translation:
MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
In the lateral compartment of the knee, large marginal osteophytes are observed without significant erosion of the articular cartilage. The lateral meniscus is normal.

In the medial compartment of the knee, severe degenerative osteoarthritis is observed with erosion of the articular cartilage of the femoral and tibial condyle respectively (ICRS grade 4) and accompanying degenerative tear and extrusion of the medial meniscus. Presence of marginal osteophytes as well as multiple ganglion cysts proximal to the joint space with anteroposterior diameter of 2.5 cm and craniocaudal diameter of 2.5 cm.

In the anterior compartment, presence of osteophytosis and mild erosion of the articular cartilage of the patella is noted.

Emphasis is placed on the presence of newly formed bony projections in the intercondylar notch. It is considered likely that the presence of these proliferative structures is responsible for the chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament and the myxoid degeneration of the distal half of the posterior cruciate ligament.

A small joint effusion is observed in the knee joint in communication with a Baker's synovial cyst.

The bone marrow shows benign hyperplasia in the distal femoral metadiaphysis.

translation: LEFT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: There is a horizontal tear extending from the posterior horn to the body of the medial meniscus. report:

2. Synovitis of right knee and patellar plicae.
3. Grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration.

Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

report:

There is a mild superficial chondrosis at the lateral patellar facet (9-35) and less pronounced at the medial patellar facet. 1. No acute meniscal or ligamentous injury.
2. Mild superficial patellar chondrosis, with a small focus full thickness cartilage denuding medial patellar facet.

report:
Zentrierte Stellung im rechten Kniegelenk. Zentrierte Stellung der Patella. Fokal tief greifende Chondropathie retropatellar am Patellafirst (4/17). Korrespondierend fokal tief greifende Chondropathie des femoralen Gelenkknorpels am Retropatellargelenk (4/20). Vollschichtige langstreckige Chondropathie am medialen Gelenkspalt mit nahezu vollständig aufgebrauchtem Knorpelbesatz femorotibial (5/22). Kniegelenkserguss im Recessus suprapatellaris. Intakte Darstellung der Quadrizeps- sowie Patellasehne.
Intakte Darstellung des Faserverlaufes des vorderen und hinteren Kreuzbandes, unauffällige Signalgebung. 11 mm messender kalzifizierter freier Gelenkkörper im vorderen Kniegelenkspalt (6/20). Osteophytäre Randausziehungen des Tibiaplateaus sowie der Femurkondyle am medialen und lateralen Gelenkspalt, jedoch betont medial. Medial betonte Gelenkspaltverschmälerung.
Komplexer Lappenriss des Innenmeniskus mit Beteiligung des Vorderhornes(7/14), Substanzdefekt der Pars intermedia und Auslaufen bis an das Hinterhorn ohne abgrenzbare Verletzung der Hinterwurzel; Keine Hernierung/Luxation von Meniskus-Anteilen, laterale noch schmale Pars intermedia (6/8). Mukoide Degeneration des Außenmeniskusvorderhornes und geringer des Hinterhornes ohne Rissbildung.
Im suprapatellaren Recessus fettisointense Proliferationen an der Synovia (3/27, 4/13).
translation:
Centered alignment of the right knee joint. Centered position of the patella. Focal deep chondropathy retropatellar at the patellar ridge (4/17). Corresponding focal deep chondropathy of the femoral articular cartilage at the retropatellar joint (4/20). Full-thickness long-segment chondropathy at the medial joint space with nearly completely depleted cartilage femorotibially (5/22). Knee joint effusion in the suprapatellar recess. Intact appearance of the quadriceps and patellar tendons.
Intact fiber course of the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments, unremarkable signal intensity. 11 mm calcified loose body in the anterior knee joint space (6/20). Osteophytic marginal spurs of the tibial plateau and femoral condyles at the medial and lateral joint space, but predominantly medial. Medially predominant joint space narrowing.
Complex flap tear of the medial meniscus with involvement of the anterior horn (7/14), substance defect of the pars intermedia and extension to the posterior horn without definable injury of the posterior root; no herniation/dislocation of meniscal portions, laterally still narrow pars intermedia (6/8). Mucoid degeneration of the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus and to a lesser degree of the posterior horn without tear.
Fat-isointense proliferations of the synovium in the suprapatellar recess (3/27, 4/13).

report: Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı hafif derecede artmış. Diz eklemindeki bikompartmantal osteoartrit patellofemoral > medyal femoral tibyal eklemlerde izlenmekte olup, medyal patellar fasetteki ve medyal femoral kondilin ağırlık taşıyan yüzeyindeki kondral kalınlığın %50'sini aşan fokal incelme subkondral fibrovasküler değişiklikler ve milimetrik çaplı marjinal osteofitlerle karakterize. Lateral menisküs ön boynuzu-gövdesindeki dejenerasyon üst ve alt eklem yüzeyleri ile ilişkilenen kompleks dejeneratif yırtık ve parameniskal alandaki (menisküsü anteriyor ve lateralden çevreleyen kalınlığı 3-4 mm olan) kistlerle birlikte. Medyal menisküste ön boynuz - gövdesi ve arka boynuzu düzeyindeki dejeneratif yapı içi intensite artışı üst ve alt eklem yüzleri ile ilişkilenen esas olarak gövdesi ve arka boynuza lokalize kompleks dejeneratif yırtıklarla birlikte. İç yan bağın derin bileşenleri ödemli. Çapraz ve yan bağlar bunun dışında korunmuş. Kuadriseps yağ yastığında minimal ödem izleniyor. Semimembranozus tendonozisi insersiyon düzeyinde hafif-orta dereceli. Proksimal tibyofibuler eklem çevresinde büyüğü 1 cm çapa ulaşan gangliyon kistleri mevcut. Ekstensör mekanizma korunmuş (kuadriseps tendonu ve patellar tendon, patella ve yerleşimi, femoral troklear oluk ve patellofemoral bağlar normal). Diz eklemini çevreleyen kaslar atrofik.
translation: The amount of intra-articular fluid in the knee joint is mildly increased. Bicompartmental osteoarthritis of the knee joint is observed in the patellofemoral > medial femorotibial compartments, characterized by focal thinning exceeding 50% of the cartilage thickness on the medial patellar facet and the weight-bearing surface of the medial femoral condyle, subchondral fibrovascular changes, and millimeter-sized marginal osteophytes. Degeneration in the anterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus with a complex degenerative tear communicating with the superior and inferior articular surfaces, and cysts in the parameniscal area (surrounding the meniscus anteriorly and laterally, 3–4 mm in thickness). Degenerative intrasubstance signal intensity increase at the level of the anterior horn, body, and posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with complex degenerative tears communicating with the superior and inferior articular surfaces, predominantly localized to the body and posterior horn. The deep components of the medial collateral ligament are edematous. The cruciate and collateral ligaments are otherwise intact. Minimal edema is observed in the quadriceps fat pad. Semimembranosus tendinosis, mild to moderate at the insertion level. Ganglion cysts are present around the proximal tibiofibular joint, the largest reaching 1 cm in diameter. The extensor mechanism is intact (quadriceps tendon and patellar tendon, patella and its position, femoral trochlear groove, and patellofemoral ligaments are normal). The muscles surrounding the knee joint are atrophic.

There is a moderate knee joint effusion with a tiny popliteal cysts.

There are mild degenerative changes involving the patellofemoral and lateral compartment with moderate degenerative changes in the medial compartment. CONCLUSION:

1. Mild to moderate degenerative changes most pronounced in the medial compartment.
2. Intrasubstance degeneration of the medial meniscus with associated longitudinal horizontal tear and displaced flap component as detailed above.
3. Knee joint effusion with tiny popliteal cyst.

translation:
LEFT KNEE MRI

Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.

Findings:
The medial meniscus is mildly extruded medially by 4 mm from the knee joint. Grade III degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of the meniscus. The lateral meniscus is normal. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Periligamentous edema is observed in the medial collateral ligament. Diffuse fluid increase is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Joint space narrowing is observed in the medial compartment of the tibiofemoral joint. Subarticular fracture and signal change consistent with bone marrow edema are observed in the medial femoral condyle adjacent to the joint. Thinning of the femoral and tibial cartilages is observed. A Baker's cyst measuring 8.5 x 2 cm is observed in the popliteal fossa.

CONCLUSION: Mild gonarthrosis, subarticular fracture in the medial femoral condyle and bone marrow edema diffusely involving the medial condyle. Grade III meniscopathy in the medial meniscus. Myxoid degeneration in the anterior cruciate ligament. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Suprapatellar bursitis, synovitis of the knee joint. Baker's cyst in the popliteal fossa.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Minimal reactive subchondral bone marrow edema is present at the peripheral margin of the medial tibiofemoral compartment, related to adjacent meniscal tear. A small, 8 mm enchondroma is incidentally noted within the distal femoral metaphysis anteriorly. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. There is evidence of a 9 x 9 x 2 mm intra-articular body in the anterior tibiofemoral joint recess. Minimal, ruptured Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is tearing of the inner margin along the body and posterior horn. Evidence of a small tear at the posterior root attachment. Mild extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Cartilage appears intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Cartilage appears intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is mild cartilage fissuring at the medial patellar facet. Otherwise, cartilage appears intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Medial meniscal tear with mild extrusion.

2. Mild patellar chondrosis.

3. Evidence of an intra-articular body in the anterior tibiofemoral joint recess.

4. Moderate joint effusion. Minimal, ruptured Baker cyst.

report:
MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Instability.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact. There is patella alta with the Insall Salvati ratio measuring 1.38.

Patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable.

The TT-TG distance measures about 1 cm, within normal limits. Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint demonstrates mild chondral fraying inferiorly consistent with moderate chondrosis. Articular cartilage of the femoral trochlea is well-maintained.
There is edema within the infrapatellar fat pad laterally. This finding may be seen in extensor mechanism impingement.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including IT band, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus tendon and biceps femoris tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is no evidence of a significant Baker's cyst. No evidence of a significant knee effusion.

Marrow signal is within normal limits.

INTERPRETATION: 

Patella alta with moderate chondromalacia patella. There is also edema in Hoffa's fat inferior to the patella laterally compatible with the extensor mechanism impingement.

There is no evidence of internal derangement.

[DATE]: MRI Left Knee

Clinical information: Hyperextension trauma left knee, McMurray medially painful.

Diagnostic question: Meniscal injury? Other?

Findings:
Limited bone edema anteriorly on the medial femoral condyle, just medial to the medial facet of the trochlea, with increased T2 signal, relatively poorly defined, with a maximum diameter of approximately 2 cm, mildly T1 hypointense with possibly some linear T1 hypointense elements and contusion, possibly a non-displaced fracture.
Minimal distension of the suprapatellar recess, nonspecific.
Quadriceps and patellar tendon, normal appearance.
Undulated appearance of the anterior cruciate ligament, with fanning out of the proximal fibers and loss of parallelism to Blumensaat's line.
At least partial desinsertion of the proximal medial gastrocnemius insertion on top of the medial femoral condyle, with local fluid accumulation against the cortex, T2 hyperintense, with dimensions 4 x 9–10 x 4 mm, accompanied by very extensive hemorrhagic changes along the neurovascular axis and around the medial gastrocnemius; the gastrocnemius itself with completely normal signal.
Normal appearance of the menisci.
Lateral ligaments intact.

Conclusion:
Distortion of the left knee with:
- At least partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament;
- Partial desinsertion of the medial gastrocnemius head insertion on top of the medial femoral condyle.

translation:
MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

Technique: The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences after application of fat signal suppression.

Findings:
A degenerative tear of the body of the medial meniscus is observed with subluxation of it. In the medial compartment there are coexisting marginal osteophytes and erosion of the articular cartilage in the setting of mild osteoarthritis. On evaluation of the lateral meniscus, the cruciate ligaments and the collateral ligaments, no pathological findings are observed. In the patellofemoral compartment, areas of erosion of the articular cartilage of the patella are identified. Specifically, a superficial tear along the midline (ICRS I), and a linear tear of 1 mm thickness on the medial articular surface (ICRS III). On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, prepatellar edema in the subcutaneous tissue is observed. The bone marrow is evaluated with normal signal intensity. A moderate amount of intra-articular effusion is observed with extension into a Baker's cyst of craniocaudal diameter ~6 cm in the medial popliteal fossa.

report: МР находка: Няма МР данни за ставен излив. МР данни за едемни промени на лигамента на пателата. Същият е с дифузно повишен сигнален интензитет в PDW SPAIR секвенцията на протежение от около 15 мм. Няма МР данни за скъсване на пателарния лигамент. Нормално изобразяване на сухожилието на m. quadriceps femoris. Костите, формиращи дясната колянна става са с нормална форма и сигнална характеристика. Артикулиращият хрущял на бедрената кост и тибията е със запазена цялост. Патела, хрущял на пателата – б.о. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. Визуализира се лезия в задния рог на медиалния менискус. Лезията е с хоризонтален ход, като достига на единичен срез до тибиалната ставна повърност. Нормално изобразяване на предния рог на медиалния менискус. Предната и задната кръстна връзка са интактни. Колатерални лигаменти, ретинакулуми – нормално изобразяване. Не се изобразяват патологични изменения в скенираните мускулни групи. Поплитеална ямка – наличие на фабела и малка Бекерова киста. Заключение: МР данни за възпаление на лигамента на пателата /Jumper’s knee/. Парциална увреда на задния рог на медиален менискус – grade 2b. Малка Бекерова киста.
translation: MRI findings: No MRI evidence of joint effusion. MRI evidence of edematous changes of the patellar ligament. It shows diffusely increased signal intensity on the PDW SPAIR sequence over a length of approximately 15 mm. No MRI evidence of tear of the patellar ligament. Normal appearance of the quadriceps femoris tendon. The bones forming the right knee joint are of normal shape and signal characteristics. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia is intact. Patella, patellar cartilage – unremarkable. Normal appearance of the lateral meniscus. A lesion is visualized in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. The lesion has a horizontal course, reaching the tibial articular surface on a single slice. Normal appearance of the anterior horn of the medial meniscus. The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact. Collateral ligaments, retinacula – normal appearance. No pathological changes are visualized in the scanned muscle groups. Popliteal fossa – presence of a fabella and a small Baker's cyst. Conclusion: MRI evidence of inflammation of the patellar ligament (Jumper's knee). Partial injury of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 2b. Small Baker's cyst.

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: 6 months of knee pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tear of the medial meniscus with a predominant oblique radial tear at the posterior root with additional tearing of the medial meniscus body with severe extrusion into the meniscotibial gutter. Reactive edema along the medial joint line.
Medial compartment cartilage: High-grade cartilage loss along the periphery of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 4 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Complex tear of the medial meniscus with a predominant oblique radial tear at the posterior root with additional tearing of the medial meniscus body with severe extrusion into the meniscotibial gutter. Reactive edema along the medial joint line.
2.	Medical compartment chondrosis.

report:
There is a complex degenerative tear through the posterior horn and root of the medial meniscus, with a predominantly radial component, with consequent significant medial extrusion at the level of the body.
There are no accompanying displaced meniscal fragment.

A small subarticular, horizontally oriented fracture line is noted at the medial tibial plateau, with accompanying surrounding marrow oedema like signal change but with no associated articular surface collapse being demonstrated. 
Diffuse grade 2/3 medial weightbearing articular cartilage damage, there is furthermore a moderate suprapatellar effusion that is communicating with a leaking, 5 cm maximal diameter Baker's cyst.

Grossly intact lateral meniscus, cruciate and lateral collateral ligaments, a grade 1 superficial MCL sprain is present.
Normal popliteus musculotendinous unit, extensor tendons and the distal iliotibial band.

No other skeletal abnormality of note, minor, focal medial retropatellar articular cartilage damage.
Well-maintained remaining patellofemoral and lateral weightbearing articular cartilage surfaces.

Grossly unremarkable remaining imaged extra-articular soft tissues.

Impression:
Unstable complex medial meniscal tear as detailed above, along with insufficiency type bony injury at the medial tibial plateau.
Temporary nonweightbearing advisable in the first instance, together with screening for possible underlying risk factors.

report:
Findings:  Small suprapatellar knee joint effusion. No sinister bone marrow changes. Small 10 mm x 3 mm intra-articular retropatellar soft tissue focus.  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments.  Intact medial meniscus. Horizontal tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus which breaches the inferior meniscal surface. Radial fraying of the inner free edge of the anterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus.  Normal appearance of the pes anserine tendons, popliteus tendon, distal biceps femoris tendon and distal iliotibial band.  Intact extensor mechanism. No evidence of fat pad impingement.  Minor fibrillation of the hyaline articular cartilage in the lateral tibiofemoral compartment. Otherwise well maintained tricompartmental hyaline articular cartilage.  
Conclusion:  Horizontal tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus which breaches the inferior meniscal surface. Radial fraying of the inner free edge of the anterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus. Small 10 mm x 3 mm intra-articular retropatellar soft tissue focus. Possibly represents a small focus of PVNS - patient will be recalled for dedicated sequences.
Exam performed: MR Recall of [DATE]:  Findings:  The previously described small intra-articular retropatellar soft tissue focus cannot be readily appreciated on the current scan. There are no intra-articular soft tissue foci which demonstrate blooming artefact to suggest PVNS.

report: SAĞ DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Lateral menisküs normaldir.  Medial menisküs posterior horn ve gövde kesimde grade II dejenerasyon izlendi.Arka çapraz bağ, lateral kollateral ligaman normaldir.Anterior çapraz bağda miksoid dejenerasyona sekonder sinyal değişikliği izlendi.Medial kollateral ligamande periligamantöz ödem izlenmektedir.Patella medial fasette subkondral 7x4 mm boyutlu fokal osteokondral defekt izlenmektedir.Prepatellar cilt altı yağ dokuda ödem izlendi.Tibia medial platoda subartiküler fraktür ve komşu kemik iliğinde ödem ile uyumlu sinyal değişikliği izlendi.Femur medial kondilde tibiofemoral eklem komşuluğunda subkondral alanda 10x5 mm boyutlu osteokondral defekt ve komşu kemik iliğinde ödem izlendi.Femur interkondiler alan anteriorunda da subkondral alanda 9x5 mm boyutlu osteokondral defekt izlenmektedir.Diz anteroinferior kesiminde cilt altı yağ dokuda ödeme sekonder retiküler tarzda sıvı artışı izlendi.SONUÇ: Tibia medial platoda subartiküler mikrofraktür ve komşu kemik iliği ödemi. translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings:
The lateral meniscus is normal. Grade II degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. Periligamentous edema is observed in the medial collateral ligament. A focal osteochondral defect measuring 7x4 mm is observed in the subchondral region of the medial patellar facet. Edema is observed in the prepatellar subcutaneous fat tissue. Signal change consistent with subarticular fracture and adjacent bone marrow edema is observed in the medial tibial plateau. An osteochondral defect measuring 10x5 mm in the subchondral area adjacent to the tibiofemoral joint and adjacent bone marrow edema are observed in the medial femoral condyle. An osteochondral defect measuring 9x5 mm is also observed in the subchondral area of the anterior intercondylar region of the femur. Reticular-pattern fluid increase secondary to edema is observed in the subcutaneous fat tissue of the anteroinferior aspect of the knee.
CONCLUSION:
Subarticular microfracture and adjacent bone marrow edema in the medial tibial plateau. Osteochondral defects at the intercondylar level of the medial femoral condyle and the medial patellar facet. Grade II meniscopathy of the medial meniscus. Myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Edema in the prepatellar subcutaneous fat tissue.
