report:
Right knee MRI:

INDICATION: Right knee [Age] female with remote history of right meniscal tearing seen for subacute, traumatic bilateral medial knee pain right more than left.? Degenerative.

COMPARISON: No prior images available at time of interpretation.

FINDINGS:

Mild knee joint effusion. Tiny 2.7 x 1.8 x 0.6 cm Baker's cysts.

ANTERIOR COMPARTMENT:
Overall moderate to severe chondrosis more prominent on the medial facet of the patella. No significant subchondral marrow edema but full-thickness cartilage denuding. Extensor mechanism is intact. Hoffa's fat pads unremarkable.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Moderate chondrosis. Small osteophytes. There is macerated posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with multidirectional tearing extension to the meniscal undersurface with slightly medially extruded meniscus, no flipped fragment or free fragment identified. 2.3 x 1.2 x 0.8 cm posterior parameniscal cyst. Medial collateral ligament and pes anserine tendons are intact. Mild semimembranosus tendinosis.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Mild chondrosis with minimal thinning. No subchondral bone change. Tiny osteophytes. Minimal heterogeneous signal to the posterior horn of the meniscus without discrete tear related to chronic degeneration. Lateral collateral ligament and biceps femoris tendons are intact. Popliteus tendon is intact. The iliotibial band is unremarkable.

INTERCONDYLAR COMPARTMENT:
Anterior cruciate and posterior cruciate ligament are intact. Effusion/ganglion cyst extending into the posterior intercondylar notch.

IMPRESSION:
1. Moderate to severe chondrosis of the femoral patellar compartment, moderate chondrosis of the medial femoral tibial compartment and mild chondrosis of the lateral compartment. Degenerative changes associated with mild knee joint effusion.
2. Complex multidirectional degenerative tear of the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with mild meniscal extrusion but no flipped or free fragment. Associated parameniscal cyst.

KNEE MRI

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
Bilaterally, on evaluation of the menisci, cruciate and collateral ligaments, no significant findings are observed.

translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings:
The lateral meniscus is normal. Grade I degeneration is observed in the body–posterior horn of the medial meniscus. The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps is normal. There is no retinacular discontinuity. A nondisplaced vertically oriented fracture is observed in the medial patella. Bone marrow edema is observed at this level and in the central patella. Additionally, bone marrow edema is noted in the anterolateral aspect at the level of the lateral femoral epicondyle. The current findings are thought to be related to a prior lateral patellar dislocation. Effusion is observed in the knee joint and suprapatellar bursa. A cortically based bone lesion measuring approximately 14×7 mm, hypointense on T1-weighted and hyperintense on T2-weighted images, is observed in the distal femoral metaphysis (NOF).
Conclusion:
Vertically oriented fracture in the medial patella due to prior patellar dislocation, edema in the patella and lateral femoral epicondyle. Knee joint effusion. Grade I degeneration in the medial meniscus. Benign bone lesion in the distal femoral metaphysis (NOF).

translation:
MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
In the medial compartment, simple degeneration of the meniscus is observed without tear of it. Also, a marginal osteophyte is observed on the medial femoral condyle as well as a small defect of the articular cartilage, most likely of traumatic origin.

On examination of the lateral compartment, marginal osteophytes are also observed as well as degeneration of the lateral meniscus without findings of tear of it. The articular cartilage presents on the weight-bearing axis a focal defect of anteroposterior diameter 6mm and in the anterior portion of the lateral femoral condyle over an extent of approximately 2cm total erosion of the articular cartilage (ICRS grade 4) with subarticular osteomedullary edema.

On examination of the anterior compartment, total erosion of the articular cartilage of the lateral superior articular surface of the patella is observed (ICRS grade 4) with subarticular bone marrow lesions.

Intra-articularly, a large fluid collection is observed with focal projections of fatty tissue composition, while additionally a large synovial fold is observed in both the medial and lateral suprapatellar regions. A Baker's synovial cyst is observed in the popliteal fossa with findings of microtears of its wall. Incidentally, intra-articularly posterior to the medial femoral epicondyle, an osteochondral loose body of maximum diameter 6mm is observed.

CONCLUSION:
1. Degenerative osteoarthritis of the lateral compartment.
2. Degenerative osteoarthritis of the patellofemoral joint at its superior portion.
3. Hydrarthrosis with presence of secondary villous lipoma (lipoma arborescens) within it as well as a small loose body.

translation:
Clinical History:
Obs. Hoffitis.
Findings:
Mild diffuse thinning of the ACL, likely sequela. PCL and lateral collateral ligament without alterations.
Mild sequela thickening of the proximal third of the superficial component of the medial collateral ligament. The remaining components without alterations.
Lateral meniscus with preserved morphology and signal, no signs of tear. Discrete increased signal at the meniscocapsular junction of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus, which could represent a regional partial lesion, correlate clinically.
Cartilage of the femorotibial and patellofemoral compartments without significant alterations.
No joint effusion or pathological popliteal cysts. Discrete soft tissue edema between the medial femoral condyle and the pes anserine tendons.
Mild increased signal at the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon, no signs of tear. Discrete edema of the retroquadriceps, suprapatellar fat pad.
Patellar tendon, pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Discrete soft tissue edema between the iliotibial band and the lateral femoral condyle.
Impression:
Discrete thinning appearing sequela of the ACL.
Mild sequela thickening of the medial collateral ligament.
Probable partial lesion of the meniscocapsular junction at the level of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus.
Probable friction phenomena of the iliotibial band and posteromedial knee.
Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis. Edema of the retroquadriceps suprapatellar fat pad, nonspecific finding, could represent patellar malalignment phenomena.

translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Central-marginal osteophyte formation was observed in all three compartments of the knee joint. The medial meniscus is extruded 6 mm medially from the knee joint. Volume loss, loss of integrity in the body segment, and grade III degeneration in the posterior horn were observed in the meniscus. Grade II degeneration in the anterior and posterior horn and body segment of the lateral meniscus, and a horizontal tear extending to the free edge were observed. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration was observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. Focal loss of cartilage integrity was observed in places on the medial facet of the patella. Increased fluid was observed in the suprapatellar bursa. Joint space narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral joint, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral degenerative cysts, and subchondral edema were observed on the bone surfaces adjacent to the joint. Destruction of the femoral and tibial cartilages is observed at this level. The findings were interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis.
Conclusion: Gonarthrosis. Medial extrusion of the medial meniscus, volume loss, loss of integrity in the body segment, grade III meniscopathy in the posterior horn. Grade II meniscopathy in the lateral meniscus with accompanying horizontal tear. Myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. Grade III chondromalacia of the medial facet of the patella. Suprapatellar bursitis.

report:

Im Verlauf progredienter vollschichtiger Knorpeldefekt am Patellafirst und der lateralen Facette am unteren Patellapol über ca. 1,5 x 1,0 cm. Angrenzendes intraossäres Reizödem (4/7). Auch an der lateralen Femurfacette teils vollschichtige Chondropathie (7/14). Einzelnes Ossikel im MPFL (7/10). Jedoch kein Hinweis auf eine Diskontinuität des Ligaments.
Femorotibial erhaltener Artikulation. Osteophytäre Anbauten führend am lateralen Femurkondylus (4/18) sowie am lateralen Tibiaplateau (4/19), kleinere Osteophyten auch am medialen Kompartiment sowie femoropatellar.
Lateral femorotibial abschnittsweise ausgedünnter Knorpelbelag, exemplarisch anterioren der Femurkondyle (5/23). Im medialen Kompartiment nach weitestgehend erhaltener Knorpelbelag. Menisci intakt ohne Hinweis auf eine Rissbildung. Das Innenmeniskushinterhorn gering signalangehoben in der PD, DD bei initialen mukoiden Veränderungen. Kreuzbänder ebenfalls intakt. Schmaler Flüssigkeitssaum medial des MCL, DD bei Reizzustand, kein Hinweis auf eine Ruptur. LCL unauffällig.

translation:
Preserved articulation in the left knee joint. Known patella alta (Insall-Salvati 1.85) and unchanged laterally positioned patella. Progressive full-thickness cartilage defect at the patellar ridge and the lateral facet at the inferior patellar pole measuring approximately 1.5 x 1.0 cm. Adjacent intraosseous reactive edema (4/7). Also at the lateral femoral facet, partial full-thickness chondropathy (7/14). Single ossicle within the MPFL (7/10). However, no evidence of discontinuity of the ligament.
Preserved femorotibial articulation. Osteophytic formations predominantly at the lateral femoral condyle (4/18) and at the lateral tibial plateau (4/19), smaller osteophytes also in the medial compartment and femoropatellar.
Laterally femorotibial, segmentally thinned cartilage, exemplarily at the anterior aspect of the femoral condyles (5/23). In the medial compartment, largely preserved cartilage. Menisci intact without evidence of a tear. The posterior horn of the medial meniscus shows mildly increased signal on PD, differential diagnosis of initial mucoid changes. Cruciate ligaments also intact. Narrow fluid rim medial to the MCL, differential diagnosis of reactive state, no evidence of rupture. LCL unremarkable.
Small joint effusion. Synovium mildly thickened, minimally progressive Baker's cyst compared to 06/12 (3/97). Unremarkable appearance of the surrounding musculature and subcutaneous tissue.

translation:
LEFT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade III degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus. Grade III degeneration is observed in the anterior and posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus. Signal change secondary to mucoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Edema is observed in the prepatellar subcutaneous fat tissue. Subarticular fracture in the medial femoral condyle and signal change consistent with edema in the adjacent bone marrow are observed. Mild narrowing of the joint space in the medial tibiofemoral joint and focal thinning of the femoral and tibial cartilages adjacent to the joint are observed. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space.
CONCLUSION: Subarticular fracture in the medial femoral condyle and adjacent bone marrow edema, mild gonarthrosis in the medial tibiofemoral joint, grade III meniscopathy in the medial and lateral menisci, mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament, suprapatellar bursitis, synovitis of the knee joint, edema in the prepatellar subcutaneous tissue, grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament.

report: МР находка: Дясна колянна става: Минимален ставен излив.  Костите, формиращи дясната колянна става са с нормална форма, структура и сигнален интензитет. Малка ограничена зона на костномозъчен едем в медиалния кондил на фемура. Налице е лезия и дефект  в хрущяла на пателата срединно  на протежение от 3-4мм.  Налице е кистична преустройка по задната стена на пателата към прилежащия хрущялен дефект.  Ставният хрущял на фемура и тибията е неизтънен и със запазена конгруентност. Не се изобразяват патологични лезии в латералния менискус. Малка лезия – 2а стадии с кос ход в заден рог на медиален менискус. Нормално изобразяване на предния му рог. Кръстни връзки – запазена цялост. Колатерални лигаменти със запазена цялост. Ретинакулуми на пателата – б.о. Не се изобразяват промени в меките тъкани на дясното коляно. Заключение: МР данни хондропатия на пателата с прилежаща кистична преустройка по задна стена на пателата.  Малък ставен излив в дясната колянна става.
translation: MRI findings: Right knee joint: Minimal joint effusion. The bones forming the right knee joint are of normal shape, structure, and signal intensity. There is cystic remodeling along the posterior wall of the patella adjacent to the cartilage defect. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia is not thinned and with preserved congruence. No pathological lesions are visualized in the lateral meniscus. Small lesion – grade 2a with oblique course in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Normal appearance of its anterior horn. Cruciate ligaments – intact. Collateral ligaments – intact. Patellar retinacula – unremarkable. No changes are visualized in the soft tissues of the right knee. Conclusion: MRI findings of patellar chondropathy with adjacent cystic remodeling along the posterior wall of the patella. Small joint effusion in the right knee joint.

Meniscos de morfología y señal conservadas, sin signos de rotura.
Alteración de señal intrasustancia del cartílago del platillo tibial lateral. Adelgazamiento condral de

Discreto edema del aspecto superolateral de la grasa de Hoffa. Discreto edema del paquete
adiposo retro cuadricipital suprarrotuliano.
Grupos musculares de trofismo y señal normales.

Condropatía del platillo tibial lateral y cóndilo femoral medial grado 1 y 2. Condropatía patelar
grado 1-2.
Signos de hiperpresión patelar externa. Discreto edema del paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital

rotuliano.

translation:
Clinical History:
Suprapatellar tendinitis.
Findings:
No diffuse bone marrow signal abnormalities.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments of normal thickness and signal.
Menisci of preserved morphology and signal, without signs of tear.
Intrasubstance signal alteration of the cartilage of the lateral tibial plateau. Partial-thickness chondral thinning in the posterocentral weight-bearing region of the medial femoral condyle. Increased intrasubstance signal and surface irregularity of the cartilage of the central region and lateral facet of the patella. The remaining cartilage of the femorotibial and patellofemoral compartments of normal thickness and signal.
Mild joint effusion. No popliteal cysts are observed.
Quadriceps tendon, patellar tendon, popliteus tendon, semimembranosus tendon, biceps femoris tendon, iliotibial band, and pes anserinus tendons of normal thickness and signal.
Mild edema of the superolateral aspect of Hoffa's fat pad. Mild edema of the suprapatellar retroquadriceps fat pad.
Muscle groups of normal trophism and signal.
Impression:
Chondropathy of the lateral tibial plateau and medial femoral condyle grade 1 and 2. Patellar chondropathy grade 1-2.
Signs of lateral patellar hyperpressure. Mild edema of the suprapatellar retroquadriceps fat pad, nonspecific finding, could represent patellar malalignment phenomena.
Mild joint effusion.

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee pain
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Chondral thinning along the lateral patellar facet with superimposed foci of high-grade fissuring. Broad areas of full-thickness cartilage loss along the lateral trochlea with subchondral cystic change.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: Mild proximal patellar tendinosis.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Intense soft tissue edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 8 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

Findings of lateral patellofemoral maltracking with Hoffa's fat pad impingement, mild proximal patellar tendinosis, and grade 4 patellofemoral compartment chondrosis.

report: Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı artmış. Çapraz ve yan bağlar normal. Lateral menisküs dejenerasyonuna yırtık eşlik etmiyor. Mediyal menisküs arka boynuzu-gövdesi düzeyinde alt eklem yüzeyiyle ilişkilenen horizontal-oblik longitudinal dejeneratif yırtık ile medyal menisküs gövdesine komşu milimetrik paralabral kistler izleniyor. Diz eklemindeki hafif dereceli trikompartmantal osteoartrit medyal pateller fasetindeki ve medyal femoral kondilin ağırlık taşıyan yüzeyindeki kondral kalınlığın %50'sini aşmayan kıkırdak dejenerasyonu ve buna eşlik eden milimetrik subkondral fibrovasküler değişiklik ile karakterize. Tibya proksimal metafizinin mediyalindeki intraoseöz kemik adası 6 mm çaplı. Ekstensör mekanizma korunmuş. Proksimal tibyofibular eklem normal.
translation: Increased intra-articular fluid in the knee joint. Cruciate and collateral ligaments are normal. Lateral meniscus degeneration is not accompanied by a tear. At the level of the posterior horn–body junction of the medial meniscus, a horizontal-oblique longitudinal degenerative tear communicating with the inferior articular surface is observed, along with millimetric paralabral cysts adjacent to the body of the medial meniscus. Mild tricompartmental osteoarthritis of the knee joint is characterized by cartilage degeneration not exceeding 50% of the cartilage thickness at the medial patellar facet and the weight-bearing surface of the medial femoral condyle, accompanied by millimetric subchondral fibrovascular changes. Intraosseous bone island in the medial aspect of the proximal tibial metaphysis, measuring 6 mm in diameter. The extensor mechanism is intact. The proximal tibiofibular joint is normal.

report: МР находка: Визуализира се малък ставен излив. Костите, формиращи колянната ставa, са с нормална форма и сигнален интензитет. Артикулиращият хрущял на фемура и тибията е със запазена конгруентност и дебелина. МР данни за начални дегенеративни промени в задния рог на медиалния менискус. Задният рог на този менискус е със слабо повишен интензитет на сигнала, без да се дефинира скъсване.  МР данни за частична увреда в задния рог на латералния менискус. В него се вижда зона на повишен сигнален интензитет, която не достига до края на менискуса и до артикулиращите ставни повърхности на фемура и тибията. Нормален образ на предния рог на латералния и медиалния менискус. Задната кръстна връзка е със запазена цялост. Предната кръста връзка е с уголемен напречник и повишен сигнален интензитет. Колатерални лигаменти – без особености. Патела, хрущял на пателата, ретинакулуми на пателата – нормално изобразяване. Лигамент на пателата, сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис – б.о.  Поплитеална ямка – б.о. Нормалнно изобразяване на обхванатите мускули и меки тъкани. Заключение: МР данни за частична увреда в задния рог на латералния менискус – grade 1. Дегенеративни промени в задния рог на медиалния менискус. Мукоидна дегенерация на предната кръстна връзка. Малък ставен излив.

report:
COMPARISON:[Date].

CLINICAL HISTORY:Right lateral knee pain, chronic. Suspected lateral meniscal tear/lateral collateral ligament tear.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The medial meniscus is intact. Horizontal cleavage tear with superior surfacing noted extending through the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is an additional radial tear involving the lateral meniscal body. The latter is unchanged from <[YEAR]>. The former is new since previous study. No lateral meniscal extrusion. The posterior root and anterior horn of the lateral meniscus are intact. Possible additional inferiorly subtle tear at the periphery of the junction of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus, also new since previous study.

The anterior cruciate ligament and T2 are intact. Medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact. Fibular collateral ligament is intact. Popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments are intact. Iliotibial band is intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. There is mild lateral patellar subluxation, similar to previous. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 13 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Focal soft tissue articular cartilage central femoral trochlea, also seen present. Mild chondrosis throughout the remainder the patellofemoral compartment. Mild medial and lateral femorotibial chondrosis, slightly progressed when compared to previous. Probable insertional cyst near the anterior cruciate ligament footplate. 

Prominent red marrow, similar to previous. Small knee joint effusion. Regional musculature is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION:
1. Interval development of horizontal cleavage tear extending through the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus without lateral meniscal extrusion. Unchanged radial tear involving the lateral meniscal body. Possible additional inferiorly surfacing oblique tear at the junction of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus.
2. Mild to moderate chondrosis has progressed slightly since previous study, and is compatible with evolving mild osteoarthritis of the right knee.

report: SOL  DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Diz eklemini oluşturan kemik yapılarda yaygın dejeneratif değişiklikler izlendi.Tibiada interkondiler eminencia düzeyinde milimetrik subkondral kistler izlendi. Tibia femoral eklemde medialde ekleme bakan yüzlerde minimal kemik iliği ödemi izlendi. Anterior çapraz bağda strein ile uyumlu minimal sinyal artışı dikkati çekti. Arka çapraz bağ, lateral ve medial kollateral ligaman normaldir.Medial menisküs posterior hornunda grade III yırtık izlendi. Anterior hornunda grade II dejenerasyon izlendi. Lateral menisküs posterior hornunda grade II dejenerasyon izlendi. Eklem mesafesinde ve suprapatellar bursada artmış effüzyon izlendi. Patella posteriorunda kıkırdak dokuda incelme ve subkondral minimal kemik iliği ödemi izlendi ( patellar kondromalazi ).Prepatellar yağ dokuda ödemli görünüm izlendi. Diz eklemine komşu yumuşak dokularda medialde dilate variköz venöz yapılar dikkati çekti.
translation: LEFT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: Widespread degenerative changes were observed in the bony structures forming the knee joint. Millimetric subchondral cysts were observed at the level of the intercondylar eminence of the tibia. Minimal bone marrow edema was observed on the articular surfaces facing the joint medially in the tibiofemoral joint. Minimal signal increase consistent with strain was noted in the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. Grade III tear was observed in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Grade II degeneration was observed in the anterior horn of the medial meniscus. Grade II degeneration was observed in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. Increased effusion was observed in the joint space and suprapatellar bursa. Thinning of the cartilage tissue and minimal subchondral bone marrow edema were observed on the posterior aspect of the patella (patellar chondromalacia). Edematous appearance was observed in the prepatellar fat pad. Dilated varicose venous structures were noted medially in the soft tissues adjacent to the knee joint.

translation:

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed on a 3 Tesla scanner with T1 and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
Mild degeneration is observed in the menisci without findings of tear.
On evaluation of the cruciate and collateral ligaments, articular cartilage, and bone marrow, no significant findings are observed.
On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, the quadriceps and patellar tendons appear within normal limits.
Edema is noted in the prepatellar subcutaneous tissue.
Intra-articularly, a small fluid collection is observed in communication with a small Baker's synovial cyst in the medial compartment.
At the medial posterolateral corner, at the level of the distal femoral metaphysis, edematous signal is observed at the insertion of the gastrocnemius and the surrounding soft tissues.

translation:

Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the medial and lateral menisci. The anterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The posterior cruciate ligament signal is mildly increased with focal irregularities (partial tear). The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Mild focal thinning is observed in the patellar cartilage (grade II chondromalacia). No joint effusion is detected. Signal intensities of the other bony structures forming the knee joint are normal. Diffuse bone marrow edema is observed at the level of the medial femoral condyle. Mild narrowing of the joint space and mild thinning of the adjacent cartilages are observed at the medial tibiofemoral joint. A subchondral millimetric cyst is observed at the tibial insertion site of the anterior cruciate ligament. A lobulated contour ganglion cyst measuring approximately 27x10 mm is observed at the posterior aspect of the tibiofibular joint.
Impression: Partial tear of the posterior cruciate ligament. Medial compartment subchondral marrow edema and small tibial subchondral cyst. Mild patellar chondromalacia. Ganglion cyst at the proximal tibiofibular joint.

report:

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.2 Tesla open system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytosis, most pronounced at the posterior medial femoral condyle. Osteophytes protruding into the intercondylar notch.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. 5 mm intra-articular body at the intercondylar notch. Trace leaking Baker's cyst.

Medial meniscus: Complex tearing with dominant near-complete radial tear of the posterior horn. Severe meniscal extrusion.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Focal high-grade articular cartilage loss at the weightbearing lateral femoral condyle near the intercondylar eminence with button osteophyte formation.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Large confluent regions of full-thickness articular cartilage loss at the patella and lateral trochlea with associated subchondral signal changes.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Severe mucoid degeneration.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Periligamentous edema, likely related to adjacent meniscal pathology.

Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. Nonspecific retro-quadriceps fat pad edema.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Medial tibiofemoral compartment and patellofemoral osteoarthritis. Small knee joint effusion with 5 mm intra-articular body at the intercondylar notch.
2.	Complex degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus with dominant radial tear at the posterior horn and severe meniscal extrusion.
3.	Severe mucoid degeneration of the ACL.

translation:
TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, PD fs, and T2 gradient echo sequences.

FINDINGS:
A previous MRI from [DATE] is available for comparison.
- Re-evaluated: moderate amount of intra-articular fluid in communication with a Baker's synovial cyst with a craniocaudal dimension of 5.3 cm.
- Re-evaluated: significant narrowing of the medial joint space with extensive osteophytosis of the medial femoral and tibial condyles and, focally, full-thickness erosions of greater extent on the femoral condyle and lesser extent on the tibial condyle. The subarticular bone marrow edema on both sides shows a decrease in extent, which is likely a consequence of the extensive osteoarthritis.
- Noted, without change: tear of the posterior root of the medial meniscus and the associated subluxation thereof, as well as a horizontal tear of the posterior horn with extension to the posterior portion of the body.
- Re-evaluated: the large osteophyte arising from the medial femoral condyle, which projects into the intercondylar notch, as well as the osteochondral fragment superior to the medial tibial plateau, which has not changed in position or dimensions compared to the previous examination.
- Also noted unchanged: osteophytosis of the anterior compartment with a full-thickness erosion of 3 mm (grade IV per ICRS) on the medial articular surface of the patella and a smaller longitudinal full-thickness erosion on the medial portion of the lateral articular surface.
- On evaluation of the cruciate ligaments: re-evaluated ganglion cysts in the proximal portion of the anterior cruciate ligament. No pathological findings in the posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament, or lateral collateral ligament.

CONCLUSION: Unchanged findings compared to the previous examination.

report: ΤΕΧΝΙΚΗ: Η εξέταση πραγµατοποιήθηκε µε ακολουθίες Τ1, Τ2me2d και STIR. Τα εν λόγω ευρήµατα αποδίδονται σε κατάγµατα ανεπάρκειας (SIFK), ωστόσο λόγω αναφερόµενου ιστορικού τραύµατος θα πρέπει να συνεκτίµηθει το ενδεχόµενο χρόνιων µετατραυµατικών αλλοιώσεων ισοϋψώς (προηγηθέντων οξέων καταγµάτων). - Σηµειώνονται πλάγια επιχείλια οστεόφυτα κατά το έξω µεσάρθριο, καθώς και διάχυτο παθολογικό σήµα του έξω µηνίσκου µε συνοδό ολικού πάχους απώλεια του αρθρικού χόνδρου ισοϋψώς, στο πλαίσιο εκφυλιστικών αλλοιώσεων. - Αναγνωρίζεται λέπτυνση και παθολογικό σήµα του προσθιου χιαστού συνδέσµου, χωρις ωστόσο διακοπή της συνέχειας των ινών του. - ∆ιάχυτο παθολογικό σήµα αναγνωρίζεται στον έσω µηνίσκου στο πλαίσιο εκφύλισης. - Μικρή ενδαρθρική συλλογή υγρού. - Παρατηρείται συνοβιακή κυστη Baker 3.8 X 1.8 cm. - Φυσιολογικά απεικονίζονται ο οπίσθιως χιαστός και οι πλάγιοι σύνδεσµοι. - Εντός του φυσιολογικού ελέγχεται ο λοιπός αρθρικός χόνδρος. - Με σήµα εντός του φυσιολογικού ελέγχεται ο λοιπός οστικός µυελός. - Χωρίς ευρήµατα δυσλειτουργίας του εκτατικού µηχανισµού.
translation:
TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, T2me2d, and STIR sequences.

FINDINGS:
- Bone marrow edema is identified in the lateral femoral condyle and to a lesser degree in the lateral tibial condyle posteriorly, while in both subarticular regions there is a degree of sclerosis, as well as irregularity of the margin with appearance of depression of the articular surface approximately 1-2 mm. These findings are attributed to subchondral insufficiency fractures (SIFK); however, due to the reported history of trauma, the possibility of chronic post-traumatic changes at the same level (previous acute fractures) should be considered.
- Lateral marginal osteophytes are noted at the lateral compartment, as well as diffuse abnormal signal of the lateral meniscus with accompanying full-thickness loss of articular cartilage at the same level, in the setting of degenerative changes.
- Thinning and abnormal signal of the anterior cruciate ligament is identified, without however disruption of the continuity of its fibers.
- Diffuse abnormal signal is identified in the medial meniscus in the setting of degeneration.
- Small intra-articular fluid collection.
- A Baker's cyst measuring 3.8 x 1.8 cm is observed.
- The posterior cruciate ligament and the collateral ligaments appear normal.
- The remaining articular cartilage is within normal limits.
- The remaining bone marrow signal is within normal limits.
- No findings of extensor mechanism dysfunction.

report: SAĞ DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Medial menisküs diz eklem mesafesinden 9 mm tümü ile mediale ekstrüdedir. Ekstrüde menisküste belirgin volüm kaybı ve kompleks yırtıklar izlenmiştir.Lateral menisküs anterior hornu ve gövde kesiminde grade III dejenerasyon izlenmektedir.Lateral kollateral ligaman normaldir.Anterior çapraz bağda komplet rüptüre sekonder bütünlük kaybı izlenmiştir. Posterior çapraz bağ proksimal kesimde incelme ve sinyal artışı izlenmiştir.Medial kollateral ligamanda periligamantöz ödem izlenmiştir.Distal kuadriseps ve patellar tendonlar normaldir. Retinaküler devamsızlık yoktur.Patella medial fasette kartilajda destrüksiyon, subkondral alanda kemik iliği ödemi izlenmiştir.Suprapatellar bursa ve diz eklem mesafesinde yaygın sıvı artışı izlenmiştir.Diz eklemini oluşturan her üç kompartmanda santral-marginal osteofitik formasyonu izlenmiştir.Tibiofemoral eklem  medialinde eklem aralığında daralma, ekleme komşu kemik yüzlerde subkondral skleroz, ödem ve dejeneratif kistler izlenmiştir. Bu düzeylerde kartilajlarda desktrüksiyon izlenmiştir. Bulgular dejeneratif artrit lehine yorumlanmıştır.Tibia interkondiler eminensia anterior ve posteriorunda çapraz bağlar insersiyo düzeyinde subkortikal alanda büyüğü 1 cm çaplı kistler izlenmiştir.Popliteal fossada 7x4 cm boyutlu baker kisti izlenmiştir.Sonuç: Gonatroz, medial menisküste medial ekstrüzyon, volüm kaybı ve kompleks yırtıklar, lateral menisküste grade III meniskopati, anterior çapraz bağda komplet rüptür, posterior çapraz bağ proksimalinde diffüz incelme, tibia interkondiler eminensiada dejeneratif kistler, suprapatellar bursit, diz ekleminde sinovit, patella medial fasette grade 4 kondromalazi, popliteal fossada baker kisti .
translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings:
The medial meniscus is completely extruded medially by 9 mm from the knee joint space. Significant volume loss and complex tears are observed in the extruded meniscus. Grade III degeneration is observed in the anterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus. The lateral collateral ligament is normal. Loss of continuity secondary to complete rupture is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. Thinning and increased signal are observed in the proximal portion of the posterior cruciate ligament. Periligamentous edema is observed in the medial collateral ligament. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Cartilage destruction and bone marrow edema in the subchondral area are observed on the medial facet of the patella. Diffuse fluid increase is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Central-marginal osteophytic formation is observed in all three compartments of the knee joint. Joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, edema, and degenerative cysts are observed on the bone surfaces adjacent to the medial tibiofemoral joint. Cartilage destruction is observed at these levels. Findings are interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis. Cysts, the largest measuring 1 cm in diameter, are observed in the subcortical area at the insertion level of the cruciate ligaments on the anterior and posterior intercondylar eminence of the tibia. A Baker's cyst measuring 7x4 cm is observed in the popliteal fossa.
Conclusion: Gonarthrosis, medial extrusion of the medial meniscus, volume loss and complex tears, grade III meniscopathy of the lateral meniscus, complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament, diffuse thinning of the proximal posterior cruciate ligament, degenerative cysts of the tibial intercondylar eminence, suprapatellar bursitis, synovitis of the knee joint, grade 4 chondromalacia of the medial facet of the patella, Baker's cyst in the popliteal fossa.

report: Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı normal. Medyal menisküs arka boynuzundaki horizontal oblik-longitudinal yırtık alt eklem yüzeyine ulaşıyor. Lateral menisküs normal. Hafif dereceli patellofemoral eklem dejenerasyonu patella apeksi-medyal fasetindeki kondral kalınlığın %50'sini aşmayan kayıp ile birlikte olan dejenerasyon ile birlikte. Posteriyor oblik bağ ödemli. İç yan bağın çevresi hafifçe ödemli. Çapraz ve yan bağlar bunların dışında normal. Ekstensör mekanizma korunmuş. Proksimal tibyofibular eklem normal. Gastroknemyus semimembranozus bursasındaki 6.8 cm maksimum boyutlu sıvı lokülasyonu izlenmekte ve içerisinde ince septasyonlar mevcut ve yüksek olasılıkla sızdırmıyor.
translation: The amount of intra-articular fluid in the knee joint is normal. A horizontal oblique-longitudinal tear in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extends to the inferior articular surface. The lateral meniscus is normal. Mild patellofemoral joint degeneration with cartilage loss not exceeding 50% of the cartilage thickness at the apex–medial facet of the patella. The posterior oblique ligament is edematous. The periphery of the medial collateral ligament is mildly edematous. The cruciate and collateral ligaments are otherwise normal. The extensor mechanism is intact. The proximal tibiofibular joint is normal. A fluid loculation measuring up to 6.8 cm in maximum dimension is observed within the gastrocnemius-semimembranosus bursa, containing thin septations, and it is most likely not leaking.

translation:
MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
Partial tear is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament at its femoral attachment.
The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament appear within normal limits.
Edema is observed on the lateral aspect of the medial collateral ligament, particularly at the femoral insertion. The finding is consistent with a low-grade injury (Grade one).
The medial meniscus shows degeneration (Grade II), without findings of tear.
The lateral meniscus, articular cartilage, and bone marrow do not show pathological findings.
The imaging of the extensor mechanism is also normal.
A small collection is observed intra-articularly.
Adjacent to the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle, a small Baker's synovial cyst is observed with a maximum craniocaudal diameter of approximately 4 cm, which is accompanied by free fluid in the gastrocnemius, indicative of recent rupture of its wall.

translation:
MRI RIGHT KNEE
TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, T2 gradient echo and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.
DIAGNOSIS: [DATE].
- Intra-articularly, fluid collection is re-evaluated, with prominent appearance of synovitis. Focal high-signal on T1 sequence projections on the synovium (fatty) are re-evaluated, which had been attributed to lipoma arborescens.
- Re-evaluated with slight worsening of the medial joint space narrowing with presence of marginal osteophytic lesions, thinning up to elimination of the cartilage of the medial femoral condyle, as well as slight increase in the extent of bone marrow edema on both articular surfaces in combination with subchondral microcysts.
- Similarly, presence of marginal osteophytic lesions is noted as well as chondropathy lesions with pathological signal and erosions in the cartilage of the patella, with further erosion of the cartilage along the medial articular surface of the patella.
- From the evaluation of the menisci, linear pathological signal is re-evaluated in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, attributed to degeneration.
- Linear pathological signal is re-evaluated in the insertion portion of the quadriceps tendon, of degenerative origin.
- The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments as well as the collateral ligaments of the knee are evaluated within normal limits.
- A Baker's cyst is noted at the posterior medial margin of the knee joint.
Conclusion: Osteoarthritic lesions in the medial and anterior compartment of the joint with findings of secondary synovitis and presence of lipoma arborescens.

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]

- Presence of marginal osteophytic lesions is noted as well as chondropathy lesions, particularly along the medial articular surface of the patella, with pathological signal and erosions in the cartilage.
- From the evaluation of the menisci, degeneration without tear is observed, particularly of the medial meniscus.

Die Patella zentriert stehend. Mit nur geringen oberflächlichen chondralen Läsionen (z. B. 7/10). An der Trochlea keine tief greifende Chondropathie.

Femorotibial erhaltener Knorpelbelag ohne tief greifende Chondropathie. Die Menisken sind intakt. Vorderes und hinteres Kreuzband intakt. Kollateralbänder ebenfalls intakt. Geringer Reizzustand des MCL am tibialen Ansatz. Kein Gelenkerguss. Synovialis schlank. Kein Gelenkerguss. Keine vermehrte Flüssigkeit in den Sehnenscheiden. Die miterfassten muskulären und tendinösen Strukturen stellen sich unauffällig dar. Geringe Flüssigkeitseinlagerungen in die Subcutis.
translation:
Normal articulation of the left knee joint. Evidence of a non-displaced fracture of the medial tibial plateau with a predominantly horizontal fracture course and a vertical component extending anteriorly to the anterior horn root of the medial meniscus (8/13 or 5/7). Adjacent bone bruise in the medial tibial plateau. Otherwise no further bone marrow edema.

The patella is centered. With only mild superficial chondral lesions (e.g., 7/10). No deep chondropathy at the trochlea.

Preserved cartilage covering femorotibially without deep chondropathy. The menisci are intact. Anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments intact. Collateral ligaments also intact. Mild irritation of the MCL at the tibial insertion. No joint effusion. Synovium is thin. No joint effusion. No increased fluid in the tendon sheaths. The included muscular and tendinous structures appear unremarkable. Mild fluid accumulation in the subcutaneous tissue.

report: Flächige Ausdünnung des Gelenkknorpels in der medialen femorotibialen Belastungszone ohne höhergradige oder vollschichtige Läsion, passend zu einer beginnenden medialen Gonarthrose.  Ligamentäre Strukturen intakt. Rundliche, zystisch imponierende Struktur pararezessal an der Basis des Außenmeniskusvorderhorns, DD Meniskusganglion (3, 103). Diskrete Signalanhebung innerhalb des Hinterhorns des Innenmeniskus (5, 6), a.e. vereinbar mit mukoiden Veränderungen. Im Übrigen unauffällige Signalgebung.
translation: Diffuse thinning of the articular cartilage in the medial femorotibial weight-bearing zone without high-grade or full-thickness lesion, consistent with early medial gonarthrosis. Ligamentous structures intact. Round, cystic-appearing structure pararecessal at the base of the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus, DD meniscal ganglion (3, 103). Discrete signal increase within the posterior horn of the medial meniscus (5, 6), most likely compatible with mucoid changes. Otherwise unremarkable signal intensity.

report: МР находка: Костите, формиращи колянната става са с нормална форма и сигнална характеристика. Станият хрущял на фемура и тибията е съхранен. Кръстните връзки са със запазена цялост. МР данни за начални дегенеративни промени в задния рог на медиалния менискус. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. МР данни за пателарен тендинит. Лигаментът на пателата е със задебелен напречник, като в дисталната му трета достига до 9мм. В неговата структура на PDW TSE SPAIR серията се виждат хиперинтензни лезии, които са най-изразени около залавното му място за туберозитас тибие, както при пателарна тендинопатия.  МР данни за минимален ставен излив, разположен вентрално и зад лигамента на пателата. Нормално изобразяване на колатералните лигаменти. Патела, хрущял на пателата, ретинакулуми – б.о. Сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис – без особености. Изобразява се малка Бекерова киста с размери 29/9мм. Наличие на фабела. Заключение: МР данни за пателарна тендинопатия. Наличие на минимален ставен излив. Начални дегенеративни промени в задния рог на медиалния менискус. Бекерова киста.
translation: MRI findings: The bones forming the knee joint are of normal shape and signal characteristics. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia is preserved. The cruciate ligaments are intact. MRI findings of early degenerative changes in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Normal appearance of the lateral meniscus. MRI findings of patellar tendinitis. The patellar ligament is thickened in diameter, reaching up to 9 mm in its distal third. On the PDW TSE SPAIR sequence, hyperintense lesions are seen within its structure, most pronounced around its insertion at the tibial tuberosity, as in patellar tendinopathy. MRI findings of minimal joint effusion, located ventrally and posterior to the patellar ligament. Normal appearance of the collateral ligaments. Patella, patellar cartilage, retinacula – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon – unremarkable. A small Baker's cyst is visualized, measuring 29/9 mm. Presence of a fabella. Conclusion: MRI findings of patellar tendinopathy. Presence of minimal joint effusion. Early degenerative changes in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Baker's cyst.

report: SOL DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Medial menisküs posterior horn ve gövde kesimde grade II dejenerasyon izlendi.Lateral menisküs normaldir. Posterior çapraz bağ posterior komşuluğunda 10x8 mm boyutlu ganglion kisti izlenmektedir. Ön çapraz bağ ve arka çapraz bağ, lateral ve medial kollateral ligaman normaldir.Distal kuadriseps ve patellar tendonlar normaldir. Patella normal yerleşimlidir. Retinaküler devamsızlık yoktur. Eklemde sıvı artışı saptanmamıştır. Tibia interkondiler eminens anteriorunda anterior çapraz bağ yapışma düzeyinde subkortikal milimetrik kistler izlendi. Sonuç: Medial menisküste grade II meniskopati, tibia interkondiler eminenste subkortikal milimetrik kist.Diz eklemi posteriorda posterior çapraz bağ komşuluğunda ganglion kisti.
translation: LEFT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body segment of the medial meniscus. The lateral meniscus is normal. A ganglion cyst measuring 10x8 mm is observed in the posterior vicinity of the posterior cruciate ligament. The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. No joint effusion is detected. Subcortical millimetric cysts are observed at the anterior aspect of the tibial intercondylar eminence at the insertion level of the anterior cruciate ligament. Conclusion: Grade II meniscopathy in the medial meniscus, subcortical millimetric cyst in the tibial intercondylar eminence. Ganglion cyst in the posterior aspect of the knee joint in the vicinity of the posterior cruciate ligament.

report:
COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Right-sided knee pain.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Diminutive posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus, consistent with extensive complex tearing. The anterior horn shows intrasubstance degeneration without tear. The posterior root is barely perceptible consistent with extensive complex tear. There is peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body.

Barely perceptible posterior root of the lateral meniscus raising suspicion for complex tear of the posterior root of the lateral meniscus. No lateral meniscal extrusion. 

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with intrasubstance ganglion formation. Slight anterior tibial translation.

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the superficial fibers of the medial collateral ligament near the medial femoral condyle origin. The meniscotibial meniscal femoral component of the deep medial collateral ligament are intact. The posterior oblique ligament is intact.

Fibular collateral ligament is intact. Moderate popliteus tendinosis of the lateral femoral condylar attachment, without tear. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 15 mm, at the upper limit of normal. No patellofemoral subluxation.

There is focal full thickness cartilage denuding at the patellar apex with fissuring of articular cartilage at the patellar apex and extending along the medial patellar facet. There is diffuse full-thickness cartilage denuding throughout the weightbearing aspect of the medial femorotibial compartment with subchondral sclerosis. There is mild to moderate lateral femorotibial chondrosis. Prominent non-marginal lateral femoral condylar osteophyte.

Trace knee joint fluid. Subcutaneous edema along the lateral and posterior aspects of the knee and proximal calf. There is generalized atrophy of the regional musculature which maybe on the basis of deconditioning. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

IMPRESSION:
1. Extensive complex tear involving the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with medial meniscal extrusion and tricompartment chondrosis as pronounced along the medial femorotibial compartment, consistent with severe medial compartment predominant tricompartment osteoarthritis of the right knee.
2. Suspected complex tear of the posterior root of the lateral meniscus without lateral meniscal extrusion.
3. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the superficial fibers of the medial collateral ligament. Components of the deep medial collateral ligament are intact.
4. Popliteus tendinosis without tear.
5. Borderline lateralization of the tibial tubercle which may predispose to patellofemoral maltracking/instability. No patellofemoral subluxation.
6. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with slight anterior tibial translation.

report:
Antecedentes Clínicos:
Tendinitis.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones en significativas de la médula ósea.
Transformación quística parcial del LCA, sin signos de rotura. LCP y ligamentos colaterales dentro
de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones
significativas.
Condropatía rotuliana superficial difusa.
No hay significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Leve aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital y de la inserción proximal del
tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura. Edema del paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital
suprarrotuliano.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Discreto edema de las partes blandas entre la banda iliotibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral.
Impresión:
Condropatía rotuliana superficial.
Leve tendinosis cuadricipital distal y rotuliana proximal.
Signos de un síndrome de fricción de la banda iliotibial.
Edema del paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital suprarrotuliano, hallazgo inespecífico, podría
representar fenómenos de mal alineamiento rotuliano
translation:
Clinical History:
Tendinitis.
Findings:
No significant bone marrow alterations.
Partial cystic transformation of the ACL, without signs of tear. PCL and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
Menisci with preserved morphology and signal, without signs of tear.
Cartilage of the femorotibial compartments and femoral trochlea without significant alterations.
Diffuse superficial patellar chondropathy.
No significant joint effusion or popliteal cysts.
Mild increased signal at the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon and at the proximal insertion of the patellar tendon, without signs of tear. Edema of the suprapatellar retroquadriceps fat pad.
Pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Mild soft tissue edema between the iliotibial band and the lateral femoral condyle.
Impression:
Superficial patellar chondropathy.
Mild distal quadriceps and proximal patellar tendinosis.
Signs of iliotibial band friction syndrome.
Edema of the suprapatellar retroquadriceps fat pad, nonspecific finding, could represent patellar malalignment phenomena.

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: [REDACTED]. Pain is at the anterior aspect.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Small tricompartmental marginal osteophyte formation.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Focal cartilage fissuring at the peripheral margin of the medial tibial plateau with associated subchondral edema.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade and full thickness fissuring of the lateral patellar facet with subchondral cystic change/edema. Signal heterogeneity of the trochlear cartilage.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Focal edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Mild tricompartmental osteoarthritis, most significant within the patellofemoral compartment with focal fissuring of the lateral patellar facet.
2.	Focal edema within the lateral Hoffa's fat pad suggestive of lateral patellofemoral maltracking.

EYΡΗΜΑΤΑ: - Φυσιολογικά απεικονίζονται οι µηνίσκοι, καθώς και οι χιαστοί και πλάγιοι σύνδεσµοι άµφω. - Φυσιολογική η απεικόνιση των αρθρικών επιφανειών του έξω και έσω µεσαρθρίου διαστήµατος, χωρίς αξιόλογες εκφυλιστικές αλλοιώσεις. - Παρατηρείται µικρό ύδραρθρο σε επικοινωνία µε συνοβιακή κύστη Baker κεφαλουραίας διαµέτρου 2,5εκ και ήπιο οίδηµα του υποδοριου λιπώδους ιστού προεπιγονατιδικά. - Από τον έλεγχο του εκτατικού µηχανισµού παρατηρείται υποπλασία του έσω µηριαίου κονδύλου και εικόνα αβαθούς τροχιλίας άµφω (sulcus angle ~160)°, µε παρουσία µερικού πάχους σχισµοειδών διαβρώσεων του αρθρικού χόνδρου της επιγονατίδας και υπαρθρικών µικροκυστικών αλλοιώσεων στην έσω και µέση αρθρική επιφάνεια της. translation:
TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1 sequences in the coronal plane and PDFS in three planes.

FINDINGS:
- The menisci, as well as the cruciate and collateral ligaments bilaterally, appear normal.
- Normal appearance of the articular surfaces of the lateral and medial compartments, without significant degenerative changes.
- A small joint effusion is observed in communication with a Baker's cyst of 2.5 cm craniocaudal diameter and mild edema of the subcutaneous fat tissue prepatellarly.

report: Erhaltene Artikulation im linken Knie. Deutliche T2 Signalanhebungen intraossär in der medialen Femurkondyle sowie etwas geringer auch subchondral im medialen Tibiaplateau. Ansonsten unauffälliges Knochenmarkssignal. Geringe oberflächliche Chondropathie retropatellar (z.B. 7/11). Vollschichtig, flächige Chondropathie im medialen femorotibialen Kompartiment (z. B. 4/17). In der medialen Femurkondyle kleinzystische Veränderungen (4/17). Im lateralen femorotibialen Kompartiment keine wesentliche Chondropathie. Außenmeniskushinterhorn geringe signalalteriert. Kein Nachweis einer Rissbildung. Der Innenmeniskus ausgeprägt mukoide T2 signalalteriert und aufgefasert mit Extrusion in der Pars intermedia und Hinterhorn bei komplexer Rissbildung mit unter anderem vollständiger radiärer Komponente nahe der Hinterhornwurzel (z. B. 3/98). Kleine parameniskale Zysten (z. B. 4/22). Kreuzbänder und Kollateralbänder intakt. Geringer Gelenkerguss. Synovia verdickt und unscharf, DD bei Reiz Synovialitis. Umgebende Muskulatur und Subkutis unauffällig.
translation: Preserved articulation in the left knee. Marked T2 signal elevation intraosseously in the medial femoral condyle and somewhat less also subchondrally in the medial tibial plateau. Otherwise unremarkable bone marrow signal. Mild superficial chondropathy retropatellar (e.g., 7/11). Full-thickness, diffuse chondropathy in the medial femorotibial compartment (e.g., 4/17). Small cystic changes in the medial femoral condyle (4/17). No significant chondropathy in the lateral femorotibial compartment. Lateral meniscus posterior horn mildly signal-altered. No evidence of a tear. The medial meniscus is markedly mucoid T2 signal-altered and frayed with extrusion in the pars intermedia and posterior horn with complex tear formation including a complete radial component near the posterior horn root (e.g., 3/98). Lateral compartment cartilage: There is a full-thickness chondrosis in the central weightbearing aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and lateral plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Large areas of full-thickness cartilage loss in the lateral patellar facet and median ridge with subchondral marrow edema and cystic changes. Areas of full thickness fissuring the lateral trochlea with subchondral cystic changes.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Chronic full thickness tear
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Chronic full thickness tear

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Bowed from medial compartment pathology.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Bowed from lateral compartment pathology
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Severe tricompartmental knee osteoarthritis.

2. Complex macerated tears of the medial and lateral menisci.

3. Chronic full-thickness tears of the ACL and PCL.

translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: A bucket-handle tear is observed in the lateral meniscus. The medial meniscus is extruded 4.5 mm medially from the knee joint space. Grade II degeneration is noted in the posterior horn and body segment of the meniscus, with a horizontal tear at the free edge. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Thickening and increased signal secondary to mucoid degeneration are observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. Periligamentous edema is noted in the medial collateral ligament. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and the knee joint space. Joint space narrowing is present in the medial tibiofemoral compartment, with millimetric osteophytic spurring at the corners of the bone structures adjacent to the joint. Thinning and destruction of the femoral and tibial cartilage are observed at this level. A Baker's cyst measuring 2.5 x 1 cm is noted in the popliteal fossa.
CONCLUSION: Gonarthrosis. Medial extrusion and grade II meniscopathy of the medial meniscus. Bucket-handle tear of the lateral meniscus. Mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Suprapatellar bursitis, synovitis of the knee joint.

report: Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı orta derecede artmış. Çapraz ve yan bağlar normal. Suprapateller resesteki sinovyal (kısmen lipomatö özellikteki) villpnodüler proliferasyon lipoma arboresens ile uyumlu. Diz eklemindeki trikompartmantal dejeneratif eklem hastalığı medyal femoral tibyal eklemde en belirgin ve tam kat eklem kıkırdağı kaybına eşlik eden subkortikal medüller fibrovasküler-fibrokistik değişikliklerin yanı sıra marjinal osteofitler ile karakterize. Diz ekleminin medyalindeki iç yan bağ dış yüzeyi komşuluğundaki 4 cm çaplı 6 mm kalınlıktaki lobüle konturlu septasyonlar içeren muhtemel kistik lezyon gangliyon kistini telkin ediyor. Lateral menisküs dejenerasyonu yırtık biçiminde eklem yüzeylerine uzanmıyor. Medyal menisküs medyale 5 mm ekstrüde ve arka boynuz-gövdesindeki dejenerasyon üst ve alt eklem yüzeylerine uzanan yırtık bileşenleri olan kompleks yırtıklar ile birlikte. Ekstensör mekanizma korunmuş. Proksimal tibyofibular eklem normal.
translation: The amount of intra-articular fluid in the knee joint is moderately increased. The cruciate and collateral ligaments are normal. Synovial villonodular proliferation (partly lipomatous in character) in the suprapatellar recess is consistent with lipoma arborescens. Tricompartmental degenerative joint disease of the knee is most pronounced in the medial femorotibial joint and is characterized by marginal osteophytes as well as subcortical medullary fibrovascular-fibrocystic changes accompanying full-thickness articular cartilage loss. A probable cystic lesion measuring 4 cm in diameter and 6 mm in thickness with lobulated contours and septations, adjacent to the outer surface of the medial collateral ligament on the medial side of the knee joint, suggests a ganglion cyst. Lateral meniscus degeneration does not extend to the articular surfaces in the form of a tear. The medial meniscus is extruded 5 mm medially, and degeneration in the posterior horn-body is accompanied by complex tears with tear components extending to the superior and inferior articular surfaces. The extensor mechanism is preserved. The proximal tibiofibular joint is normal.

translation:
Clinical History:
Right knee pain.
Findings:
Thinning appearing sequela of the ACL. Correlate with clinical findings.
PCL and lateral collateral ligament without alterations. Mild thickening appearing sequela of the superficial component of the medial collateral ligament. The remaining components of the medial complex without alterations.
Increased signal at the meniscocapsular junction of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus that could represent a regional partial tear.
Complex tear at the junction of the posterior horn with the posterior meniscal root of the lateral meniscus, without significant displacement of segments.
Full-thickness chondral ulceration of the posterior aspect of the weight-bearing zone of the lateral femoral condyle measuring 8 x 5 mm in its anteroposterior and mediolateral axes respectively, with secondary bone changes. Focal full-thickness chondral ulcerations with secondary bone changes at the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau associated with bone edema and regional subcortical fracture.
No significant joint effusion or popliteal cysts.
Quadriceps tendon, pes anserinus, biceps femoris tendon and iliotibial band within normal limits. Mild increased signal of the proximal third of the patellar tendon, without signs of tear.
Impression:
Thinning appearing sequela of the ACL, correlate with clinical findings. Associated bone edema and small subcortical fracture of the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau that could represent an instability event.
Complex tear at the junction of the posterior horn with the posterior meniscal root of the lateral meniscus.
Increased signal at the meniscocapsular junction of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus that could represent a regional partial tear.
Chondropathy with grade 4 lesions of the posterior aspect of the weight-bearing zone of the lateral femorotibial compartment.

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.16 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is intense bone marrow edema within the medial femoral condyle with a subchondral crescent of low signal at the central weightbearing aspect, consistent with a subchondral insufficiency fracture. There is no significant articular surface collapse. No evidence of osteonecrosis. Mild degenerative subchondral cystic change is present at the inferior patella. Background bone marrow signal is otherwise normal. 

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small, ruptured Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a large radial tear at the posterior root attachment. Moderate extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Mild to moderate cartilage thinning/fissuring diffusely.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: There is fraying of the inner margin along the body and posterior horn. Small tear at the posterior root attachment.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Cartilage appears intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is moderate to severe cartilage loss at the patella and trochlea, with mild subchondral cystic change.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intact, with surrounding edema compatible with hyperemia related to adjacent medial compartment disease.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 8 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Diffuse periarticular soft tissue edema, most prominent medially.

IMPRESSION:

1. Subchondral insufficiency fracture at the weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle.
2. Tear at the posterior root attachment of the medial meniscus with moderate extrusion. Small tear of the lateral meniscus.
3. Chondrosis in the patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartment.
4. Small, ruptured Baker cyst.

RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body segment of the medial meniscus. Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Mild fluid increase is observed in the suprapatellar bursa. Signal intensities of the bony structures forming the knee joint are normal.
Conclusion: Grade II meniscopathy in the medial and lateral menisci. Myxoid degeneration in the anterior cruciate ligament. Mild suprapatellar bursitis.

translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Degenerative changes are observed in the bony structures forming the knee joint. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior and posterior horns of the lateral meniscus. A grade III tear and extrusion beyond the joint space are noted in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Additionally, a suspicious appearance for a root tear is observed in the medial meniscus. Increased effusion is noted in the joint space and suprapatellar bursa, and a plica appearance is noted in the suprapatellar bursa. A Baker's cyst is observed in the popliteal fossa.

report: Τεχνική: Η εξέταση πραγµατοποιήθηκε µε ακολουθίες παλµών Τ1, πυκνότητας πρωτονίων µε καταστολή του σήµατος του λίπους και Τ2 βαθµιδωτής ηχούς υψηλής ευκρινείας. Ευρήµατα: - Παρατηρείται έντονο οστεοµυελικό οίδηµα στην πρόσθια επιφάνεια του έσω µηριαίου κονδύλου καθώς και στην πρόσθια επιφάνεια του έσω κνηµιαίου κονδύλου, µε συνοδές περιεχόµενες περιοχές χαµηλής έντασης σήµατοςσε Τ1 ακολουθία που πιθανολογούν την παρουσία µικροδοκιδωδων καταγµάτων. Ηπιο οστεοµυελικό οίδηµα αναγνωρίζεται επίσης στην οπίσθια επιφάνεια του έσω και έξω κνηµιαίου κονδύλου. - Από τον έλεγχο του εκτατικού µηχανισµού παρατηρείται έντονο παθολογικό σήµα πέριξ του ασαφοποιηµένου έσω καθεκτικού συνδέσµου της επιγονατίδας, η οποία ελέγχεται σε ήπια έξω πλάγια υπεξαρθρηµατική θέση. Συνυπάρχει διάχυτο παθολογικό σήµα στον έσω πλατύ µύ παρακείµενα του προαναφερθέντος οστικού οιδήµατος. Τα ανωτέρω είναι απότοκα κάκωσης ισούψώς µε συνοδό ρήξη του έσω καθεκτικού συνδέσµου. Μικρές αιµορραγικές συλλογές επιπολής του έσω καθεκτικού συνδέσµου. Οριακά υψηλή θέση της επιγονατίδας (patella alta - Insall-salvai index 1,5) και αβαθής τροχιλία. - Αναγνωρίζεται ικανή ποσότητα ύδραρθου. - Ο αρθρικός χόνδρος, οι µηνίσκοι, οι χιαστοί και πλάγιοι σύνδεσµοι ελέγχονται χωρίς παθολογικά ευρήµατα. Ακέραια ελέγχεται η λαγονοκνηµιαία ταινία. - Παρουσία επικουρικού οσταρίου παρά την κεφαλή της περόνης (parafibula).
translation:
Technique: The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat suppression, and high-resolution T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

Findings:
- Intense bone marrow edema is observed on the anterior surface of the medial femoral condyle as well as on the anterior surface of the medial tibial condyle, with accompanying areas of low signal intensity on T1 sequence suggesting the presence of microtrabecular fractures. Mild bone marrow edema is also identified on the posterior surface of the medial and lateral tibial condyle.
- On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, intense pathological signal is observed around the indistinct medial patellofemoral ligament, with the patella examined in mild lateral subluxation. There is coexisting diffuse pathological signal in the vastus medialis adjacent to the aforementioned bone edema. The above findings are consistent with a patellar dislocation injury with accompanying rupture of the medial patellofemoral ligament. Small hemorrhagic collections superficial to the medial patellofemoral ligament. Borderline high position of the patella (patella alta – Insall-Salvati index 1.5) and shallow trochlea.
- A significant amount of joint effusion is identified.
- The articular cartilage, the menisci, the cruciate and collateral ligaments are examined without pathological findings. The iliotibial band is intact.
- Presence of an accessory ossicle adjacent to the fibular head (parafibula).

report:
Interprétation :

Minime épanchement intra-articulaire d’allure physiologique. Liséré de liquide au sein du récessus poplité sans kyste de Baker significatif.

Les ménisques interne et externe sont intacts sans déchirure. Le ménisque externe est légèrement discoïde.

Le ligament collatéral interne, le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe, les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts sans déchirure. Légère infiltration kystique ganglionnaire au sein du ligament croisé antérieur distal et en intra-osseux sous son insertion distale.

Légère atténuation des surfaces chondrales au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne et aspect légèrement hétérogène avec fissure chondrale superficielle le long du compartiment fémoro-tibial externe en lien avec une légère chondropathie. Foyer de chondropathie focale sévère le long de la surface portante du condyle fémoral interne avec fissure chondrale transfixiante et changements sous-chondraux réactionnels.

L’alignement patellofémoral est préservé. Les tendons du quadriceps distal et patellaire sont intacts sans déchirure. Légère tendinose du tendon patellaire proximal. Légère chondropathie diffuse au compartiment patellofémoral avec fibrillation chondrale superficielle et fissures plus marquées, partielle, le long de la facette patellaire externe et transfixiante le long de la facette patellaire interne avec début de changements sous-chondraux réactionnels, en lien avec des foyers de chondropathie respectivement modéré sévère.

Conclusion :

Il n’y a pas de dérangement interne (pas de déchirure méniscale ou ligamentaire significative). 

Pas d’épanchement intra-articulaire significatif. 

Légère chondropathie tricompartimentale avec foyer de chondropathie focale sévère le long de la surface portante du condyle fémoral interne et le long de la facette patellaire interne.
translation:
Interpretation:

Minimal intra-articular effusion of physiological appearance. Thin rim of fluid within the popliteal recess without significant Baker's cyst.

The medial and lateral menisci are intact without tear. The lateral meniscus is slightly discoid.

The medial collateral ligament, the lateral collateral ligament complex, and the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact without tear. Mild cystic ganglion infiltration within the distal anterior cruciate ligament and intraosseous beneath its distal insertion.

Mild attenuation of the chondral surfaces in the medial femorotibial compartment and slightly heterogeneous appearance with superficial chondral fissure along the lateral femorotibial compartment related to mild chondropathy. Focal severe chondropathy along the weight-bearing surface of the medial femoral condyle with full-thickness chondral fissure and reactive subchondral changes.

Patellofemoral alignment is preserved. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact without tear. Mild tendinosis of the proximal patellar tendon. Mild diffuse chondropathy in the patellofemoral compartment with superficial chondral fibrillation and more marked fissures, partial-thickness along the lateral patellar facet and full-thickness along the medial patellar facet with early reactive subchondral changes, related to moderate and severe chondropathy foci respectively.

Conclusion:

There is no internal derangement (no significant meniscal or ligamentous tear).

No significant intra-articular effusion.

Mild tricompartmental chondropathy with focal severe chondropathy along the weight-bearing surface of the medial femoral condyle and along the medial patellar facet.
