FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Moderate joint effusion. Small popliteal cyst. Large intra-articular organized soft tissue hematoma measuring 5.2 x 1.5 x 5.8 cm.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
High-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal medial collateral ligament with full-thickness tearing of the deep meniscofemoral ligament.
Longitudinal horizontal tear of the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with mild loss of substance of the posterior horn.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Complete avulsion of the biceps femoris from the fibular head associated with a large multiloculated soft tissue hematoma surrounding the tear extending along the lateral gastrocnemius muscle.
Complete avulsion of the popliteus tendon at its insertion on the lateral femoral condyle.
Severe edema and irregularity of the lateral collateral ligament proper with high-grade partial-thickness tear from its femoral attachment and complete avulsion from its fibular attachment.
No fracture of the fibular head is identified.

Longitudinal vertical tear of the peripheral posterior horn and body of lateral meniscus.
Diffuse chondral thinning without deep fissuring.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament. Avulsion of the posterior cruciate ligament from its femoral attachment.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Normal.

Bones:
Osteochondral impaction fracture of the medial femoral condyle/trochlea associated with underlying bone marrow reactive changes/contusions.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Diffuse edema of the visualized proximal anterior compartment of the leg muscles. Associated diffuse thickening and increased signal intensity of the common peroneal nerve suggesting traumatic injury without fiber discontinuity or transection.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:

1.Sequela of knee dislocation with complete tears of the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments.
2.Extensive injury of the posterolateral corner with complete avulsion of the lateral collateral ligament proper, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon as described above.
3.High-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal medial collateral ligament with complete tearing of the deep meniscofemoral ligament.
4.Longitudinal horizontal tear of the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with mild substance loss of the posterior horn.
5.Longitudinal vertical peripheral tear of the posterior horn and body of lateral meniscus compatible with a Wrisberg rip.
6.Osteochondral impaction fracture of the medial femoral condyle/trochlea associated with underlying bone marrow reactive changes/contusions.
7.Diffuse thickening and increased signal intensity of the common peroneal nerve suggesting low-grade traumatic injury without fiber discontinuity or transection. Associated denervation edema of the visualized anterior muscle compartment of the proximal leg.
8.Moderate knee joint effusion with large intra-articular organized hematoma

Lichte inflammatie van het superolaterale deel van de Hoffa vetpad, gelegen tussen proximale laterale deel van de patellapees enerzijds, en de anterieure zijde van de laterale femorale condyl anderzijds. T1 en T2 hypo-intens intra osseuze letsel van 6\~mm in het laterale tibiaplateau: boteiland . Besluit: - Complexe scheur van de posterieure hoorn van de mediale meniscus, gepaard gaand met matig botoedeem op de mediale boord van het mediale tibiaplateau. - Beperkte Hoffa vetpad impingement (patellar tendon lateral femoral condyle friction syndrome).
translation:
[DATE]: MR Knee Right 15ch
AA: Clinical information: See scanned request. Diagnostic question: See scanned request.
Findings:
Complex tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with large horizontal component, small vertical component peripherally, accompanied by extensive bone edema on the medial border of the medial tibial plateau. Moderate distension of the suprapatellar recess. Mild inflammation of the superolateral part of the Hoffa fat pad, located between the proximal lateral part of the patellar tendon on one side, and the anterior side of the lateral femoral condyle on the other side. T1 and T2 hypointense intraosseous lesion of 6~mm in the lateral tibial plateau: bone island.
Conclusion:
- Complex tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, accompanied by moderate bone edema on the medial border of the medial tibial plateau.
- Limited Hoffa fat pad impingement (patellar tendon lateral femoral condyle friction syndrome).

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse cartilage thinning weightbearing medial femoral condyle with focal high grade chondrosis near the intercondylar notch.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Mild edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. There is lateral patellar tilt without translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Findings suggestive of mild active lateral patellar maltracking.
2.	Mild medial compartment chondrosis.

Gonalgia en estudio. Dolor opaco poplíteo. Antecedentes de gonartrosis bilateral.

con segmento parcialmente desplazado hacia la región intercondílea posterior.

resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales y patelofemorales sin alteraciones.

tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.

Menisco lateral de morfología discoidea con extensa rotura y segmento parcialmente desplazado hacia la

Leve derrame articular. Pequeño quiste poplíteo complicado.

translation:
Clinical History:
Knee pain under investigation. Dull popliteal pain. History of bilateral gonarthrosis.
Findings:
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
Discoid lateral meniscus with extensive tear of the anterior horn, body, and posterior horn with a segment partially displaced toward the posterior intercondylar region.
Complex tear of the posterior meniscal root, posterior horn, and part of the body of the medial meniscus with moderate extrusion and edema of the regional soft tissues.
Diffuse bone marrow edema of the medial femoral condyle with an image suggestive of subcortical fracture of the anterior weight-bearing zone, without signs of articular collapse. This is associated with edema of the soft tissues surrounding the medial femoral condyle.
Partial-thickness chondral ulcers of the central region of the weight-bearing zone of the medial femoral condyle. The remaining femorotibial and patellofemoral cartilages are unremarkable.
Mild joint effusion with subtle diffuse synovitis. Small uncomplicated popliteal cyst.
Mild increased signal at the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon, without signs of tear. Patellar tendon, pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Impression:
Discoid lateral meniscus with extensive tear and a segment partially displaced toward the posterior intercondylar region.
Complex tear of the posterior meniscal root, posterior horn, and part of the body of the medial meniscus with moderate extrusion and edema of the adjacent soft tissues.
Diffuse bone marrow edema of the medial femoral condyle with an image suggestive of subcortical fracture in the anterior weight-bearing zone, without articular collapse, with edema of the regional soft tissues.
Chondropathy, grade 2 lesions of the central region of the medial femoral condyle.
Mild joint effusion. Small complicated popliteal cyst.
Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis.

translation:
Clinical History:
Obs. Lateral meniscal tear.
Findings:
Bone marrow of normal signal intensity.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments without alterations.
Lateral meniscus of normal morphology and signal without categorical criteria for tear.
Medial meniscus of normal morphology without criteria for tear.
Signal alteration and decreased thickness of the lateral femorotibial cartilage in the middle third of the weight-bearing surface with subtotal thickness defect, greater than 50% at the level of the lateral tibial plateau, without bone marrow edema. Similar findings with partial and subtotal thickness defects at the level of the medial femorotibial compartment.
Patellofemoral cartilage with diffuse signal alteration at the level of the patella with thickness defects greater than 50% at the level of the medial facet near the apex. Trochlear cartilage without significant chondral defects.
Mild external paracondylar inflammatory changes adjacent to the iliotibial band.
Quadriceps tendon, patellar tendon, pes anserinus tendons, biceps tendon and iliotibial band of normal thickness and signal intensity.
No joint effusion or Baker's cyst is observed. Edema of the prefemoral adipose tissue in its lateral aspect.
Impression:
Bicompartimental femorotibial chondropathy grade 2-3 with a focus of deep grade 3 chondropathy at the lateral tibial plateau.
Patellar chondropathy grade 3.
Signs of iliotibial band friction.
Edema of the prefemoral fat in its lateral aspect, may be in the context of a friction syndrome.

report:
MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] female with trauma during ski accident 1.5 weeks ago with persistent pain, swelling and limited range of motion of left knee.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

There is a complete tear of the midportion of the anterior cruciate ligament. No normal intact fibers are identified. There is a borderline anterior tibial drawer measured in the lateral joint compartment at about 5 mm. There are bone contusions seen at the lateral femoral sulcus in the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau consistent with kissing contusions related to a pivot shift mechanism of injury. There is a discrete region of linear low T1 signal along the posterior rim of the lateral tibial plateau which may indicate presence of an undisplaced lateral tibial plateau rim fracture.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

There is abnormal signal surrounding the medial collateral ligament at its origin along its course proximal to the medial joint line consistent with grade 2 sprain. There is significant disruption of the deep fibers with intact superficial fibers extending distally. The posterior oblique ligament appears intact. There is an associated partial thickness sprain of the femoral insertion of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact. There is some subtle increased signal seen in the proximal fibers of the fibular collateral ligament which could indicate presence of a low-grade sprain. The fibular collateral ligament, IT band, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon appear intact.

There is abnormal increased T2 signal seen in the periphery of the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body consistent with a meniscocapsular avulsion injury. No discrete surfacing meniscal tear is identified to the medial meniscus. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The extensor mechanism is intact. The lateral patellofemoral ligament is unremarkable. As noted the medial patellofemoral ligament at its femoral insertion demonstrates a partial thickness sprain. The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is reasonably well-maintained apart from some mild fissuring seen to the trochlear articular cartilage at the apex and involving the medial facet. Findings are consistent with moderate chondrosis.

No significant Baker's cyst is demonstrated.

There is a moderate to large knee effusion.

INTERPRETATION:
 
Complete anterior cruciate ligament tear with bone contusions corresponding to a pivot shift mechanism of injury and with possible undisplaced posterior tibial plateau fracturing. Plain film correlation is recommended.

Grade 2 medial collateral ligament sprain associated with partial-thickness sprain of the insertional fibers of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

Evidence of meniscocapsular injury to the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body with no discrete surfacing tear identified.

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Moderate knee effusion.

Findings are consistent with moderate chondrosis.

No significant Baker's cyst is demonstrated.

There is a moderate to large knee effusion.

Complete anterior cruciate ligament tear with bone contusions corresponding to a pivot shift mechanism of injury and with possible undisplaced posterior tibial plateau fracturing. Plain film correlation is recommended.

Grade 2 medial collateral ligament sprain associated with partial-thickness sprain of the insertional fibers of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

Evidence of meniscocapsular injury to the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body with no discrete surfacing tear identified.

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Moderate knee effusion.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Mild interval reduction in moderate joint effusion. No popliteal cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Unchanged multidirectional tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with longitudinal horizontal and complete radial components. Unchanged mild meniscal extrusion. Unchanged displacement of the posterior medial meniscal root into the medial aspect of the intercondylar notch. This represents an unstable meniscal tear.
Normal medial collateral ligament. Partial-thickness fissuring of medial compartment articular cartilage.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Normal meniscus. Normal lateral collateral ligament complex. Unchanged partial-thickness chondral fissuring within the lateral compartment.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Unchanged complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is approximately 9 mm of anterior tibial translation. Normal posterior cruciate ligament.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Partial-thickness chondral fissuring within the medial and lateral patellar facet articular cartilage.
Normal extensor mechanism. Normal fat pads.

Bones:
Interval resolution of bone marrow edema previously seen within the posterolateral tibial plateau

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Small T1 hyperintense fluid collection within the muscle belly of the medial head of gastrocnemius measuring maximally up to 1 cm in craniocaudal dimension, is likely a small intramuscular hematoma.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
1.No significant interval change other than for resolution of posterolateral tibial plateau bone marrow edema compared to the previous MRI.
2.Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
3.Unchanged unstable tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with displacement of the posterior medial meniscal root into the medial intercondylar notch.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Complex tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus which appears diminutive and irregular, extending into the body. There is peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The posterior root and anterior horn are intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

Medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact. The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. Moderate popliteus tendinosis without tear. The iliotibial band is intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. No patellofemoral subluxation. The TT-TG distance measures 4 mm, within normal limits.

Mild quadriceps insertional tendinosis without tear. The patellar tendon is intact.

Preserved patellofemoral articular cartilage. Focal full thickness cartilage denuding posterior nonweightbearing aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. The remainder of the lateral femorotibial articular cartilage is preserved. There is subtle thinning of articular cartilage involving the peripheral posterior aspect of the medial tibial plateau. The remainder of the medial femorotibial articular cartilage is preserved.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex tear posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with medial meniscal extrusion.
2. Popliteus tendinosis without tear. Quadriceps tendinosis without tear.
3. Focal areas of medial and lateral femorotibial chondrosis as detailed above.

report:
Interprétation :

Minime liséré de liquide au sein du récessus supra-patellaire sans épanchement intra-articulaire significatif. Kyste de Baker multi-lobulé et allongé s’étendant jusqu’à 8cm de diamètre CC. Pas d’évidence de complication ou signe de rupture.

Légère anomalie de signal linéaire iso-intense d’allure horizontale longitudinale s’étendant de la corne postérieure au corps méniscal et impliquant la surface articulaire supérieure, suggérant une déchirure d’allure chronique. Minimes changements dégénératifs mucoïdes par ailleurs.

Le ligament collatéral interne est intact sans déchirure. 

Légère atténuation des surfaces chondrales au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne sans atteinte transfixiante.

Petite déchirure radiaire partielle focale au rebord libre à la jonction de la corne antérieure et du corps du ménisque externe. Le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe est intact sans déchirure.

Légère atténuation des surfaces chondrales, en particulier la surface portante du compartiment fémoro-tibial externe sans atteinte transfixiante.

Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts sans déchirure. Petit kyste ganglionnaire intra-osseux sous l’insertion distale du ligament croisé antérieur.

Artéfacts de susceptibilité magnétique en projection du rétinaculum interne et des tissus sous-cutanés. À corréler cliniquement. Est-ce qu’il y a déjà eu une intervention chirurgicale locale à ce niveau ?

La rotule est hautement située avec une légère patella alta suspectée. Il y a un petit foyer d’œdème au versant supéro-externe de la graisse de Hoffa suggérant un syndrome de friction du tendon patellaire et du condyle fémoral externe.

Il y a une atténuation diffuse modérée des surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment patellofémoral avec une atteinte transfixiante le long de l’apex patellaire et de la facette patellaire externe, avec changements réactionnels sous-chondraux associés, en lien avec une chondropathie sévère. Petits ostéophytes marginaux au compartiment patellofémoral avec petit kyste adjacent à l’extrémité externe de la facette trochléaire externe.

Légère tendinose du quadriceps distal sans déchirure. Le tendon patellaire est intact sans déchirure.

Conclusion :

Déchirure longitudinale horizontale d’allure chronique à la corne postérieure et au corps du ménisque interne.

Petite déchirure focale radiaire au rebord libre à la jonction de la corne antérieure et du corps du ménisque externe.

Légère chondropathie au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne et externe.

Chondropathie modérée à sévère au compartiment patellofémoral avec atteinte sévère, transfixiante à l’apex patellaire et le long de la facette patellaire externe tel que détaillé ci-haut.

Légère patella alta suspectée avec petit foyer d’œdème au versant supéro-externe de la graisse de Hoffa suggérant un syndrome d’accrochage de la graisse de Hoffa/syndrome de friction du tendon patellaire et du condyle fémoral externe.

Pas d’épanchement intra-articulaire significatif. Kyste de Baker allongé non-compliqué tel que décrit ci-haut.
translation:
Interpretation:

Minimal rim of fluid within the suprapatellar recess without significant intra-articular effusion. Multi-lobulated and elongated Baker's cyst extending up to 8 cm in CC diameter. No evidence of complication or sign of rupture.

Mild linear iso-intense signal abnormality with a horizontal longitudinal orientation extending from the posterior horn to the meniscal body and involving the superior articular surface, suggesting a chronic-appearing tear. Minimal mucoid degenerative changes elsewhere.

The medial collateral ligament is intact without tear.

Mild attenuation of the chondral surfaces in the medial femorotibial compartment without full-thickness defect.

Small focal partial radial tear at the free edge at the junction of the anterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus. The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact without tear.

Mild attenuation of the chondral surfaces, particularly the weight-bearing surface of the lateral femorotibial compartment without full-thickness defect.

The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact without tear. Small intraosseous ganglion cyst beneath the distal insertion of the anterior cruciate ligament.

Magnetic susceptibility artifacts in projection of the medial retinaculum and subcutaneous tissues. Clinical correlation recommended. Has there been prior local surgical intervention at this level?

The patella is high-riding with mild patella alta suspected. There is a small focus of edema at the superolateral aspect of Hoffa's fat pad suggesting a friction syndrome between the patellar tendon and the lateral femoral condyle.

There is moderate diffuse attenuation of the cartilaginous surfaces in the patellofemoral compartment with a full-thickness defect along the patellar apex and the lateral patellar facet, with associated subchondral reactive changes, consistent with severe chondropathy. Small marginal osteophytes in the patellofemoral compartment with a small cyst adjacent to the lateral end of the lateral trochlear facet.

Mild tendinosis of the distal quadriceps without tear. The patellar tendon is intact without tear.

Conclusion:

Chronic-appearing horizontal longitudinal tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus.

Small focal radial tear at the free edge at the junction of the anterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus.

Mild chondropathy in the medial and lateral femorotibial compartments.

Moderate to severe chondropathy in the patellofemoral compartment with severe full-thickness defect at the patellar apex and along the lateral patellar facet as detailed above.

Mild patella alta suspected with a small focus of edema at the superolateral aspect of Hoffa's fat pad suggesting Hoffa's fat pad impingement syndrome / friction syndrome between the patellar tendon and the lateral femoral condyle.

No significant intra-articular effusion. Elongated uncomplicated Baker's cyst as described above.

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: pain effusion; bilateral knee pain for one month, no known injury
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Multifocal areas of subchondral edema along the lateral tibial plateau and femoral condyles.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with synovitis. No intra-articular bodies. Small, ruptured Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Periligamentous edema about the lateral collateral ligament with intact fibers.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.  

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 16 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
Edema of the popliteus muscle. No muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Moderate joint effusion with synovitis as well as subchondral marrow edema along both tibial plateau and femoral condyles and edema of the posterolateral corner. Findings are concerning for early inflammatory arthritis, for which aspiration should be considered.

No significant knee joint effusion, there is however intra-articular fluid within the superomedial and to a lesser extent inferomedial recesses of the knee knee joint.  
Grossly intact lateral meniscus, allowing for mild mucoid degeneration at the level of the body.  Normal cruciate and collateral ligaments, popliteus, extensor tendons and the distal iliotibial band.  Mild distal femoral trochlear dysplasia with no associated patellofemoral articular cartilage damage. 
Well-maintained medial and lateral tibiofemoral articular cartilage surfaces. No marrow signal abnormality of concern, mild edema like signal change noted within the prepatellar soft tissues with no discrete bursal formation.

report: SAĞ DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Lateral menisküs  normaldir. Medial menisküste grade II dejenerasyon izlendi. Medial menisküs posterior hornunda volüm kaybı ve radyal yırtık ile uyumlu görünüm mevcuttur. Ayrıca medial menüsküs laterale doğru 5 mm ekstrüde görünümdedir.Arka çapraz bağ komşuluğunda ve gastokinemius medial kurus tendonu komşuluklarında büyüğü 2cm çapta multiseptalı lobule konturlu kistler izlendi ( ganglion kisti ).Arka çapraz baş  lateral ve medial kollateral ligaman normaldir. Ön çapraz bağda diffüz sinyal artışıı ve dejenerasyon mevcuttur(mukoid dejenerasyon?).Distal kuadriseps ve patellar tendonlar normaldir. Patella normal yerleşimlidir. Retinaküler devamsızlık yoktur.Suprapatellar bursada sıvı artışı izlenmiştir. Tibia interkondiler tüberkulum emincia ve anterior çapraz bağ yapışma lokalizasyonlarında subkondral kemik iliği ödemi ve dejeneratif kistler izlenmiştir. Femur inter kondiler düzeyde subkondral milimetrik kistler izlendi. Diz eklemini oluşturan kemik yapılarda osteofitik değişiklikler özellikle medialde eklem mesafesinde daralma ve subkondral skleroz bulguları izlenmiştir ( dejeneratif artrit bulguları ).
translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings:
The lateral meniscus is normal. Grade II degeneration is observed in the medial meniscus. There is volume loss and an appearance consistent with a radial tear in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Additionally, the medial meniscus appears extruded laterally by 5 mm. Multiseptated, lobulated-contoured cysts, the largest measuring 2 cm in diameter, are observed in the vicinity of the posterior cruciate ligament and the medial head of the gastrocnemius tendon (ganglion cyst). The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral collateral ligament, and medial collateral ligament are normal. There is diffuse signal increase and degeneration in the anterior cruciate ligament (mucoid degeneration?). The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa. Subchondral bone marrow edema and degenerative cysts are observed at the tibial intercondylar eminence and at the attachment sites of the anterior cruciate ligament. Subchondral millimetric cysts are observed at the femoral intercondylar level. Osteophytic changes in the bony structures forming the knee joint, with narrowing of the joint space particularly medially and subchondral sclerosis, are observed (findings of degenerative arthritis).

report: ΤΕΧΝΙΚΗ: Η εξέταση πραγματοποιήθηκε με ακολουθίες Τ1, πυκνότητας πρωτονίων με καταστολή του σήματος του λίπους και Τ2 βαθμιδωτής ηχούς. ΙΣΤΟΡΙΚΟ: Άλγος γόνατος από μηνών, μη υφιόμενιο με ενδαρθρικές εγχύσεις - παρακεντήσεις, πιθανό ρευματολογικό νόσημα ΕΥΡΗΜΑΤΑ - Αν και η εξέταση πραγματοποιήθηκε χωρίς την εφ χορήγηση παραμαγνητικής ουσίας (λόγω αναφερόμενης αλλεργίας σε αυτή), δίδεται η εντύπωση αξιολογήσιμης πάχυνσης του υμένα (υμενίτιδας), ενώ τονίζεται η παρουσία ενδαρθρικής συλλογής με περιεχόμενα ελεύθερα μικροσκοπικά στοιχεία χαμηλής έντασης σήματος. - Σημειώνεται διάβρωση σε μη φορτιζόμενη μοίρα του έσω μηριαίου κονδύλου, οπισθίως και σε "γυμνή" περιοχή, με συνοδό μικρής έκτασης οίδημα παρακείμενου οστικού μυελού. Τα εν λόγω ευρήματα θα μπορούσαν να αποδοθούν καταρχάς σε φλεγμονώδη αρθρίτιδα (είτε Ρ.Α. ή και axSpA). - Χωρίς παθολογικά ευρήματα από τους χιαστούς / πλαγίους συνδέσμους, τους μηνίσκους και τον αρθρικό χόνδρο. - Χωρίς ευρήματα δυσλειτουργίας εκτατικού μηχανισμού.
translation:
TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo sequences.
HISTORY: Knee pain for months, not subsiding with intra-articular injections – aspirations, possible rheumatological disease.
FINDINGS:
- Although the examination was performed without the administration of paramagnetic contrast agent (due to reported allergy to it), there is the impression of appreciable synovial thickening (synovitis), while the presence of an intra-articular effusion containing free microscopic low signal intensity elements is emphasized.
- Erosion is noted in a non-weight-bearing portion of the medial femoral condyle, posteriorly and in a "bare" area, with accompanying small extent edema of the adjacent bone marrow. These findings could primarily be attributed to inflammatory arthritis (either RA or axSpA).
- No pathological findings from the cruciate / collateral ligaments, the menisci, and the articular cartilage.
- No findings of extensor mechanism dysfunction.

Retinaküler devamsızlık yoktur.Patellar kıkırdakta yer yer incelme  ve komşu kemikte hafif subkondral kemik iliği ödemi izlenmiştir (medial fasette grade 3 lateral fasette grade 2 kondromalazi ).Suprapatellar bursada sıvı artışı, diz eklemi içerisinde sıvı artışı izlenmiştir.Tibia arka çapraz bağ ve ön çapraz bağ yapışma düzeyinde subkondral milimetrik kistler izlenmiştir.Diz eklemini oluşturan kemik yapılarda belirgin osteofitik değişiklikler, tibiofemoral diz eklemi aralığı mesafesinde daralma, kartilajlarda incelmeler mevcuttur . Ayrıca femur lateral kondil medial düzeyinde subkondral milimetrik kist ve kemik iliği ödemi izlenmiştir(dejeneratif artrit bulguları ).
translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings:
Grade III degeneration is present in the lateral meniscus. Maceration and a complex tear are observed in the medial meniscus, and the medial meniscus appears extruded. Signal increase consistent with mucoid degeneration is present in the anterior cruciate ligament. Diffuse signal increase is observed in the posterior cruciate ligament, with an appearance consistent with a partial tear at the distal level. The lateral collateral ligament is normal. Periligamentous edema is present around the medial collateral ligament (grade I sprain). The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Focal thinning of the patellar cartilage and mild subchondral bone marrow edema in the adjacent bone have been observed (grade 3 chondromalacia on the medial facet, grade 2 chondromalacia on the lateral facet). Increased fluid in the suprapatellar bursa and increased fluid within the knee joint have been observed. Subchondral millimetric cysts are observed at the tibial attachment levels of the posterior cruciate ligament and anterior cruciate ligament. Prominent osteophytic changes in the bony structures forming the knee joint, narrowing of the tibiofemoral joint space, and cartilage thinning are present. Additionally, a subchondral millimetric cyst and bone marrow edema are observed at the medial aspect of the lateral femoral condyle (findings of degenerative arthritis).

report: МР находка: МР данни за дегенеративна промяна и скъсване в областта на задния рог на медалния менискус. Задният рог на медиалния менискус е с повишен сигнален интензитет и е уголемен. В него се изобразява хиперинтензна линия, съответстваща на скъсване, достигаща до края на менискуса. МР данни за медианна гонартроза. Ставният хрущял на фемура и тибията от медиалната страна е изтънен и е с неравни контурни очертания. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. Не се намират изменения в ставния хрущял от латералната страна на ставата и на пателата. Наличие на ставен излив. Вижда се голяма мултилокуларна Бекерова киста с размер 57/36мм. Част от кистата е руптурирала – изобразява се течна колекция под нея, около сухожилията и мускулните групи  на м. семимебранозус и м. семитендинозус. МР данни за частично скъсване на залавното място на сухожилието на м. семимебранозус. Костите формиращи лявата колянна става са с нормална форма и сигнална характеристика.  Кръстни връзки – със запазена цялост. Колатерални лигаменти – нормално изобразяване. Ретинакулуми – б.о. Сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис и лигамент на пателата – б.о. Заключение:  МР данни за медианна гонартроза. Дегенеративна промяна и grade III лезия на задния рог на медиалния менискус. Ставен излив. Мултилокуларна Бекерова киста, частично руптурирала.  Частично скъсване на залавното място на сухожилието на м. семимебранозус.
translation: MRI findings: MRI findings of degenerative change and tear in the region of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. The posterior horn of the medial meniscus shows increased signal intensity and is enlarged. A hyperintense line is visualized within it, corresponding to a tear, reaching the meniscal surface. MRI findings of medial gonarthrosis. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia on the medial side is thinned and has irregular contour outlines. Normal appearance of the lateral meniscus. No changes are found in the articular cartilage on the lateral side of the joint and of the patella. Presence of joint effusion. A large multilocular Baker's cyst is seen measuring 57/36 mm. Part of the cyst has ruptured – a fluid collection is visualized beneath it, around the tendons and muscle groups of the semimembranosus and semitendinosus muscles. MRI findings of partial tear at the insertion site of the semimembranosus tendon. The bones forming the left knee joint are of normal shape and signal characteristics. Cruciate ligaments – with preserved integrity. Collateral ligaments – normal appearance. Retinacula – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon and patellar ligament – unremarkable. Conclusion: MRI findings of medial gonarthrosis. Degenerative change and grade III lesion of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Joint effusion. Multilocular Baker's cyst, partially ruptured. Partial tear at the insertion site of the semimembranosus tendon.

Longitudinalna ruptura posteromedijalnog aspekta crvene zone medijalnog meniska uz edem

translation:
The visualized bony structures are of normal morphology.
A larger zone of bone marrow edema in the region of the lateral femoral condyle and a smaller zone of bone marrow edema in the region of the lateral tibial plateau - likely post-contusion.
The visualized articular bodies are appropriately articulated.
Chondromalacia grade I of the condylar and tibial cartilage of the lateral compartment. Signal intensities of the remaining visualized articular cartilages are normal.
The anterior cruciate ligament shows signs of distension with reduced tension of part of the fibers of the posterolateral bundle, consistent with a partial tear at the tibial insertion.
The posterior cruciate ligament is of normal signal intensity and intact continuity.
The lateral meniscus shows no signs of tear or degeneration.
Longitudinal tear of the posteromedial aspect of the red zone of the medial meniscus with edema of the posteromedial joint capsule - the finding corresponds to a "ramp" lesion.
The lateral collateral ligament is of normal signal intensity, with intact continuity.
The medial collateral ligament shows increased signal intensity, in the region of the middle third it is more inhomogeneous in appearance, and edema is visible in the surrounding soft tissues. The finding is consistent with a significant partial tear of the ligament.
Normal appearance of the popliteus tendon, iliotibial tract, and pes anserinus.
The quadriceps tendon and patellar ligament are of normal signal intensity, with intact continuity.
The patellar retinacula are intact.
A small amount of effusion in the suprapatellar recess.
A popliteal cyst measuring 7 mm in diameter.

translation:

Findings:

translation:

translation:
MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1 pulse sequences, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo.

FINDINGS:
There is an area of low signal on T1 sequence (1.2 x 0.7 cm) in the region of the medial femoral condyle – medial compartment, subchondrally, with a fracture line on PdFS sequence and surrounding bone marrow edema. The findings are attributed to a microtrabecular insufficiency fracture (synonym of "spontaneous osteonecrosis"). There is coexisting reactive edema of the medial collateral ligament. A similar lesion, of lesser extent, is observed in the lateral portion, near the midline, of the tibial epiphysis. Increased amount of intra-articular fluid is noted. The lateral meniscus is depicted with diffusely increased signal in the setting of a degenerative tear. The medial meniscus is depicted subluxated, with diffusely increased signal mainly in the posterior horn and body in the setting of a degenerative tear. A few erosions of the patellofemoral joint are observed with mild thinning of the cartilage at the same level in the setting of early osteoarthritis. The cruciate ligaments and the lateral collateral ligament appear normal.

translation:
LEFT KNEE
On evaluation of the menisci, simple degeneration without tear is observed. The articular cartilage in the medial and lateral compartments has satisfactory appearance. On evaluation of the anterior compartment, lateral subluxation of the patella is observed, with erosion of the articular cartilage ICRS grade 4, presence of small subchondral bone marrow lesions, and accompanying joint effusion.
Conclusion: The findings are consistent with degenerative osteoarthritis of the patellofemoral joint.

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.
FINDINGS
RIGHT KNEE
On evaluation of the lateral compartment, degenerative tear of the lateral meniscus and subluxation of the latter are observed, erosion of the articular cartilage ICRS grade 4, presence of marginal osteophytes, and small subchondral bone marrow lesions of the lateral femoral condyle. On evaluation of the medial compartment, degeneration of the meniscus without tear is observed, presence of osteophytes, and mild erosion of the articular cartilage. On evaluation of the anterior compartment, lateral subluxation of the patella is observed with erosion of the articular cartilage ICRS grade 4 at the lateral articular surface and presence of subchondral bone marrow lesions. Intra-articularly, joint effusion is observed with presence of small cartilaginous loose bodies. In the intercondylar notch, osteophytic formations are observed accompanied by myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament secondary to impingement syndrome. Additionally, on evaluation of the articular cartilage, extensive chondrocalcinosis is observed in the context of CPPD.
Conclusion: Degenerative osteoarthritis of the lateral and anterior compartments.

report: Hochgradige MCL-Ruptur sowie der ventromedialen Kapselstruktur mit insbesondere femoralseitig Ruptur der tiefen Anteilen (4/19) und auch aufgetriebene Elongation der oberflächlichen Anteile, diese teils auch im mittleren bis distalen Abschnitt gewellt verlaufend (4/20); zart unter den Pes anserinus verfolgbare Bandstruktur (4/18). Verletzung der posteromedialen Ecke bei Mitbeteiligung des POLs. VKB und HKB intakt. Menisken intakt. Oberflächliche Chondropathie retropatellar (7/11). Geringe T2-Signalanhebung in der lateralen Femurkondyle (4/12). Fokale Ödemzone auch tibial angrenzend an das proximale Tibiofibulargelenk. Begleitend geringer Hämarthros, kleine Plica mediopatellaris (3/33). Periartikulär dtl. Einblutungen, medial führend.
translation: High-grade MCL rupture as well as rupture of the ventromedial capsular structure, with in particular femoral-sided rupture of the deep fibers (4/19) and also swollen elongation of the superficial fibers, these partly running in a wavy course in the middle to distal segment (4/20); delicate band structure traceable beneath the pes anserinus (4/18). Injury of the posteromedial corner with involvement of the POL. ACL and PCL intact. Menisci intact. Superficial chondropathy retropatellar (7/11). Mild T2 signal elevation in the lateral femoral condyle (4/12). Focal edema zone also tibial, adjacent to the proximal tibiofibular joint. Accompanying mild hemarthrosis, small mediopatellar plica (3/33). Periarticular distinct hemorrhages, predominantly medial.

report: ΤΕΧΝΙΚΗ: Η εξέταση έγινε με ακολουθίες παλμών Τ1, Τ2 βαθμιδωτής ηχούς και πυκνότητας πρωτονίων με καταστολή του σήματος του λίπους. ΕΥΡΗΜΑΤΑ: - Αναγνωρίζεται εκφύλιση του αρθρικού χόνδρου αντίστοιχα με το έσω μεσάρθριο διάστημα (ICRS grade II). Συνυπάρχει περιεστιακό οστεομυελικό οίδημα στον έσω μηριαίο και κνημιαίο κόνδυλο. Επιπλέον, επιχείλια οστεόφυτα παρατηρούνται στο έσω διαμέρισμα του γόνατος. - Παρατηρείται εκφύλιση του χόνδρου της επιγονατίδας στο έσω τμημα της (ICRS grade II). Eπιπλέον, μικρά επιχείλια οστεόφυτα σημειούνται στην επιγονατίδα. - Οι χιαστοί και οι πλάγιοι σύνδεσμοι ελέγχονται χωρίς παθολογικά ευρήματα. - Από τον έλεγχο του εκτατικού μηχανισμού δεν αναγνωρίζονται άλλα παθολογικά ευρήματα. - Μετρία συλλογή υγρού παρατηρείται ενδαρθρικά σε επικοινωνία με συνοβιακή κύστη κεφαλουραίας διαμέτρου 3cm στην έξω ιγνυακή κοιλότητα. Πάχυνση του υμένα παρατηρείται στην άρθρωση αλλά και στην συνοβιακή κύστη. Η υμενίτιδα σε συνδυασμό με υποφλοιώδη κύστη 5mm στην οπίσθια κνήμη παρά τη συνάρθρωση με την περόνη, με παρουσία πέριξ αυτής οστεομυελικού οιδήματος, θέτει υπόνοια φλεγμονώδους αρθροπάθειας.  Συμπέρασμα 1. Ηπια εκφυλιστική οστεοαρθρίτιδα έσω και πρόσθιου διαμερίσματος. 2. Υπόνοια φλεγμονώδους αρθρίτιδας ως περιγράφεται.
translation:
TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, T2 gradient echo, and proton density sequences with fat suppression.

FINDINGS:
- Articular cartilage degeneration is identified corresponding to the medial joint space (ICRS grade II). There is coexisting focal bone marrow edema in the medial femoral and tibial condyles. Additionally, marginal osteophytes are observed in the medial compartment of the knee.
- Cartilage degeneration of the patella is observed in its medial portion (ICRS grade II). Additionally, small marginal osteophytes are noted on the patella.
- The cruciate and collateral ligaments are examined without pathological findings.
- On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, no other pathological findings are identified.
- Moderate joint effusion is observed intra-articularly, communicating with a synovial cyst of craniocaudal diameter 3 cm in the lateral popliteal fossa. Synovial thickening is observed in the joint as well as in the synovial cyst. The synovitis in combination with a 5 mm subcortical cyst in the posterior tibia adjacent to the tibiofibular articulation, with surrounding bone marrow edema, raises suspicion of inflammatory arthropathy.

CONCLUSION:
1. Mild degenerative osteoarthritis of the medial and anterior compartments.
2. Suspicion of inflammatory arthritis as described.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is moderate bone marrow edema within the medial tibial epimetaphysis, with areas of linear low signal consistent with stress fracture. Background bone marrow signal is normal. 

JOINT SPACE:
Minimal joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Cartilage appears intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Cartilage appears intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is moderate to severe cartilage loss at the lateral patellar facet, with areas of full-thickness fissuring and minimal subchondral cystic change. Mild cartilage surface irregularity is present at the medial patellar facet. Trochlear cartilage appears intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild tendinosis with interstitial tearing at the patellar attachment.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. There is mild lateral patellar subluxation, suggesting underlying patellar maltracking. Borderline patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 16 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:


1. Stress fracture at the medial aspect of the proximal tibia.

2. Patellofemoral chondrosis with evidence of underlying patellar maltracking.

3. Mild quadriceps tendinosis with interstitial tearing.

4. Minimal Baker cyst.

MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Low-grade intermediate grade osseous contusion involving the superior posterior lateral femoral condyle. Background marrow signal is otherwise normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Trace joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Mucoid degeneration without full-thickness disruption.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Low to intermediate grade osseous contusion involving the superior posterolateral femoral condyle.
2.	Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis, no tendon tear.

translation:
MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
Intra-articularly, a moderate joint effusion is observed, within which in the suprapatellar pouch a large synovial fold is identified.
On evaluation of the lateral meniscus, the cruciate and collateral ligaments, no significant findings are observed.
In the medial compartment, a degenerative tear of the meniscus is observed with mild bone marrow edema on both sides of the joint and thinning of the articular cartilage of the medial femoral and tibial condyles (ICRS grade II).
On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, focal thinning of the articular cartilage of the medial surface of the patella is observed (ICRS grade II).
Small osteophytes are observed in the intercondylar notch as well as on the femoral condyles.

CONCLUSION:
Findings of degenerative osteoarthritis of the medial compartment with degenerative meniscal tear and joint effusion, as well as mild degenerative osteoarthritis of the anterior compartment.

translation:
Clinical History:
Medial osteoarthritis.
Findings:
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
The lateral meniscus has a discoid morphology, without categorical criteria for an evident tear.
Complex tear of the body, posterior horn, and part of the posterior meniscal root of the medial meniscus with significant meniscal extrusion, in particular, with a segment displaced toward the meniscofemoral recess with edema of the adjacent soft tissues.
Partial and full-thickness chondral ulcers of the weight-bearing zone of the medial femorotibial compartment with secondary bone changes and peripheral bone proliferations. Cartilage of the lateral femorotibial compartment without alterations. Full-thickness chondral ulcer with partial chondral reparative phenomena of the central region of the femoral trochlea. Fine focal full-thickness chondral ulcers of the medial facet and apex of the patella with minimal secondary bone changes.
Mild to moderate joint effusion with diffuse synovitis. No pathological popliteal cysts.
Quadriceps tendon, patellar tendon, pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Impression:
Degenerative complex tear with maceration and extrusion of the medial meniscus, as previously described.
Advanced degenerative chondropathy of the medial femorotibial compartment.
Focal grade 3 and 4 chondropathy lesions of the patellofemoral joint.
Lateral meniscus with discoid morphology, without criteria for tear.
Mild to moderate joint effusion with diffuse synovitis.

translation:
Clinical History:
Popliteal cyst.
Findings:
No diffuse bone marrow signal abnormality.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments are intact.
Signal abnormality due to degenerative changes of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus associated with a full-thickness radial tear at the posterior horn–posterior root junction, resulting in mild meniscal extrusion. Reactive bone changes of the immediately underlying tibial plateau.
Lateral meniscus with preserved morphology and fibrillation of the free edge of the body.
Medial femorotibial cartilage with a subtotal-thickness chondral defect and reactive bone changes in the posterior third of the weight-bearing surface of the medial femoral condyle, extending 11 mm laterally by 13 mm anteroposteriorly. Medial tibial plateau cartilage without deep chondral defects.
Lateral femorotibial cartilage with signal abnormality and partial-, subtotal-, and full-thickness ulcerations on both articular surfaces with reactive bone changes in the condyle.
Patellofemoral cartilage with extensive subtotal-/full-thickness defects and reactive bone changes in both patellar facets and the central region of the trochlea.
Signal abnormality of the proximal medial/central fibers and distal lateral fibers of the patellar tendon.
Remaining regional tendons with preserved thickness and signal.
Moderate joint effusion with signs of diffuse synovitis of chronic appearance. Mild distension of the gastrocnemius-semimembranosus recess. Edema of the intermuscular planes.
Muscle planes with preserved trophism and signal.
Impression:
Full-thickness radial tear at the posterior horn/posterior root junction of the medial meniscus associated with mild meniscal extrusion.
Fibrillation of the free edge of the body of the lateral meniscus.
Femorotibial chondropathy with extensive grade 3–4 chondral defect of the medial femoral condyle and grade 3 and 4 lesions on both articular surfaces of the lateral compartment.
Patellofemoral chondropathy with extensive grade 3–4 defect in both patellar facets and the central region of the trochlea.
Proximal and distal patellar tendinosis.
Moderate joint effusion with signs of diffuse synovitis.

MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, T2 gradient echo, and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
On evaluation of the medial meniscus, the cruciate and collateral ligaments, the articular cartilage, and the extensor mechanism, no significant findings are observed.
Degeneration without tear is observed in the lateral meniscus.
Bone marrow edema is observed in the lateral epiphysis of the proximal tibia.
Intra-articularly, a significant fluid collection is noted which communicates with a cystic formation adjacent to the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle.

CONCLUSION:
1. Intraosseous bruise (Bone Bruise) of the lateral tibial condyle.
2. Joint effusion and Baker's synovial cyst.

Findings:
No significant bone marrow alterations.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
Increased central signal of the body of the medial meniscus that does not appear to contact the articular surface, without features of a tear. The lateral meniscus is of preserved morphology and signal, without signs of tear.
Cartilage of the femorotibial compartments and femoral trochlea without alterations. Partial and full-thickness chondral ulcers of diffuse distribution of the patella, without secondary bone changes.
Minimal joint effusion. No pathological popliteal cysts.
Increased signal of the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon and the proximal insertion of the patellar tendon, without signs of tear. Mild soft tissue edema between the iliotibial band and the lateral femoral condyle as well as of the superolateral aspect of Hoffa's fat pad.
Pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris tendon and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Impression:
Chondropathy grade two and three lesions of the patella.
Minimal joint effusion.
Mild distal quadriceps and proximal patellar tendinosis. No probable friction phenomena of the iliotibial band and a lateral patellar hyperpressure syndrome.

MRI of right Knee with

> Obliteration of lateral meniscus with linear signal intensity in anterior to posterior horn of medial meniscus, it extends into the surface, in favor of tear.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with suspicious of extending into the surface, in favor of degeneration  of posterior horn of medial meniscus with R/O tear.
> Wearing of articular cartilage and spur formation and subchondral cysts of right knee, reflecting osteoarthritis.
    An osteochondral defect with concave abormal bone marrow signal in lateral femoral condyle, R/O osteonecrosis (srs: 6001, Img:5-7)
> The contour of ACL & PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst.
> Subcutaneous inifltration over right knee
> Increased interstitial signal intensity of iliotibial band on F/S T2WI, R/O tendinosis.

Impression: 
1. C/W osteoarthritis of right knee, more severe at lateral compartment.
2. R/O osteonecrosis of lateral femoral condyle or degeneration related subchondral bone marrow edema in lateral femoral condyle.
3. Tear of lateral meniscus and R/O degeneration and tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
4. Synovitis of right knee and Baker's cyst; complex patellar plicae.
* Suspicious of MR artifact over infrapatellar region (srs:5001,6001, Img:9-10) 

Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

report:
Clinical information: Left knee pain, refractory to opioids. Please assess for internal derangement.

Technique: Unenhanced multiplanar multiphase MRI of the left knee performed at 3.0 Tesla MRI scanner.

Findings:
The cruciate ligaments are intact. There is mild thickening of the proximal medial collateral ligament. Otherwise the collateral ligaments are intact. There is mild tendinosis of the distal quadriceps tendon. Otherwise extensor mechanism of the knee is unremarkable.

There is a degenerative oblique tear at the posterior horn/posterior aspect body of the medial meniscus extending into the tibial meniscal surface (12-20). There are no unstable meniscal fragments. There is a mild mucoid degeneration of the lateral meniscus.

There is a mild chondrosis in the medial femorotibial joint compartment. There is a moderate chondrosis in the lateral femorotibial joint compartment with a focal button osteophyte at the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle measuring 0.8 x 0.5 x 0.3 cm. There is no adjacent bone marrow edema. There is a moderate patellofemoral chondrosis with focal cartilage fibrillation and deep cartilage defects at the lateral patellar facet. The joint indications are well-maintained.

The infrapatellar fat pad is unremarkable. There is a mild joint effusion. There are no intra-articular bodies. 

There is a low volume Baker's cyst. There is a thickening with associated edematous changes involving the medial patellar plica (13-10)

The visualized muscle bulk is unremarkable. There is mild thickening with associated T2 hyperintensity of the proximal popliteal tendon in keeping with a mild tendinosis.

Conclusion:
1. Degenerative oblique tear posterior horn/posterior aspect body of the medial meniscus.
2. No acute ligamentous injury.
3. Moderate chondrosis in the lateral femorotibial joint compartment with a small button osteophyte.
4. Moderate patellofemoral chondrosis.
5. Thickening with associated edematous changes of the medial patellar plica. This may be seen in medial patellar plica syndrome. Please correlate clinically.

report:
Erhaltene Artikulation im linken Kniegelenk. Postoperativer Hämarthros mit einzelnen Synovialenproliferationen.

Patella gering lateralisiert stehend. Mit 1,2 normwertiger Insall-Salvati-Index. Unauffällige Darstellung der Quadrizeps- und Patellasehne. An der medialen Patellafacette überwiegend oberflächliche, teils tief greifende Chondropathie (8/10). Ebenfalls fokale teils tiefergehende chondrale Läsion in der Trochlea (z. B. 7/24).
Femorotibial im medialen Kompartiment entsprechende deutliche Signalanhebungen des Innenmeniskus im Hinterhorn und Pars intermedia mit entsprechendem Substanzdefekt nach Z. n. Meniskusresektion am Vortag mit insbesondere in der Femurkondyle fokal tief greifender Chondropathie (5/23). Kleine osteophytäre Ausziehungen am Tibiaplateau und der Femurkondyle (5/22). Kleines Reizödem im medialen Tibiaplateau (5/24). Der Außenmeniskus ist intakt. Überwiegend oberflächliche Chondropathie auch im lateralen Kompartiment mit kleinen Osteophyten am Femurkondylus (5/24). Kleine chondrale Ossifikation an der lateralen Kondyle (6/27).  Diffuse Flüssigkeitseinlagerungen in den Hoffa'schen Fettkörper mit kleinem Hämatom (9/20). HKB sowie VKB sowie Kollateralbandapparat intakt. Postoperative Veränderungen im Zugangsweg über das mediale Retinaculum (8/18). Ansonsten unauffällige Darstellung der umgebenden Weichteile.
translation:
Preserved articulation in the left knee joint. Postoperative hemarthrosis with individual synovial proliferations.

Patella slightly laterally positioned. Normal Insall-Salvati index of 1.2. Unremarkable appearance of the quadriceps and patellar tendons. Predominantly superficial, partly deep-reaching chondropathy at the medial patellar facet (8/10). Also focal partly deeper chondral lesion in the trochlea (e.g., 7/24).
Femorotibial in the medial compartment, corresponding marked signal elevations of the medial meniscus in the posterior horn and pars intermedia with corresponding substance defect after meniscal resection on the previous day, with particularly focal deep-reaching chondropathy in the femoral condyle (5/23). Small osteophytic spurs at the tibial plateau and femoral condyle (5/22). Small reactive edema in the medial tibial plateau (5/24). The lateral meniscus is intact. Predominantly superficial chondropathy also in the lateral compartment with small osteophytes at the femoral condyle (5/24). Small chondral ossification at the lateral condyle (6/27). Diffuse fluid accumulation in Hoffa's fat pad with a small hematoma (9/20). PCL as well as ACL as well as collateral ligament apparatus intact. Postoperative changes in the access route via the medial retinaculum (8/18). Otherwise unremarkable appearance of the surrounding soft tissues.

translation:

AA: Clinical information: See scanned request
Diagnostic question: See scanned request

Findings:
Moderate to advanced medial femorotibial cartilage disease, with near-complete cartilage loss on the weight-bearing portion of the medial femoral condyle and the tibial plateau, accompanied by small subchondral geodes, marginal osteophytosis. Degenerative appearance of the medial meniscus with irregular contour, however without a clear tear. Early to moderate lateral femorotibial cartilage disease, with superficial and deep fissures. Normal appearance of the various tendons.

Conclusion:
Early gonarthrosis of the right knee with early to moderate to advanced cartilage disease grade 2, 3 and 4, in all 3 compartments, currently with moderate effusion.

report: SAĞ DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Lateral menisküste grade I dejenerasyon izlenmiştir. Medial menisküs ekstrüde görünümdedir. Medial menisküste grade III dejenerasyon , kök ve kompleks yırtık ile uyumlu görünüm mevcuttur.Ön çapraz bağda mukoid dejenerasyon ile uyumlu sinyal artışı mevcuttur. Arka çapraz bağ, lateral kollateral ligaman normaldir. Medial kollateral ligaman çevresinde sıvı artışı izlenmiştir. Medial ve lateral reseslerde sıvı artışı mevcuttur.Distal kuadriseps ve patellar tendonlar normaldir. Retinaküler devamsızlık yoktur.Patellar kemikte subkondral skleroz bulguları, medial fasette kıkırdakta bütünlük kaybı, ayrıca komşu kemikte subkondral milimetrik kist ve ödem ile uyumlu görünüm mevcuttur (tip 4 kondromalazi ).Suprapatellar bursada sıvı artışı, diz eklemi seviyesinde sıvı artışı izlenmiştir.Diz eklemini oluşturan femoral ve tibial kartilajlarda subkondral skleroz bulguları mevcuttur. Ayrıca tibia medial plato düzeyinde arka çapraz bağ yapışma lokalizasyonunda ve femur interkondiler düzeyde ve lateral kondil düzeyinde subkondral ödem ve milimetrik kistler ile uyumlu görünüm mevcuttur.Diz eklemi çevresindeki çevre yumuşak dokularda cilt altı ödematöz görünüm mevcuttur.Gastroknemius medial kruris bacağında tendonda tendinozis ile uyumlu sinyal artışı mevcuttur.

Grade I degeneration is observed in the lateral meniscus. The medial meniscus appears extruded. Grade III degeneration is present in the medial meniscus, with an appearance consistent with root and complex tear. Signal increase consistent with mucoid degeneration is present in the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Fluid increase is observed around the medial collateral ligament. Fluid increase is present in the medial and lateral recesses. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Subchondral sclerosis findings are present in the patellar bone, with loss of cartilage integrity on the medial facet, and additionally an appearance consistent with subchondral millimetric cyst and edema in the adjacent bone (type 4 chondromalacia). Fluid increase in the suprapatellar bursa and fluid increase at the level of the knee joint are observed. Subchondral sclerosis findings are present in the femoral and tibial cartilages forming the knee joint. Additionally, an appearance consistent with subchondral edema and millimetric cysts is present at the level of the medial tibial plateau at the posterior cruciate ligament attachment site, at the intercondylar level of the femur, and at the level of the lateral condyle. Subcutaneous edematous appearance is present in the surrounding soft tissues around the knee joint. Signal increase consistent with tendinosis is present in the tendon of the medial gastrocnemius crus.

report:

> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of  grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration or  peripheral prominent vascularity.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis and bulging lateral aspect synovial recess over popliteal fossa.
> Wearing of articular cartilage of right knee, especially at patellar  ridge and femoral trochlea with subchondral edema over femoral trochlea, reflecting grade 4 chondromalacia of patellofemoral joint
> Patellar enthesophyte and mild tendinosis of quadriceps tendon and patellar tendon.

Impression: 
1. Grade 4 chondromalacia of right patellofemoral joint, reflecting osteoarthritis.
2. Synovitis of right knee with suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae.
3. Grade 1 injury or mucoid degeneration of ACL.
4. Grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, R/O degeneration or  peripheral prominent vascularity.
5. Patellar enthesophyte with mild adjacent tendinosis.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

translation:
TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, Pd fs, T2 me2d sequences.

FINDINGS:
- A significant amount of intra-articular fluid collection is identified with accompanying fatty hyperplasia of the synovium in the suprapatellar recess, which does not exclude the possibility of lipoma arborescens. A large Baker's synovial cyst measuring 5.6 x 2 cm (transverse x anteroposterior) coexists, with accompanying mild fluid infiltration of the adjacent soft tissues, suggesting prior rupture.
- A large tear of the body of the medial meniscus is identified with accompanying folding in an atypical position between the medial femoral condyle and the medial patellar retinaculum.
- Partial thickness loss of articular cartilage of the medial compartment in the context of grade III chondropathy and irregularity of the articular cartilage margin of the patella (grade I-II chondropathy). Full thickness loss of articular cartilage in the medial part of the lateral femoral condyle.
- Minimal marginal osteophytes are identified in the medial compartment.
- The cruciate and collateral ligaments are normal.
- The bone marrow signal is within normal limits.

translation:

Findings

The described findings correspond to OA changes.
A small amount of effusion in the suprapatellar and posterior joint recess.

The popliteus tendon shows altered signal intensity at the femoral attachment, probably consistent with chronic changes.

The distal part of the semimembranosus tendon shows altered signal intensity with signs of bursitis, probably in the context of chronic changes.
Normal signal intensity of the quadriceps tendon and patellar ligament attachments.
No signs of a popliteal cyst.
The congruence of the articular surfaces of the femoropatellar joint is normal.

report:
FINDINGS: A partial injury of the anterior cruciate ligament is demonstrated - anatomical continuity is best appreciated in the coronal plane. There is in fact no associated anterior tibial translation.  Well-preserved medial and lateral tibiofemoral hyaline articular cartilage surfaces, a subcentimeter focus of grade 3/4 articular cartilage loss is noted at the midline femoral trochlea anteriorly. Well-preserved retropatellar articular cartilage.  There is a significant, incompletely imaged knee joint effusion with nonspecific synovitis, no intra-articular loose bodies are present.  There is a popliteus muscle strain posteriorly, there is however no disruption of the corresponding musculotendinous unit or tendon.  The popliteofibular ligament appears sprained, there is furthermore soft tissue edema like signal change at the position of the arcuate ligament complex, suggestive of a sprain pattern - both limbs of the arcuate ligament can however be appreciated on coronal images (series 301 image 26), implying gross structural continuity.  Both collateral ligaments appear intact, as do the PCL, medial meniscus, patellar tendon, distal iliotibial band and marrow signal characteristics.  A tiny cleft is affecting the free edge of the lateral meniscus, at the junction between the body and anterior horn. Minor non calcific distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis also present. No other finding of note.   
</IMPRESSION/> Partial ACL injury with involvement of the popliteus muscle, popliteofibular and arcuate ligaments posterolaterally. Subcentimeter diameter focus of full-thickness cartilage loss with associated reactive marrow changes noted at the midline femoral trochlea.

translation:

Osteoarthritis

Complex tear with main oblique horizontal component of the body, posterior horn, and part of the posterior meniscal root of the medial meniscus with mild meniscal extrusion.
Full-thickness chondral ulcers of the weight-bearing zone of the lateral femorotibial compartment with secondary bone changes and peripheral bone proliferations. Partial-thickness chondral ulcers of diffuse distribution of the medial femorotibial compartment.

Diffuse cystic transformation of the ACL, without criteria for tear.
Extensive complex degenerative tear of the lateral meniscus with associated extrusion.
Tear of the medial meniscus, with mild meniscal extrusion.

report: SOL DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Lateral menisküs ve medial menisküsler eklem aralığından ekstrude olup menisküslerde belirgin hacim kaybı, maserasyon ve grade III dejenerasyonlar izlendi. Anterior çapraz bağda komplet rüptüre sekonder bütünlük kaybı izlenmektedir. Posterior çapraz bağ belirgin kıvrımlı görünümdedir. Diz eklemini oluşturan her 3 kompartmanda santral-marjinal osteofit formasyonu izlendi. Tibiofemoral eklem medial ve lateralinde eklem aralığında daralma, ekleme komşu kemik yüzlerde subkondrial skleroz, ödem ve milimetrik kistler izlendi. Bu düzeyde femoral ve tibial kartilajlarda destrüksiyon izlendi. Bulgular dejeneratif artrit lehine yorumlandı.Diz eklemi posteriorunda, popliteus tendon kılıf komşuluğunda snovial sıvının çevrelediği büyüğü 7 mm çaplı ossifiye nodüler lezyonlar izlendi. Bulgular snovial kondromatozis lehine yorumlanmıştır. Diz eklem kapsülü posterior superiorunda yırtık, yırtık ile ilişikli 2.5x1.5 cm boyutlu ganglion kisti izlendi. Diz eklem posteriorunda 3x2 cm boyutlu ekstraartiküler ganglion kisti izlenmektedir. Suprapatellar bursa ve diz eklem mesafesinde sıvı artışı izlendi. Tibianın tibiafibular eklemden anteriora doğru sublüksasyonu izlenmektedir. Patella lateral fasette kartilaj belirgin incelmiştir. Sonuç: Gonartroz.Medial ve lateral menisküslerde ekstrüzyon, volüm kaybı, maserasyon ve grade IIII meniskopati.Anterior çapraz bağda komplet rüptür ve posterior çapraz bağda kıvrımlı görünüm.Medial kollateral ligamende grade I sprain. Diz eklem  kapsülü posteriorunda yırtık ve yırtık ile ilişkili ganglion kistleri.Suprapatellar bursit ve diz ekleminde sinovit.Tibianın sublüksasyonu.Patella lateral fasette grade II kondromalazi.
translation: LEFT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: The lateral meniscus and medial menisci are extruded from the joint space with significant volume loss, maceration, and grade III degeneration observed in the menisci. Loss of continuity secondary to complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament is observed. The posterior cruciate ligament has a markedly buckled appearance. Central-marginal osteophyte formation is observed in all three compartments of the knee joint. Joint space narrowing in the medial and lateral tibiofemoral compartments, subchondral sclerosis, edema, and millimetric cysts on the bone surfaces adjacent to the joint are observed. Destruction of the femoral and tibial cartilage is observed at this level. Findings are interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis. Ossified nodular lesions, the largest measuring 7 mm in diameter, surrounded by synovial fluid are observed posterior to the knee joint, adjacent to the popliteus tendon sheath. Findings are interpreted in favor of synovial chondromatosis. A tear in the posterosuperior aspect of the knee joint capsule with an associated 2.5x1.5 cm ganglion cyst is observed. A 3x2 cm extra-articular ganglion cyst is observed posterior to the knee joint. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Anterior subluxation of the tibia from the tibiofibular joint is observed. The cartilage on the lateral facet of the patella is markedly thinned. Conclusion: Gonarthrosis. Extrusion, volume loss, maceration, and grade IIII meniscopathy in the medial and lateral menisci. Complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament and buckled appearance of the posterior cruciate ligament. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Tear of the posterior knee joint capsule and associated ganglion cysts. Suprapatellar bursitis and synovitis of the knee joint. Subluxation of the tibia. Grade II chondromalacia of the lateral facet of the patella.
