translation:
Clinical History:
Left knee trauma.

Findings:
Full-thickness and full-width tear of the ACL in its proximal third, this is associated with bone edema, subcortical and cortical fractures of the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau and the peripheral weight-bearing zone of the lateral femoral condyle.
PCL and lateral collateral ligament within preserved limits.
Increased signal with partial loss of continuity of the femoral insertion of the deep meniscofemoral component with edema of the regional soft tissues and a laminar amount of fluid between the components of the medial complex. The remaining components of the medial complex appear intact.
The lateral meniscus appears of preserved morphology and signal, without signs of a definite tear.
Increased signal of the meniscocapsular attachment of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, which could represent a regional partial lesion.
Cartilage of the femorotibial compartments and femoral trochlea without alterations. Superficial patellar chondropathy.
Minimal joint effusion. Small popliteal cyst with a laminar amount of perifascial fluid extending cephalad and caudad.
Quadriceps tendon, patellar tendon, pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band within normal limits.

Impression:
Full-thickness and full-width tear of the ACL associated with bone edema, subcortical and cortical fractures of the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau and the weight-bearing zone of the lateral femoral condyle.
Signs of a grade II sprain of the femoral insertion of the deep meniscofemoral component with edema of the regional soft tissues and a laminar amount of fluid of the components of the medial complex.
Signs of at least a partial lesion of the meniscocapsular attachment of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, correlate clinically.
Minimal joint effusion. Small popliteal cyst with signs of rupture.

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is linear edema through the medial tibial metaphysis, consistent with stress fracture as suggested on radiographs. Additionally, mild bone marrow edema is present at the posterior margin of the medial tibial plateau related to adjacent meniscal tear. Background bone marrow signal is normal. 

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate, ruptured Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a complex tear involving the posterior horn and body, with a radial tear near the posterior root attachment. Moderate extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is moderate cartilage thinning and surface irregularity at the weightbearing aspect diffusely. Full-thickness cartilage fissuring at the posterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Cartilage appears intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Patellar cartilage appears intact. Mild cartilage thinning is present at the trochlea diffusely.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm. Small medial patellar plica.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Stress fracture of the medial tibial metaphysis.
2. Complex tear of the medial meniscus with moderate extrusion.
3. Chondrosis in the patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartment.
4. Moderate joint effusion. Moderate, ruptured Baker cyst.

medijalnog kompartmenta femorotibijalnog zgloba i lateralnog kompartmenta femoropatelarnog
zgloba. Vidljive su erozije trohlearne hrskavice i fisure patelarne hrskavice u smislu
hondromalacije trećeg stupnja.
Vidljiva je veća zona denudacije hrskavice medijalnog kondila femura. Stanjena i dijelom
erodirana hrskavica medijalnog tibijalnog platoa. Nalazi se manji areal koštanog edema u
anteriornom dijelu medijalnog femoralnog kondila u smislu hondromalacije četvrtog stupnja. Zone
subhondralnog edema uz rubne osteofite medijalnog kompartmenta femorotibijalnog zgloba.
Održani su križni ligamenti, prednji početno degenerativno promijenjen.
Degenerativne promjene lateralnog meniska, bez evidentne rupture.
Degenerativno promijenjen medijalni menisk uz znakove horizontalne rupture stražnjeg roga i
trupa, vjerojatno starijeg datuma, a koja se otvara na tibijalnu plohu meniska.
Ekstruzija trupa i stražnjeg roga meniska pod medijalni kolateralni ligament koji je posljedično
blago distendiran, bez znakova rupture.
Lateralni kolateralni ligament je održanog kontinuiteta, entezopatski promijenjen na femoralnom
hvatištu.
Degenerativne promjene hvatišta medijalne glave muskulusa gastroknemijusa za femur.
Manja količina izljeva u burzi semimembranozusa.
Primjeren prikaz tetive muskulus kvadriceps i patelarnog ligamenta. Wiberg 3 tip patele.

Ostali nalaz u granicama normale.
translation:
On the performed sequences through the right knee, gonarthrotic changes are present, more pronounced in the medial compartment of the femorotibial joint and the lateral compartment of the femoropatellar joint. Erosions of the trochlear cartilage and fissures of the patellar cartilage are visible, consistent with grade 3 chondromalacia.
A larger zone of cartilage denudation is visible on the medial femoral condyle. Thinned and partially eroded cartilage of the medial tibial plateau. A smaller area of bone edema is present in the anterior part of the medial femoral condyle, consistent with grade 4 chondromalacia. Zones of subchondral edema with marginal osteophytes of the medial compartment of the femorotibial joint.
The cruciate ligaments are intact, the anterior one is initially degenerative changed.
Degenerative changes of the lateral meniscus, without evident tear.
Degeneratively changed medial meniscus with signs of horizontal tear of the posterior horn and body, probably of older date, which opens onto the tibial surface of the meniscus.
Extrusion of the body and posterior horn of the meniscus under the medial collateral ligament, which is consequently mildly distended, without signs of tear.
The lateral collateral ligament is of maintained continuity, with enthesopathic changes at the femoral attachment.
Degenerative changes of the attachment of the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle to the femur.
A small amount of effusion in the semimembranosus bursa.
Adequate visualization of the quadriceps tendon and patellar ligament. Wiberg type 3 patella.
Incomplete suprapatellar plica. A small amount of joint effusion.
Other findings within normal limits.

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The medial meniscus is intact.

Previous MRI was reviewed, showing findings of complete anterior cruciate ligament tear. No tibial translation. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 10 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

IMPRESSION:
1. The appearance of the anterior cruciate ligament on the current study is statically low-grade partial-thickness tear without tibial translation. In light of this, findings on the previous MRI may have represented a high-grade partial-thickness tear rather than a full-thickness tear. Continued close clinical follow-up recommended, with follow-up MRI recommended if the patient demonstrates findings of knee instability in the future.
2. The remainder of the examination is unremarkable.

translation:
Clinical History:
Acute traumatic knee.

Findings:
The cruciate ligaments and lateral collateral ligament are unremarkable.
Mild thickening and increased signal of the superficial component of the medial collateral ligament with partial loss of continuity at its femoral insertion. No increased signal is observed, with partial loss of continuity of the femoral insertion of the deep meniscofemoral ligament of the medial complex, with a small amount of fluid between the components.
Bone edema with subcortical fracture of the anterior and peripheral aspect of the lateral tibial plateau with minimal depression, without segment displacement.
Menisci with preserved morphology and signal, without categorical criteria for tear.
Cartilage of the femorotibial and patellofemoral compartments is unremarkable.
Mild to moderate lipohemarthrosis. No pathological popliteal cysts. Distension with fluid surrounding the pes anserinus tendons at their distal insertion.
The quadriceps tendon, patellar tendon, pes anserinus tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band are within normal limits.

Impression:
Signs of a grade II sprain of the proximal third of the superficial and deep components of the medial ligamentous complex with regional soft tissue edema.
Bone edema with subcortical fracture of the anterior and peripheral aspect of the lateral tibial plateau with minimal depression, without segment displacement.
Mild to moderate lipohemarthrosis.
Distension with fluid of both pes anserinus tendons at their distal insertion, probably reactive in nature.

Otherwise normal cartilage coverage in the patellofemoral compartment. Also preserved cartilage coverage in the femorotibial compartment without chondropathy. Cruciate ligaments intact. Otherwise surrounding musculature and soft tissues unremarkable.

report:
МР находка: Наличие на минимален ставен излив – вижда се малко количество течност дорзално на нивото на медиалния кондил на фемура. Костите, формиращи колянната става са с нормална форма и структура. Наличие на слабо изразен костномозъчен едем във фемура и тибията от медиалната страна. Запазена е цялостта на ставния хрущял. Нормално изобразяване на предната и задната кръстна връзка. Виждат се слабо изразени дегенеративни промени в задните рога на двата менискуса, без данни за руптура. Нормално изобразяване на предните рога на мениксусите. Ретинакулуми на пателата, колатерални лигаменти – б.о. Сухожилие на m. quadriceps femoris и лигамент на patella – със запазена цялост и сигнален интензитет. Поплитеална ямка- б.о. В подкожните меки тъкани от медиалната страна на колянната става се вижда малка зона на едемни промени. 
Заключение: МР данни за минимален ставен излив. Начални дегенеративни изменения в задните рога на менискусите. Малка зона на едемни промени в меките тъкани от медиалнаа страна на колянната става.
translation:

report: МР находка: МР данни за минимален ставен излив. Изобразява се фрактура в долния полюс на пателата, без данни за дислокация на костните фрагменти. Налице е дифузен костномозъчен едем на пателата предимно в долна и средната й трета във връзка с травматичната увреда. Няма данни за костномозъчен едем на тибията, фибулата и фемура. Визуализират се малки остеофитни наслоявания по кондилите на фемура и тибията. Интеркондиларните еминенции са изострени. Ставният хрущял на фемура и тибията от медиалната страна е силно изтънен, на места до липсващ. Предната и задната кръстна връзка са интактни. Колатерални лигаменти – без особености. Ретинакулуми – б.о.  В задният рог на латералния менискус се изобразява хиперинтензна лезия с радиерен  ход, съответстваща на скъсване. Скъсването достига до края на менискуса, като видимо се проследява до ставните повърхности на фемура или тибията – увреда 3-тa степен. Нормално изобразяване на предните рога на двата менискуса. Задният рог на медиалния менискус е експулсиран от медиалната страна на колянната става като частично повдига медиалния колатерален лигамент. Задният рог на медниалния менискус е с дифузно повишен сигнален интензитет. Сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис, лигамент на пателата – нормално изобразяване. Поплитеална ямка – б.о. Наличие на дискретни едемни промени в подкожието на предната повърхност на подбедрицата и коляното. Заключение: МР данни за фрактура в долния полюс на пателата, без данни за дислокация на костните фрагменти. Костномозъчен едем на пателата. Минимален ставен излив. Медиална гонартроза. МР данни за скъсване в задните рога на двата менискуса.
translation: MRI findings: MRI evidence of minimal joint effusion. A fracture is visualized at the inferior pole of the patella, without evidence of displacement of the bone fragments. There is diffuse bone marrow edema of the patella predominantly in its inferior and middle thirds related to the traumatic injury. No evidence of bone marrow edema of the tibia, fibula, and femur. Small osteophytic deposits are visualized along the femoral and tibial condyles. The intercondylar eminences are sharpened. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia on the medial side is severely thinned, in places absent. The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact. Collateral ligaments – unremarkable. Retinacula – unremarkable. In the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, a hyperintense lesion with a radial course is visualized, corresponding to a tear. The tear reaches the edge of the meniscus, visibly extending to the articular surfaces of the femur or tibia – grade 3 injury. Normal appearance of the anterior horns of both menisci. The posterior horn of the medial meniscus is extruded medially from the knee joint, partially elevating the medial collateral ligament. The posterior horn of the medial meniscus shows diffusely increased signal intensity. Quadriceps femoris tendon, patellar ligament – normal appearance. Popliteal fossa – unremarkable. Presence of discrete edematous changes in the subcutaneous tissue of the anterior surface of the lower leg and knee. Conclusion: MRI evidence of a fracture at the inferior pole of the patella, without evidence of displacement of the bone fragments. Bone marrow edema of the patella. Minimal joint effusion. Medial gonarthrosis. MRI evidence of tears in the posterior horns of both menisci.

report:

Останалите кости формиращи лявата колянна става се изобразяват с хомогенна структура и сигнален интензитет. Изострени се представят интеркондиларните еминенции. МР данни за руптура на задния рог на медиалния менискус с наличие на коса хиперинтезна лезия достигаща долната ставна повърхност, както при руптура-grade III. Нормално изобразяване на преден рог на медиален менискус и на латерален менискус. 
Oбективизира се малка зона на повишен сигнален интензитет, в PDW FAT SAT серии на сканиране, медиално в хрущяла на пателата. Находката кореспондира на начална хондромалация. Останалият хрущял покриващ ставните повърхности на пателата и  ставен хрущял са съхранен, с хомогенна структура и сигнален интензитет. Двете кръстни връзки се проследяват до залавните си места с правилна форма и сигнален интензитет.
Двата колатерални лигамента са с правилна форма, хомогенна структура и сигнален интензитет до залавните им места. Ретинакулуми – б.о. Мастната тъкан на Хофа е с хомогенна структура и сигнален интензитет. Пателата се представя Wiberg II. Insall-Salvati- 1.2. Малък ставен излив. Заключение: МР данни за увреда на заден рог на медиален менискус grade III. Сhondromalacia patellae- grade I. Малък ставен излив.
translation:
MRI findings: Presence of two tibial rounded osteosclerotic lesions, the larger of which measures 4/5 mm, located in the lateral tibial condyle. The remaining bones forming the left knee joint demonstrate homogeneous structure and signal intensity. The intercondylar eminences appear sharpened. MRI evidence of rupture of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with an oblique hyperintense lesion reaching the inferior articular surface, consistent with a grade III tear. Normal appearance of the anterior horn of the medial meniscus and of the lateral meniscus.
A small zone of increased signal intensity is identified on PDW FAT SAT sequences, medially in the patellar cartilage. The finding corresponds to early chondromalacia. The remaining cartilage covering the articular surfaces of the patella and the articular cartilage are preserved, with homogeneous structure and signal intensity. Both cruciate ligaments are traced to their attachment sites with normal shape and signal intensity.
Both collateral ligaments have normal shape, homogeneous structure and signal intensity to their attachment sites. Retinacula – unremarkable. Hoffa's fat pad has homogeneous structure and signal intensity. The patella presents as Wiberg type II. Insall-Salvati ratio – 1.2. Small joint effusion.
Conclusion: MRI evidence of posterior horn medial meniscus tear grade III. Chondromalacia patellae – grade I. Small joint effusion.

Marginal osteophytes are observed in the lateral joint space. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. Diffuse mild signal increase is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Minimal effusion is present in the suprapatellar recess. Signal intensities of the bony structures forming the knee joint are normal. Minimal subchondral edema is present in the tibial eminence. CONCLUSION: Complex tears in the lateral meniscus, joint effusion, lateral femoral and tibial chondromalacia, signal increase in the anterior cruciate ligament.

report: МР находка: МР данни за ставен излив, като сред излива се намират зони със сигнална характеристика на разпадни продукти на хемоглобина, както при хемартроза. Вижда се изразен костномозъчен едем в кондилите на фемура и тибията, по-изразен от латералната страна. Не се открива фрактура на костите. МР данни за лезия на задния лог на медиалния менискус. Вижда се скъсване на задния рог на менискуса с формиране на свободен фрагмент. Визуализира се лезия и на задния рог на латералния менискус. В задния рог на латералния менискус се вижда хиперинтензна линеарна лезия с кос ход, която достига до края на менискуса и до ставния хрущял на тибията – grade 3. Хиалинният хрущял на тибията и фемура е съхранен. Не се визуализират изменения в хрущяла на пателата. МР данни за частично скъсване на предната кръстна връзка. Предната кръстна връзка е с увеличен напречник и повишен сигнален интензитет. Нормално изобразяване на задната кръстна връзка. Вижда се частично скъсване на медиалния колатерален лигамент при залавното му към фемура място.  Латерален колатерален лигамент – без особености. translation:
MRI findings: MRI evidence of joint effusion, with areas within the effusion showing signal characteristics of hemoglobin degradation products, as in hemarthrosis. Pronounced bone marrow edema is seen in the femoral and tibial condyles, more pronounced on the lateral side. No fracture of the bones is detected. MRI findings of a lesion of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. A tear of the posterior horn of the meniscus is seen with formation of a free fragment. A lesion of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus is also visualized. In the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, a hyperintense linear lesion with oblique course is seen, reaching the meniscal surface and the articular cartilage of the tibia – grade 3. The hyaline cartilage of the tibia and femur is preserved. No changes are visualized in the patellar cartilage. MRI findings of a partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. The anterior cruciate ligament is increased in diameter and shows increased signal intensity. Normal appearance of the posterior cruciate ligament. A partial tear of the medial collateral ligament is seen at its femoral attachment. Lateral collateral ligament – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon and patellar ligament – unremarkable. Fluid in the popliteal fossa, as in a Baker's cyst, most likely ruptured.
Conclusion: MRI findings of a fragmented posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Lesion of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus – grade 3. Partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. Partial tear of the medial collateral ligament. Hemorrhagic joint effusion. Contusion-related bone marrow edema in the femur and tibia. Ruptured Baker's cyst.

Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.

Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.

Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Mild cartilage heterogeneity at the lateral patellar facet

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

report:
МР находка: Наличие на малък ставен излив. Изобразяват се остеофити по латералните и медиалните ставни краища на тибията и фемура, по задната повърхност на медиалния кондил на тибията, по предната повърхност на латералния кондил на тибията, по кондилите на фемура отпред и в двата полюса на пателата. Изтънен е артикулиращият хрущял на пателата и фемура в латералната половина на феморопателарната става. Наличие на отграничена зона на костномозъчен едем в пателата от тази страна. Без МР данни за хондромалация на пателата. Субхондрално разположени костни кисти в латералния кондил на бедрената кост. Изобразява се вътреставно разположена лезия с овална форма и нисък сигнален интензитет в PD и PD SPAIR. Находката е с размер 5/3 мм и е зад залавното място на задната кръстна връзка за тибията. Около описаната находка има малко количество течност. МР данни за хиперинтензна лезия с хоризонтален ход в задния рог на латералния менискус, която се проследява в тялото и в участък от предния рог на менискуса. Мултилокуларна киста на латералния менискус.
МР данни за хиперинтензна лезия с кос ход в задния рог на медиалния менискус, която достига до края на менискуса, без видимо да е в контакт с артикулиращите повърхности на тибията и фемура. Нормално изобразяване на предния рог на медиалния мениксус. Кръстните връзки са интактни. Ретинакулуми на пателата, колатерални лигаменти – б.о. Сухожилие на m. quadriceps femoris и лигамент на patella – със запазена цялост и сигнален интензитет. Наличие на подкожен едем по преднолатералната повърхност на подбедрицата. Заключение: МР данни малък ставен излив. Артрозни промени в латералната половина на феморопателарната става. Отграничен костномозъчен едем в пателата. Ставна „мишка“. Лезия в задния рог, тялото и част от предния рог на латералния менискус – grade 2a. Киста на латералния менискус. Лезия в задния рог на медиалния менискус – grade 2a. Подкожен едем на подбедрицата.
translation:
MRI findings: Small joint effusion is present. Osteophytes are seen along the lateral and medial articular margins of the tibia and femur, along the posterior surface of the medial tibial condyle, along the anterior surface of the lateral tibial condyle, along the femoral condyles anteriorly, and at both poles of the patella. The articular cartilage of the patella and femur is thinned in the lateral half of the patellofemoral joint. A well-defined zone of bone marrow edema is present in the patella on this side. No MRI evidence of chondromalacia of the patella. Subchondrally located bone cysts in the lateral femoral condyle. An intra-articularly located lesion of oval shape with low signal intensity on PD and PD SPAIR is seen. The finding measures 5/3 mm and is located behind the insertion site of the posterior cruciate ligament on the tibia. A small amount of fluid is present around the described finding. MRI evidence of a hyperintense lesion with horizontal course in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, which extends into the body and a portion of the anterior horn of the meniscus. Multilocular cyst of the lateral meniscus.
MRI evidence of a hyperintense lesion with oblique course in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, which reaches the edge of the meniscus, without visible contact with the articular surfaces of the tibia and femur. Normal appearance of the anterior horn of the medial meniscus. The cruciate ligaments are intact. Patellar retinacula, collateral ligaments – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon and patellar ligament – with preserved integrity and signal intensity. Subcutaneous edema is present along the anterolateral surface of the leg.
Conclusion: MRI evidence of small joint effusion. Arthritic changes in the lateral half of the patellofemoral joint. Well-defined bone marrow edema in the patella. Joint loose body. Lesion in the posterior horn, body, and part of the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus – grade 2a. Cyst of the lateral meniscus. Lesion in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 2a. Subcutaneous edema of the leg.

translation:

Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the lateral meniscus and medial meniscus. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The signal of the anterior cruciate ligament is diffusely increased and its integrity cannot be assessed secondary to complete rupture. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. ΕΥΡΗΜΑΤΑ Ικανή συλλογή υγρού παρατηρείται στην άρθρωση του γόνατος, η οποία επικοινωνεί µε συνοβιακή κύστη Baker παρά την έσω κεφαλή του γαστροκνηµίου µυός, µε κεφαλουραία διάµετρο 5cm περίπου. Από τον έλεχγο των πλαγίων συνδέσµων, του οπίσθιου χιαστού συνδέσµου και του έξω µηνίσκου δεν παρατηρούνται παθολογικά ευρήµατα. Προσθίως του έσω πλαγίου συνδέσµου παρατηρείται πάχυνση και οίδηµα στον έσω επιγονατιδοµηριαίο σύνδεσµο, εύρηµα συµβατό µε ήπια κάκωση αυτού. Στο σώµα και οπίσθιο κέρας του έσω µηνίσκου παρατηρείται γραµµοειδής αλλοίωση η οποία εκτείνεται ως την αρθρική επιφάνεια. ∆εν παρατηρείται πλέον η οστική θλάση που είχε παρατηρηθεί στην προηγούµενη εξέταση κατά τον έξω κνηµιαίο κόνδυλο. Μερική χρονία ρήξη πρόσθιου χιαστού συνδέσµου. 2. Υδραρθρο και συνοβιακή κύστη Baker. 3. Ρήξη έσω µηνίσκου. 

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]

MRI ΔΕ ΓΟΝΑΤΟΣ ΤΕΧΝΙΚΗ Η εξέταση έγινε με ακολουθίες παλμών Τ1, πυκνότητας πρωτονίων με καταστολή του σήματος του λίπους και Τ2 βαθμιδωτής ηχούς. ΕΥΡΗΜΑΤΑ Φυσιολογική είναι η απεικόνιση έσω μηνίσκου. Ο έξω μηνίσκος παρουσιάζει γραμμοειδές παθολογικό σήμα στο πρόσθιο κέρας του στα πλαίσια ήπιας εκφύλισης.  Ο πρόσθιος χιαστός ελέγχεται με εικόνα ασυνέχειας και οιδηματώδους απεικόνισης, ιδίως στην οπισθοπλάγια δέσμη.  Οι πλάγιοι σύνδεσμοι και ο οπίσθιος χιαστός σύνδεσμος έχουν φυσιολογική απεικόνιση. Μερική κάκωση με οίδημα παρουσιάζει ο έσω επιγονατιδομηριαίος σύνδεσμος. Μικρή συλλογή υγρού αναγνωρίζεται ενδαρθικά. Ο οστικός μυελός ελέγχεται με εικόνα οστικού οιδήματος στον έξω κνημιαίο και έσω μηριαίο κόνδυλο. Κύστη Baker και γαγγλιακή κύστη 1cm αναγνωρίζονται στην έσω ιγνυακή κοιλότητα. Συμπέρασμα Μερική ρήξη πρόσθιου χιαστού συνδέσμου κατά την οπισθοπλάγια ιδίως δέσμη, με οστικό μώλωπα (bone bruise).
translation:
MRI RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
A significant joint effusion is observed in the knee joint, which communicates with a Baker's cyst adjacent to the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle, with a craniocaudal diameter of approximately 5 cm.
On evaluation of the collateral ligaments, the posterior cruciate ligament, and the lateral meniscus, no pathological findings are observed.
Anterior to the medial collateral ligament, thickening and edema are observed in the medial patellofemoral ligament, a finding compatible with mild injury of it.
In the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus, a linear abnormality is observed extending to the articular surface.
The bone contusion that had been observed on the previous examination at the lateral tibial condyle is no longer seen.
The articular cartilage has normal appearance.
The anterior cruciate ligament shows thinning at its proximal and distal thirds.

CONCLUSION:
1. Partial chronic tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
2. Joint effusion and Baker's cyst.
3. Medial meniscus tear.

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]

MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
The medial meniscus has normal appearance.
The lateral meniscus shows linear pathological signal in its anterior horn in the setting of mild degeneration.
The anterior cruciate ligament is examined with an image of discontinuity and edematous appearance, especially in the posterolateral bundle.
The collateral ligaments and the posterior cruciate ligament have normal appearance.
Partial injury with edema is present in the medial patellofemoral ligament.
A small joint effusion is identified intra-articularly.
The bone marrow is examined with an image of bone edema in the lateral tibial and medial femoral condyle.
A Baker's cyst and a ganglion cyst of 1 cm are identified in the medial popliteal fossa.

CONCLUSION
Partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, especially of the posterolateral bundle, with bone bruise.

translation: LEFT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: Grade III degeneration is present in the medial meniscus, with an appearance consistent with a root tear in the posterior horn and a complex tear at the free edge. The medial meniscus appears extruded medially. The lateral meniscus is normal. The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament, and the lateral collateral ligament are normal. Periligamentous edema was observed in the medial collateral ligament (grade 1 sprain). Loss of cartilage integrity and bone marrow edema in the adjacent bone were observed in the medial facet of the patellar cartilage (type IV chondromalacia). Ossified nodular lesions, the largest measuring 8 mm in diameter, are present posterior to the knee joint (synovial chondromatosis). Mild effusion was observed within the knee joint. Mild osteophytic spurring was observed in the bony structures forming the knee joint. Joint space narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral joint with thinning of the femoral cartilage adjacent to the joint was observed (degenerative arthritis). Mild signal increase was observed in the medial crus tendon of the gastrocnemius.

translation: RIGHT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: Bone marrow edema is observed in the posterolateral aspect of the tibia. At this level, a linear hypointense line on T1-weighted sequences is suspicious for fracture. Cortical integrity and medullary signal intensities of the other bony structures included in the examination are normal. The integrity and signal intensity of the quadriceps and patellar tendons and the posterior cruciate ligament are normal. There is a marked increase in signal of the anterior cruciate ligament, with undulation in its course. There is a markedly deformed appearance of the ligament at its insertion site (rupture). There is signal increase consistent with grade II sprain in the lateral and medial collateral ligaments. There is a deformed appearance in the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus. Grade II degeneration is observed in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Minimal effusion is observed in the joint space and suprapatellar bursa. There is an edematous appearance in the prepatellar soft tissue. No space-occupying lesion was detected in the popliteal fossa.

translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: The lateral meniscus is normal. Grade II degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus. The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. No joint effusion is detected. The signal intensities of the bony structures forming the knee joint are normal.
Conclusion: Grade II meniscopathy of the medial meniscus.

report:
Trouvailles :

Il y a un épanchement intra-articulaire modéré avec synovite. Il y a un kyste poplité non-rupturé de 2 x 3 x 5cm.

Il y a changements dégénératifs sévères du compartiment externe avec perte de cartilage complet impliquant le plateau tibial externe et le condyle fémoral externe. Il y a une irrégularité osseuse suggestive d’une ancienne fracture du plafond tibial externe. Il y a changement réactif sous-chondral. Il y a macération et extrusion avec changements dégénératifs et déchirure dégénérative du ménisque externe. Il n’y a pas d’évidence de fragment déplacé.

Il y a légers changements dégénératifs au niveau patellofémoral et du compartiment interne sans région de perte de cartilage complet.

Il y a changements dégénératifs intra-substance impliquant le corps et la corne postérieure du ménisque interne sans déchirure linéaire bien définie.

Autrement le ligament croisé antérieur, le ligament croisé postérieur, le mécanisme des extenseur, le ligament collatéral interne, le semi-membraneux, le muscle et tendon du poplité, le biceps fémoris distal, le ligament collatéral externe et la bandelette ilio-tibiale sont sans particularité.

Conclusion :

1. Changements dégénératifs au niveau des trois compartiments sévères au niveau du compartiment externe tel que détaillé ci-haut.

2. Déchirure dégénérative avec macération et extrusion du ménisque externe. Il n’y a pas de fragment déplacé. Changements dégénératifs intra-substance du ménisque interne sans déchirure linéaire bien définie.

3. Aucune blessure ligamentaire.

4. Épanchement intra-articulaire avec synovite et kyste poplité non-rupturé.
translation:
Findings:

There is a moderate intra-articular effusion with synovitis. There is a non-ruptured popliteal cyst measuring 2 x 3 x 5 cm.

There are severe degenerative changes of the lateral compartment with full-thickness cartilage loss involving the lateral tibial plateau and the lateral femoral condyle. There is bony irregularity suggestive of an old fracture of the lateral tibial plateau. There is subchondral reactive change. There is maceration and extrusion with degenerative changes and a degenerative tear of the lateral meniscus. There is no evidence of a displaced fragment.

There are mild degenerative changes at the patellofemoral compartment and the medial compartment without any area of full-thickness cartilage loss.

There are intrasubstance degenerative changes involving the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus without a well-defined linear tear.

Otherwise, the anterior cruciate ligament, the posterior cruciate ligament, the extensor mechanism, the medial collateral ligament, the semimembranosus, the popliteus muscle and tendon, the distal biceps femoris, the lateral collateral ligament, and the iliotibial band are unremarkable.

Conclusion:

1. Degenerative changes involving all three compartments, severe in the lateral compartment as detailed above.

2. Degenerative tear with maceration and extrusion of the lateral meniscus. There is no displaced fragment. Intrasubstance degenerative changes of the medial meniscus without a well-defined linear tear.

3. No ligamentous injury.

4. Intra-articular effusion with synovitis and a non-ruptured popliteal cyst.

translation:
Clinical History:
Patellar chondropathy. Rule out lateral meniscal tear. Rule out loose body.

Findings:
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
Marginal fibrillation of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. No other abnormalities of the medial meniscus are observed.
The lateral meniscus has preserved morphology and signal, without criteria for a definite tear.
Partial-thickness chondral ulcers of the central region of the weight-bearing zone of the medial femoral condyle. The remaining femorotibial cartilages without significant abnormalities.
Full-thickness chondral ulcers with secondary bone changes at the patellofemoral joint with lateral predominance and peripheral bone proliferations.
Mild joint effusion with diffuse synovitis. Intra-articular bodies in the posterior recess measuring up to 7 mm.
Mild increased signal at the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon, without signs of tear. Discrete edema of the retro-quadriceps suprapatellar fat pad in a reactive manner. Patellar tendon, pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris, and iliotibial band within normal limits.

Impression:
Advanced degenerative changes of the patellofemoral joint with lateral predominance.
Marginal fibrillation of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus.
Mild joint effusion with diffuse synovitis. Intra-articular bodies in the posterior recess.
Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis with discrete edema of the retro-quadriceps suprapatellar fat pad in a reactive manner.

translation:
On the series of MR images of the right knee, there is normal morphology and signal intensity of the medial collateral ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, iliotibial tract, patellar ligament, and quadriceps tendon.
Complex degenerative rupture of both menisci. The lateral meniscus is completely radially ruptured posteriorly and flips anteriorly as a flap. The medial meniscus is subtotally radially ruptured posteriorly and is peripherally displaced beyond the joint space.
Rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament of older date.
Scarring changes of the proximal portion of the lateral collateral ligament.
Complete loss of articular cartilage of the middle and posterior third of the femoral and tibial condyles with subchondral bone edema.
Full-thickness cartilage fissures of the femoral trochlea.
Marginal osteophytosis of the joint bodies.
Extensive knee effusion. No popliteal (Baker's) cyst is found.
Other visualized bony, soft tissue, and neurovascular structures are of normal morphology and signal intensity.

report:
Knochen: Unauffällige erfassten knöchernen Strukturen. Zentrierte Stellung der Patella, zentrierte Stellung femoro-tibial. Beginnende Osteophytenbildung der Femurkondylen im medialen und lateralen Kompartiment.
Knorpel: Patella Untersuchung fokales vollschichtige Chondropathielinie bei korrespondierender bis vollschichtige Ausdünnung des Knorpelbesatz ist der Trochlea ([DATE]). Fokal bis tief greifende Chondropathie femoralseitig im medialen femorotibialen Kompartiment (5/17, 7/7). Fokales tief greifende Chondropathie an der lateralen Femurkondyle im lateralen femorotibialen Kompartiment (5/19 und 7/19).
Menisci: Unauffällige Formgebung der Menisci. Horizontale Rissbildung am Inenmeniskushinterhorn (5/21 + 20, 6/6). Desweiteren keine Rissbildung. Keine wesentliche mukoide Degeneration des Außenmeniskus, keine Herniation. Keine parameniskale Zystenbildung. 
Bänder/Kapsel/Sehnen: Intakte Darstellung des vorderen und hinteren Kreuzbandes in Bezug auf Signalgebung und Verlauf. Intakte Darstellung der Quadrizepssehne und Patellasehne. Intakte Darstellung des medialen und lateralen Kollateralbandes, geringe Reizzustand des MCL. Medialer und laterale patellare Retinacula intakt. Mäßig Gelenkerguss ohne Nachweis freier intraartikulärer Gelenkkörper.
Fettkörper: Z.n. Teilresektion am Hoffa-Fettkörper mit gering narbigen Veränderungen ohne eindeutig noduläre Arthrofibrose. 
Weichgewebe: Unauffällig, kein Muskelödem.
translation:
Bone: Unremarkable osseous structures visualized. Centrally positioned patella, centrally positioned femorotibial alignment. Early osteophyte formation of the femoral condyles in the medial and lateral compartments.
Cartilage: Focal full-thickness chondropathy line at the patella with corresponding full-thickness thinning of the cartilage covering of the trochlea ([DATE]). Focal deep chondropathy on the femoral side in the medial femorotibial compartment (5/17, 7/7). Focal deep chondropathy at the lateral femoral condyle in the lateral femorotibial compartment (5/19 and 7/19).
Menisci: Unremarkable morphology of the menisci. Horizontal tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus (5/21 + 20, 6/6). No further tear. No significant mucoid degeneration of the lateral meniscus, no herniation. No parameniscal cyst formation.
Ligaments/Capsule/Tendons: Intact appearance of the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments with respect to signal intensity and course. Intact appearance of the quadriceps tendon and patellar tendon. Intact appearance of the medial and lateral collateral ligaments, mild irritation of the MCL. Medial and lateral patellar retinacula intact. Moderate joint effusion without evidence of free intra-articular bodies.
Fat pad: Status post partial resection of the Hoffa fat pad with mild scarring changes without definite nodular arthrofibrosis.
Soft tissue: Unremarkable, no muscle edema.

report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for 4 days.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.2 Tesla open system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. Small multiloculated Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Radial tear at the posterior root.
Medial compartment cartilage: Low-grade articular cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade articular cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Low-grade articular cartilage loss at the patella.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Shallow trochlear groove. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 4 mm, normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Focal radial tear at the medial meniscus posterior root.
2.	Mild tricompartmental chondrosis. Small knee joint effusion with mild synovitis. Small multiloculated Baker's cyst.
3.	Superolateral Hoffa's fat pad impingement, suggesting lateral patellofemoral maltracking.

translation:
MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
On evaluation of the menisci, the cruciate and collateral ligaments, the articular cartilage, and the bone marrow, no pathological findings are observed.
On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, the patella has normal morphology and articulation with the femoral trochlea.
Posterior to the quadriceps tendon in the suprapatellar space, edematous appearance of the fat pad is observed, measuring 3 cm transversely and 2 cm craniocaudally.

IMPRESSION
The edema of the suprapatellar fat pad is consistent with quadriceps tendon impingement syndrome against the anterior surface of the femur.

translation:
Clinical History:
Left patellar tendinopathy.
Findings:
No significant bone marrow signal abnormalities.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
The lateral meniscus is of preserved morphology and signal, without signs of tear.
Increased central signal of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus, which on these sequences does not appear to categorically contact the articular surface, without features of a tear.
Cartilage of the femorotibial and patellofemoral compartments without alterations.
No joint effusion or pathological popliteal cysts.
Thickening and increased signal of the proximal third of the patellar tendon with partial-thickness and partial-width tear at the proximal insertion of the central fibers measuring approximately 7 x 6 mm in its mediolateral and anteroposterior axes respectively, involving approximately 40% of the thickness and 30% of the width of the tendon, with an intrasubstance delaminating component of 9 mm.
Increased signal of the superolateral aspect of Hoffa's fat pad.
Quadriceps tendon, pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Impression:
Proximal patellar tendinosis with partial-thickness and partial-width tear at the proximal insertion of the central fibers with an intrasubstance delaminating component.
Signs of lateral patellar hyperpressure syndrome.

report: МР находка: МР данни за медиална гонартроза. МР данни за дегенеративни промени в медиалния менискус. Медиалният менискус се представя с дифузно повишен интензитет на сигнала и е експулсиран встрани. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. Наличие на ставен излив. Колатерални лигаменти – б.о.  Патела, ретинакулуми – б.о. Сухожилие на м квадрицепс феморис и лигамент на пателата – б.о. Едемни промени в меките тъкани на коляното. Заключение: МР данни за медиална гонартроза. Дегенеративно променен медиален менискус. Мукоидна дегенерация на предна кръстна връзка.

translation:

translation: RIGHT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior and posterior horns and body of the lateral meniscus. Grade II degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus. The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Periligamentous edema is observed in the medial collateral ligament. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Signal change consistent with tendinosis is observed at the proximal insertion level of the medial head of the gastrocnemius. Increased fluid and synovial thickening are observed in the suprapatellar bursa. Increased fluid is observed in the tibiofemoral joint space. Millimetric osteophytic spurring is observed at the corners of the bony structures at the tibiofemoral joint level. Joint space narrowing is observed in the medial tibiofemoral joint, with thinning of the adjacent femoral and tibial cartilage. A Baker's cyst measuring 6x3 cm is observed in the popliteal fossa. Conclusion: Mild gonarthrosis, Grade II meniscopathy of the medial and lateral menisci, Suprapatellar bursitis, Mild synovitis of the knee joint, Tendinosis of the medial head of the gastrocnemius, Baker's cyst in the popliteal fossa, Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament.

report:
Regelrechte Stellungs- und Artikulationsverhältnisse im linken Knie. Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal ohne Hinweis auf einen Ödem. Kein Nachweis einer frischen Fraktur.
Bekannte fokale Chondropathie zentral und medial in der Trochlea (4/14). Regelrechter retropatellarer Knorpel. Unauffällige Darstellung des Hoffa'schen Fettkörpers.
Unauffällige Darstellung des medialen femorotibialen Gelenkes mit intaktem Innenmeniskus und mediales Kollateralband.
Konstante posttherapeutische Signalanhebungen des Außenmeniskus mit geringem Substanzdefekt im Vorderhorn. Suszeptibilitätsartefakte im lateralen femorotibialen Kompartiment, DD postop. (zB 3/107). Keine neue menisceale Rissbildung. Bekannter 3 mm messender nach oberflächlich reichender Knorpeldefekt der lateralen Femurkondyle (7/25). Konstante im Knorpelniveau gelegene Verknöcherung anstelle des vormals vordokumentierten vollschichtigen Knorpeldefektes (6/95 oder 7/25). Weiterhin kein Knochenmarködem nach Glättung des Knorpeldefektes an der lateralen Femurkondyle.
Kreuzbänder vollständig abgrenzbar. Laterales Kollateralband intakt. Akzentuierte Gelenksflüssigkeit.
translation:
Normal alignment and articulation in the left knee. Normal bone marrow signal without evidence of edema. No evidence of acute fracture.
Known focal chondropathy centrally and medially in the trochlea (4/14). Normal retropatellar cartilage. Unremarkable appearance of Hoffa's fat pad.
Unremarkable appearance of the medial femorotibial joint with intact medial meniscus and medial collateral ligament.
Stable post-therapeutic signal alterations of the lateral meniscus with minor substance defect in the anterior horn. Susceptibility artifacts in the lateral femorotibial compartment, DD postoperative (e.g., 3/107). No new meniscal tear. Known 3 mm measuring superficially extending cartilage defect of the lateral femoral condyle (7/25). Stable ossification at cartilage level in place of the previously documented full-thickness cartilage defect (6/95 or 7/25). Still no bone marrow edema after smoothing of the cartilage defect at the lateral femoral condyle.
Cruciate ligaments fully delineable. Lateral collateral ligament intact. Prominent joint effusion.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:

Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.

Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Partial-thickness thinning of the superolateral patellar cartilage with foci of high-grade fissuring. Trochlear cartilage is maintained.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	No acute osseous or meniscal injury.

report:
Findings:  Moderately sized joint effusion. No intra-articular loose bodies. No sinister bone marrow changes.  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments. Intact lateral meniscus.  Degenerate tearing/maceration of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus.  Normal appearance of the distal biceps femoris tendon, distal iliotibial band, pes anserine tendons and popliteus tendon.  Intact quadriceps and patellar tendons. Borderline patella alta. The patella is lateralized relative to the femoral trochlear groove. 
Evidence of trochlear dysplasia with a shallow trochlear groove and borderline reduced lateral trochlear inclination. Normal TTâ€“TG. The MPFL and medial patellar retinaculum are intact. Normal.

None

report: Stigmata der Inaktivitätsosteopenie sowie verbliebenes bone bruise im posterolateralen Tibiaplateau nahe der Eminentia bei subchondraler Impression mit teils punktuell chondralen Läsionen. Anamnestisch bek. VKB Ruptur mit wohl ligamentärer Ruptur des anteromedialen Bündels sowie knöchernem Ausriss des posterolateralen Bündels (4/23). Weiteres Ossikel/Flake angrenzend an die nicht sicher abgrenzbare Außenmeniskushinterhornwurzel, hier DD ebenfalls Mitbeteiligung/knöcherner Ausriss. Innenmeniskus mit horizontalem Riss Pars intermedia bis ins Hinterhorn ziehend bei mukoider Vorschädigung. Zusätzlich noch Knochenödem im medialen femorotibialen Gelenkkompartiment randständig, tibial führend, bei vorrangig Chondropathie. Begleitend geringer Gelenkerguss, Reizsynovialitis sowie gering Flüssigkeit gefüllte Baker-Zyste mit CC 3,2 cm. Kl. Plica mediopatellaris.
translation: Signs of disuse osteopenia as well as residual bone bruise in the posterolateral tibial plateau near the eminence with subchondral impression and partly focal chondral lesions. Historically known ACL rupture with likely ligamentous rupture of the anteromedial bundle and bony avulsion of the posterolateral bundle (4/23). Additional ossicle/flake adjacent to the not clearly delineable lateral meniscus posterior horn root, here DD also involvement/bony avulsion. Medial meniscus with horizontal tear extending from the pars intermedia into the posterior horn with mucoid degeneration. Additionally bone edema in the medial femorotibial compartment, marginal, predominantly tibial, with primarily chondropathy. Accompanying mild joint effusion, reactive synovitis, and mildly fluid-filled Baker's cyst with CC 3.2 cm. Small mediopatellar plica.

report:
MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:[Age] female history of MS and ongoing left knee pain-please assess for meniscal tear and/or left hip labral tear.

PRIOR IMAGING: No relevant priors.

TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact. Thinning of articular cartilage overlying the medial patellar facet. The trochlear cartilage is intact. Lateral subluxation of the patella within the patellofemoral compartment with abnormal joint space interval. The TT-TG distance measures 13 mm, within normal limits. Attenuated appearance of the medial patellofemoral ligament suggestive of prior tear.

The anterior, posterior, and medial cruciate ligaments are intact. Lateral collateral stabilizers including the lateral collateral ligament, popliteus tendon, iliotibial band and biceps femoris tendon are intact.

Medial meniscus is intact. Diminutive appearance of the lateral meniscus at the junction of the posterior horn and body consistent with complex tear. The lateral meniscal body is also peripherally extruded and shows apical truncation consistent with a partial radial tear.  Articular cartilage medial femorotibial compartment is preserved. Questionable mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis.

Small knee joint effusion. No Baker's cyst.

Marrow signal is unremarkable. Soft tissues is unremarkable.

INTERPRETATION: 
1. Complex tear at the junction of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus with partial radial tear involving the body, as well as lateral meniscal extrusion as described.
2. Focal mild to moderate chondrosis medial patellar facet. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis.
3. Suspected remote prior tear of the medial patellofemoral ligament. There is mild lateral subluxation of the patella. No discrete osteochondral impaction injury detected.

report: Diz eklemindeki trikompartmantal dejeneratif eklem hastalığı medyal femoral tibyal ve patellofemoral kompartmanlarda en belirgin ve tam kata ulaşan eklem kıkırdağı kaybı ve dejenerasyonu, subkondral medüller fibrokistik ve fibrovasküler değişiklikler ve marjinal osteofitlerle karakterize. Medyal menisküs arka bonuzu ile arka kapsülü arasında milimetrik çaplı serbest cisimler mevcut. Bilateral suprakondiler düzeyde posteriyorda eklem içinde 3-4 mm çaplı serbest cisimler gözleniyor. Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı hafif derecede artmış. Çapraz ve yan bağlar normal. Medyale 8 mm ekstrüde medyal menisküs arka kökünde tam kat dejeneratif yırtığa arka kökündeki 6 mm çaplı intrameniskal osikül eşlik ediyor. Arka boynuz- gövdesi bileşkesinde alt eklem yüzeyi ile ilişkilenen horizontal oblik yırtık da mevcut. Lateral menisküsteki minimal dejeneratif yapı içi intensite artışına yırtık eşlik etmiyor. Ekstensör mekanizma korunmuş. Diz anteriyorunda cilt altı bağ dokusu ödemli. Gastrokinemyus-semimambranozus bursasındaki sıvı lokülasyonu en kalın yerinde 6 mm olup sızdırmıyor. Diz eklemini çevreleyen kaslarda hafif hacim kaybı ve Goutalier evre 1-2 yağlanma mevcut.
translation: Tricompartmental degenerative joint disease of the knee, most prominent in the medial femorotibial and patellofemoral compartments, characterized by full-thickness articular cartilage loss and degeneration, subchondral medullary fibrocystic and fibrovascular changes, and marginal osteophytes. Millimeter-sized loose bodies are present between the posterior horn of the medial meniscus and the posterior capsule. 3–4 mm diameter loose bodies are observed intra-articularly at the bilateral supracondylar level posteriorly. The intra-articular fluid volume is mildly increased. The cruciate and collateral ligaments are normal. The medial meniscus is extruded 8 mm medially. A full-thickness degenerative tear at the posterior root of the medial meniscus is accompanied by a 6 mm diameter intrameniscal ossicle at the posterior root. A horizontal oblique tear communicating with the inferior articular surface is also present at the posterior horn–body junction. Minimal degenerative intrasubstance signal intensity increase in the lateral meniscus is not accompanied by a tear. The extensor mechanism is intact. Subcutaneous connective tissue edema is present anterior to the knee. Fluid loculation in the gastrocnemius-semimembranosus bursa measures 6 mm at its thickest point and is not leaking. Mild volume loss and Goutallier stage 1–2 fatty infiltration are present in the muscles surrounding the knee joint.

translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings:
The medial meniscus is extruded 6 mm medially from the knee joint space. Grade III degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of the meniscus. Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior horn, posterior horn, and body of the lateral meniscus. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. Periligamentous edema is observed in the medial collateral ligament. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Osteophytic spurring is observed at the corners of the bony structures at the tibiofemoral joint level. Narrowing of the joint space in the medial tibiofemoral joint, and thinning of the femoral and tibial cartilages adjacent to the joint are observed. Additionally, mild destruction is observed in some areas. Findings are interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis. A multiseptated ganglion cyst measuring 3x2.5 cm is observed posterior to the tibiofemoral joint, in the posterior vicinity of the posterior cruciate ligament. Signal change consistent with tendinosis is observed in the tendon at the proximal insertion level of the medial head of the gastrocnemius. Mild increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa.
CONCLUSION: Gonarthrosis. Medial extrusion and grade III meniscopathy of the medial meniscus. Grade II meniscopathy of the lateral meniscus. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Periarticular ganglion cyst at the tibiofemoral joint level. Tendinosis of the medial head of the gastrocnemius. Mild suprapatellar bursitis.

translation:
TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1 and PD sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
- A significant amount of joint effusion is identified, with accompanying synovitis.
- On evaluation of the anterior compartment, chondral lesions of the patella are observed, without erosion of the underlying bone (ICRS 3). The infrapatellar Hoffa's fat pad shows pathological signal, while in the same anatomical region 4 nodular formations are identified, the largest measuring 1.8 cm in diameter, which contain cortex and bone marrow.
- Evaluation of the medial compartment revealed chondral lesions of the femoral condyle (up to ICRS 3 focally). Subarticular cysts are noted in the posterior aspect of both femoral condyles with accompanying bone marrow edema. Additionally, marginal osteophytes are noted on both sides of the femoral condyles as well as in the intercondylar notch, which do not, however, cause significant narrowing of it. The cruciate ligaments are normal. Degenerative changes, without tear, are observed in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus.
- No pathological findings were noted on evaluation of the posterior compartment.

CONCLUSION
- Findings of early osteoarthritis in the setting of inflammatory arthritis.
- Nodular formations in Hoffa's fat pad, most likely representing secondary synovial osteochondromatosis.

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The TT-TG interval measures 10 mm, within normal limits.

Small knee joint effusion. No Baker's cyst.

Bone marrow ill-defined T2 hyperintense signal within the medial patella, femoral trochlea apex and posterior medial rim.

INTERPRETATION: 
No evidence of anterior cruciate ligament injury. Medial and lateral menisci are intact. 

Bone marrow T2 signal changes of the patella and lateral femur suggestive of osseous contusion, however chondromalacia cannot be excluded. Short-term interval follow-up MRI Knee in 6 weeks could differentiate between these 2 entities. Also, clinical correlation regarding a history of direct trauma.

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanisms are intact. The patellar cartilage is intact. The trochlear cartilage is intact. The patellar soft tissues are normal.

The TT-TG interval measures 10 mm, within normal limits.

The anterior cruciate, posterior cruciate, medial collateral and lateral collateral stabilizers, including the fibular collateral collateral ligament, piriformis, biceps femoris and iliotibial tendons, appear intact. No measurable anterior tibial translation.

Medial and lateral menisci are intact. Articular cartilage of the medial and lateral femoral condyle are intact.

Small knee joint effusion. No Baker's cyst.

Bone marrow ill-defined T2 hyperintense signal within the medial patella, femoral trochlea apex and posterior medial rim.

INTERPRETATION: 
No evidence of anterior cruciate ligament injury. Medial and lateral menisci are intact. 

Bone marrow T2 signal changes of the patella and lateral femur suggestive of osseous contusion, however chondromalacia cannot be excluded. Short-term interval follow-up MRI Knee in 6 weeks could differentiate between these 2 entities. Also, clinical correlation regarding a history of direct trauma.

Medial menisküs posterior hornunda grade II dejenerasyon izlenmiştir.Ön çapraz bağ sinyalinde hafif diffüz sinyal artışı mevcuttur. Arka çapraz bağ proksimalinde parsiyel yırtık ile uyumlu olabilcek görünüm izlendi.Arka çapraz bağ Lateral ve medial kollateral ligaman normaldir.Distal kuadriseps tendon normaldir. Retinaküler devamsızlık yoktur.Patellar kıkırdakta medial fasette yer yer fissür hatları ve komşu kemikte subkondral kemik iliği ödemi izlenmiştir (grade IV kondromalazi ).Tibifibular eklem ve patellofemoral eklem mesafesinde hafif daralma izlenmiştir.Suprapatellar bursada ve diz eklemi düzeyinde sıvı artışı izlenmiştir.Diz eklemi düzeyinde prepatellar düzeyde cilt altı yağlı doku ödematöz görünümdedir.Popliteal fossada en kalın yerinde 12 mm'ye varan Baker kisti izlenmiştir.
translation:
RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade I degeneration is observed in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. Grade II degeneration is observed in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is mild diffuse signal increase in the anterior cruciate ligament. An appearance compatible with a partial tear is observed in the proximal portion of the posterior cruciate ligament. The lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps tendon is normal. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Fissure lines are observed in places on the medial facet of the patellar cartilage, with subchondral bone marrow edema in the adjacent bone (grade IV chondromalacia). Mild narrowing is observed in the tibiofibular joint and patellofemoral joint space. Fluid increase is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and at the level of the knee joint. The subcutaneous fatty tissue at the prepatellar level at the knee joint appears edematous. A Baker's cyst measuring up to 12 mm at its thickest point is observed in the popliteal fossa.

Indication: Sprain of right knee; 4 months of inner right knee pain after skating and running injury

MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild cartilage heterogeneity along the lateral tibial plateau without focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full thickness fissuring along the medial facet and median ridge with underlying subchondral edema.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Mild patellofemoral chondrosis.

stupnja hrskavice lateralnog kondila femura te III. stupnja hrskavice lateralnog platoa tibije.

translation:
Advanced degenerative changes of the femorotibial joint with extensive osteophytes, more pronounced in the medial compartment where denudation of the cartilage of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau is visible. Small subcortical cyst of the medial femoral condyle. Grade II chondromalacia of the cartilage of the lateral femoral condyle and grade III chondromalacia of the cartilage of the lateral tibial plateau.
Advanced degenerative changes of the femoropatellar joint with extensive osteophytes and grade III chondromalacia and zones of cartilage denudation of both patellar facets and the femoral trochlea.
Small zone of bone marrow edema in the region of the lateral femoral condyle and in the region of the lateral tubercle of the intercondylar eminence.
The anterior cruciate ligament shows appropriate signal intensity, with intact continuity.
The posterior cruciate ligament shows appropriate signal intensity and intact continuity.
The medial meniscus is thinned in the region of the body and posterior horn, with altered signal intensity in the region of the anterior horn, consistent with a complex tear on the background of advanced degenerative changes. The meniscus itself is extruded beneath the extensive femoral osteophyte with consequent distension of the medial collateral ligament, which shows no signs of tear.
The lateral meniscus is degenerative in appearance, with no signs of tear.
The lateral collateral ligament has intact continuity, with enthesopathic changes of the proximal attachment.
Tendinopathic changes of the popliteus tendon with associated bursitis and a small ganglion cyst.
Normal appearance of the iliotibial tract and pes anserinus.
The quadriceps tendon and patellar ligament show appropriate signal intensity, with intact continuity.
The patellar retinacula are intact.
No signs of a popliteal cyst are found.
A small ganglion cyst anterior to the fibular head.
A large amount of joint effusion with visible synovial hypertrophy.

report: МР находка: МР данни за едем на костния мозък в латералните кондили на фемура и тибията. Отокът е локализиран субхондрално по предната повърхност на фемура и дорзално в епифизата на тибията. МР данни за частична увреда на предната кръстна връзка. Последната е с уголемен напречник, с повишен интензитет на сигнала в проксималната си ½. Задна кръстна връзка – б.о. Нормално изобразяване на менискусите. Колатерални лигаменти – б.о. Ставният хрущял на фемура и тибията е съхранен. Поплитеална ямка – б.о. Наличие на малък ставен излив. Сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис и лигамент на пателата – б.о. Патела, хрущял на пателата, ретинакулуми – б.о. Заключение: МР данни за частична увреда на предна кръстна връзка. Отграничен едем на костния мозък във фемура и тибията с описаната локализация.
translation: MRI findings: MRI evidence of bone marrow edema in the lateral condyles of the femur and tibia. The edema is localized subchondrally along the anterior surface of the femur and dorsally in the epiphysis of the tibia. MRI evidence of partial injury of the anterior cruciate ligament. The latter is enlarged in diameter, with increased signal intensity in its proximal ½. Posterior cruciate ligament – unremarkable. Normal appearance of the menisci. Collateral ligaments – unremarkable. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia is preserved. Popliteal fossa – unremarkable. Presence of a small joint effusion. Quadriceps femoris tendon and patellar ligament – unremarkable. Patella, patellar cartilage, retinacula – unremarkable. Conclusion: MRI evidence of partial injury of the anterior cruciate ligament. Demarcated bone marrow edema in the femur and tibia with the described localization.

report: Diz eklemindeki trikompartmantal dejeneratif eklem hastalığı medyal femoral tibyal kompartmanda en belirgin ve tam kata ulaşan eklem kıkırdağı kaybı ve dejenerasyonu, subkondral medüller fibrovasküler değişiklikler ve marjinal osteofitlerle karakterize. Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı hafif derecede artmış. Çapraz bağlar normal. Dış yan bağın femoral insersiyonunda fokal dejeneratif kalınlık ve intensitesi mevcut. İç yan bağın femoral tarafında kronik zorlanma ile uyumlu kalınlık ve intensite artışı ile çevresinde ödem mevcut. İnsersiyonel semimembranozus tendonozisi peritendinöz ve intratendinöz küçük gangliyon kistleri ile birlikte. Popliteus tendonozisi hafif derecede. Medyale 5 mm ekstrüde dejenere medyal menisküsün gövdesindeki kompleks dejeneratif yırtık süperiyor ve inferiyor eklem yüzeylerine ulaşıyor. Lateral menisküs normal. Ekstensör mekanizma korunmuş.
translation: Tricompartmental degenerative joint disease of the knee, most prominent in the medial femorotibial compartment, characterized by full-thickness articular cartilage loss and degeneration, subchondral medullary fibrovascular changes, and marginal osteophytes. Mild joint effusion. Cruciate ligaments are normal. Focal degenerative thickening and increased signal intensity at the femoral insertion of the lateral collateral ligament. Thickening and increased signal intensity at the femoral side of the medial collateral ligament, consistent with chronic strain, with surrounding edema. Insertional semimembranosus tendinosis with small peritendinous and intratendinous ganglion cysts. Mild popliteus tendinosis. Complex degenerative tear in the body of the degenerate medial meniscus, extruded 5 mm medially, extending to the superior and inferior articular surfaces. Lateral meniscus is normal. Extensor mechanism is intact.

report:
COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Significant left knee pain.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Diminutive posterior root and posterior horn of the medial meniscus consistent with complex tear. Displaced 6 x 6 x 6 mm meniscal fragment adjacent to the posterior root. There is peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The anterior horn is intact.

Intrasubstance degeneration of the anterior root of the lateral meniscus without discrete lateral meniscal tear.

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament involving the posterior lateral bundle. The anteromedial bundle is intact. No tibial translation. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

Low-grade partial-thickness tears of the superficial medial collateral ligament as well as deep medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament. Mild fluid accumulation within the pes anserine bursa.

Popliteus tendinosis without tear. The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact.

Attenuated appearance of the medial patellofemoral ligament suggestive of prior tear. Mild lateral patellar subluxation. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 8 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

There is generalized thinning of patellofemoral articular cartilage. There is mild to moderate medial femorotibial chondrosis. There is a nondisplaced 10 x 5 mm subchondral insufficiency fracture involving the weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle with exuberant surrounding marrow edema. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis.

Trace knee joint fluid. Small Baker's cyst. Regional musculature is within normal limits. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex medial meniscal tear with medial meniscal extrusion and 6 mm displaced meniscal fragment noted adjacent to the posterior root.
2. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament without tibial translation.
3. Low-grade partial-thickness tears involving the superficial and deep fibers of the medial collateral ligament.
4. Mild pes anserine bursitis.
5. Suspected prior tear of the medial patellofemoral ligament with only mild lateral patellar subluxation.
6. Popliteus tendinosis without tear.
7. Tricompartment chondrosis consistent with mild-to-moderate tricompartment osteoarthritis of the left knee.
8. Nondisplaced 10 x 5 mm subchondral fracture medial femoral condyle with exuberant surrounding marrow edema.

report:
MRI LEFT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
History of left knee giving out

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
None

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: No surfacing hyperintensity of the posterior horn is probably due to intrasubstance degeneration. No definite meniscal tear detected. No para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: intact

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: Chronic complete tear with anterior tibial translation of approximately 1.0 cm.

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact but buckled from the anterior tibial translation.

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. Trace Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Medial compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Lateral compartment: Up to severe chondral loss at the tibial plateau with chondral fissures and subchondral edema.

Others:

Hoffa's fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Full-thickness chronic tear of the anterior cruciate ligament resulting in anterior tibial translation approximately 1 cm. Posterior cruciate ligament is intact but is buckled from the anterior tibial translation.

Up to severe chondrosis at the lateral tibiofemoral compartment with full-thickness chondral fissures and loss at the lateral tibial plateau associated subchondral edema.

Minimal joint effusion.

report:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Intrasubstance degeneration within the medial meniscus without discrete tear. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

Mild patellofemoral chondrosis with focal full thickness cartilage denuding medial patellar facet, unchanged. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis, unchanged. Subtle chondral fibrillation involving the central weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle, unchanged.

Regional musculature is within normal limits. Trace joint fluid. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. No interval change since [Date].
2. No evidence of discrete meniscal, ligament, or tendon tear.
3. Subtle chondrosis as detailed above, without interval change.

report:
MRI of right  Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

* Interstitial hyperintensity signal of ACL, in favor of grade 1 injury.
* Interstitial hyperintensity signal of MCL, medial patellar retinaculum and laxity of the deep fibers, R/O partial tear.
* Interstitial increased signal intensity of quadriceps tendon on F/S T2WI, in favor of grade 1 injury; subcutaneous edema over anterior aspect of right knee
* Bone marrow edema in posterior lateral tibial plateua, in favor of bone contusion.

> The lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.

2. Grade 1 injury of ACL.
3. Grade 1 strain of Quadriceps tendon
4. Bone contusion of right posterior lateral tibial plateua.
5. Suprapatellar bursitis and mild synovitis of right knee and patellar plicae.
6. Subcutaneous edema over anterior and medial aspect of right knee.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.
